Vlach pastor (dušobrižnik) of Morlak pastiri in the Vitorog/Ljubuša area, recorded in Marijan-Lisnjic-b????‘s 1670–71 visitation Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Jurišić 1972:58).

people/Antonia-Reci-b-Zadar.title: Antonia-Reci-b????-Zadar
people/Antonia-Reci-b-Zadar.content:
Antonia Reci (?–1687)
Second wife of Stojan Janković; from a Greek-of-Latin-rite Zadar family (daughter of donna Nicolotta and q. Apostolo Rezzi; see Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I doc. 228 for marriage 16 Aug 1676).
Died 29 Jan 1687 in Zadar; buried at Sv. Šime, Zadar Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Mother of Stojan’s surviving sons Josip, Konstantin and of the children Marietta (d. 2 Feb 1686) and Liberal (d. 23 Aug 1686), all buried in Zadar in 1686–87.

people/Antonio-Canagetti-b.title: conte; sergente maggiore di battaglia; colonnello di dragoni
people/Antonio-Canagetti-b.content:
Conte Antonio Canagetti (Kanađeti)
Conte; sergente maggiore di battaglia; later colonnello of dragoons. Implicated in the tax extortion (~300 zecchini) that triggered the 1704 Bukovica revolt (docs 352, 389) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
In 1703 instructed to approach the line during the Alaibeg Mustafa raid; advanced 200 zecchini to Morlacchi (doc 352).
In 1707 killed Vid Petrović in ambush at Bruvno, together with a son of conte Obradović of Bruvno (doc 365) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 352, 363, 365, 389.

people/Antonio-Civran-b-Venice.title: kapetan gulfa
people/Antonio-Civran-b-Venice.content:
Antonio Civran (1615)
Venetian kapetan gulfa (commander of the Adriatic). His 18 March 1615 relacija records oral tradition collected directly from the Krmpoćani in negotiations to relocate them from Lic / Bakar area to Venetian territory (Commissiones et Relationes Venetae VI/1960:223) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
The relacija is the single most important narrative source for the Krmpote migration: Civran reports that the Carapotani had moved ~150 years before from somewhere into the area “around Gracac” (likely the older form Gradac); when they became suspect there (“in sospetto”), they relocated to the area around Novigrad; eventually, “fastiditi dell’Imperio de’Turchi”, they moved to “un certo luoco sopra Buccari quindeci miglia” (= Lic above Bakar) on the Habsburg nadvojvoda’s territory Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Šarić cross-validates this oral tradition against the 1477 defter, the Kijani stećak (Ivan-Balenovic-b????-Kijani), and Pavličević 1989 to construct the canonical Krmpote itinerary: Hercegovina → Gračac (~1465?) → Medviđa/Krmpote (1528 / post-Cyprus War 1573–74) → Lič (1605, 1627) → Vinjerac (1647).
Likely descendant of Andrea-Civran-b????-Venice (providur Dalmacije 1524) — same Venetian patrician family.

people/Antonio-Michielo-b-Venice.title: zadarski knez
people/Antonio-Michielo-b-Venice.content:
Antonio Michielo
Zadarski knez (1557). Reported the Morlachs on Zadar territory as “neukrotivi i mnogi od njih lopovi” Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Antonio-Molin-b-Venice.title: provveditor estraordinario commissario / vice commissario in Dalmazia
people/Antonio-Molin-b-Venice.content:
Antonio Molin
Venetian provveditor estraordinario commissario (and at times styled vice commissario) in Dalmatia from autumn 1686, succeeding Marin Michiel at Zadar while Cornaro held overall command from Split/Šibenik.
Timeline (this source)

1686-09-17 — Cornaro from Salona (doc. 144) records that Molin “rimasto ultimamente a Zara” with multiple charges relating to that piazza.
1686-10-07 — Issues the alert to giudici e capitanii of the Kotari villages to remove non-combatants, livestock and goods to safe places, and to keep all able-bodied men under arms; mandate handed to Stojan Janković for execution (doc. 146; Zad. st. arh. Spisi Molin, knj. jedina, str. 24).
1686-11-10 — Reports to Cornaro on the slow Morlach response, the dispatch of Janković to Nadin and Bortulačić to Tinj, and the cavalry’s logistics issues at Malpaga (doc. 149).

people/Antonio-Zen-b-Venice.title: provveditor estraordinario at Cattaro; later provveditor general della cavalleria
people/Antonio-Zen-b-Venice.content:
Antonio Zen (Zeno)
Venetian provveditor extraordinario at Cattaro in 1686 (doc. 131, dispatching Korponež’s galeotta to relieve the Pastrovići siege).
Subsequently provveditor general della cavalleria. Reports from Zadar 12 April 1686 and 18 June 1687 (docs. 133, 134) on Janković’s 1,600-man command, on the cavalry’s incursions, on harambaša Boža Milković’s ambush of Knin Turks at Bukovica, and on Zaviša Janković’s capture of the Udbina disdar Ibrahim-aga and the spahija Muhamed-beg (nephew of Ibrahim Pašić of Ripač) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Antonio-de-Mula-b-Venice.title: zadarski knez
people/Antonio-de-Mula-b-Venice.content:
Antonio de Mula
Zadarski knez (1540). Retained ~1,000+ Vlach defectors on Zadar territory after the October 1540 peace, against Ottoman recall — origin of the “Morlaci Istrijani” community on the Zadar contado Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Antun-Bortulacic-b-Zadar.title: dottor (jurist / doctor of letters)
people/Antun-Bortulacic-b-Zadar.content:
Antun (Antonio) Bortulačić, dottor
Zadar patrician; dottor. Brother of Šimun Bortulačić (one of the four Morlak capi). Drafted petitions on behalf of the four Morlak capi (Posedarski, Bortulačić, Janković, Smiljanić) to the Venetian Senate against Mocenigo’s appointment of the four “new” sub-leaders, July 1684 (doc 22) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Also referenced doc 58.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 22, 58.

people/Anzolo-Miani-b-Venice.title: senator
people/Anzolo-Miani-b-Venice.content:
Anzolo Miani
Venetian senator. Signed Senate decree of July 1684, doc 22 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 22.

people/Armus-pasa-Livno-b.title: Turkish pasha
people/Armus-pasa-Livno-b.content:
Armus-paša (Ormuz-paša?)
The other of two Turkish pashas at Livno October 1684, doc 40 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 40.

people/Athanasio-Georgiceo-b.title: izvještač (Habsburg agent / Catholic visitator)
people/Athanasio-Georgiceo-b.content:
Athanasio Georgiceo (1626)
Author of a 1626 izvješće on demographic conditions in Sandzak-Klis and the Vlach migration to Podunavlje (Batinić 1885:116–150) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Key data points:

The seoba “preko Dunava” was driven “ponajviše iz straha od Mehmed-bega i njegova oca” (i.e. Mustafa-beg-Klis-b???? and Mehmed-beg-Klis-b????).
Sandžak Klis raja population dropped from ~30,000 houses to ~20,000 between 1600 and 1624 — 25 godina nestajanja.

people/Augustin-Vlatkovic-b.title: fra; vojvoda
people/Augustin-Vlatkovic-b.content:
Fra Augustin Vlatković
Member of Catholic Bosnian-Hum noble house Jurjević-Vlatković. Around 1482 entered Ottoman service with peasant and Vlach subjects, governing the western frontier of Sandzak-Hercegovina (later nahije Fragustin, Primorje, Ljubuški) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Balthazar-Hacquet-b.title: francuski liječnik u austrijskoj službi
people/Balthazar-Hacquet-b.content:
Balthazar Hacquet (1802–05)
French physician in Austrian service, author of Abbildung und Beschreibung der südwest und östlichen Wenden, Illyrer und Slaven (1802–05). Records the Bunjevci as part of the Likaner Volk — the bravest of all Ličani (whom he called “austrijski Crnogorci”), poludivlji, prone to pljačka, with women of greatest virtue Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Hacquet 1802–05:165, 177).

people/Bartolomej-fra-b-Kapucin.title: fra (Capuchin), vojni kapelan
people/Bartolomej-fra-b-Kapucin.content:
fra Bartolomej, kapucin (1649)
Vojni kapelan whose 1649 izvješće documents Catholic conversion movement in the Zadar and Šibenik zaleđe (Bogović 1993:167–170) Saric-2008-Bunjevci — Candian War-era data point for confessional shifts in the Bunjevac/Vlach population on the Venetian-Ottoman frontier.

people/Bartolomeo-Varisano-Grimaldi-b-Ve.title: cavalier; Governator General dell'armi (commander of paid militia)
people/Bartolomeo-Varisano-Grimaldi-b-Ve.content:
Bartolomeo Varisano Grimaldi
Cavalier; Governator General dell’armi (commander of the paid militia), 1684, docs 33, 38 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 33, 38.

people/Bassa-di-Bosna-1684-b.title: bassa di Bosna (Pasha of Bosnia)
people/Bassa-di-Bosna-1684-b.content:
Bassa di Bosna (1684, unnamed)
Unnamed Pasha of Bosnia, May 1684; reported to be heading to Belgrade and onward to Hungary Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes

Distinct from the later Bosnian Pasha of April 1685 (who led the Sinj relief and took Alberti as personal slave).

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — various docs.

people/Bassa-di-Bosna-1685-b.title: bassa di Bosna (Pasha of Bosnia)
people/Bassa-di-Bosna-1685-b.content:
Bassa di Bosna (1685, unnamed)
Unnamed Pasha of Bosnia in 1685. Led the Sinj relief and Venetian rout April 1685; took Ivan Alberti as his personal slave; offered to return Valier’s silver, docs 60, 61, 62, 65 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes

Distinct from the Bosnian Pasha of 1684.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 60, 61, 62, 65.

people/Bastic-pasha-b-Zvornik.title: newly-named pasha of Zvornik (1686)
people/Bastic-pasha-b-Zvornik.content:
Bastić, pasha of Zvornik
Newly-named pasha of Zvornik (sandžak Zvornik) in 1686. Sent to Livno in early September 1686 with a kapidžibaša and the new Bosnian alajbeg Filipović plus 600 Turks, to repair the towers and houses burned in Janković’s first Livno raid (mid-July 1686) and to reinforce the castle. Routed in the second Livno raid (5 Sept 1686, doc. 141) when Janković and Smiljanić attacked with 6,000 men Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Battista-Contarini-b-Venice.title: Conte of Šibenik (provveditor)
people/Battista-Contarini-b-Venice.content:
Battista Contarini
Venetian noble; Conte (provveditor) of Sibenik 1684–1685. Mustered 300 pack horses + 500 Šibenik Morlaks (doc 25) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Wrote on the nature of the Morlaks (doc 59). Also doc 48.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 25, 48, 59.

people/Benedikt-Vinkovic-b-Zagreb.title: zagrebački biskup
people/Benedikt-Vinkovic-b-Zagreb.content:
zagrebački biskup Benedikt Vinković (1639)
Zagreb diocese. His 1639 izvješće documents masovno prevjeravanje s pravoslavlja na katolicizam in the Krmpote, Istra, and Kras areas (Bogović 1993:107–108) Saric-2008-Bunjevci — concrete data point for the period before the Catholic Krmpote core of Lic/Senjsko Primorje became fully homogeneous.

people/Bernardo-Balbi-b-Venice.title: šibenski knez i kapetan
people/Bernardo-Balbi-b-Venice.content:
Bernardo Balbi
Šibenski knez i kapetan. 4 May 1532: distinguished between cooperative border Vlachs and the more aggressive Vlachs from northern mountain regions raiding Šibenik territory Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Bijovce-sin-Vuckov-b-Ostrovica.title: knez
people/Bijovce-sin-Vuckov-b-Ostrovica.content:
Bijovče, sin Vučkov
Knez of an 86-house dzemat in nahija Ostrovica in 1550 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Likely orthodox; gives his name to today’s Biovičino Selo kod Kistanja. Dzemat included Međare, Žaževiž (Žažvić), Putičane, Dubravice, Dobra Voda, Bratiškovac, Čulišić.

people/Bili-Vucic-b-Vrana.title: harambaša of Vrana
people/Bili-Vucic-b-Vrana.content:
Bili Vučić
Harambaša of Vrana in 1684; co-signed petitions of September 1684 from the Vrana Morlaks, docs 35, 36 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 35, 36.

people/Biljan-Jancic-b-Kucista.title: Biljan-Jancic-b????-Kucista
people/Biljan-Jancic-b-Kucista.content:
Biljan, sin Jančića
Resident of Kućišta (nahija Zrmanja) in 1528 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Bogdan-Prejic-b.title: timarnik (after 1557)
people/Bogdan-Prejic-b.content:
Bogdan Prejić
Son of Petar-Prejic-b????. As a child fled to Habsburg territory c. 1538; later returned to Ottoman side, converted to Islam in mature age, and in 1557 received a timar on the recommendation of Malkoc-beg-b???? (Klis sanjakbeg) — sign of the family’s continued standing Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Boza-Milkovic-b-Bukovica.title: harambaša / karambaša (Bukovica)
people/Boza-Milkovic-b-Bukovica.content:
Bože Milković
Karambaša heading the guardia estraordinaria of 50 cavalrymen in Bukovica in spring 1686. Tasked by provveditor Antonio Zen with watching the Knin Turks; on a raid by ~30 Knin Turks toward Skradin (April 1686), he occupied the passes, ambushed them on the return, captured 2, took a banner, killed 7 — five heads + the banner brought to Zadar; Bože received a medal forwarded from Cattaro (doc. 133, 12 April 1686) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Boza-Sarcevic-b-Subotica.title: pokretač narodnoga preporoda u Bačkoj
people/Boza-Sarcevic-b-Subotica.content:
Boza (Ambrozije) Šarčević (1868)
Subotica intellectual; in 1868 launches the Bunjevački kalendar — the founding publication of the 19th-c. Bunjevac narodni preporod in Backa Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Counterpart in Subotica to Ivan-Antunovic-b1815-Backa in Kaloča.

people/Bucco-engineer-b.title: ingegnere (engineer)
people/Bucco-engineer-b.content:
Signor di Bucco (Boucaut), engineer
Engineer; drew the plan for the Skradin walls in 1685 (doc 50). Fell ill before the Sinj battle April 1685 (doc 60) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 50, 60.

people/Bun-praotac-b-Tudoricevci.title: Bun-praotac-b????-Tudoricevci
people/Bun-praotac-b-Tudoricevci.content:
Bun (1330)
Vlach forebear named in the 1330 Dečanska povelja (Stefan Uroš III’s hrisovulja for manastir Dečani). Listed by name with sons Nikola, Tvrtko, Tvrde, Tudorica, brother Rade, and Rade’s son Vojisil Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Ivanović 1951–52:260).
The clan Bunovići in the Tudoricevci katun (29 ognjišta) descends from him. Onomastic relic: Bunova livada / Livadhi i Bon’s in selo Shaptej near Dečani (Gashi 1982).
Šarić takes the name Bun/Bunj to be a vlach personal name from Latin Bonifacius via Balkan-Romance vocalic shift o > u; this Bun is a key 14th-c. attestation of the anthroponym from which the etnik Bunjevac is derived.

people/Bunac-Rusovic-b-Buncici.title: Bunac-Rusovic-b????-Buncici
people/Bunac-Rusovic-b-Buncici.content:
Bunac Rušović
Named on a tall medieval stećak in Buncici (Radmilović-Dubrava, near Bileća). Cyrillic inscription. Bešlagić 1971:390 Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
The size of the stećak suggests an imućnija osoba, likely a vlach starešina. Šarić connects him to the Vlasi Banjani aglomeracija, in which Rušovići are documented in dubrovački sources as starešine.
Personal name Bunac is itself a slavicized hipokoristik of the vlach name Bun/Bunj (< Latin Bonifacius).

people/Bunjak-sin-Radovana-b-Rudine.title: Bunjak-sin-Radovana-b????-Rudine
people/Bunjak-sin-Radovana-b-Rudine.content:
Bunjak sin Radovanov (1477)
Member of the džemat of Poblah sin Radovana in nahija Rudine, 1477 Hercegovina defter (Aličić 1985:68) Saric-2008-Bunjevci. One of only two Bun-stem personal names found among 7,822 Vlach-household-heads + comparable patronymic-fathers in the entire Hercegovina defter (the other being Bunus-sin-Petra-b????-Bjelopavlici).
Onomastic significance: by the late 15th c. Bun-stem names had become very rare in Hercegovinian vlach society — even when, by Šarić’s argument, the Bunjevci themselves were forming there. Šarić reads this as evidence that vlach personal-name stocks were already heavily slavicized (rad-, vuk-, drag-, mil-) by 1477 and the romanic Bun-stem was archaic.

people/Bunus-sin-Petra-b-Bjelopavlici.title: Bunus-sin-Petra-b????-Bjelopavlici
people/Bunus-sin-Petra-b-Bjelopavlici.content:
Bunuš sin Petra (1477)
Recorded in nahija Bjelopavlići, 1477 Hercegovina defter (Aličić 1985:102) Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Together with Bunjak-sin-Radovana-b????-Rudine, one of only two Bun-stem personal-name attestations across the entire Hercegovina defter.

people/Camucio-engineer-b.title: ingegnere (engineer)
people/Camucio-engineer-b.content:
Camucio (engineer)
Engineer (ingegnere) at the Sinj siege April 1685, docs 60, 61 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 60, 61.

people/Capitan-Solimano-b.title: capitan of light cavalry
people/Capitan-Solimano-b.content:
Capitan Solimano
Captain of light cavalry on Marin Michiel’s Knin reconnaissance tour February 1685, doc 51 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes

“Solimano” is the Italian rendering of Sulayman; possibly a convert.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 51.

people/Capitanio-Segna-b-Senj.title: capitanio (Senjski Hungarian-nationality captain)
people/Capitanio-Segna-b-Senj.content:
Capitanio Segna
Senjski (from Senj) captain, of Hungarian nationality. At the Sinj battle April 1685, his alfier (standard-bearer) gave Marin Michiel his horse to escape, doc 61 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes

“Segna” is the Italian for Senj — used as descriptor in the source rather than a strict surname.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 61.

people/Capo-Palese-b-Zadar.title: capo (Zadar officer)
people/Capo-Palese-b-Zadar.content:
Capo Palese di Zara
Zadar officer; spiked the cannon at the Sinj battle April 1685 and died defending it, doc 60 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 60.

people/Cejvan-aga-Lopusic-b-Knin.title: aga
people/Cejvan-aga-Lopusic-b-Knin.content:
Čejvan-aga Lopušić
“De’ principali e forse il più infesto tra tutti i confinanti” — one of the most dangerous Turkish notables of the Knin frontier. Killed by Dragoja Avramović in a skirmish, doc 49 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 49.

people/Cejvan-beg-b.title: Ottoman official
people/Cejvan-beg-b.content:
Ćejvan-beg
Ottoman official involved in the Klis sandžak demarcation correspondence with the Visoka porta in mid 16th c., describing damage to “Stari Obrovac” by neighboring Christians (Istrans and others) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Cesare-Casanova-b.title: capitan / governator di Obrovazzi
people/Cesare-Casanova-b.content:
Cesare Casanova
Italian; previously kept a galeotta in the Dalmatian waters and spent years at Spalato; appointed by Molin capitan / governator of Obrovac in January 1690 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 226, 227). Died c. 1693; succeeded as governor of both Obrovacs by Dimo Vlastò (Dolfin’s appointment 10 Jan 1693, doc 260) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (also docs 256, 260).

people/Conte-Marianovic-b.title: conte; capitano
people/Conte-Marianovic-b.content:
Conte Marianović
Captain who died after the Sinj battle April 1685; Alberti was named to be his successor, doc 65 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 65.

people/Conte-Sabbini-b-Venice.title: conte
people/Conte-Sabbini-b-Venice.content:
Conte Sabbini
Venetian conte exchanged for Zelel-aga Babahmetović during the last (Cretan/Candian) war, doc 56 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 56.

people/Culina-sin-Milica-b-Bjeline.title: knez (timarnik)
people/Culina-sin-Milica-b-Bjeline.content:
Čulina, sin Milića
Knez residing on mezra Stara Bilina (today Bjeline); held a timar in Lika Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Possible (but unconfirmed) ancestor of the Culina / Čulinović lineage attested in 16th–17th c. on the original Tromeđa.

people/Cvijan-Saric-b-Sibenik.title: harambaša → serdar de Morlacchi di Šibenik (orthodox)
people/Cvijan-Saric-b-Sibenik.content:
Cvijan Šarić — serdar šibenskih pravoslavnih Morlaka
The Cvitko / Cvijan Šarić of Evlija Çelebi (1660, “hrvatski razbojnik”) and of the Sv. Zulijan Šibenik baptismal registers is the same man who appears across the Desnica corpus 1647–66 as harambaša → serdar of the Šibenik Orthodox Morlachi.
Family

Wife: Dessa (Sv. Zulijan baptismal registers, doc. 81, 83, 144).
Sons:

Iuan/Ivan — baptised 1654-07-02 at Sv. Zulijan, Šibenik; compare Prodan Zubićević (docs. 81, 83). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
Žorži/Zorzi Šarić — harambassa in the 1654 Sv. Zulijan parish protest (doc. 84).
Zuanne/Jovan Šarić — Cvijan’s pay (4 ducati + peso di biscotto) transferred to him 1662-03-14 by provveditore Andrea Korner (doc. 123). Jovan still alive 1682-06-03, when Doge orders the back-pay arrears settled (doc. 285).



Timeline

1652-12 / 1653-01-03 — Among the carambasse who captured the alaj-beg Filipović at Duare; pay renewed (docs. 68, 69).
1653-04-04 — Provveditore Foscarini grants 4 ducati + peso di biscotto/month for capturing alaj-beg Filipović (doc. 69 — the man transferred is in fact a leader from this same operation).
1654-07-02 — Son Ivan/Iuan Šarić baptised at Sv. Zulijan (orthodox), Šibenik (docs. 81, 83). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1654-07-26 — Cuitho Sarich harambassa heads a 37-name list of the šibenski Orthodox Morlachi (mostly harambasse — see Saric-Sibenik-Pravoslavni-Morlaci-1654) who collectively defend their parohijski sveštenik fra Cirilo Gabrieli against Jovan Vuković Obrad (doc. 84). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1662-03-14 — Pay transferred to son Jovan “in attentione di esser augmentate per la fruttuose operatione contribute anco nel corso di questa nostra carica” (doc. 123) — i.e. Cvijan was still alive but stepping back. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1664-01-07 — Provveditore Contarini frees the galiot Jakov Vučić “ricercato in gratia da esso Sarich et altri Morlacchi di Šibenik” — recompense for burning all the Turkish hay reserves around Knin (doc. 136). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1665-10-15 — Cvijan now serdar Cuitco Sarich: his wife Dessa is comare at the baptism of Lukas Zubičević (whose mother Catarina was widow of Ilija Smiljanić — doc. 144). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1666-04-05 — Cetina rotta: Cornaro to Senate names “harambassa di Sebenico Sarich, che vecchio, ardito e pieno d’ avidità, niente cura i pericoli” as the principal concertatore of the doomed Cetina raid in which Stojan Janković was captured (doc. 148). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1666-05-21 — Cornaro signs Cvijan’s pay-renewal (date terminus post quem of his death; transferred to brother Vučen 1666-05-21, doc. 155 — but doc. 155 concerns Močivuna not Šarić; Cvijan’s son was already collecting since 1662).
1668-06-13 — Provveditore Priuli orders the camera fiscal di Veglia to pay Cvijan 10 ducati/month back-pay from October 1667 — therefore Cvijan was still alive in 1668 (doc. 159). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1668-10-06 — “a nome anco di tutti i Morlacchi che seguono il rito vecchio” he and pop Cirilo press provveditor Priuli for action against Mihovil Kapuano of Šibenik who throws garbage at the Orthodox church and verbally abuses the parish priest (doc. 162). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Notes

Religious profile: explicitly rito greco (Orthodox); curate is fra Cirilo Gabrieli, parish church Sv. Zulijan, Šibenik (an old Orthodox enclave). Šarić is its de facto patron — leads the parish’s collective defence in 1654, 1668. The Ottoman administrative label “Hrvat” used by Evlija Çelebi for him is, per Šarić 2008, an example of how the Vilajet-Hrvati (abolished 1537) designation persisted across confessional boundaries.

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 68, 69, 81, 83, 84, 123, 136, 144, 148, 159, 162, 285.
Saric-2008-Bunjevci — Evlija Čelebi 1660 attestation as “hrvatski razbojnik.”

people/Dadoje-vojvoda-b-Hercegovina.title: vojvoda
people/Dadoje-vojvoda-b-Hercegovina.content:
vojvoda Dadoje
Vlach voivode in the 1477 Hercegovina defter for nahija Humska zemlja. Head of a knežinska aglomeracija analogous to vojvoda Vladimir-vojvoda-b????-Hercegovina in nahija Mostar. The Krmpote katun (Vukic-Krmpotic-b????-Hercegovina) was part of his domain area Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
The 2024 article (Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre) names him as Radoje (“Dadoj”); the same person, distinguishing variants in Cyrillic/Ottoman transcription.

people/Damjan-Klokocic-b.title: knez
people/Damjan-Klokocic-b.content:
Damjan Klokočić
Croatian knez who crossed to the Ottoman side and converted to Islam in 1523 — one of the early documented cases of noble vjeroprijelaz on the original Tromeđa Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Damjan-Santic-b.title: Damjan-Santic-b????
people/Damjan-Santic-b.content:
Damjan Šantić (Damian Santich)
Member of the Radoš consortium that owned Ivisa Mandić as slave 1685, doc 65 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 65.

people/Damjan-Zdunic-b-Lovinac.title: župnik
people/Damjan-Zdunic-b-Lovinac.content:
Damjan Zdunić (1712)
Catholic župnik of Lovinac during the 1712 Lika–Krbava popis Saric-2008-Bunjevci — one of four Bunjevac priests at the four major Bunjevac parishes (with Petar-Butkovic-b????-Novo, Simun-Zdunic-b????-Smiljan, Juraj-Smolcic-b????-Pazariste).
Identified in Saric-2008-Bunjevci with the “pop Zduna” of folk tradition.

people/Daniel-Dolfin-IV-b-Venice.title: kavalier; provveditor general di Dalmazia (1696–1697); later again 1737–1738
people/Daniel-Dolfin-IV-b-Venice.content:
Daniel Dolfin (IV)
Venetian provveditor general of Dalmatia. Predecessor of Mocenigo II in the first generalate; gave the 1697 relazione to the Senate documenting Morlach manpower, character, and deployment (doc 305) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
A later Daniel Dolfin “quarto” (likely the same office-holder dynasty’s descendant) served as provveditor general 1737–1738, handling pop Petar Jagodić’s correspondence (docs 386, 387, 388) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 305, 386, 387, 388.

people/Daniel-Dolfin-b-Venice.title: kavalier; provveditor generale in Dalmazia
people/Daniel-Dolfin-b-Venice.content:
Daniel Dolfin
Venetian patrician, kavalier provveditor. Provveditor generale in Dalmazia from February 1692, succeeding Alessandro Molin; held the post (with one interval) through 1696, when he was succeeded by Aluise Mocenigo II Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (multiple docs from 243 onward).
Major acts in this source

March 1692 — Reconciled the warring Mitrović and Milković kuće after the killing of Bože Milković’s brother by Ilija Mitrović’s followers; mediated the parallel reconciliation between the Mitrovići and Sinobadi Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 247).
1692-04-01 — Restored Ilija Mitrović’s 15-ducat/month terminacija (originally granted by Mocenigo 15 July 1684) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 248).
1692-04-01 — Appointed Nicolò Mitrović (son of Ilija) capitano of the Croat cavalry company formerly held by his cousin Konstantin Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 249).
June 1692 — Authorized 10 ducats + biscuit/month to Conte Paolo Đurić capo of Bjelaj province for leading ~5,000 souls into Venetian devotion Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 251).
1692-10 — Settled Ivan Rašić’s 200 souls / 25 families at Zavojane / Stigli / Hadži Lukovo near Makarska Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 258).
1693-01-10 — Appointed Dimo Vlastò governor of both Obrovacs after Casanova’s death Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 260).
1693-02-23 — Granted Đuro Popović Opačić of Mokro Polje 15 stara of millet as seed Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 265).
1693-11-06 — At Šibenik when Stefano Capelo reported the Gorica raid of 4 Nov 1693 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 268).
1694-03 — Reappointed Francesco Spingaroli governor of Biograd, Pakoštane and Vrana Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 275).
1694 — Authorized the Brochno-Blato-Goranci migration of ~5,000 souls under 5 serdari and 22 harambasse, settling them at Zadvarje and Vrgorac Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 274).
1694-08-21 — Appointed Mihail Sinobad capitano of Zvonigrad Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 277).
1694-12-23 — Appointed Janko Vrsalj harambaša at Plavno Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 278).
1696-02 — Appointed Mirko Jokić capitano of Obrovac inhabitants; promulgated the Liga statute of 12 Feb 1696 (the second great Liga reform after Cornaro 1689) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 284, 286).
1696 — Led the Ulcinj campaign; while at Ulcinj, Selman pasha of Hercegovina raided the Knin area (doc 293) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1696-11 — Appointed Vid Katalinić captain of a new 50-man Starigrad company Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 290–291, 294).
December 1696 — Released Oratio Lantana from his 2,000-ducat surety bond for Zaviša Mitrović Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 297).

Notes

Two stints as provveditor generale; held the post during the most consequential 5-year stretch of the Morean War on the Dalmatian front.
Succeeded by Aluise Mocenigo II in late 1696.

people/Daughter-of-Zelel-aga-b.title: Daughter-of-Zelel-aga-b????
people/Daughter-of-Zelel-aga-b.content:
Daughter of Zelel-aga Babahmetović
Unnamed daughter of Zelel-aga Babahmetović; a widow returning to her father; in Mehmed-beg Durakbegović’s escort during the March 1685 ambush, doc 56 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 56.

people/Domenico-Mocenigo-b-Venice.title: Provveditor general estraordinario dell'armi in Dalmatia et Albania (May 1684 – late 1684)
people/Domenico-Mocenigo-b-Venice.content:
Domenico Mocenigo (Domeniko Moćenigo)
Venetian noble; Provveditor general estraordinario dell’armi in Dalmatia et Albania. Arrived in Dalmatia May 1684 to replace the ailing Lorenzo Donà, doc 1 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Main correspondent in docs 1–43 of this volume.
Timeline

1684-05 — Arrives in Dalmatia; finds outgoing Provveditor Donà ill and bedridden at scoglio del Lantana near Zadar (doc 1) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1684-07 — Awards 15 ducats/month pension to Ilija-Mitrovic-b????-Zegar in recognition of Janko Mitrović’s deeds in the past war and Stojan Janković’s continuing service (doc 20) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1684-07 — Appoints four “new” sub-leaders (Alberti, Soppe, Soppe Fortezza, Ventura) over the Kotari, in parallel with the four Morlak capi (doc 19); subsequently abolished by Senate (doc 23) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1684-08-31 — Awards Stojan Janković 10 ducats/month durante bello (doc 29) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1684 — Petition by the four Morlak capi (Posedarski, Bortulačić, Janković, Smiljanić) to Senate against his appointments; Senate rules in favor of the capi (docs 22, 23) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1684 (late) — Replaced; eventually scapegoated for the subsequent Sinj defeat Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 1–43 passim.

people/Dragic-Avramovic-b.title: Dragic-Avramovic-b????
people/Dragic-Avramovic-b.content:
Dragić Avramović (Draghich Abramovich)
Morlak suddito (newcomer). Petitioner for relief for the widow and children of his deceased brother Dragoja, who killed Čejvan-aga Lopušić of Knin in a skirmish and was himself killed. Awarded 1 peso of biscuit/month by Mocenigo February 1685, doc 49 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 49.

people/Dragisa-sin-Dragoja-b-Plavna.title: vojvoda
people/Dragisa-sin-Dragoja-b-Plavna.content:
Dragiša, sin Dragoja
Vojvoda in Plavna in the 1540 register — replaced the fugitive Zakman-Gledjevac-b????-Karin as the leading vojvoda among the Vlasi Istre after the 1538 mass defection Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Resident in selo Podlužje, leading 37 houses.

people/Dragoja-Avramovic-b.title: Dragoja-Avramovic-b????
people/Dragoja-Avramovic-b.content:
Dragoja Avramović (Dragoglia)
Morlak; brother of Dragić Avramović. Killed in a skirmish with Knin Turks; killed Čejvan-aga Lopušić first, doc 49 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Left widow and children, for whom his brother petitioned successfully for support.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 49.

people/Dure-Dekic-b-Vrana.title: harambaša of Vrana
people/Dure-Dekic-b-Vrana.content:
Đure Đekić (Giure Giechich)
Harambaša/capo of Vrana Morlaks; co-signed petition of September 1684, doc 35 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 35.

people/Ferhad-Prejic-b-Novosel.title: Ferhad-Prejic-b????-Novosel
people/Ferhad-Prejic-b-Novosel.content:
Ferhad, sin Prijića (Pribića)
Possible Muslim convert of the Prejić lineage in selo Novosel (nahija Obrovac), 1528. Reading of the patronymic could be either “Prijić” or “Pribić” Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Ferhat-beg-Sokolovic-b.title: kliški sandžakbeg
people/Ferhat-beg-Sokolovic-b.content:
Ferhat-beg Sokolović
Klis sanjakbeg active 1568–1574+. 1568: settled ~200 “nevjernika Istre” families from Venetian territory near Knin (Plavno?), authorized by Porte ferman 21 November 1568 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1574: uvakufio Tinj for Zemunik vakuf (six villages) and Hrvace; resettled with Vojnic Bunjevac colonists from nahija Sinj.

people/Filip-Lastric-b.title: bosanski povjesničar (fra)
people/Filip-Lastric-b.content:
fra Filip Lastrić
18th-c. Bosnian Franciscan historian. Cited by Šarić for his vivid characterization of the Bosanska franjevačka provincija – Dalmatian dioceses dispute over jurisdiction over Catholic Vlachs:

“dalmatinskim biskupima nije stalo do spasa ovaca, nego se bore za njihovu vunu”

(Zirdum 1982:86) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
The dispute (which structured the Buna-river origin legend that Bosnian franjevci constructed) was, in Lastrić’s reading and Džaja’s confirmation, a borba za osiguranje materijalnih dobara i karijerizam sudionika, not for vjernike.

people/Filip-Smiljanic-b-Udbina.title: harambaša → kapetan oklopnika → kapetan lake konjice → glavni harambaša (1654)
people/Filip-Smiljanic-b-Udbina.content:
Filip Smiljanić (c. 1633 – January 1656)
Younger son of Petar. “basso, occhi uarii, pelcastagno, prima lanugine, d’ anni venti in circa” (doc. 53, terminacija 1650-03-01). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
Timeline

1650-03-01 — 4 ducati/month (doc. 53). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1653-05-03 — Provveditore Dolfin replaces him into the compagnia di corazze of the banished Frane Jeremija; Dolfin reduces it to cavalleria leggera capelletta (doc. 72). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1654-09-08 — Eyewitness deposition of his brother Ilija’s death at Vučjak (doc. 86). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1654-09-16 — Universal Morlachi petition gets him named principal harambaša after Ilija; Dolfin grants it but warns him about “ferocità del suo ardire, che dal bollore della gioventù suole ricevere dannose instigationi” (doc. 88). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1656-01-29 — Buried at the cathedral (Sv. Stošija) Zadar, alongside his alfier Frane Marininić (doc. 99). Killed in Šibenik in a brawl with a Venetian plaćeni vojnik of the šibenska posada — Desnica’s footnote (doc. 99). The deaths caused major Morlach unrest in Šibenik; provveditore Zen sent col. Davila to restore order (doc. 98). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 53, 72, 86, 88, 97, 98, 99.

people/Filip-Starcevic-b-Pazariste.title: seoski knez
people/Filip-Starcevic-b-Pazariste.content:
Filip Starčević
Grandson of Jakov-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste, great-grandson of porkulab Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik. Seoski knez at the end of the 18th c. (a function by then largely overtaken by militarized Vojnokrajiška hierarchy) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Father of Sime-Starcevic-b1784-Lika.

people/Filip-Zupanovic-b-Tinj.title: knez
people/Filip-Zupanovic-b-Tinj.content:
knez Filip Županović (1647)
Successor starešina figure (after Milos-Zupanovic-b????-Tinj) of the Vlasi Vojnići of Tinj / Županovići. In 1647 during the Candian War, led the migration of part of the Vojnići onto Venetian territory, settling Valtura near Pula Saric-2008-Bunjevci (see Krmpote-Migration-Vinjerac-1647).

people/Filippo-Mitrovic-b-Obrovac.title: capitano (56-piede company); nephew of [[Zavisa-Jankovic-b????-Zegar|Zaviša]]
people/Filippo-Mitrovic-b-Obrovac.content:
Filippo (Filip) Mitrović
Capitano of a 56-foot company at Obrovac from 1688; dismissed by Molin in January 1690 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 227). Identified in the source as nephew of Zaviša Mitrović — possibly a son of a third Mitrović brother (otherwise unattested in Janko’s documented sons Stojan, Zaviša, Ilija). Distinct from Filip Smiljanić.
Notes

Confidence medium because no parental link to the wider Mitrović-Janković kuća is explicitly named; Desnica records only the “nephew of Zaviša” formula.

people/Filippo-Tintor-b-Sibenik.title: Filippo-Tintor-b????-Sibenik
people/Filippo-Tintor-b-Sibenik.content:
Filippo Tintor
Cavalry harambaša from the Šibenik–Skradin area. Arrives at Bribir 12 Nov 1686 with 10 horse to join Stojan Janković at the Bosnian-pasha alarm; immediately re-dispatched to all the capi and karambaše of the Kotari to drive the muster (doc. 155) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Fran-Prejic-b-Opatija.title: Fran-Prejic-b????-Opatija
people/Fran-Prejic-b-Opatija.content:
Fran, sin Prejića
Resident of Opatija (today’s Kula-Atlagica) in 1528 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Francesco-Gritti-b-Venice.title: senator / consigliere
people/Francesco-Gritti-b-Venice.content:
Francesco Gritti
Venetian senator/consigliere, 1684; signed Senate decree (doc 22) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 22.

people/Francesco-Morosini-b-Venice.title: Doge of Venice
people/Francesco-Morosini-b-Venice.content:
Doge Francesco Morosini
Doge of Venice during much of the Morean War. Ducale of 21 May 1690 awarding 10 ducats/month to capt. Marko Smiljanić for service in the Morean campaigns Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 233). Ducale of 22 October 1692 confirming Nicolò Lomazzi as Illyrian interpreter at Zadar Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 257).

people/Francesco-Ventura-b.title: capitano; sub-leader for Castel Venier–Razanci–Ljuba–Radovin–Polešnik (1684)
people/Francesco-Ventura-b.content:
Francesco (Frane) Ventura
Capitano; one of four “new” sub-leaders Mocenigo appointed in 1684 over the Kotari sub-region of Castel Venier–Razanci–Ljuba–Radovin–Polešnik, doc 19 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Position abolished by Senate in doc 23.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 19, 23.

people/Frane-Mircetic-b-Vrana.title: harambaša of Vrana Morlaks
people/Frane-Mircetic-b-Vrana.content:
Frane Mirčetić (Francesco Mircetich)
Harambaša of Vrana Morlaks. Co-signed petitions of September 1684 against Šimun Bortulačić’s appointment as their capo, asking for Smoljan Smiljanić instead, docs 35, 36 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 35, 36.

people/Frane-Peraica-b-Zegar.title: harambaša / serdar of Peraica's people (from Oct 1685)
people/Frane-Peraica-b-Zegar.content:
Frane (Francesco) Peraica
Brother of serdar Ilija Peraica, who in earlier years had brought 1,600 souls from Ottoman territory under Venetian devotion (Mocenigo’s pay-grant of 10 ducati/month, 15 July 1684). Ilija was killed in combat with an Ottoman corsair fusta off Rogoznica while transporting his family to Zadar (autumn 1685).
Timeline (this source)

1685-10-01 — Terminacija of generalni providur Petar Valier in Split (doc. 104): assigns to Francesco Peraizza the 10 ducati/month previously paid to his deceased brother Ilija, “come quello che elletto dalle genti d’Elia in capo, promette eguale puntualità, fede et rassegnatione ai pubblici cenni” (Zad. drž. arh., Spisi P. Valier, knj. II, str. 156) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685 — His followers (“Peraizza’s people”) counted in the 1685 settlement census (doc. 107): 400 fighters / 1,400 souls scattered across the territories of Zadar and Šibenik per the parish priest’s lists.

Notes
The 1685 raid on Bjelaj-Vakuf (early Sept 1685) reports the bassà of Bosnia trying to recall “li morlacchi di Peraiza e Nachich” (doc. 74), so the family’s people were a known migration cohort.
Disambiguation: Peraica ≠ Mitrović of Žegar
The Peraica brothers (Ilija and Frane) led the March 1685 Cetina migration of 600 armed men + ~1,600 souls into Trogir territory. They are distinct from Ilija Mitrović of Žegar — brother of Stojan and Zaviša Janković — who lived through 1693 (per chunk-3 attestation, died of natural causes). One of the original chunk extractions conflated the two Ilijas; this wiki treats them as separate persons until further evidence emerges. The “-Zegar” in this filename is a legacy of that conflation; the Peraica clan’s actual base was the Cetina valley. See also Ilija-Mitrovic-b????-Zegar and Cetina-Migration-Peraica-1685.

people/Frane-Posedarski-b.title: knez
people/Frane-Posedarski-b.content:
Frane Posedarski
Knez who converted to Islam — listed among 16th-c. cases of noble defection on the original Tromeđa Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Franjo-Filipovic-b-Zagreb.title: kanon
people/Franjo-Filipovic-b-Zagreb.content:
Franjo Filipović
Canon of Zagreb, converted to Islam in 1578 — Šarić cites alongside other 16th-c. cases of noble or clerical defection across the Tromeđa Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Gabriel-Lombardo-b.title: nobleman attached to commissario Mikiel
people/Gabriel-Lombardo-b.content:
ser Gabriel Lombardo
Nobleman attached to commissario Marin Michiel. Missing or captured at the Sinj battle April 1685, docs 60, 61 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 60, 61.

people/Gaspar-Mauric-b.title: pazinski kapetan
people/Gaspar-Mauric-b.content:
Gašpar Maurić
Pazinski kapetan in 1571. Wrote 4 September 1571 to the Kranjska vicedom blaming his predecessor Jakob for the bloody clash that drove many Ćići to flee back to Ottoman territory after the Pazin-Peasant-Revolt-1570 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Gazi-Husrev-beg.title: bosanski sandžakbeg
people/Gazi-Husrev-beg.content:
Gazi Husrev-beg
Bosnian sanjakbeg and conqueror of central Croatia. Patron and superior of Murat-beg-Gajdic-b????-Sibenik Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Initiated the istimâlet return migration of the Vlasi Istre 1528. Founded the Kožulova polje vakuf in 1531 (later Kozulova-Polje nahija). His Bosnia hasovi in 1530 covered 10 cities, 158 villages, 64 čiftluks (annual revenue 643,979 akči). 1524: addressed by Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik proposing 100 Vlach families’ transfer.

people/Giacomo-Califfi-b-Zadar.title: conte
people/Giacomo-Califfi-b-Zadar.content:
Conte Giacomo Califfi (q. Francesco)
Conte; son of quondam conte Francesco Califfi. Sold half of Olib island to Zaviša Mitrović for 8000 ducats by contract of 26 November 1701 (doc 336) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. The sale included peculiar dynastic conditions binding the half-island to alternate between Zaviša’s male line and his deceased brother Ilija’s male line.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 336.

people/Giacomo-Sinobad-b-Posedarje.title: cornetta riformato; serdar of Knin (1729)
people/Giacomo-Sinobad-b-Posedarje.content:
Giacomo (Jakov) Sinobad
Cornetta riformato; cousin (“cugino”) of the deceased Andrea Sinobad; described as “ultimo superstite della famiglia.” Supplicated 1727 to be made serdar of Knin per family tradition; appointed serdar of Knin 1 December 1729 by ducal of Doge Mocenigo (replacing Petar Mitrović-Stojisavljević) (docs 378, 380) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 378, 380.

people/Giovan-Battista-Soppe-b-Zadar.title: kavalier; governator; sub-leader for Vrana–Tinj–Jagodnja–Skradin–Ostrovica–Bribir–Kosovo Polje (1684)
people/Giovan-Battista-Soppe-b-Zadar.content:
Giovan Battista Soppe (“Soppe Fortezza”)
Kavalier; Zadar noble; sub-leader appointed by Mocenigo in 1684 over the sub-region of Vrana–Tinj–Jagodnja–Skradin–Ostrovica–Bribir–Kosovo Polje (near Knin), doc 19 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Led a successful expedition (doc 24); also docs 15, 23, 32. Already attested in Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I as “governator Battista Sopino” (kompare at Stojan Janković’s son’s baptism 1674; at Janja Janković’s wedding 1675).
Notes

Distinct from Giulio Soppe (different sub-region).
The epithet “Fortezza” (fortress) distinguishes him from other Soppe bearers.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 15, 19, 23, 24, 32.
Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs 207, 210.

people/Giovanni-Antonio-Novelo-b-Venice.title: providur Sopraintendanture za granicu
people/Giovanni-Antonio-Novelo-b-Venice.content:
Giovanni Antonio Novelo
Venetian providur Sopraintendanture za granicu. 14 April 1559: reported to the Great Council that 3 of the 10 uskok leaders in Senj and Bakar were “turski prebjezi” Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Giovanni-Battista-Zappich-b-Zadar.title: segretario di camera at Zadar
people/Giovanni-Battista-Zappich-b-Zadar.content:
Giovanni Battista Žapić
Segretario di camera at Zadar in 1684, doc 10 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 10.

people/Girolamo-Cornaro-b-Venice.title: kavalier; provveditor general in Dalmazia et Albania (from 1686)
people/Girolamo-Cornaro-b-Venice.content:
Girolamo Cornaro
Provveditor generale in Dalmazia et Albania from 1686, succeeding Petar Valier. Brother of cavalier Catterino Cornaro of “ben degna memoria” who had earlier defended the tower of Lapsach/Lapčanj in the Makarska primorje (Senate dispatch of 27 July 1686, doc. 138).
Timeline (this source)

1686-07-19 (doc. 136) — Cornaro reports to the Senate from Split on the first Livno raid: 5,000 Morlach foot and 1,500 horse under Janković, Smiljanić, Posedarski (tenente collonnello) and Bortulačić — 400 Turks killed, 30 Christian slaves liberated, 1,800 houses burned. Requests medals and rings for the most valorous.
1686-09-17 (doc. 144, “from the tent at Salona”) — Reports the war-council decision to attempt Sinj with prince of Parma and S. Polo; raising 2,000 from garrisons + 1,000 sbarcati + cavalry + 3,000 Morlachi. Notes the death of provveditor general de cavalli Polo Michiel (with regret).
1686-09-30 (doc. 145, from camp at Sinj) — Reports the conquest of Sinj (assault night of 29 Sept; piazza taken). 150+ Turks killed in assault; 25–30 Venetians dead, 120 wounded; cannon recovered. Antonio Bollani named provveditore di Sinj at the Klis salary.
1686-10-30 (doc. 147) — Letter to the Inquisitori di Stato warning that the Ragusans are pushing the Habsburgs toward Bosnia and Herzegovina to forestall a Venetian conquest of Hercegnovi, and forwarding the suspicious Iljanović letter (doc. 139) addressed to Stojan Janković as “generale”. Receivedat Venice 9 Nov 1686.
1686-11-12 to 11-19 — Coordinates the response to the Bosnian pasha’s raid on the Kotari (16,000 Turks, 5 paše); writes from Šibenik and Skradin, urges Stojan Janković at Bribir, sends 200 reinforcements; the Turks ultimately retreat to Knin without significant booty (docs. 150–157).

In this source (1689 — chunk 3)

1689-03-11 — Promulgated the Liga statute of 1689, dividing the Zadar contado into 9 pertinenze with named governors and judges (Cassio at Nin, Calčina at Posedarje, Belglava at Novigrad area, Begna at Nadin, Spingaroli at Zaravecchia, etc.) — the canonical organizing document of the post-1684 administrative landscape (doc 224) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1689-03-30 — Issued the attestato on Zaviša Mitrović’s warlike deeds (Sinj, Zara, Vrcerev Vakup wounded, Knin) (doc 225) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Succeeded by Alessandro Molin later in 1689.

people/Girolamo-Zen-b-Venice.title: procurator (senator)
people/Girolamo-Zen-b-Venice.content:
Girolamo Zen
Venetian procurator; senator. Signed Senate decree of July 1684 (doc 22). Also referenced as illustrissimo Zen in doc 57 (possibly a different role — provveditor in the Levant) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 22, 57.

people/Giulio-Soppe-b-Zadar.title: sub-leader for Diklo–Kožino–Petrčane–Bokanjac–Gruhe–Dračevac (1684)
people/Giulio-Soppe-b-Zadar.content:
Giulio (Julije) Soppe
Zadar noble (Soppe family); sub-leader appointed by Mocenigo in 1684 for the Kotari sub-region of Diklo–Kožino–Petrčane–Bokanjac–Gruhe–Dracevac, doc 19 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Position abolished by Senate (doc 23).
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 19, 23.

people/Governator-Rados-b.title: colonnello / governator
people/Governator-Rados-b.content:
Governator / Colonnello Radoš
Brother of conte cavalier Ivan Radoš; governator / colonnello. Killed or missing at the Sinj battle April 1685, docs 60, 61 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 60, 61.

people/Grgur-Bratic-b-Ostrovica.title: primićur
people/Grgur-Bratic-b-Ostrovica.content:
Grgur Bratić
Primićur and head of a 29-house Vlasi Istre dzemat in nahija Ostrovica (1327 akči) in 1530 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Grgur-Lepur-b-Vrana.title: harambaša of Vrana
people/Grgur-Lepur-b-Vrana.content:
Grgur Lepur (Gregorio Lepur)
Vrana harambaša; co-signed petitions of September 1684, docs 35, 36 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 35, 36.

people/Grgur-Milohanovic-b-Nova-Vas.title: Grgur-Milohanovic-b????-Nova-Vas
people/Grgur-Milohanovic-b-Nova-Vas.content:
Grgur Milohanović
Returnee colonist from Nova-Vas near Poreč; in 1561 founded selo Miljacki in present-day Zemunik Gornji Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. After Ottoman conquest of Zemunik in 1570 led 40 families back to Istria, settling Zbandalj near Poreč with Ivan-Filipini-b????.

people/Grgur-Sutic-b-Vrana.title: fra (Franciscan); cappellano della natione (Morlak chaplain)
people/Grgur-Sutic-b-Vrana.content:
Fra Grgur Šutić (padre fra Gregorio Sutich)
Cappellano della natione (chaplain of the Morlak community). Convinced the Vrana Morlaks to seize Vrana from the Turks; trusted by Mocenigo as informant on Vrana sentiment, docs 34, 36 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 34, 36.

people/Gvozden-Sladovic-b-Mostar.title: vojvoda
people/Gvozden-Sladovic-b-Mostar.content:
vojvoda Gvozden Sladović
Starešina of the Sladović (sub)katun in the early 17th c., active across Bukovica and Podgorje Saric-2008-Bunjevci. The Sladović group of this period is known as “Gvozdenovi ljudi” after him.
In 1605 Gvozdenovi ljudi (20 families) joined the first Krmpote migration to Lič on the Zrinski Hreljin estate. Surnames in the 1605 group: Balinović, Brošković, Ilnić, Karanović, Lovrić, Martinović, Mihovilović, Mikulić, Sladović, Veljanić, Vilenica.
After 1605 the Sladović fate intertwines with the Krmpotić branch.

people/Hajra-Lakic-b-Karin.title: Hajra-Lakic-b????-Karin
people/Hajra-Lakic-b-Karin.content:
Hajra (Aire) — formerly Kosa — Lakić
Daughter of Matija Lakić of Karin. Captured August 1684 by Gračac Turks while threshing millet; sold at Knin to sandžak-beg Mehmed-beg Durakbegović, who Islamized her (“Aire” replacing “Cosa”) and made her his favorite. Recaptured March 1685 in a Klis–Trogir Morlak ambush, doc 56 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 56.

people/Hamza-beg-b.title: hercegovački sandžakbeg
people/Hamza-beg-b.content:
Hamza-beg
Hercegovački sandžakbeg in 1477. Concluded istimâlet contract with vlach vojvoda Vladimir-vojvoda-b????-Hercegovina returning Vlachs to Mostar/Hum nahija Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Harambasa-Njegovan-b-Medvidja.title: harambaša
people/Harambasa-Njegovan-b-Medvidja.content:
harambaša Njegovan (1647)
Krmpote starešina who led the final mass exodus of Krmpote families from Ottoman selo Krmpote (today Medvidja) during the 1647 migration of the Candian War Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Pavličević 1989).
Brought 40–50 Krmpote families to Venetian territory: settled primarily Vinjerac and Starigrad; some onward to Pag (later switching to Habsburg subjecthood). Crucial figure in the third and final reset of the Krmpote demographic split between Habsburg and Venetian sides of the Tromeđa.

people/Hasan-Prejic-b-Surozani.title: Hasan-Prejic-b????-Surozani
people/Hasan-Prejic-b-Surozani.content:
Hasan, sin Prejića (Surožani)
Muslim convert of the Prejić lineage; resident of Surozani (Ostrovica nahija) in 1540 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Hasan-aga-Frletic-b-Dracevac.title: aga; Venetian informant
people/Hasan-aga-Frletic-b-Dracevac.content:
Hasan-aga Frletić
Recorded 1590 as Venetian informant on the Novigradsko more frontier, residing in Dracevac Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Convert from the Frletić Vlach kindred — relative of the Tornik Firultić sons and the Senj uskok branch.

people/Hasan-aga-Mandic-b-Sinj.title: Hasan-aga-Mandic-b????-Sinj
people/Hasan-aga-Mandic-b-Sinj.content:
Hasan-aga Mandić
Son of Šain-aga Mandić of Sinj. Captured at the Kaštela in autumn 1685; held in the Zadar captain’s prison from 1 Oct 1685 alongside Šakija-aga.
Timeline (this source)

1685 (spring) — Slave of the Radoš consortium (Ivan Radoš, Matija Strmić, Damjan Šantić); ransom set at 2,000 reali plus 4 horses, of which 800 paid (docs 65, 68). Referred to as “Hasan-beg / Ivisa figliuolo del sudetto agà”.
1685-10-01 — Arrives in Zadar as prisoner, six weeks before doc. 109 (17 Nov 1685).
1685-11-17 (doc. 109) — Writes (probably to his father) complaining that captain Marušić had cut off his biscotto allowance; gives daily food rates (8 aspri + 1.5 lbs biscotto per 30 days under Rados).
Undated, autumn 1685 (docs. 111, 112) — Reports (probably to Šain-aga) the news that Janković has gone to Lika with 2,000 men, that Esztergom (Neuhäusel) and Coron have fallen, and that “il karambassà Peraizza” (Ilija Peraica) has been broken on the 8th of September with 175 captured by Turkish corsair fuste off the Šibenik coast.

people/Hasan-beg-Durakbegovic-b.title: Hasan-beg-Durakbegovic-b????
people/Hasan-beg-Durakbegovic-b.content:
Hasan-beg Durakbegović (Hassam)
Brother of Mehmed-beg Durakbegović (sandžak-beg of Knin); father of Mehmed-nephew. Killed earlier at Zemunik (date unclear; pre-1685), doc 56 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 56.

people/Hasan-beg-Mandic-b-Sinj.title: Hasan-beg-Mandic-b????-Sinj
people/Hasan-beg-Mandic-b-Sinj.content:
Hasan-beg / Ivisa Mandić — DEPRECATED
This page is a stub created in error during ingestion. The “Hasan-beg / Ivisa Mandić” referenced in docs 65 and 68 (slave of the Radoš consortium 1685, ransom 2,000 reali) is the same person as the existing Hasan-aga Mandić (son of Šain-aga); the source uses both “aga” and “beg” titles for him, and “Ivisa” appears as an alternate form.
See Hasan-aga-Mandic-b????-Sinj for canonical entry.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 65, 68.

people/Herak-sin-Radice-b-Zrmanja.title: knez
people/Herak-sin-Radice-b-Zrmanja.content:
Herak, sin Radice
Knez of the joint Zrmanja–Bukovica Vlasi Istre dzemat in 1540 — 61 houses Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Replaced by a different leader by 1550 (when Stepan-sin-Radovana-b????-Zrmanja heads the new “Zrmanja Istrija” group).

people/Hlapac-sin-Radovana-b-Plavna.title: primićur (knez)
people/Hlapac-sin-Radovana-b-Plavna.content:
Hlapac, sin Radovana
Primićur (knez) of the new “Plavna Istrija” nahija formed in 1540 from returning Vlasi Istre after the 1540 peace — 32 houses Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Husein-sin-Poropata-b-Krupa.title: Husein-sin-Poropata-b????-Krupa
people/Husein-sin-Poropata-b-Krupa.content:
Husein, sin Poropata
Muslim convert of the Poropat kindred; recorded in Krupa in nahija Zrmanja in 1528 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Ibrahim-Pasic-b-Ripac.title: signore di stima e facoltà
people/Ibrahim-Pasic-b-Ripac.content:
Ibrahim Pašić of Ripač
Major Bosnian beg of Ripač (on the Una). Owner of a fortified palace near Boričevac on the Lapac plain, burned in Stojan Janković’s January 1686 raid (doc. 118). Uncle of Muhamed-beg, spahija of Udbina, whom provveditor Antonio Zen describes as “di nascita nobile; è nipote d’Imbrahim Passich da Ripaz, ch’è signore di stima e facoltà” (doc. 134, 18 June 1687) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Ibrahim-aga-b-Udbina.title: disdar of Udbina
people/Ibrahim-aga-b-Udbina.content:
Ibrahim-aga, disdar of Udbina
Disdar (fortress commander) of Udbina, age ~24 (in 1687). Captured spring 1686 by Zaviša Janković’s četa along with Muhamed-beg and Aga Kumalić (doc. 133, 12 April 1686).
Zen’s report (doc. 134): “huomo molto accorto, soldato coraggioso e ardito, temuto, stimato, e da Turchi di sua giurisdittione obedito.” Salary from sultan: 20 aspri/day. Bought by Zaviša Janković and partners for 260 reali at auction Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Ibrahim-pasa-Livno-b.title: Turkish pasha
people/Ibrahim-pasa-Livno-b.content:
Ibrahim-paša (Imbraim passa)
One of two Turkish pashas gathering at Livno October 1684, doc 40 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 40.

people/Idris-aga-b-Bihac.title: Idris-aga-b????-Bihac
people/Idris-aga-b-Bihac.content:
Idris-aga of Bihać
Aga of Bihać, elderly. Captured with his wife and a daughter-in-law during Stojan Janković’s January 1686 raid on the Lapac plain (doc. 118): “in una delle ville depredate s’attrovava ai suoi poderi l’aga da Biachi, chiamato Idris con due figlioli, questi sono foggiti, ma lui per esser vecchio è stato fatto schiavo con la moglie et una nuora, spogliandoli la casa” Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Ilija-Mitrovic-b-Zegar.title: harambaša → bandito (1680) → reconciled, sardar
people/Ilija-Mitrovic-b-Zegar.content:
Ilija Mitrović (the bandit)
Brother of Stojan Janković. Eponymous figure in the Vrana uprising 1683–84 — Provveditore Donà repeatedly calls him “sempre la pietra di scandalo a questo confine et principal autore delle confusioni” (doc. 365).
Timeline

1680-03-30 — Banished with capital sentence by provveditore Valier; ignored the bando (doc. 314 cites this earlier sentenza). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1683-09-13 — Donà reissues the bando: “ricerca, capi, giudici e habitanti delle ville, che capitando in alcuna delle suddette ville, debbano fermarlo vivo o morto” (doc. 314). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1683-10-22 — Joined the Senjski raid on the Vrana–Kosulovo polje area; described as “fratello del kavalier Gianco” (doc. 322). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1683-12-02 — Leads 300 men into Ottoman territory to raid Morlachi sudditi (doc. 343 — gov. Alberti to Donà). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1683-12-07 — With Vukanović and 120 Senjani depredates Žegar Morlachi (their own home village!) — 700 cavalli/manzi, 1 Senjanin and 5 Žegarci killed (docs. 345, 348). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1683-12-07 — Same day raids the Erveničane Morlaks (chained for ~16 lost compagni in earlier Vrana fighting) — 600 manzi + 1000 minuti + 2 dead villagers (doc. 344). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1684-01-02 — Occupies abandoned Obrovac with men of Novigrad / Castel Venier / Starigrad and demands a Venetian stipendio “or we shift to the Habsburgs”; brother Stojan dispatched to defuse (doc. 360, 365). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1684-01-11 — Brother Stojan Janković forces his men out of Obrovac (doc. 364). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1684-04-07 — Donà orders him and his Budin-based companions to restore goods plundered after the murder of Perica Sinobad (doc. 391). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1684-04-18 — Sinobad case escalates: Ilija accused of murdering Perica Sinobad (Jovan’s father) and a brother, of incendij, plunder, and of armed prevention of cultivation (doc. 396). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1684-04-16 (recapitulation) — Donà to Senate: “il principal fomentatore di tali disordini si conosce sempre più essere Elia fratello del kavalier Gianco Mitrovich” — ineffective brother Stojan, asks the Senate’s express command “il rimoverlo in qualche maniera da queste parti crederei alle congionture, che accorrono, molt’ opportuno.” (doc. 394). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Timeline (continued — 1684 to 1693, from Desnica II)

1684-07-15 — Mocenigo’s terminacija grants him 15 ducats/month “in atto di riconoscimento” of father Janko’s deeds and brother Stojan’s continuing service; described as “il più ardito, e il più temerario fra Morlacchi” but profligate with earnings, generous to Morlachs, with strong following — Mocenigo notes the alternatives are to “remove him from the world or keep him content” (doc 20, 21) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685-09-05 — Petitions Senate to raise his stipend from 15 to 40 ducats (doc 96) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1693 (late) — Dies of natural causes (Desnica II attestation) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Note on possible namesake
A figure called “Peraica” / “famoso Peraizza” appears in 1685 (Cetina-region migration leader, killed Aug-Sept 1685 by Turkish corsair fusta off Rogoznica; pension passed to brother Frane Peraica) — see chunk-1 extraction. Some readings identify “Peraica” with Ilija Mitrović; Desnica II doc 96 references Ilija Mitrović as petitioner in Sept 1685; the chronology of that petition is hard to reconcile with a death at sea in the same window. This wiki treats Ilija Mitrović of Žegar and “Peraica” of the Cetina migration as distinct persons until further evidence; flagged as open question.
Companions / drugovi (named in 1684 Sinobad case, doc. 396)

Vuk Ćulić
Petar Smirić
Bože Ostraević
Dragić Matić
Radan Matić
Nikola Vrhes
Sangulin Barićević

Notes

His sister was wife of Mitar Nikolić (Bajo Pivljanin’s brother — Desnica’s footnote on doc. 376) — kinship with the Pivljanini explains why Mitar joined his rebellion.
The 1683–84 Vrana uprising arc in this volume cannot be told without him — he is the prime instigator on the Venetian side.

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 314, 322, 343, 344, 345, 348, 360, 364, 365, 376, 391, 394, 396.

people/Ilija-Nanic-b-Zegar.title: captain (capitan) of [[Islam]] and [[Kasic|Kašić]]
people/Ilija-Nanic-b-Zegar.content:
Ilija Nanić (Žegar)
Captain (“capitan”) of Islam and Kašić from 1698 (doc 309) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. In 1702 named arbitrator for the Brgud villagers in their dispute with Lisičić/Podgrađe (doc 348) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. One of the three ringleaders of the 1704 Bukovica revolt alongside pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža and Mattio Žabetić; banished and fled to Lika (Habsburg side) after suppression (docs 352, 356, 357). Source identifies him as “Illia Nanich da Xegar / da Segar” — explicitly from Zegar.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 309, 348, 352, 356, 357.

people/Ilija-Peraica-b-Cetina.title: sardar (from March 1685) for ~1,600 souls
people/Ilija-Peraica-b-Cetina.content:
Ilija Peraica
“Famoso Peraizza”; previously suspect (had served the Turks). In March 1685 led 600 armed men plus families, 30,000 small animals, and 10,000 cattle from the Cetina region to Venetian-held Trogir territory; awarded 10 ducats/month and made sardar over ~1,600 people, doc 59 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Also referenced docs 60, 61, 66.
Timeline

1685-03 — Defects with ~1,600 souls from Cetina to Trogir territory; awarded 10 ducats/month; made sardar (docs 59, 66) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685-04-07 — Mentioned in connection with Sinj battle aftermath (docs 60, 61) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685 (between Aug and Oct) — Killed by Turkish corsair fusta off Rogoznica while transporting his family to Zadar; 175 of his people captured (docs 104, 112). His pension transferred to brother Frane Peraica (terminacija of Valier 1 Oct 1685) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Disambiguation
Ilija Peraica is distinct from Ilija Mitrović of Žegar — the brother of Stojan and Zaviša Janković — who survived to die of natural causes in 1693 (per chunk-3 attestation). One of the chunk-1 agent extractions conflated the two; this wiki treats them as separate persons until further evidence emerges. The Peraica clan operated out of the Cetina valley; the Mitrovići of Žegar were Bukovica-origin Janković kin. See also Cetina-Migration-Peraica-1685.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 59, 60, 61, 66, 104, 107, 112.

people/Ilija-Radasinovic-b-Vrana.title: knez (conte); proposed captain of Vrana Morlaks 1684
people/Ilija-Radasinovic-b-Vrana.content:
Ilija Radašinović (conte Illia)
Conte (knez) of Vrana Morlaks. Proposed by the Vrana Morlaks themselves as their captain in petitions of September 1684, docs 34, 35, 36 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 34, 35, 36.

people/Ilija-Smiljanic-b-Udbina.title: harambaša → serdar (1653)
people/Ilija-Smiljanic-b-Udbina.content:
Ilija Smiljanić (c. 1622 – 8 September 1654)
Son of Petar Smiljanić. “basso, bruno, segnato da varoli, occhi varii, giovane, mostachi castagni” (doc. 36, terminacija 1648-07-14). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
Timeline

1648-07-14 — 4 ducati/month assigned by Foscolo (doc. 36). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1648-07-17 — Deposes about Ribnik: lost his father, “di questi ne sono periti, compresa la persona di mio padre, nove” out of 100 men (doc. 38). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1648-07-31 — Bukovčani re-elect him as their capo in Foscolo’s presence after Ribnik (doc. 41). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1648-08-01 — At the Battle of Zečevo I, fights alongside Vuk Mandušić (whose corpse he helps bury); Vuk killed (doc. 42). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1653-04-06 — Senate gives him a house in Zadar (the quondam Girolamo Capello house; if redeemed by Capello heirs the State will provide a substitute) — doc. 71. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1653-09-20 — Dolfin’s attestato recapitulates his deeds: twice under Knin “facendo alcuni schiavi de principali”; in Glamoč campaign 6 grosse terre burned; in two attacks on Udbina captured a banner (doc. 75). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1654-09-08 — Killed at Vučjak (a mountain pass between Krupa and Gračac, on the Lika–Dalmacija border). On a 70-strong horse-raid with Janko Mitrović into Lika, attacked the village of Ondić near Udbina, killed 30 and took 15 schiavi. On retreat over Velebit, ambushed at Vučjak — Ilija the first wounded, dragged from the saddle, killed by an archibugiata in the back (docs. 86, 87). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Family

Wife: Kata — Turca di nascita, baptised Christian on her marriage to Ilija. After his death, priva delle facoltà paterne (her wealthy Turkish family disowned her). Provveditore Dolfin granted her 12 ducati + 2 pesi di pane / month (doc. 89). She remarried harambaša Milivoj Zubičević of Šibenik in 1655-11-01 (doc. 97 — full inventory of her dote: 432 ducati 4 lire). On 1665-10-15 she had a son with Zubičević, Lukas, baptised at Sv. Zulijan Šibenik (doc. 144). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 36, 38, 41, 42, 71, 75, 86, 87, 89, 97, 144.

people/Ivan-Antunovic-b1815-Backa.title: naslovni biskup, "ugarski Bunjevac"
people/Ivan-Antunovic-b1815-Backa.content:
Ivan Antunović (1815–1888)
“Ugarski Bunjevac” — naslovni biskup, central figure of the 19th-c. Bunjevac narodni preporod in Backa Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Works

1870 — launches Bunjevačke i šokačke novine in Kaloca (parallel to Boza-Sarcevic-b????-Subotica’s Bunjevački kalendar 1868 in Subotica).
1882 — publishes in Vienna Razprava o podunavskih i potisanskih Bunjevcih i Šokcih u pogledu narodnom, vjerskom, umnom, građanskom i gospodarskom — the foundational text reaffirming bunjevaštvo as a distinct individuality within Strossmayer’s jugoslavenstvo idea. The poticaj for Ivan-Murgic-b????-Perusic’s 1882 article in Vienac came from Antunović.

Antunović’s bačka project ran in the opposite direction from the contemporary Lika trajectory: while Lika Bunjevci absorbed into modern Hrvatstvo, Bačka inteligencija was reaffirming the Bunjevac name as a defense against Hungarian magyarization Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Note on identity
Antunović himself wrote that as late as 1848 he openly used the Rac name in private and public life — “ime Rac ni u privatnu ni u javnu životu nikad nisam zastidio” — documenting the 19th-c. dvojna identifikacija Rac–Bunjevac in Bačka.

people/Ivan-Balenovic-b-Kijani.title: Ivan-Balenovic-b????-Kijani
people/Ivan-Balenovic-b-Kijani.content:
Ivan Balenović sin Mihovilov
Buried in selo Kijani near Gracac in Lika. Cyrillic-inscribed krstača (cross-stećak) from the first half or middle of the 16th c. (Bašagić 1971:72–73) reads:

totu leži Ivan Balenović, sin Mihovilov

Šarić Saric-2008-Bunjevci:

The given name Ivan indicates a Catholic.
The surname Balenović is a Krmpote Bunjevac surname (the Balinovići/Baleni were one of the 1605 Lič-migration families).
The patronymic father Mihovil is plausibly knez Mihovil-knez-b????-Pounje of the 1528–30 Lika–Pounje popis.

Together this is read as a mid-16th-c. Catholic Vlach (proto-Bunjevac) burial in Lika, anchoring the Krmpote re-settlement of the Gračac area c. 1528.

people/Ivan-Bozinovic-b-Klis.title: don, kapelan vlaški
people/Ivan-Bozinovic-b-Klis.content:
don Ivan Božinović (1659)
Catholic kapelan of župa kliške, vranjicke i kamenske (svjetovni svećenik / ilirski kler). In a 1659 ćirilična isprava signs himself “kapelan vlaški” (Klaić 1899:V, 15) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Documents the Dalmatian secular-clergy practice of openly using vlaško (=morlačko) ime for their flock — in stark contrast to the Bosanska franjevačka provincija practice of avoiding it. The mletačka administrative terminologija (Morlachi catholici) was adopted by the dalmatinski klerici and gave the morlačko (vlaško) name a continuity in Dalmatia that it lost elsewhere.

people/Ivan-Brkljaca-b-Radovin.title: Ivan-Brkljaca-b????-Radovin
people/Ivan-Brkljaca-b-Radovin.content:
Ivan Brkljača (Ivanne Berchliazza)
Villager of Radovin. Took multiple gecerme (woolen vests) and silver tokens from Mihajlo Radmilović as he was escaping from Žegar to Venetian territory, doc 31 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 31.

people/Ivan-Filipini-b.title: Ivan-Filipini-b????
people/Ivan-Filipini-b.content:
Ivan Filipini
Led 40 families from Miljacki (Zemunik Gornji) back to Venetian Istria after Ottoman conquest, settling them in Zbandalj near Porec in 1570 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Ivan-Gledjevac-b-Karin.title: Ivan-Gledjevac-b????-Karin
people/Ivan-Gledjevac-b-Karin.content:
Ivan, sin Gleđevca
Resident of selo Dasidžmani in nahija Karin (1528) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Ivan-Karlovic-b-Krbava.title: krbavski knez
people/Ivan-Karlovic-b-Krbava.content:
Ivan Karlović
Krbavski knez. 1514: Ottoman raid took 3,000 of his subjects captive; same autumn several hundred peasant and Vlach families fled his estates in Odorjan, Hotuča, Krbava to Ottoman territory in western Bosnia Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Sometimes paid Ottoman harač. His chaplain Stjepan-Posedarski-b???? addressed Pope Leo X in his name in 1519. Mills on Zrmanja later went to the Husrev-beg vakuf.

people/Ivan-Kracic-b-Split.title: Ivan-Kracic-b????-Split
people/Ivan-Kracic-b-Split.content:
Ivan (Zuanne) Kračić
From the suburb of Split; former Turkish slave. Returned with intelligence to the Venetian command October 1684, doc 40 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 40.

people/Ivan-Lenkovic-b.title: senjski kapetan
people/Ivan-Lenkovic-b.content:
Ivan Lenković
Senjski kapetan in 1560. Venetian Senate sought his intervention through the Habsburg ambassador to release Venetian Morlach subjects captured by Senj uskoks on Velebit summer pastures (June 1560) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Ivan-Murgic-b-Perusic.title: pukovnik (Vojna krajina, umirovljen)
people/Ivan-Murgic-b-Perusic.content:
Ivan Murgić († 1881)
Born in Perusic (Lika). Career officer in the Vojna krajina from 1828 onward; served at posts in Primorje and Lika. Author of Uspomene na gornju Krajinu s osobitim obzirom na Bunjevce, published posthumously in Vienac (Zagreb, 1882, br. 2–8) Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Murgić 1882:2, 29).
Records what Šarić considers the last izvorna svjedočanstva of self-identifying Bunjevci in Lika–Primorje:

“Svi se ovi još i sada sami zovu Bunjevci i kažu: mi smo vridna braća Bunjevci.”
“Ako bi jih tko upitao, koje su vjere… a Bunjevac kazao je… vaviek ‘ja sam pravi Bunjevac’.”

By Murgić’s own framing, the Bunjevci were already “ništa drugo nego Hrvati” — recording the moment of disappearance of the autonomous Bunjevac identity in the Lika–Primorje branch.
Erdeljanović 1930 mistakenly assumed Murgić was himself of Bunjevac origin (he was not).

people/Ivan-Prejic-b-Zacadje.title: Ivan-Prejic-b????-Zacadje
people/Ivan-Prejic-b-Zacadje.content:
Ivan, sin Prejića (Začađe)
Resident of Zacadje in nahija Zrmanja, 1540 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Ivanis-Nenadic-b-Poljica.title: Ivanis-Nenadic-b????-Poljica
people/Ivanis-Nenadic-b-Poljica.content:
Ivaniš Nenadić
Brother of the then-Mostar voivod; in 1506 fled from Poljica to Ottoman territory at Ottoman invitation Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Ivanis-Poropat-b-Mirko.title: timarnik
people/Ivanis-Poropat-b-Mirko.content:
Ivaniš Poropat
Brother of Jakov-Poropat-b????-Zacadje. Held a joint timar (with Ivaniš sin Mirka) in Donje and Gornje Miranje worth 2,000 akči, split equally between them Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Jakob-Foscari-b-Venice.title: dalmatinski providur
people/Jakob-Foscari-b-Venice.content:
Jakob Foscari (Foscarini)
Dalmatinski providur (1572). Reported many Ottoman-side Vlachs willing to defect during Cyprus-War-1570-1573 but kept on Ottoman side by lack of Venetian land Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Jakov-Bistric-b-Radovin.title: Jakov-Bistric-b????-Radovin
people/Jakov-Bistric-b-Radovin.content:
Jakov Bistrić (Giacomo Bistrich)
Villager of Radovin. With Ivan Brkljača took garments from Mihajlo Radmilović during his flight to Venetian territory, doc 31 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 31.

people/Jakov-Poropat-b-Zacadje.title: primićur
people/Jakov-Poropat-b-Zacadje.content:
Jakov Poropat
Primićur and head of the Zrmanja Vlasi Istre dzemat (67 houses, 3063,5 akči) in 1528–1530, residing in Zacadje Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Brother of Ivanis-Poropat-b????-Mirko (timarnik).

people/Jakov-Poropatic-b-Rezane.title: kmet
people/Jakov-Poropatic-b-Rezane.content:
Jakov Poropatić
Recorded as kmet in selo Režane (novigradski distrikt) in 1562 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Likely close kin of the earlier knez Jakov-Poropat-b????-Zacadje.

people/Jakov-Starcevic-b-Pazariste.title: kapetan (Lika regiment)
people/Jakov-Starcevic-b-Pazariste.content:
Jakov Starčević
Son of porkulab Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik. Listed in 1712 popis at age 20 (born c. 1692).
In 1746 appointed kapetan in the newly-formed Lika regiment (alongside his brother Matija-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In 1756 Andrija-Kacic-Miosic-b???? in Razgovor ugodni naroda slovinskoga celebrates a Jakov Starčević among the vitezovi hrvatski (“Ali evo zmaja ognjenoga / po imenu Starčević Jakova!”). Šarić: this is early evidence that Bunjevac kin in Lika were absorbing a Hrvatski (regimental/zemaljski) identity, even when commemorated in epic mode that misplaces them temporally Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Father (or grandfather, depending on reading) of Filip-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste.

people/Janja-Jankovic-b1655-Zadar.title: Janja-Jankovic-b1655-Zadar
people/Janja-Jankovic-b1655-Zadar.content:
Janja Janković (c. 1655 – 9 January 1680)
Sister of Stojan Janković. Married Dmitar Nikolić (brother of Bajo Pivljanin) on 17 January 1675 at Sv. Ilija (Orthodox), Zadar — “sposato Dimitri Nicolich con la donna Anna Giancovichi. Compare illustrissimo signor Battista Sopino.” (doc. 210). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

1677-10-01 (st. v.) — Birth of son Nikola Nikolić baptised at Sv. Ilija (doc. 236). Compare: gov. Battista Sopini. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1680-01-09 — Died, age 25, fell and broke her neck — zabilješka u matici umrlih parohije Sv. Stošije u Zadru, cited in Desnica’s footnote on doc. 211. Birth therefore c. 1655.

Notes

The kinship-link Janković ↔ Pivljanin through her marriage anchors the brothers Bajo and Mitar Nikolić-Pivljanin in Zadar from the end of the Candian War to the Morean War (Desnica, fn. doc. 211).

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 210, 211, 236.

people/Janko-Bunjevcevic-b-Vilic.title: porkulab
people/Janko-Bunjevcevic-b-Vilic.content:
porkulab Janko Bunjevčević (1715)
Porkulab in selo Vilić, Otočka kapetanija, recorded in Spomenici Hrvatske krajine III/1885:307 Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Confessional affiliation difficult to determine from the source.

people/Janko-Jankovic-b-Zadar.title: Janko-Jankovic-b????-Zadar
people/Janko-Jankovic-b-Zadar.content:
Janko Janković (?–1685)
Son of Stojan Janković. Death recorded 23 Aug 1685 in Zadar parish register: “Obito di Gianco figliolo del signor kavalier Stogian Gianco Mitrovich sepolto nella chiesa di S. Elia” (doc. 94, Liber Obitum VI, parish archive of Sv. Stošija, Zadar) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Janko-Mitrovic-b1605-Zegar.title: harambaša → serdar (1656); cavaliere de cavalleria leggera (1652)
people/Janko-Mitrovic-b1605-Zegar.content:
Janko Mitrović (c. 1605/14 – 28 February 1659)
Summary
Founder of the kotarska line that became the Janković-Mitrović of Ravni Kotari. Originally harambaša from Žegar (Bukovica) under Ottoman rule with two armed sons (Ilija and Filip — the latter likely an early death; later texts give Stojan, Zaviša, Ilija) Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I (doc. 20: “Pietro Smiglianich da Vavina … fu il primo ad adoprarsi … Illia antedetto ed altro Filippo” — careful, this attestation is for Smiljanić, not Mitrović; Janko’s earliest dated attestation is doc. 49, 4 Aug 1649, “Gianco Mitrovich da Zegar, statura comune, occhi vari, pel castagno, mostachi biondi, d’ anni 35 in circa” → birth c. 1614).
Stojan’s 1670 supplica (doc. 170) names five brothers who “abbandonando la lor patria natia di Segar paese turchesco, si sono fedelmente portati sotto l’ insegne gloriose della serenità vostra coll’ haver a ciò persuaso altre settanta case, quali formavano un corpo di centocinquanta sperimentati guerrieri”: Janko, Giovanni, Steffano, Paolo, Andrea. The Mitrović uskakanje thus brought ~70 households / ~150 fighting men from Žegar to Venetian Ravni Kotari at the start of the Candian War.
Timeline

c. 1614 — Born in Žegar (per harambaša-pay terminacija doc. 49, “d’ anni 35 in circa” in 1649). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
c. 1646–47 — Crossed (uskočio) with brothers and ~70 households from Ottoman Žegar to Venetian territory; settled at Posedarje. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1648-05-11 — Returns from raid on Unac with brother harambaše; defeated Lika-Udbina Turks at Šuplja Crkva; brought 30 Morlach houses incl. spahija Busović (doc. 28). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1648-05-15 — Foscolo names him poglavica Morlaka iz Bukovice with judicial first-instance authority over their disputes (doc. 29). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1649-08-04 — 4 ducat/month pay assigned by provveditore Foscolo (terminacija doc. 49). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1651-02-01 — peso di pane added to monthly pay (doc. 54, terminacija; original parchment in Arhiv porodice Desnica u Obrovcu). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1651-12-10 — Foscarini orders him enrolled as soldato di cavalleria leggera under generalni providur konjice (doc. 58). Now of Posedarje. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1654-01-10 — Pay raised to 20 ducati/month + peso di biscotto for repulsing Turks at the Posedarje guazzo (doc. 78). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1656-03-25 — Provveditore Zen names him serdar de Morlacchi to replace the murdered Filip Smiljanić (doc. 102) — the first attestation of the Venetian title serdar in this corpus (Desnica’s footnote). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
