1656-08-04 — Co-signs (with harambaša Ilija Milković and all kotarski harambaše) the petition to Bernardo from Bigliane: refuses any colonnello over the Morlachi who is not a Venetian patrician (doc. 105). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1659-02-11 — Severely wounded at the Cetina battle alongside Ilija Milković (doc. 112, lettera Zorzi Papali); a nipote (nephew) of his died in Šibenik the next day (doc. 112). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1659-02-28 — Died in Zadar of those wounds; buried in Sv. Ilija (Greek-rite Orthodox), Zadar — liber obitum (doc. 113). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1659-03-07 — Bernardo to Senate: “il commando che egli si haveva assonto eccedente, ho diviso fra diversi” — i.e., his serdarsko ovlaštenje was split among multiple successors (doc. 116). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Family

Father: q. Dmitar Mitrović (cf. doc. 58 “harambassà Gianco Mitrovich quondam Dimitri da Xegar”).
Brothers (per Stojan’s 1670 supplica): Giovanni, Steffano, Paolo, Andrea — and probably Vukadin Mitrović (d. Novigrad 1653, doc. 74 — same kin-cluster but explicitly distinct in pay-rolls; possibly cousin rather than brother).
Sons: Stojan-Jankovic-b1635-Zegar (b. c. 1635), Zavisa-Jankovic-b????-Zegar (also “Sabba”), Ilija-Mitrovic-b????-Zegar (the later bandit; died in violence).
Widow and posterity received pay-augmentations after his death (doc. 73, 116).

Notes

The shift from Mitrović (the patronymic, used by his contemporaries and on the pay-rolls) to Janković (the patronymic of his son’s son etc., from Janko) happens within his own lifetime in Venetian usage: dispatches and parish entries use “Mitrovich”, “Giancovich”, “Mitrovich detto Giancovich” interchangeably. The single canonical form for filing is Mitrović as the surname stem; Janković is the patronymic-derived hereditary form that fixes among his descendants.
The line is Pravoslavna (Greek-rite Orthodox) — buried at Sv. Ilija u Zadru, the Orthodox parohiska crkva.
Per Desnica’s footnote (doc. 215) Stojan in 1675 had brothers who could be confused with “Janko” — that Janko is patronymic shorthand for one of the actual brothers (Zaviša or Ilija), not a literal sibling named Janko.

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 28, 29, 49, 54, 58, 78, 102, 105, 112, 113, 116, 170, 215, with original terminacije drawn from the family archive in Obrovac.

people/Johann-Joseph-Rabatta-b.title: grof, zapovjednik Karlovačkoga generalata
people/Johann-Joseph-Rabatta-b.content:
Johann Joseph grof von Rabatta (1709–1730)
Habsburg commander of the Karlovački generalat for two decades. His izvješća — analyzed in detail by Lazanin 2002 — divide the population of Hrvatska / Primorska krajina + Lika–Krbava into two etnije by etnokulturni ključ Saric-2008-Bunjevci:

Hrvati = old Habsburg Catholic subjects, Krajina starosjedioci, doseljenici from provincial Hrvatska (Gornje Pokuplje, Vinodol) and Kranjska.
Vlasi = all bearers of patrijarhalno-pastoralna kultura of the Dinaric arc, irrespective of confession; both older and newer prebjega from Ottoman/Venetian areas.

Striking detail: bivši “lički Turci” who were Catholicized in late 17th c. are called “novokrštenim Vlasima” in one Rabatta report. Confessional differences are secondary in his framework.

people/Jovan-Sinobad-b-Budin.title: Jovan-Sinobad-b????-Budin
people/Jovan-Sinobad-b-Budin.content:
Jovan / Ivan Sinobad
Budin Morlak (per existing wiki, Budin is in Korlat region). Distinguished himself at the Grahovo battle August 1684 against Mazut-paša; awarded 2 ducats/month, doc 30 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 30.

people/Jovan-Sinobad-b-Posedarje.title: kavalier sopraintendente; serdar
people/Jovan-Sinobad-b-Posedarje.content:
Jovan (Zuanne) Sinobad
“Kavalier sopraintendente,” chief Venetian Morlach intermediary of the Knin–Zvonigrad area; principal investigator and witness across 1697–1715. Son of quondam Pera Sinobad; killed in clash with Ottomans at Glamoč in 1715 (doc 372) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Timeline (selected)

1701 — Witness in oath at Knin (son of quondam Pietro); pursued Radan Matić in vendetta (doc 331). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1702 — His slave Seifulah confessed in Travnik, ransom recorded; nephew (sister’s son) and Vid Petrović reported as raiders on Mt. Prolog (docs 343, 346). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1715 — Killed at Glamoč in clash with Ottomans; Andrija Butković succeeded him as sopraintendente of Knin/Vrlika (doc 372). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Family

Father: Pera Sinobad (killed by Radan Matić at start of Morean War).
Sons: Andrija Sinobad (later serdar of Knin, d. 1725).
Sister: mother of haiduk nephew on Mt. Prolog (with Vid Petrović) 1702.
Uncle: Gvozden (“zio del cavalier Zuanne Sinobad” — doc 313); not the same as Gvozden Radasović.
Cousin: Giacomo Sinobad (cornetta riformato; later serdar Knin 1729).

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 302, 304, 311, 313, 314, 331, 343, 346, 370, 372.
Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs 279, 391, 396.

people/Jovan-Sudarovic-b-Lika.title: Jovan-Sudarovic-b????-Lika
people/Jovan-Sudarovic-b-Lika.content:
Jovan Sudarović
Morlach harambaša from Parčići in Lika, of fede vecchia (Orthodox). After scoring with the Kotarani in Lika 1685, retreated his 150-house / 300-fighter cohort partly to Karlobag, partly to Obrovac.
Interrogated in Split 23 Nov 1685 (doc. 114) together with his companion Rade Rkać (in original Rado Grego — “Greek” in pejorative for Orthodox). They report that the Habsburg imperial commissar of the Karlović family had tried to fix them at Karlobag with promises of a captaincy and privileges, but they preferred Venetian devotion if granted the kaštel at Žegar (across the Zrmanja from Sebenico, key to closing the Knin–Skradin axis). They had a small cannon taken from the Turks at Udbina that they would bring to Žegar; needed only a 100-man company, food until next harvest, and habitations. Valier rewarded them with 4 cecchini for the journey and sent them back to the cavalry commander and Janković Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Juraj-Firultic-b-Tornik.title: Juraj-Firultic-b????-Tornik
people/Juraj-Firultic-b-Tornik.content:
Juraj, sin Firultića
Resident of Tornik in nahija Podgorje (1528) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Juraj-Jancic-b-Glucje.title: Juraj-Jancic-b????-Glucje
people/Juraj-Jancic-b-Glucje.content:
Juraj, sin Jančića
Resident of Glucje (1528) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Juraj-Matkovic-b-Biograd.title: biogradski kapetan
people/Juraj-Matkovic-b-Biograd.content:
Juraj Matković
Biogradski kapetan (1581) in Venetian service Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Likely descendant of the 60 families resettled from Tinj to Biograd 1572–1575 under providur Alvise Grimani.

people/Juraj-Parcic-b-Nin.title: ninski biskup
people/Juraj-Parcic-b-Nin.content:
ninski biskup Juraj Parčić (1692)
Ninski biskup. His 1692 izvješće documents prevjeravanje in Posedarje, Ražanac, and broader “Morlakija” (Bogović 1993) Saric-2008-Bunjevci — late-17th-c. data point on the confessional-shift dynamics that consolidated the Catholic Bunjevac core of the Venetian frontier.

people/Juraj-Poropatic-b.title: kapetan
people/Juraj-Poropatic-b.content:
Juraj Poropatić
Venetian plaćenik from Zadar area; brought a group of Morlachs to Venetian Istria after the Cyprus-War-1570-1573 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Juraj-Smolcic-b-Pazariste.title: župnik
people/Juraj-Smolcic-b-Pazariste.content:
Juraj Smolčić (1712)
Catholic župnik of Pazariste during the 1712 Lika–Krbava popis Saric-2008-Bunjevci — the parish of porkulab Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik.

people/Jurasin-Vucina-b-Parcic.title: glavar Parčića
people/Jurasin-Vucina-b-Parcic.content:
Jurašin Vučina
“Glavar Parčića” (headman of Parčići) in 1697, party to the Krmpote-area church dispute over Modrino selo near St. Peter’s church (doc 301 footnote) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 301.

people/Jure-Heracic-b.title: katunar (morlački katun Ružić)
people/Jure-Heracic-b.content:
Jure Heračić
Katunar of the morlački katun “Ružić” in 1553 — successor leadership of the Ruzic kindred after their post-1540 return to Šibenik area Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Jure-Matasovic-b-Nin.title: don (ninski arhiprezbiter)
people/Jure-Matasovic-b-Nin.content:
Don Jure Matasović
Ninski arhiprezbiter (1579), originally from Ottoman territory. Charged with pastoral care of Catholic faithful on Ottoman territory south of Velebit Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Karalija-b.title: famoso četobaša
people/Karalija-b.content:
Karalija (četobaša)
A celebrated Ottoman četobaša (“famous Caralia”). Killed by Janković’s returning party from the second Livno raid in early September 1686, together with two other principal companions; their heads taken (doc. 141, attested by Stojan Janković and Smoljan Smiljanić in Zadar, 7 Sept 1686) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Kojadin-Zepina-b-Plavno.title: alfiere (standard-bearer)
people/Kojadin-Zepina-b-Plavno.content:
Kojadin Žepina (Coiadin Zepina)
Morlak alfiere (standard-bearer). Lost an arm under Durak-beg’s tower at Plavno in 1684. Granted 1 ducat/month for one year by Mocenigo, doc 2 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 2.

people/Konstantin-Jankovic-b-Zadar.title: capitano di 50 fanti (1679); designated capitan di cavalleria (7 Nov 1686)
people/Konstantin-Jankovic-b-Zadar.content:
Konstantin Janković
Son of Stojan Janković and Antonia Reci. Already named capitano of a 50-fanti company on 1679-02-09 “in tenera età” (Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I doc. 255).
Timeline (this source)

1686-11-07 — Ducal of Marc’Antonio Giustinian (doc. 148): once Stojan’s regiment is fully assembled, Konstantin is to be commander of an oltramarino cavalry company raised at Stojan’s own expense, “d’esser commandata dal tenente della medesma sin a tanto che si renda habile il figliolo stesso al commando”. Original ducal on parchment in Arhiv B. Desnice Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Krsto-I-Frankapan-b.title: magnate
people/Krsto-I-Frankapan-b.content:
Krsto I. Frankapan
Croatian magnate. Lost his estates in Istria, Kras, and Notranjska in spring 1527 after siding with Ivan Zápolya against Ferdinand Habsburg in the contested royal election Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. The dispossession of his Vlach subjects was a possible trigger for the 1528 return migration of Vlasi-Istre to Ottoman territory.

people/Lazaro-Cona-b-Sibenik.title: Lazaro-Cona-b????-Sibenik
people/Lazaro-Cona-b-Sibenik.content:
Lazaro Cona
Morlach figure dispatched on 12 Nov 1686 by Stojan Janković from Bigliane (Biljane near Posedarje) to commissario Molin (out at Malpaga) and to the other serdari to ask whether he should remain at Biljane or move; intermediary at the start of the November Bosnian-pasha raid (doc. 155) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
One of the capi of the Šibenik–Skradin Morlachs (with Cvitanović, Tintor, Goreta, Palikuća, Žinović).

people/Lazaro-Smiljanic-b-Bukovica.title: capitan
people/Lazaro-Smiljanic-b-Bukovica.content:
Lazaro (Lazzaro) Smiljanić
Son of Smoljan Smiljanić and Marija née Bolić. In tenera età in 1679 when named capitan of his father’s 50-fanti company (Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I doc. 255).
In this source

Heir per his mother Marija’s testament 5 Oct 1693 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 267).
Wrote his own will 28 July 1696, leaving his estate to his wife Maria Bolić (then pregnant) and the unborn child — or, failing them, to Christian slaves and the Dominicans Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 289). Commissario: Sebastian Matiazi.
Commended at the siege of Ulcinj in 1696 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 299).

Family

Father: Smoljan Smiljanić.
Mother: Marija Smiljanić née Bolić.
Sister: Margarita (living 1693).
Wife: Maria Bolić (pregnant in 1696).
Uncle: Marko Smiljanić.

people/Leonardo-Bondumeri-b-Split.title: splitski nadbiskup
people/Leonardo-Bondumeri-b-Split.content:
splitski nadbiskup Leonardo Bondumeri (1663)
Split nadbiskup. His 1663 izvješće documents Orthodox-to-Catholic prevjeravanje in the Klis and Vranjic areas (Bogović 1993) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

people/Liberal-Jankovic-b-Zadar.title: Liberal-Jankovic-b????-Zadar
people/Liberal-Jankovic-b-Zadar.content:
Liberal Janković (?–1686)
Son of Stojan Janković. Death recorded 23 Aug 1686 (doc. 140): “Obito di Liberal figlio del signor kavalier Gianco del rito greco sepolto a s. Elia” (Liber Obitum VI, Zadar) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Lorenzo-Dona-b-Venice.title: Provveditor general (predecessor of Mocenigo, 1684)
people/Lorenzo-Dona-b-Venice.content:
Lorenzo Donà (Donado)
Outgoing Venetian Provveditor general in Dalmatia, May 1684. When Mocenigo arrived to assume the office, Donà was ill and bedridden at scoglio del Lantana (Lantana islet near Zadar), doc 1 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Also referenced doc 36.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 1, 36.

people/Luigi-Marsigli-b.title: count, predsjednik habsburškoga povjerenstva
people/Luigi-Marsigli-b.content:
count Luigi Marsigli (1699)
Italian-Habsburg polymath and military commissioner; led the Habsburg boundary commission negotiating the Karlovački mir 1699 with the Ottoman side.
In commission documents he refers to the Bunjevci of the Senjska-Kapetanija as “Meerkroaten” — Sea-Croats (Kaser 2003:21) Saric-2008-Bunjevci. The label captures the Habsburg administrative perception: a population still called catholic Vlach / Rascianus / Walach / Meerkroat by various official observers, before Martin-Brajkovic-b????-Senj’s 1702 introduction of Bunievczi into ecclesiastical record.

people/Macedonia-officer-b.title: officer
people/Macedonia-officer-b.content:
Macedonia (officer)
Officer killed or missing at the Sinj battle April 1685, doc 60 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes

“Macedonia” may be a nationality / epithet rather than a true surname — recorded as written.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 60.

people/Magdalena-Jankovic-b-Zadar.title: Magdalena-Jankovic-b????-Zadar
people/Magdalena-Jankovic-b-Zadar.content:
Magdalena Janković (d. 13 May 1684)
Daughter of kavalier Stojan Janković (Stojan Mitrović). Buried in Zadar in the Greek rite on 13 May 1684, doc 3 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Source records the burial at the church of Sv. Stošija (parish archive header) and the body laid in the Greek-rite chapel of Sv. Ilija (Zadar).
Mother not named in source.
Notes

Source-page header is “Parohijski arh. crkve Sv. Stošije” (St. Anastasia parish archive); body of the entry says “sepolta nella chiesa di sant’ Elia” — interpreted as Sv. Ilija (Greek-rite) being administratively under Sv. Stošija.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 3.

people/Maggior-Municasa-b.title: maggior of corazze (heavy cavalry)
people/Maggior-Municasa-b.content:
Maggior Municasa
Major of corazze (heavy cavalry) on Marin Michiel’s Knin reconnaissance tour February 1685, doc 51 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Maggior-Tanusi-b.title: maggior; Oltramarini officer
people/Maggior-Tanusi-b.content:
Maggior Tanusi
Major in the Oltramarini. In July 1684 commanded 100 oltramarini sent to support Janković and Bortulačić (doc 17) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Killed at the Sinj battle April 1685, doc 60.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 17, 60.

people/Maljko-b-Karin.title: primićur
people/Maljko-b-Karin.content:
Maljko
Primićur of the Vlasi Istre dzemat in nahija Karin in the 1540 register — 29 houses Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Malkoc-beg-b.title: kliški sandžakbeg
people/Malkoc-beg-b.content:
Malkoč-beg
Kliški sandžakbeg in 1557; recommended Bogdan-Prejic-b???? for a timar upon his return to Ottoman territory and conversion to Islam Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Manojlo-Bunieuach-b-Donje-Moravic.title: Manojlo-Bunieuach-b????-Donje-Moravice
people/Manojlo-Bunieuach-b-Donje-Moravic.content:
Manojlo Bunieuach (1670)
Vlah on the Zrinski estate at Donje Moravice in 1670 (Burić 1979:74) Saric-2008-Bunjevci. The personal name Manojlo + the Bunjevac surname suggests an Orthodox bearer — concrete evidence that the surname Bunjevac (etnik origin) attached primarily in Orthodox-Vlach milieux to former Catholic Bunjevac neighbors.

people/Manojlo-Sladovic-b-Lika.title: povjesničar
people/Manojlo-Sladovic-b-Lika.content:
Manojlo Sladović
19th-c. Croatian historian, author of Pověsti biskupijah Senjske i Modruške ili Krbavske (Trst, 1856) — a key source on the Senjsko-Modruska-Biskupija and Bunjevac integration into the Croatian sphere.
Šarić cites him for vivid description of bunjevački material culture and continued vlach-Dinaric character of compact Lika–Primorje Bunjevac villages into the mid-19th c. Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Sladović 1856:28–29, 49, 435). Probably descends from the Senj branch of the Sladovići who later moved into Licko-Lesce in the Otočac kapetanija.

people/Marchese-Carlotti-b.title: marchese
people/Marchese-Carlotti-b.content:
Marchese Carlotti
Marchese. Last to leave the Sinj battlefield April 1685 together with the unnamed son of Provveditor Valier, doc 60 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 60.

people/Maria-Bolic-Smiljanic-b-Zadar.title: Maria-Bolic-Smiljanic-b????-Zadar
people/Maria-Bolic-Smiljanic-b-Zadar.content:
Marija (Maria) Smiljanić née Bolić
Widow of qu. sardar Smoljan Smiljanić. Wrote her testament at Zadar 5 October 1693; died before 13 April 1694 (the date of apertura of the will); buried at San Domenico, Zadar Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 267).
Will

Heir: son Lazaro Smiljanić.
Daughter Margarita (living 1693).
Son-in-law: governor Salentich (received green velvet jacket).
Nephews Aloisi (silver buttons) and Giovanni / Zuanne (silk sash).
Compare (godparent): quartier mastro Luca Sbizza — executor and legatee.
Recipients: Caterina Pizzocara (twice mentioned, one residing near terra ferma); Vincenza Pastrović and her son Antonio; Ellena daughter of dottor Cassio (diamond ring); padre Scutari (Dominican provinciale); don Gregorio Begna (deceased; debtor to her for 4 zecchini); the late servant Ellena; Angiolina Dominis (mentioned in scritto).
Commissari of the will: Casseretti, dottor Biagio Soppe (consigliere of corte di Zara), Antonio Canaletti.
Notary recording and opening the will: Andreas de Toris, dottor and cancelliere mag. com.
Testimon at apertura: Zorzi Smirich.
Apertura witnessed by curato don Andrea Caldana.

Family

Spouse: Smoljan Smiljanić (predeceased her).
Son: Lazaro Smiljanić.
Daughter: Margarita; a son-in-law surnamed Salentich.
Brother-in-law (her husband’s brother): Marko Smiljanić.

Notes

Distinct from her son Lazaro’s wife, also Maria Bolić (Maria Bolich miga legitima consorte of Lazaro, 1696 testament). The two Marije Bolić across one generation suggest cousin-marriage but are not linked in the source.

people/Marija-Jankovic-b-Zadar.title: Marija-Jankovic-b????-Zadar
people/Marija-Jankovic-b-Zadar.content:
Marija (Marietta) Janković (?–1686)
Daughter of Stojan Janković. Death recorded 2 Feb 1686 (doc. 127): “Obito di Marietta figliola del signor cavalier Gianco Mitrouich del rito greco sepolta a s. Elia” (parish archive of Sv. Stošija, Zadar, Liber Obituum VI) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Marija-Mitrovic-b-Zegar.title: Marija-Mitrovic-b????-Zegar
people/Marija-Mitrovic-b-Zegar.content:
Marija Mitrović
Daughter of Ilija Mitrović (the rebellious brother of Stojan and Zaviša). Married Vučen Stojisavljević of a village under Vrlika; after her husband’s death, raised son Petar in the Mitrović household, hence Petar’s adoption of the Mitrović cognomen (doc 379) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 379.

people/Marijan-Lanosovic-b.title: fra (Kapistranska provincija); slavonski književnik
people/Marijan-Lanosovic-b.content:
fra Marijan Lanosović (1794)
Tajnik Kapistranske franjevačke provincije, slavonski književnik, and member of the carskog povjerenstva for the ilirski pravopis i gramatika. In the Pridgovor bogulyubnim shtiocem of his Evangyelistar Iliricski (Budim, 1794) he records the Buna-river origin legend among podunavski Bunjevci Saric-2008-Bunjevci:

…Bunyevac, tako nazvani od vode Bune u Dalmaciji, otkuda u Maxarsku doseli, svojim slavise, izuschenyem.

Lanosović’s attestation is the Bačka-side parallel to Alberto-Fortis-b????‘s 1778 Velebit-side recording.

people/Marijan-Lisnjic-b.title: makarski biskup, fra
people/Marijan-Lisnjic-b.content:
fra Marijan Lišnjić, makarski biskup (1670–71)
Makarski biskup; visitator of mountains Vitorog and Ljubusa in summer 1670–71 Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Jurišić 1972:58).
His report is among the rare Bosnian-Franciscan opaske about catholic Vlachs — describing pastire “Morlake” and their dušobrižnik Anto-Ripcanin-b???? in not-flattering terms. A characteristic example of Bosanska franjevačka provincija reluctance to use either vlaški or bunjevački for their flock.

people/Marin-Cavalli-b-Venice.title: bailo
people/Marin-Cavalli-b-Venice.content:
Marin Cavalli
Venetian bailo at Constantinople (1560). Recommended Venice “rid itself of Morlachs” in Dalmatia even at cost of leaving land uncultivated, as their Ottoman ties created security risks Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Marin-Michiel-b-Venice.title: Provveditor estraordinario commissario in Dalmazia (1685)
people/Marin-Michiel-b-Venice.content:
Marin Michiel (Marin Mikiel)
Venetian nobleman; Provveditor estraordinario commissario in Dalmatia 1685. Distinct from Marin-Cavalli-b????-Venice (different family, 1560) and from Polo-Michiel-b????-Venice.
Timeline

1685 (Feb) — Conducts a reconnaissance tour of the Knin frontier; with Stojan-Jankovic-b1635-Zegar and Smoljan-Smiljanic-b????-Bukovica in a 600-strong force burned outlying Knin houses while only 8 Turkish horses were watering; 4 Turks captured (doc 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685-04 (7 April) — At the Sinj battle; horse killed under him; saved by an alfier (standard-bearer) of capitanio Segna (Senjski Hungarian-nationality captain) who gave him his own horse (docs 44, 51, 61) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Karambaša Nakić also offered him a horse (doc 61).

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 44, 51, 61.

people/Marin-Michiel-consigliere-b-Venic.title: consigliere (senator)
people/Marin-Michiel-consigliere-b-Venic.content:
Marin Michiel (consigliere)
Venetian consigliere (senator) — distinct from Marin-Michiel-b????-Venice (the Provveditor estraordinario commissario in Dalmatia 1685). Signed Senate decree (doc 22) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Filename disambiguated to avoid collision with the Provveditor commissario of the same name.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 22.

people/Marin-Zane-b-Venice.title: provveditor general di Dalmazia
people/Marin-Zane-b-Venice.content:
Marin Zane
Venetian provveditor general of Dalmatia 1703–1705. Suppressed the 1704 Bukovica revolt led by pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža, Ilija Nanić and Mattio Žabetić (docs 351–357). Later “ritornato di provveditor general” (doc 389) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 351, 352, 353, 354, 355, 356, 357, 359, 389.

people/Marko-Butorac-b-Lika.title: vojvoda
people/Marko-Butorac-b-Lika.content:
vojvoda Marko Butorac (1702)
Local Lika vojvoda at Ribnik; antagonist of porkulab Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik in the conflict that sparked the  Bunjevačka buna of 1702 Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
The surname Butorac (older patronymic form Butorčić) is documented among Krmpote founder families of the 1605 first Lič migration.

people/Marko-Matak-b-Razanci.title: Marko-Matak-b????-Razanci
people/Marko-Matak-b-Razanci.content:
Marko Matak (Marco Mattach)
Villager of Razanci (Rasanze). Took a gecerma (woolen vest) of crimson-violet from Mihajlo Radmilović as he was escaping from Žegar to Venetian territory, doc 31 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 31.

people/Marko-Mesic-b-Lika.title: voditelj katoličkog svećenstva
people/Marko-Mesic-b-Lika.content:
Marko Mesić (1712)
Leader of katoličkog svećenstva in Lika during the 1712 popis. Mediated the Catholic-side input to the popisivanje Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

people/Marko-Perpich-b-Krmpote.title: starešina Vlaha Krmpoćana
people/Marko-Perpich-b-Krmpote.content:
Marko Perpić de Krmpoti (1681)
Starešina (Vlach Krmpotian elder) registered as “Marcus Perpich de Kernpothi Rascianus” in a 13 May 1681 zapisnik of the Dvorska komora inquiry into Zrinski estate obligations Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Dabić 2000:107).
Together with Stephanus-Duich-b????-Krmpote, summoned to testify about the prior obligations of the Krmpotians in Lic, Krmpote-Senj, and Ledenice toward the Zrinski grofovi.
The “Rascianus” attribution in the Habsburg register is, in Šarić’s reading, an administrative classification, not a self-identification — it captures the Habsburg perception of all Catholic Vlach prebjega from Ottoman territory as part of a “racka nacija” overlapping with vlach-Orthodox neighbors. Vojin Dabić 2000 reads the same record as evidence the Krmpotians “smatrali sebe Srbima”; Šarić rejects this as anachronistic flattening of pre-modern administrative attribution.

people/Marko-Saric-b-Zagreb.title: povjesničar
people/Marko-Saric-b-Zagreb.content:
Marko Šarić
Croatian historian (Filozofski fakultet Sveučilišta u Zagrebu, Zavod za hrvatsku povijest, Ivana Lučića 3). Specialist in early-modern Dinaric Vlach studies and the history of the Triplex Confinium.
Author of two ingested sources in this wiki:

Saric-2008-Bunjevci — Bunjevci u ranome novom vijeku: Postanak i razvoj jedne predmoderne etnije (Živjeti na Krivom Putu, 2008).
Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre — Osmanski Vlasi Istre na izvornoj Tromeđi (2024).

Other works cited in those articles:

1999 — Društveni odnosi i previranja u sandžaku Lika-Krka u 16. i početkom 17. stoljaća. In: Diplomska radionica 1 prof. dr. Drage Roksandića. Zagreb, 67–128.
2005 — Dinarski Vlasi između Osmanskog Carstva i Venecije. Povijest pravnih institucija jednog krajiškog društva (15–17. st.). Magistarski rad, FFZG.

The 2005 thesis is the unifying foundation: Šarić 2008 (Bunjevci synthesis) and Šarić 2024 (Vlasi Istre case) are companion case-applications of the framework developed in it.

people/Marko-Smiljanic-b1647-Bukovica.title: capitan
people/Marko-Smiljanic-b1647-Bukovica.content:
Marko Smiljanić (c. 1647 – 23 February 1693)
Capitan; brother of Smoljan Smiljanić. Awarded 10 ducats/month by Doge Francesco Morosini (ducale 21 May 1690) for service in the Morean War — at Calamata, Navarino, Modon, Napoli di Romania, Negroponte, and at Malvasia with his company on 12 Aug 1689 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 226, 233).
Died 23 February 1693, age ~46; buried in San Domenico, Zadar; given last unction by curato don Andrea Caldana of the Zadar duomo (S. Stošija) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 264).
Family

Brother: Smoljan Smiljanić (sardar; deceased by 1693).
Sister-in-law: Marija Smiljanić née Bolić (Smoljan’s widow; testament 1693).

Notes

His extensive Morean War record fixes him on the eastern Mediterranean front during the early 1690s, away from the Bukovica/Kotari theatre.

people/Marko-sin-Lipovica-b.title: knez (timarnik)
people/Marko-sin-Lipovica-b.content:
Marko, sin Lipovića
Knez sharing a timar in Vrbljani near Ostrovica with vojvoda Zakman-Gledjevac-b????-Karin (2,000 akči, split) in 1528–1530 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Martin-Brajkovic-b-Senj.title: senjski biskup
people/Martin-Brajkovic-b-Senj.content:
biskup Martin Brajković (1702)
Senjski biskup who in 1702 introduced the dvojni naziv “catholici Valachi alias Bunievczi” into official ecclesiastical record — the first formal adoption of the Bunjevac ethnonym in Catholic administration Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In subsequent years under his successors (Bedeković, Ratkaj, Pohmajević, Benzoni, Čolić) the vlaški part dropped, leaving only Bunievczi. The 1733 izvješće of Andrija-Josip-Mandal-b????-Lika documents the completed transition.

people/Martin-Jancic-b-Kucista.title: Martin-Jancic-b????-Kucista
people/Martin-Jancic-b-Kucista.content:
Martin, sin Jančića
Resident of Kućišta (nahija Zrmanja) in 1528 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Martin-Prejic-b-Nunic.title: Martin-Prejic-b????-Nunic
people/Martin-Prejic-b-Nunic.content:
Martin, sin Prejića
Resident of Nunic in 1528 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Martin-sin-Vrbaca-b.title: primićur
people/Martin-sin-Vrbaca-b.content:
Martin, sin Vrbača (?)
Primićur recorded in the 1530 sumarni defter as a Vlasi Istre dzemat head (patronymic reading uncertain) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Marton-Bunavac-b-Marok.title: Marton-Bunavac-b????-Marok
people/Marton-Bunavac-b-Marok.content:
Márton Bunavac
Rajetin (peasant taxpayer) recorded in the 1554 Mohač defter for selo Marok as “Márton Bunavácz” and in the 1561 defter for nearby selo Izsep as “Martin Bunivac” (Velics 1890:398) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Significance: earliest possible “Bunjevac”
Possibly the earliest written form of the etnik/surname “Bunjevac” — but Šarić maintains caveats:

Transcription uncertainty. Ottoman Turkish script renders the prezime ambiguously; could be Dunavac (suggested by Kornelija Jurin Starčević).
Etnik logic. If Bunjevac, the name as etnik would imply the carrier moved from a Bunjevac region — therefore Márton himself was not in his Bunjevac homeland but in a Bačka/Baranja exile.

Other 1554/1561 entries from the same registers list raja designated “Hirvat” (Croatian) in selo Sukit and selo Ata — Ottoman regional Croat designation for migrants from the abolished Vilajet-Hrvati (1537). This contemporary toponymic-administrative context strengthens the case that Márton was indeed an early Bunjevac migrant in Podunavlje.
The 1530s+ Ottoman deportations from Vilajet Hrvati to Podunavlje (cited in 1564–65 ferman) provide the migration mechanism. A 1582 Anto-Matkovic-b????-Temisvar school for “Dalmatince” in the Temišvar diocese, and the 1581 mention of knez Vranes-Ivanovic-b????-Kaloca in Kaloča area, document the same demographic substrate.

people/Marusic-officer-b.title: officer
people/Marusic-officer-b.content:
Marušić (officer)
Officer killed or missing at the Sinj battle April 1685, doc 60 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Mate-Krstivojevic-b.title: primićur
people/Mate-Krstivojevic-b.content:
Mate Krstivojević
Primićur recorded in the 1530 sumarni defter as a Vlasi Istre dzemat head Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Mate-Milkovic-b-Krusevo.title: Mate-Milkovic-b????-Krusevo
people/Mate-Milkovic-b-Krusevo.content:
Mate, sin pok. Pere Milkovića
Ottoman-subject Vlach from Kruševo near Obrovac, recorded as a debtor (to a Šibenik butcher) in 1554 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Šarić identifies the Milkovići as a Bunjevac starešina family from Medvidja.

people/Mate-Rojic-b-Podgorje.title: primićur
people/Mate-Rojic-b-Podgorje.content:
Mate Rojić (Matije Rožića)
Primićur and head of the largest Vlasi Istre dzemat in 1528–1530 — 80 houses in nahija Podgorje Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. (Šarić’s text and tables alternate “Mate Rojić” and “Matija Rožić”.)

people/Mate-Sikic-b.title: Mate-Sikic-b????
people/Mate-Sikic-b.content:
Mate Šikić
Co-founder, with Sime-Sikic-b????, of the Šikići hamlet near Pula in 1586 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Mate-Vuksic-b-Tinj.title: starešina (Vojnić)
people/Mate-Vuksic-b-Tinj.content:
Mate Vukšić (1619)
Vojnić starešina who together with Milos-Zupanovic-b????-Tinj negotiated the abortive 1619 plan to bring ~1500 Vojnići onto Habsburg territory (Hrabak 1982–83:391–92) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

people/Matej-Danilovic-b-Polaca.title: don (župnik)
people/Matej-Danilovic-b-Polaca.content:
Don Matej Danilović
Župnik in Polaca (1591). His deposition before the Nin bishop documented widespread konkubinat among glagoljaški priests in Banadego and Lika Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Matheus-Bunievza-b-Glamoc.title: Matheus-Bunievza-b????-Glamoc
people/Matheus-Bunievza-b-Glamoc.content:
Matheus Bunievza (1743)
Catholic, recorded in 1743 biskupskoj vizitaciji of Gornje Glamocko-Polje (Erdeljanović 1930:306) Saric-2008-Bunjevci — late attestation of Bunjevac surname-bearers in the prekoplaninska imigracijska zona (“stariji” zapadnobosanski Bunjevci, Bosanska-Krajina).

people/Matija-Bajcic-b-Vrana.title: harambaša of Vrana
people/Matija-Bajcic-b-Vrana.content:
Matija Bajčić
Harambaša of Vrana; co-signed petition of September 1684, doc 36 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 36.

people/Matija-Boljac-b-Vinjerac.title: Matija-Boljac-b????-Vinjerac
people/Matija-Boljac-b-Vinjerac.content:
Matija Boljač (Mattio Bogliach)
Villager of Castel Venier. Took two dolame (long coats) from Mihajlo Radmilović during his flight to Venetian territory, doc 31 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 31.

people/Matija-Lakic-b-Karin.content:
Matija Lakić (Mattio Lachìch)
Karin Morlak; father of Hajra Lakić (captured by Turks 1684), doc 56 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Matija Pančić

people/Matija-Pop-b-Vrana.content:
Matija Pop
Vrana harambaša; co-signed petition of September 1684, doc 35 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Matija-Starcevic-b-Pazariste.title: kapetan (Lika regiment)
people/Matija-Starcevic-b-Pazariste.content:
Matija Starčević
Son of porkulab Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik; brother of Jakov-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste. Appointed kapetan in the newly-formed Lika regiment in 1746 Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

people/Matija-Strmic-b.title: Matija-Strmic-b????
people/Matija-Strmic-b.content:
Matija Strmić (Mattio Starmich)
Member of the Radoš consortium that owned Ivisa Mandić as slave 1685, doc 65 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 65.

people/Mato-iz-Kresevo-b.title: fra (franjevac)
people/Mato-iz-Kresevo-b.content:
Fra Mato (Matija) iz Kreševa
Bosnian Franciscan (provincija Bosna Srebrena, samostan Visovac). 1550: took over the abandoned Franciscan house in Karin (Bezgrešnoga začeća BDM), pastoring local Catholic Vlachs after the original brotherhood’s flight in 1538 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Catholic colonists led by him recorded in Karin area.

people/Mattio-Zabetic-b-Zaravecchia.title: captain of Zaravecchia
people/Mattio-Zabetic-b-Zaravecchia.content:
Mattio Žabetić
Captain of Zaravecchia (Biograd na Moru) and one of the three ringleaders of the 1704 Bukovica revolt alongside pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža and Ilija Nanić (docs 352, 356, 357) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Banished after suppression. In 1704 located in Venice; observed there by the Franciscan father Pavlo Vušković in Cà Mocenigo (doc 357).
His brother was quartered (“squartato”) in the 1690s for participation in the murder of governator Bortolazzi (doc 357) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. The Žabetić family was thus already deeply implicated in violent opposition to Venetian governance before the 1704 events.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 352, 356, 357.

people/Mazut-pasa-b-Livno.title: Turkish pasha at Livno
people/Mazut-pasa-b-Livno.content:
Mazut-paša (Mazul-paša)
Turkish pasha at Livno. Came to Grahovo to avenge the Glamoč defeat August 1684; defeated; his kjehaja (lieutenant) killed by Tomo Sinovčić, docs 30, 32 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes

Possibly a rendering of Mahmud-paša.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 30, 32.

people/Mede-Miljkovic-b-Krmpote.title: capo di Crampote (head of Krmpote)
people/Mede-Miljkovic-b-Krmpote.content:
Mede(t) Miljković
“Capo di Crampote” (chief/headman of Krmpote) in 1696, in conflict with Parčić villagers over Modrino selo near St. Peter’s church (Bukovica), Zadar 1696 (doc 301) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Italian rendering: Mede Milicovich.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 301.

people/Mehmed-Atlagic-b-Knin.title: pasha (later)
people/Mehmed-Atlagic-b-Knin.content:
Mehmed Atlagić
Member of the Atlagić beg-line of Knin (see Atlagic surname page). Mentioned only obliquely in the chunk-2 documents (the Torre dell’ Atlaghich, an Atlagić tower in the Kotari hinterland, appears in doc. 155 as a meeting point used by Stojan Janković in November 1686). His major personal documentation is in chunk 3 of this source Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Mehmed-Durakbegovic-nephew-b.title: Mehmed-Durakbegovic-nephew-b????
people/Mehmed-Durakbegovic-nephew-b.content:
Mehmed Durakbegović (nephew)
Son of Hasan-beg Durakbegović; nephew of Mehmed-beg Durakbegović (sandžak-beg of Knin). Survived a March 1685 ambush, doc 56 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 56.

people/Mehmed-Terzibasic-b-Drnis.title: drniški aga
people/Mehmed-Terzibasic-b-Drnis.content:
Mehmed Terzibašić, drniški aga (1608)
Local Ottoman aga of Drnis. Led the 1608 Drniš revolt (drniški muslimani + Vlasi) against provincijska upravljačka elita of Sandzak-Klis Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Suppression of the revolt directly triggered the 1608 transfer of 2,000 morlach houses across the Danube (Šibenik knez to Venetian senate) — the largest single demographic event in early Bunjevac history.

people/Mehmed-beg-Durakbegovic-b-Knin.title: sandžak-beg of Knin (until early 1685)
people/Mehmed-beg-Durakbegovic-b-Knin.content:
Mehmed-beg Durakbegović
Sandžak-beg of Knin until early 1685. Had a tower at Plavno (where Kojadin Žepina lost his arm in 1684, doc 2). Replaced and went to Livno March 1685; ambushed; nephew Mehmed survived; favorite Hajra/Kosa Lakić captured, docs 2, 56, 57 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Family

Brother: Hasan-beg Durakbegović (killed earlier at Zemunik) — father of Mehmed-nephew.
Nephew: Mehmed Durakbegović (son of Hasan).

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 2, 56, 57.

people/Mehmed-beg-Klis-b.title: kliški sandžak-beg
people/Mehmed-beg-Klis-b.content:
Mehmed-beg, kliški sandžak-beg
Tatar-origin kliški sandžak-beg of the early 17th c.; son and successor of Mustafa-beg-Klis-b????. Together with his father, the antagonist whose extortion drove the major Bunjevac flight to Backa (Georgiceo 1626) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Distinct from the Hercegovinian sandžak-beg Mehmed-beg-b????-Poljica in the wiki (Saric-2024 ingest).

people/Mehmed-beg-b-Poljica.title: hercegovački sandžakbeg
people/Mehmed-beg-b-Poljica.content:
Mehmed-beg
Hercegovački sandžakbeg, early 16th c., born in Poljica. Invited his kinsmen to join him on Ottoman territory — example of how Ottoman policy used kin networks to woo border populations Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Mihael-Sinobad-b-Posedarje.title: capitan of the paesana company at Zvonigrad
people/Mihael-Sinobad-b-Posedarje.content:
Mihael (Michel) Sinobad
Captain (“capitan”) of the paesana company at the advanced post of Zvonigrad. Died c. 1697; replaced by the boy Andrea Sinobad (doc 304) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Relationship to Pera Sinobad unclear in source — possibly brother.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 304.

people/Mihajlo-Radmilovic-b-Zegar.title: Mihajlo-Radmilovic-b????-Zegar
people/Mihajlo-Radmilovic-b-Zegar.content:
Mihajlo Radmilović (Mihailo Radmilovich)
Morlak who escaped from Žegar to Venetian territory in 1684. His goods were stolen by Venetian subjects on the way; Mocenigo ordered restitution, doc 31 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 31.

people/Mihovil-Jancic-b-Kucista.title: Mihovil-Jancic-b????-Kucista
people/Mihovil-Jancic-b-Kucista.content:
Mihovil, sin Jančića
Resident of Kućišta (nahija Zrmanja) in 1528 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Mihovil-Vojihnic-b-Sinj.title: knez
people/Mihovil-Vojihnic-b-Sinj.content:
Mihovil, sin Radoja Vojihnića
Knez of a Vojnić Catholic Vlach (later “Bunjevac”) dzemat in nahija Sinj in 1550 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Vojnić families later resettled the Tinj vakuf after the Cyprus-War-1570-1573.

people/Mihovil-Zavorovic-b-Sibenik.title: Capitano del contado di Šibenik
people/Mihovil-Zavorovic-b-Sibenik.content:
Mihovil Zavorović (Michiel Zavoreo)
Capitano del contado of Šibenik. Co-led the Cetina expedition with Stojan Janković in March 1685 (docs 42, 51, 54, 59); present at the Sinj battle April 1685 (docs 61) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 42, 51, 54, 59, 61.

people/Mihovil-knez-b-Pounje.title: knez
people/Mihovil-knez-b-Pounje.content:
knez Mihovil (1528–30)
Vlach knez attested in the 1528–30 Ottoman defter for the ličko-pounsko krajište. Settled the depopulated krajište with hajmane (newly-arrived Vlach colonists not yet on the regular tax rolls; paid only resm-i haymane) by Ottoman command (Vasić 1963:244) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Šarić proposes Mihovil is the father of Ivan-Balenovic-b????-Kijani, whose mid-16th-c. krstača-stećak in selo Kijani near Gracac reads “totu leži Ivan Balenović, sin Mihovilov.” This would associate Mihovil with the Krmpote re-settlement of Lika c. 1528 — converging the genealogical, archaeological, and register evidence.

people/Mijo-Radnic-b.title: fra (franjevac, vizitator)
people/Mijo-Radnic-b.content:
Fra Mijo Radnić
Bunjevac, vizitator provincije Bosne Srebrene (1684). Defined the “herceštvo sv. Save” as covering the entire territory from Gacko in eastern Hercegovina to Gračac in Lika Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Šarić Saric-2008-Bunjevci reads Radnić’s “panhercegovizam” (Roksandić 1991:32) two ways: (1) as Roksandić frames it, a stanje svijesti formed by long-term seobe across the entire space, viewed as a unified “morlačka” cjelina; (2) as Šarić argues, also a prostorno legitimiranje of the bosanska provincija at the moment when Ottoman retreat made eklezijalno uređenje questions inevitable — anticipating the bosansko-dalmatinski crkveni zapletaji to come.

people/Mikula-Blazic-b-Zecevo.title: knez
people/Mikula-Blazic-b-Zecevo.content:
Mikula Blažić
Knez and head of the Zecevo Vlasi Istre dzemat (50 houses, 2312 akči) in 1528–1530 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Mikula-Rojnovic-b-Podgorje.title: primićur
people/Mikula-Rojnovic-b-Podgorje.content:
Mikula Rojnović
Primićur and head of a 57-house dzemat in nahija Podgorje in 1528–1530 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Milan-sin-Radka-b-Ostrovica.title: primićur
people/Milan-sin-Radka-b-Ostrovica.content:
Milan, sin Radka
Primićur of the Vlasi Istre dzemat in nahija Ostrovica in the 1540 register — 154 houses Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Milanko-Gledjevac-b-Karin.title: knez
people/Milanko-Gledjevac-b-Karin.content:
Milanko, sin Gleđevca
Knez, resident of selo Dasidžmani in nahija Karin (1528) — one of five Gleđevac houses there alongside vojvoda Zakman-Gledjevac-b????-Karin Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Milic-Jancic-b-Kucista.title: Milic-Jancic-b????-Kucista
people/Milic-Jancic-b-Kucista.content:
Milić, sin Jančića
Resident of Kućišta (nahija Zrmanja) in 1528 — one of four Jančić houses there Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitn.title: porkulab
people/Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitn.content:
porkulab Miloš Starčević (1656 – ?)
Bunjevac settler at Pazariste in 1690 (during the Lika-Bunjevac-Colonization-1690). Founder of the Lika branch of the Starčević lineage Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
1712 popis (Kaser 2003:343)

Held 168 štrikova zemlje in Pazariste, Vaganac, Veliki-Zitnik (“pod kućom” + Vaganac + Žitnik + “Brizah” + sve počasbine).
Age c. 56 (born c. 1656).
Son Jakov then 20.
5 other family members in the household.

1702 — Ribnička buna
Conflict with vojvoda Marko-Butorac-b????-Lika sparked the  Bunjevačka buna. Šarić uses Miloš’s biography (Bunjevac at issuance, Lika porkulab in role) as paradigmatic of how, in komorske vlasti and Catholic Church eyes, settlers like him were catholic Vlach or Bunjevac — clearly distinct from the contemporaneous Hrvati settling Lika Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Family

Sons: Jakov-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste, Matija-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste (1746 Lika regiment kapetani).
Great-grandson: Sime-Starcevic-b1784-Lika.
Great-great-nephew: Ante-Starcevic-b1823-Veliki-Zitnik (founder of HSP).

people/Milos-Zupanovic-b-Tinj.title: starešina (Vojnić)
people/Milos-Zupanovic-b-Tinj.content:
Miloš Županović (1619)
Starešina of the Vlasi Vojnići settled in the Tinj / Županovići area after the post-Cyprus War rekolonizacija under Ferhat-beg Sokolović.
In 1619, jointly with Mate-Vuksic-b????-Tinj, negotiated with the senjski kapetan to bring ~1500 Vojnići onto Habsburg territory; the migration ultimately did not happen (Hrabak 1982–83:391–92) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Eponymous starešina for the village name Županovići that replaced (or co-existed with) Vojnići in the Tinj-area cadastres.

people/Milosav-sin-Sladica-b-Mostar.title: glava džemata
people/Milosav-sin-Sladica-b-Mostar.content:
Milosav sin Sladića (1477)
Head of the Sladović katun in the 1477 Hercegovina defter, nahija Mostar, 19 houses Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Distinctive among Bunjevac founder katuns: organized by villages (Podaca, Igrane, Kozica) rather than by transhumant pastures. Šarić: this suggests either vlahizirano sedentary peasants given Vlach status, or a fully teritorijalizirani vlach katun — a third structural type alongside the Krmpote (transhumance) and Vojnić (mixed) patterns.
Eponymous founder of the Sladovic lineage; the patronymic suffix -ić remains the canonical form, with -ović in later attestations.

people/Milovan-Firultic-b-Tornik.title: Milovan-Firultic-b????-Tornik
people/Milovan-Firultic-b-Tornik.content:
Milovan, sin Firultića
Resident of Tornik in nahija Podgorje (1528) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Modre-b-Modro.title: Modre-b????-Modro
people/Modre-b-Modro.content:
Modre (il Turco Modre)
The original Ottoman owner (“un Turco detto Modre”) of the casale at Modro village near St. Peter’s church in Bukovica, pre-1692. Described as a congiunto (kinsman) of Sinobad (doc 302) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. The toponym Modrino selo likely derives from him.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 302.

people/Muhamed-beg-b-Udbina.title: spahija of Udbina
people/Muhamed-beg-b-Udbina.content:
Muhamed-beg of Udbina
Spahija of Udbina, aged ~26 in 1687. Three brothers; nephew of Ibrahim Pašić of Ripač. Captured by Zaviša Janković’s četa in spring 1686 along with the Udbina disdar Ibrahim-aga and Aga Kumalić while supervising the cultivation of his lands.
Provveditor Zen’s report (doc. 134, 18 June 1687): “di poco spirito, non soldato. Considerato però da Turchi, per esser di nascita nobile.” Bought at auction by Zaviša and partners for 650 reali; expected to be ransomed via his uncle Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Murat-beg-Gajdic-b-Sibenik.title: subaša/voivod, then sanjakbeg
people/Murat-beg-Gajdic-b-Sibenik.content:
Murat-beg Gajdić (Tardić)
Croatian-origin convert; ćehaja of Gazi-Husrev-beg, then subaša/voivod of Vilajet-Hrvati, and from 1537 first sanjakbeg of the new Sandzak-Klis Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Architect of the istimâlet policy bringing Vlasi-Istre back from Habsburg Istria in 1528–1530 and again in 1540. Born in Sibenik area; old surname Tardić (Juran 2016). 1527: led a 2,000-man raid via Lika to Metlika and Novigrad on Kras; 1530: ordered Velebit timber-cutting for Obrovac fleet construction.

people/Mustafa-Jasko-b.title: janissary; Polish convert
people/Mustafa-Jasko-b.content:
Mustafa Jasko (“the Pole”)
Janissary under the Bosnian Pasha; described as a Polish convert (Pollaco). Captured at the Kaštela attack April 1685, doc 62 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 62.

people/Mustafa-Poprzen-aga-b.title: aga
people/Mustafa-Poprzen-aga-b.content:
Mustafa Popržen-aga
Turk captured by Janković’s troops in May 1685 near Knin; held as a state captive, doc 70 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 70.

people/Mustafa-beg-Klis-b.title: kliški sandžak-beg
people/Mustafa-beg-Klis-b.content:
Mustafa-beg, kliški sandžak-beg
Tatar-origin Klis sandžak-beg of the early 17th c. Father of Mehmed-beg-Klis-b???? Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Together they constituted the “tatarska dinastija” against whose extortive provincial rule the Bunjevac Vlachs of Sandzak-Klis rebelled and from which they fled to Backa. Athanasio Georgiceo (1626) noted that the seoba “preko Dunava” was “ponajviše iz straha od Mehmed-bega i njegova oca” (Batinić 1885:116–150).

people/Nenad-Jancic-b-Dobruca-Vas.title: Nenad-Jancic-b????-Dobruca-Vas
people/Nenad-Jancic-b-Dobruca-Vas.content:
Nenad, sin Jančića
Recorded in Dobruca-Vas in 1528, probable kinsman of Petar-Najcinovic-b????-Dobruca-Vas Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Nicola-Bunieuaz-b-Sibenik.title: Nicola-Bunieuaz-b????-Sibenik
people/Nicola-Bunieuaz-b-Sibenik.content:
Nicola Bunieuaz (1680)
Recorded 1680 among Šibenik inhabitants as a doseljeni Morlak (Ostojić 1989–90:275) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

people/Nicolo-Corner-b-Venice.title: senator
people/Nicolo-Corner-b-Venice.content:
Nicolò Corner
Venetian senator. Signed Senate decree of July 1684, doc 22 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 22.

people/Nicolo-del-Borro-b.title: marchese; sergente maggior di battaglia
people/Nicolo-del-Borro-b.content:
Nicolò del Borro (marchese del Borro)
Marchese; sergente maggior di battaglia in 1684 (doc 33). Present at Sinj 1685; sent to Klis after the defeat (docs 60–61) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 33, 60, 61.

people/Nikola-Bunjevac-b-Otres.title: Nikola-Bunjevac-b????-Otres
people/Nikola-Bunjevac-b-Otres.content:
Nikola Bunjevac (1662)
Earliest known written attestation of the surname “Bunjevac” Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Desnica 1950:I/106).
Recorded among Morlaci who fell in a clash with Turks at Otres during the Candian War. He had defected (prebjeg) from Ottoman territory. Note in matičnih knjiga of the novigradska i ražanačka župa for 1662.
The surname Bunjevac as etnik attaches in non-Bunjevac milieux — typically among Orthodox Vlach neighbors, who differentiated incoming Catholic Vlachs by this name.

people/Nikola-Bunjevac-b-Selna.title: Nikola-Bunjevac-b????-Selna
people/Nikola-Bunjevac-b-Selna.content:
Nikola Bunjevac (1698)
Catholic refugee from Bosnia, registered with his family in selo Selna near Garčin (NE of Slavonski Brod) in the 1698 popis (Zirdum 2001:100) Saric-2008-Bunjevci — example of “šokačke” Bosnian katoličke refugee families that adopted the Bunjevac surname through their displacement and integration into otherwise non-Bunjevac milieu.

people/Nikola-Jankovic-b-Zadar.title: designated colonel of oltramarino regiment (7 Nov 1686)
people/Nikola-Jankovic-b-Zadar.content:
Nikola Janković
Eldest surviving son of Stojan Janković, from his first marriage (mother Vinka/Vuka). Already enrolled in cavalry from 1675-08-24 by Senate order (Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I doc. 215).
Timeline (this source)

1686-11-07 — Ducal of Doge Marc’Antonio Giustinian (doc. 148) authorises Stojan Janković’s oltramarino regiment of 500 fanti in 10 companies of 50; Nikola is designated colonnello of the colonel’s company, with 40 ducats/month, “adempite le conditioni infrascritte”. Original ducal on parchment in Arhiv B. Desnice Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Nikola-Jurisic-b.title: kapetan
people/Nikola-Jurisic-b.content:
Nikola Jurišić
Habsburg kapetan; from 1528 held Podgrad and Postojna estates (taken from Krsto-I-Frankapan-b????) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1538: led ~40,000 head of livestock and Ćići families from Zrmanja back to N Istria/Kras under Habsburg protection, calling them “Alt Römer”.

people/Nikola-Klacic-b.title: kapetan
people/Nikola-Klacic-b.content:
Nikola Klačić
Venetian kapetan. April 1572: helped a group of Ottoman-subject Vlachs cross to Venetian territory, settling them in Nin Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Nikola-Milokanic-b1521.title: Nikola-Milokanic-b1521
people/Nikola-Milokanic-b1521.content:
Nikola Milokanić (Osman)
70-year-old former Muslim from Banpolje in Lika; born c. 1521 in Istria, fled to Ottoman territory c. 1550 where he married, and in old age returned to Istria with 184 kin Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Testified before dalmatinski providur Ferigo Nani 16 April 1591.

people/Nikola-Rauber-b.title: tršćanski kapetan
people/Nikola-Rauber-b.content:
Nikola Rauber
Tršćanski kapetan. In 1523 administered Habsburg Rašpor villages (Jelovica, Vodice) after their transfer from Venice Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Nikola-Zrinski-b.title: knez
people/Nikola-Zrinski-b.content:
Nikola Zrinski
Croatian magnate. 25 June 1544: granted hereditary libertini status to 25 Mušković Vlach families settled at Prilisce and Rosopajnik (Vukova Gorica) on his ribničko vlastelinstvo Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Novko-Stojisavljevic-b-Vrlika.title: Novko-Stojisavljevic-b????-Vrlika
people/Novko-Stojisavljevic-b-Vrlika.content:
Novko Stojisavljević
Father of Vučen Stojisavljević; grandfather of Petar Mitrović-Stojisavljević; referenced only as quondam Nouco in 1729 paternity investigation (doc 379) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 379.

people/Ostoja-Gagic-b-Lika.title: Ostoja-Gagic-b????-Lika
people/Ostoja-Gagic-b-Lika.content:
Ostoja Gagić (Osta Gahich)
Lika-born Morlach who uskočio with the 1685 wave; settled at Biljane in the Kotari. In Jan 1686 (doc. 124) detained in Zadar prison on the suit of Rade Tepšić over an unliquidated debt; Stojan Janković stood as personal pieggio (surety) for his release, the bond being signed on Janković’s behalf by Ivan Bortulačić “per non saper lui [Janković] scriver” — a notable confirmation that Stojan was illiterate. Document in Spisi Mikiel, knj. jedina, str. 5 verso Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/P-Santo-Capuzino-b.title: P. (padre) santo Capuzino
people/P-Santo-Capuzino-b.content:
P. santo Capuzino (unnamed Capuchin friar)
Unnamed Capuchin friar at the Sinj battle April 1685, carrying the banner of the Virgin and a brandistocco (boar-spear); presumed enslaved after the defeat, doc 60 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 60.

people/Palikuca-b-Sibenik.title: capo Morlach of Šibenik–Skradin
people/Palikuca-b-Sibenik.content:
Palikuća
One of the three capi of the Šibenik–Skradin Morlachs (with Goreta and Žinović) at the November 1686 Bribir defence. Paired with them in the desertion of the post when the Bosnian pasha approached (doc. 155) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Parisic-b-Vrana.title: harambaša of Vrana
people/Parisic-b-Vrana.content:
Parišić
Harambaša of Vrana; co-signed petition of September 1684, doc 36 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Given name not recorded.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 36.

people/Pavel-Bunyevacz-b-Drava.title: Pavel-Bunyevacz-b????-Drava
people/Pavel-Bunyevacz-b-Drava.content:
Paval Bunyevacz (1697)
Catholic, registered 1697 in a newly-founded village on a Drava-river island in Slavonia (Erdeljanović 1930:294) Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Late-17th-c. evidence of Bunjevac surname-bearers in post-Ottoman Slavonia.

people/Pavel-Jancic-b-Glucje.title: Pavel-Jancic-b????-Glucje
people/Pavel-Jancic-b-Glucje.content:
Pavel, sin Jančića (Glučje)
Resident of Glucje in nahija Karin (1528), brother of Radul; close kinsman of Petar-Najcinovic-b????-Dobruca-Vas Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Pavel-Najcinovic-b.title: kapetan
people/Pavel-Najcinovic-b.content:
Pavel Najčinović
Brother of Petar-Najcinovic-b????-Dobruca-Vas; rewarded along with him by the Venetian Senate for leading the 1538 migration; resettled at Podnovje Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Pavel-Rudelja-b-Obrovac.title: knez (primićur)
people/Pavel-Rudelja-b-Obrovac.content:
Pavel Rudelja
Knez and primićur of the smallest Vlasi Istre dzemat (5 houses, 24 in sumarni) in the varoš of Obrovac in 1528–1530 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Pavko-Firultic-b-Tornik.title: Pavko-Firultic-b????-Tornik
people/Pavko-Firultic-b-Tornik.content:
Pavko, sin Firultića
Resident of Tornik in nahija Podgorje (1528) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Among the four sons of Firultić — likely the ancestral form of the Frletic surname.

people/Pavle-Gledjevac-b-Karin.title: Pavle-Gledjevac-b????-Karin
people/Pavle-Gledjevac-b-Karin.content:
Pavle, sin Gleđevca
Resident of selo Dasidžmani in nahija Karin (1528) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Pavo-Rudelic-b-Smiljan.title: Pavo-Rudelic-b????-Smiljan
people/Pavo-Rudelic-b-Smiljan.content:
Pavo Rudelić
Recorded in Smiljan, Lika in 1686 — descendant of the Rudelic families relocated from Radovin to Karlobag/Šugarje in 1683, with some onward to Lika Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Pejan-Mivcanica-b-Podgorje.title: primićur
people/Pejan-Mivcanica-b-Podgorje.content:
Pejan Mivčanica
Primićur recorded in the 1530 sumarni defter as head of a 16-house dzemat in nahija Podgorje Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Petar-Butkovic-b-Novo.title: župnik
people/Petar-Butkovic-b-Novo.content:
Petar Butković (1712)
Catholic župnik of selo Novo (one of the major Bunjevac parishes) during the 1712 Lika–Krbava popis Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

people/Petar-Hrabren-b-Hercegovina.title: vojvoda
people/Petar-Hrabren-b-Hercegovina.content:
vojvoda Petar Hrabren
Notable vlach voivode of the Donji Vlasi in Hercegovina, ktitor of several Hercegovinian Orthodox monasteries Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
The 1477 defter for nahija Blagaj records his katun’s knežinska aglomeracija — Šarić uses this as evidence that the Vlach population around the Buna river in the 15th c. was predominantly Orthodox, not Bunjevac. This is one strand of the argument against the Buna-river origin legend (which would require a Catholic Vlach population east of the Neretva that the records do not support).
Among the 36 vlach džemats popisanih in nahija Blagaj 1477, none can be confidently identified as Bunjevac (Aličić 1985).

people/Petar-Jagodic-Kuridza-b1666-Bukov.title: pop
people/Petar-Jagodic-Kuridza-b1666-Bukov.content:
Pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža (c. 1666 – 9 April 1749)
Orthodox parish priest at the church of Sv. Petar in Bukovica; principal instigator of the 1704 Bukovica Revolt against Venetian decima reform and Canagetti’s tax extortion. Spent 40+ years in Venetian prisons (Camerotti, then the Pozzi), released 29 March 1746 at age 80 — by then blind and deaf — and died three years later in Zadar.
Timeline

c. 1666 — Born (back-calculation from age 80 at 1746 release). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1704 — Together with Ilija Nanić of Žegar and Mattio Žabetić of Zaravecchia, leads the Bukovica revolt (docs 352, 356, 357). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1704 — Condemned to death in absentia by Marin Zane after the revolt’s suppression; flees to Lika (Habsburg side) (doc 357). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
post-1704 — Eventually arrested in Venetian territory; imprisoned in the Camerotti, later the Pozzi (docs 385, 389). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1734 — Nikola Stojanović named messenger to forward funds to imprisoned Petar Jagodić (doc 385). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1737 — Daughter Magdalena (Manda) Jagodić travels to Zadar to claim her father’s property (doc 387). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1746-03-29 — Released from prison at age 80, blind and deaf; supported in his last years by Greek Pietro/Petar Spiro who was ordered to remove him from the Greek quarter at first opportunity (doc 390). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1749-04-09 — Dies in Zadar, age ~83; recorded in matica umrlih of Orthodox Sv. Ilija church Zadar (doc 392). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Family

Brother: Petar Jagodić (lay) — d. ~1733; left a widow (“cognata”). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Cousin (germano): pop Mihailo (Mijat) Jagodić — paroh of Bilisane. Managed the lay brother’s estate; renounced power-of-attorney 2 January 1738 (doc 388). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Daughter: Magdalena/Manda Jagodić — came to Zadar 1737 to claim her father’s property.

Notes

Surname spellings in the source vary widely: Zagotich, Curelia, Cureggia, Jagodich, Jagodovich, Giadovich, Giagodich, Godovich. Canonical form is Jagodić-Kuridža (Desnica 1951 footnotes).
The 40+ year imprisonment is one of the longest carceral cases documented in the Desnica corpus.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 352, 356, 357, 385, 386, 387, 388, 389, 390, 391, 392.

people/Petar-Milovanic-b-Medvidja.title: knez (catonarius)
people/Petar-Milovanic-b-Medvidja.content:
Petar Milovanić
Attested 1518 in a Zadar deed as Petri Milouanich catonarii districtus Zelengradi — the earliest dated record of the Milovanić Vlach lineage Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Migrated to Habsburg Istria c. 1520, returned by 1528. Knez and head of the Bukovica dzemat in Medvidja (6 houses). Defected to Venice 1538 with his kindred.

people/Petar-Mitrovic-Stojisavljevic-b-V.title: captain of overseas company (1716); serdar of Knin Krajina (1726–1729)
people/Petar-Mitrovic-Stojisavljevic-b-V.content:
Petar Mitrović (born Stojisavljević)
Born to Vučen Stojisavljević and Marija Mitrović in a village under Vrlika. After his father’s death raised in the Mitrović household and assumed the Mitrović cognomen.
Timeline

1716 — Appointed captain of an overseas company by provveditor Anđelo Emo (doc 379). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1726-02-23 — Named serdar of Knin Krajina by Niccolo Erizzo under the cognomen Mitrović (docs 376, 379). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1729 — Investigation under provveditor Pietro Vendramin establishes his actual paternity (Stojisavljević) (doc 379). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1729-12-01 — Removed by ducal of Doge Mocenigo II in favor of Giacomo Sinobad (doc 380). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 376, 379, 380.

people/Petar-Najcinovic-b-Dobruca-Vas.title: knez (later kapetan)
people/Petar-Najcinovic-b-Dobruca-Vas.content:
Petar Najčinović (Jančić)
Knez and head of the Benković Vlasi Istre dzemat in 1528–1530, residing in Dobruca-Vas Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1533: signed Zadar contract for 2,000 kvarti of wheat to be delivered to Karin. Led 1538 migration to Venetian territory; resettled in Podnovje as kapetan. His brother Pavel-Najcinovic-b???? also rewarded by the Senate.

people/Petar-Prejic-b.title: knez (timarnik)
people/Petar-Prejic-b.content:
Petar Prejić
Knez and largest non-Muslim timarnik in the entire Vilajet-Hrvati in 1530, holding a timar worth 3,908 akči (or 4,043 by older iltizam) covering numerous mezras and čiftluks across both sides of Velebit Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Possibly an ex-Bosnian sipahi (Jurin Starčević 2022); not formally listed as a Vlasi Istre dzemat head despite clear connection. Father of Bogdan-Prejic-b????.

people/Petar-Smiljanic-b-Udbina.title: harambaša → poglavica Bukovčana
people/Petar-Smiljanic-b-Udbina.content:
Petar Smiljanić (d. July 1648)
Origin: Udbina, not Smiljan. Desnica’s footnote on doc. 20 (1647-12-28, Foscolo’s attestato): “Nema sumnje da je ‘Vavina’ greška prepisivača mesto Undina t.j. Udbina. Ovim je dakle dokumentarno utvrđeno da su Smiljanići poreklom iz Udbine, a ne kako se priča i veruje, iz Smiljana u Lici.” This is the canonical genealogical correction — overrides any received tradition.
Timeline

1647 — At the start of the Candian War, “si diede al publico servizio con due figli atti al armi, Illia antedetto ed altro Filippo” (doc. 20). Enrolled in capt. Bošičio Renesi’s company. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1647-08-16 (= the Grazac raid): “fu il karambassà capo dell’ esecuzione, conducendo nonanta sette schiavi oltre la quantità de Turchi periti.” Demolished the Nezven bridge over Krka. Distinguished at Ostrovica, Piromatovci, Birbir (doc. 20). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1648-05-11 — Returns from Unac raid (doc. 28).
1648-05-15 — Foscolo creates him capo of the Morlachi from Bukovica (doc. 29) — “colla debita mira di elleggerlo con soddisfazione loro, intese l’ istanze fatteci da tutti gli harambassà.” Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1648-06-21 — Leads 1000+ men in the Udbina raid; with brother (sic — i.e. son) Ilija and pop Sorić (doc. 32). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1648-07-16/17 — Killed at Ribnik along with pop Stjepan Sorić and most other senior harambaše (doc. 37 — Foscolo’s dispatch from 1648-07-14; doc. 38 — son Ilija’s deposition: “ho perso per primo capo il padre, che commandave a 1000 e più fanti.”). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Sons

Ilija-Smiljanic-b????-Udbina (b. ?, “giovane, mostachi castagni” in 1648-07-14 → b. ~1620–25; serdar; killed 1654-09-08 at Vučjak above Krupa).
Filip-Smiljanic-b????-Udbina (b. ?; capitan; killed 1656-01-29 in Šibenik in a brawl with a Venetian soldier).
(probable nephew, not son): Smoljan Smiljanić = serdar Smoglian Smoglianovich, in the next generation; later docs call him nepote of Ilija and Filip.

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 20, 28, 29, 32, 37, 38.

people/Petar-sin-Jancica-b-Ostrovica.title: primićur
people/Petar-sin-Jancica-b-Ostrovica.content:
Petar, sin Jančića (Ostrovica)
Primićur recorded in the 1530 sumarni defter as head of a 30-house Vlasi Istre dzemat (1,365 akči) in nahija Ostrovica Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Likely the same person as Petar-Najcinovic-b????-Dobruca-Vas, whose family name is recorded interchangeably as “Jančić” / “Najčinović”.

people/Pietro-Antonio-Gratarol-b-Venice.title: secretary of the Senate
people/Pietro-Antonio-Gratarol-b-Venice.content:
Pietro Antonio Gratarol
Secretary of the Venetian Senate, doc 23 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 23.

people/Pietro-Calcina-b-Zadar.title: captain
people/Pietro-Calcina-b-Zadar.content:
Pietro Calcina
Captain; son of “il quondam signor kavalier Calcina” (the deceased cancelliere illirico actual, who had let his son substitute for him in office). Claimed to have been invested in the cancelleria illirica position 1675/1680, opposed Nicolò Lomazi in 1701 (doc 327) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Previously served as cavalier in the Levant under Venetian generals; was also a member of a 1698 commission (doc 312).
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 312, 327.

people/Pietro-Sinobad-b-Posedarje.title: Pietro-Sinobad-b????-Posedarje
people/Pietro-Sinobad-b-Posedarje.content:
Pietro (Petar / Perica) Sinobad
Father of Jovan Sinobad. Killed at Brgud at the start of the Morean War by Radan Matić (doc 331) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Of Posedarje origin. The 1684 Sinobad case in Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I (docs 391, 396) attributes his murder more directly to Ilija Mitrović’s band; the 1701 vendetta record (doc 331) names Radan Matić specifically — a long-running blood feud followed.
Same person as Pera/Periza Sinobad, kapetan di Budin in the Sinobad surname page.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 331.
Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs 279, 391, 396.

people/Pietro-Valier-b-Venice.title: Provveditor general estraordinario dell'armi (late 1684 – 1685)
people/Pietro-Valier-b-Venice.content:
Pietro Valier
Venetian noble; Provveditor general estraordinario dell’armi from late 1684. Successor to Mocenigo in the Dalmatian command. Presided over the disastrous April 1685 Sinj campaign.
Timeline

1684 (late) — Assumes provveditor generalship (docs 41–43 onward) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685-02-12 — Rules on the dispute over voting rights in the Sv. Ilija (Greek-rite) confraternity in Zadar, between Greek confrères and the Croatian/Albanian cavalry officers (doc 47) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685-04-07 — Present at Sinj; his unnamed son was last to leave the battlefield together with marchese Carlotti (doc 60) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. His vice ragionato (accountant) was killed at Sinj carrying 300 cecchini (doc 60).
1685-05-26 — Issues proclamation on Greek-rite slave registration: state to ransom unredeemed Orthodox slaves at 200 lire; sale forbidden without permission (doc 69) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 41–72 passim.

people/Polo-Michiel-b-Venice.title: venturiero (1684); Provveditor General della Cavalleria (1685)
people/Polo-Michiel-b-Venice.content:
Polo (Paolo) Michiel
Venetian nobleman, venturiero (volunteer) under Provveditor Mocenigo in 1684; later Provveditor General della Cavalleria in 1685.
Timeline

1684 — Sent by Mocenigo to mediate disputes between Vrana and Zadar Vecchia, and between Obrovac and Novigrad (docs 8, 15) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1684 — Asked to mediate the Sinobad–Vukčević vs. Mitrović feud (krvarina) among Budin Morlaks (doc 15) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685 — Provveditor General della Cavalleria; assumes authority over the 70 Lika families (~900 souls) brought in by Stojan Janković in May 1685 (doc 71) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Notes

Distinct from Marin-Michiel-b????-Venice (Provveditor estraordinario commissario), and from Andrea-Michiel-b????-Venice (Capitano of Zadar).

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 8, 15, 71.

people/Prejic-sin-Matijasa-b-Brdar.title: Prejic-sin-Matijasa-b????-Brdar
people/Prejic-sin-Matijasa-b-Brdar.content:
Prejić, sin Matijaša (Brdar)
Resident of selo Brdar (nahija Zrmanja) in 1540 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Primo-Cadi-Glamoc-b.title: primo cadi (chief Islamic judge)
people/Primo-Cadi-Glamoc-b.content:
“Il primo cadi” of Glamoč (unnamed)
Unnamed kadi (Islamic judge) of Glamoč; killed during the Morlak raid on Glamoč August 1684, doc 27 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 27.

people/Principe-di-Parma-b.title: principe di Parma
people/Principe-di-Parma-b.content:
Prince of Parma
Unnamed prince of Parma; in Zadar consultation October 1684, doc 38 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 38.

people/Rade-Rkac-b-Lika.title: Rade-Rkac-b????-Lika
people/Rade-Rkac-b-Lika.content:
Rade Rkać
Lika-born Morlach, of fede vecchia. Companion of Jovan Sudarović; jointly interrogated in Split 23 Nov 1685 (doc. 114) on the Habsburg-Venetian competition for the Lika uskoci’s settlement at Karlobag vs. Žegar. The original document renders his name as Rado Grego — Desnica’s footnote notes that Grego in this register is a pejorative for pravoslavni, equivalent to rkać. Rkać is therefore the more authentic ethnonym/surname Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Rade-Siljanovic-b.title: starešina
people/Rade-Siljanovic-b.content:
Rade Šiljanović
Istrian Vlach starešina; in 1549 led many peasants to former Vrana district as zakup on Venetian land Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Possible (but unconfirmed by Juran) continuity with medieval kraljevski Vlach katun Šiglanovići of Knin županija.

people/Rade-Tepsic-b-Lika.title: Rade-Tepsic-b????-Lika
people/Rade-Tepsic-b-Lika.content:
Rade Tepšić
Lika-born Morlach, resident at Zadar after the 1685 uskakanje. In Jan 1686 sued Ostoja Gagić of Biljane over a debt; Gagić was imprisoned in Zadar; on 29 Jan 1686 Stojan Janković stood as pieggio for his release on bail (doc. 124, Spisi Mikiel) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
For the Tepšić surname see Tepšić surname page.

people/Radic-Gledjevac-b-Karin.title: Radic-Gledjevac-b????-Karin
people/Radic-Gledjevac-b-Karin.content:
Radič, sin Gleđevca
Resident of selo Dasidžmani in nahija Karin (1528) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Radic-knez-b.title: knez
people/Radic-knez-b.content:
Radič, knez
Knez and head of a major Vlasi Istre dzemat (123 houses, 5,381 akči) in nahija Klicevac in 1528–1530 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Shared a timar in nahija Zrmanja with vojvoda Strahinja-Bratic-b????-Unac (1,135 akči, split equally).

people/Radko-Najerlovic-b-Vrana.title: conte (knez) of Vrana
people/Radko-Najerlovic-b-Vrana.content:
Radko / Radivoj Najerlović
Conte of Vrana; co-signed petitions of September 1684, docs 35, 36 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 35, 36.

people/Rados-Kresovic-b-Bukovica.title: Rados-Kresovic-b????-Bukovica
people/Rados-Kresovic-b-Bukovica.content:
Radoš Krešović
Brother of Sava Krešović. With his brother, took over Sinobad’s casale and lands at Modro near St. Peter’s church in Bukovica and refused to return them, Zadar 1697 (doc 302) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 302.

people/Radul-Jancic-b-Glucje.title: Radul-Jancic-b????-Glucje
people/Radul-Jancic-b-Glucje.content:
Radul, sin Jančića
Brother of Pavel; resident of Glucje (1528) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Roberto-Papafava-b-Venice.title: capitano di Zara
people/Roberto-Papafava-b-Venice.content:
Roberto Papafava
Venetian patrician; capitano di Zara in 1689. Received the report from governator Pietro Calčina (Posedarje pertinenza) about the defeat of the bandit Popržen Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (end of doc 224, doc 225).

people/Sain-aga-Mandic-b-Sinj.title: aga of Sinj
people/Sain-aga-Mandic-b-Sinj.content:
Šain-aga Mandić
Aga of Sinj; head of a prominent Mandić family there. Father of Hasan-aga Mandić (captured at Kaštela, prisoner in Zadar autumn 1685).
Timeline (this source)

Autumn 1685, undated (doc. 108) — Letter from Sinj to provveditor Valier asking that his son be brought to Split so accounts can be reconciled with Rados (the Venetian colonel/governor holding the captives), and pleading on behalf of his slave Mihael Milinović, whom Mattio Strmić allegedly took from him deceitfully despite a written fede. Mandić had taken captain Ivan Marušić (vojvoda) prisoner and treated his case as a parallel exchange Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Autumn 1685 (docs. 109–113) — Series of intercepted letters between Šain-aga, his son Hasan-aga and others, recording his ransom negotiations and reporting Venetian/Ottoman war news.

Notes
The Mandić ransom-correspondence is one of the most personal Ottoman-side documentary sets in the volume; preserved in Spisi P. Valier, knj. I (Zadar State Archive).

people/Sakija-aga-b-Sinj.title: Sakija-aga-b????-Sinj
people/Sakija-aga-b-Sinj.content:
Šakija-aga
Sinj aga, fellow prisoner with Hasan-aga Mandić in the Zadar captain’s prison from autumn 1685.
Timeline (this source)

Autumn 1685, undated (doc. 113) — Writes to “fratello mio caro” Šain-aga Mandić from prison, complaining of the stench, asking news of Sinj, of the effendi and of his sister; warns Šain-aga that the Venetians have spies even in Sarajevo (“ne tengono tante che loro sanno cosa si fa in fino al Saragglio”). Letters carried by the ransom-cycle messenger Janco Jankovich (a different Janković, possibly an intermediary) and conte Jure. Letter written in Italian, in Spisi P. Valier, knj. I, str. 314 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Samil-Jakovic-b-Brgud.title: starešina
people/Samil-Jakovic-b-Brgud.content:
Šamil Jaković
Vlasi Istre dzemat starešina in Brgud who converted to Islam in the interval between the 1528 mufassal and the 1530 sumarni defter — present in the latter, absent from the former Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Sangiaco-Skadar-b.title: Sandžak-beg of Skadar (Shkodër)
people/Sangiaco-Skadar-b.content:
Sandžak-beg of Skadar (unnamed)
Operating against Montenegro and Grbalj 1685, doc 72 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 72.

people/Sanzacco-Vrana-b.title: Sanjak-beg of Vrana
people/Sanzacco-Vrana-b.content:
Sanjak-beg of Vrana (unnamed)
Tried to mobilize the Vrana Morlaks for the Vienna campaign 1683; expelled by them, doc 36 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 36.

people/Sava-Kresovic-b-Bukovica.title: Sava-Kresovic-b????-Bukovica
people/Sava-Kresovic-b-Bukovica.content:
Sava Krešović
Brother of Radoš Krešović; co-occupier of Sinobad’s casale and lands at Modro in Bukovica, 1697 (doc 302) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 302.

people/Silvestro-Valier-b-Venice.title: Doge of Venice
people/Silvestro-Valier-b-Venice.content:
Doge Silvestro Valier
Doge of Venice. Signed multiple dukals in 1697–1698 (docs 303, 306, 310) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II:

1697 ducal addressed to provveditor Mocenigo, raising Zaviša Janković’s pay from 30 to 50 ducats per month.
Ducal of 18 May 1698 granting a soldier’s pay in cavalry to wounded priest Lazar Lazarić.

In this source (chunk 3 — 1696)

Ducale of 30 January 1696 investing Jovan Sinobad as cavalier of San Marco (doc 283) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Ducale of 27 June 1696 investing Zaviša Mitrović as cavalier of San Marco for his deeds at Sinj, Cyclut, and Klivno (doc 288) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 283, 288, 303, 306, 310.

people/Sime-Sikic-b.title: Sime-Sikic-b????
people/Sime-Sikic-b.content:
Šime Šikić
Co-founder, with Mate-Sikic-b????, of the Šikići hamlet near Pula in 1586 — one of the first Bunjevac stream colonists in southern Istria Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Sime-Starcevic-b1784-Lika.title: svećenik, jezikoslovac
people/Sime-Starcevic-b1784-Lika.content:
Šime Starčević (1784–1859)
Catholic priest and grammarian. Son of Filip-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste, great-grandson of porkulab Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Promicatelj “zemaljskog” i “pučkog” horvatstva — a regional/popular Croatian identity, transitional between Bunjevac etnokulturni naslijeđe and the modern etnonacionalni hrvatstvo of his nephew Ante-Starcevic-b1823-Veliki-Zitnik.

people/Simun-Bortulacic-b-Zadar.title: kavalier; capo de Morlacchi (1684); governator
people/Simun-Bortulacic-b-Zadar.content:
Šimun (Simon) Bortulačić
Zadar patrician (Bortolazzi sub-branch q. Girolamo); kavalier; one of the four capi de Morlacchi of the Zadar territory in the early Morean War period. Brother of dr. Antun Bortulačić. Already attested in Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I (kompare at Zaviša Janković’s wedding 1676; capo de Morlacchi at Vrana 1684).
Timeline (this source: 1684–1685)

1684 (April) — One of four capi over the Zadar Morlacchi; sub-region: Krmčina–Toreta–Sv. Filip i Jakov–Biograd (Zaravecchia)–Pakoštane (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1684-08-26 — Writes letter from Grahovo after the Glamoč–Grahovo campaign (docs 1, 5–6, 9, 10) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1684-09 — Vrana Morlaks reject him as capo and petition for Smiljanić instead (docs 34–36) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1684 (Oct) — Co-leads with Alvise Marcello the failed October 1684 Sinj attempt (doc 42) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1684-07-28 — Co-signs petition to Senate against Mocenigo’s appointment of new sub-leaders (doc 22) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685 — Continues among the four Morlak capi (docs 27–29, 32, 42, 58, 61) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685-07-22 — Joint Lika raid with Janković, Posedarski, Smiljanić (docs 86, 87, 89) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685-07 — Wounded (doc 89) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1686-01 — Co-accused with Janković in anonymous Lapac complaint of extortion and unlawful killing (doc 124, 126) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1686-04 — Sent to Spalato to clarify Cornaro’s orders re Lika vs Klivno (doc 93) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1686-11 — Sent to Tinj to gather men against Bosnian pasha incursion (doc 149) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1692-01-16 — Murdered at Vrana by men from Biograd and Pakoštane; aged ~31; covered with stones. Two principal perpetrators captured and condemned 1693–94 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Family

Brother: Antun-Bortulacic-b????-Zadar (dottor; lawyer/draftsman of capi petitions).

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 1, 5, 6, 9–11, 17, 19, 22, 25, 27–29, 32, 34, 36, 42, 58, 61.
Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs 229, 392, 395.

people/Simun-Matkovic-b.title: don, missionary (svjetovni svećenik)
people/Simun-Matkovic-b.content:
don Šimun Matković (1622)
