Catholic missionary (Simeon Joannis Matcovich Bosnensis) — missionarius “in patribus Serbiae, Slavoniae et Hungariae australis, Turcae subiectis” (Fermendžin 1892:367) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In 1622 he addressed a request to the Congregatio Propaganda Fide in Rome asking to be assigned the parochia Bunievczi archidioecesis Colocensis — the first explicit written attestation of the ethnonym “Bunjevac” in any official record Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Notable that the petition came from a svjetovni svećenik rather than from the Bosanski franjevci — the Franciscans avoided the Bunjevac name (deeming it deprecative or “insufficiently Catholic”) through the entire 17th and most of the 18th c.
The “parochia Bunievczi” was probably a wider community designation rather than a single naselje — barski nadbiskup’s 1633 report mentions “parochia di Backa” with 400 zaselaka of “lingua illirica” speakers.

people/Simun-Zdunic-b-Smiljan.title: župnik
people/Simun-Zdunic-b-Smiljan.content:
Šimun Zdunić (1712)
Catholic župnik of Smiljan during the 1712 Lika–Krbava popis Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Likely brother or cousin of Damjan-Zdunic-b????-Lovinac (the pop Zduna of folk tradition).

people/Sinan-beg-b-Mostar.title: mostarski vojvoda
people/Sinan-beg-b-Mostar.content:
Sinan-beg
Mostarski vojvoda in 1477. Co-signatory of istimâlet contract with vlach vojvoda Vladimir-vojvoda-b????-Hercegovina Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Slade-Livoja-b-Zrmanja.title: primićur
people/Slade-Livoja-b-Zrmanja.content:
Slade Livoja
Primićur and head of a 42-house Vlasi Istre dzemat (1921,5 akči) in nahija Zrmanja in 1530 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Slade-Milovanic-b.title: kapetan hrvatskih konjičkih jedinica
people/Slade-Milovanic-b.content:
Slade Milovanić
Captain of Croatian cavalry units on Zadar territory in 1570 — descendant of the Milovanic Vlach lineage that defected to Venice 1538 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Smoljan-Smiljanic-b-Bukovica.title: harambaša → kapitan (1664) → serdar (1664) — pay 30 ducati/mo (1669) — kavalier (1670)
people/Smoljan-Smiljanic-b-Bukovica.content:
Smoljan Smiljanić (Smoglianovich)
Nephew of Ilija and Filip Smiljanić — “ad imitazione degli quondam Elia et Filippo Smilianich suoi zii” (doc. 139). The dukal of 13 July 1669 (doc. 166) names him Smiljanić from a family that “abbandonarono il paese turchesco li progentiori” — this is the same Udbinski uskakanje as his uncles.
He had uterine half-brothers Šimun and Marko Brajinović (sons of his mother Anka by her first husband q. Frane Brajinović, son of q. Toma Brajinović). When Šimun was a slave, Smoljan held the brothers’ inherited goods in trust per provveditore Contarini’s mandate of 22 February 1664 (doc. 184, 1671 inventory of restored goods). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
Timeline

1656-06-15 — Capitan Smiglianich, “come herede e bona tenente delli quondam … Elia e Filippo Smiglianich suoi zii” — sentenced to pay medic Mistakieli for treatments (doc. 103). Listed in the document as “Smoglian Smiglianich o Mihalevich” — alternate paternal patronymic. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1664-10-01 — Provveditore Contarini names him third serdar alongside the two existing serdari Mirković and Kiakić; pay 20 ducati/month, all subordinated to col. Frane Posedarski (doc. 139). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1665-10-15 — Witness/godparent: a son Lukas of harambaša Milivoj Zubičević and donna Catarina (= widow of Ilija Smiljanić!) baptised; comare = Dessa wife of serdar Cuitco Sarich (doc. 144). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1668-12-09 — Co-leader with Janko Mitrović of the Bribir ambush — ring + reward (doc. 163, 165). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1669-07-13 — Dukal of Doge Domenico Contarini: 30 ducati/month + 100-ducat gold chain + dolama (doc. 166). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1670-01-22 — Provveditore Barbaro names him commandant of Nadin (doc. 190). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1671 — Restores the Brajinović inheritance to half-brothers Šimun and Marko (doc. 184 — full inventory of mother’s house in Spianata behind Sv. Marko, including silver-bridled saddlery, brocaded vests, jewellery, kilims, weapons; original document in Arhiv B. Desnice u Obrovcu). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1679-02-09 — His son Lazaro (in tenera età) named capitan of a 50-man company of Croata fanti raised by Smoljan (doc. 255). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1684 — Co-signatory with Stojan Janković, Frane Posedarski, Šimun Bortulačić of the proposal to raise 4 paid cavalry companies of 50 to discipline the Morlachi (doc. 395). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Timeline (continued — 1684 to 1686, from Desnica II)

1684-05-06 onwards — One of four Mocenigo-recognised capi de Morlacchi; sub-region Malpaga, Crno (Karno), Sukošan, Bibinje, Nadin (doc 1, 19). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1684-08 — Glamoč–Grahovo campaign with Janković and Bortulačić; lightly wounded in hand at Grahovo (docs 27, 30, 32). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1684-07-28 — Co-signs petition with the four capi against Mocenigo’s appointment of new capi (doc 22). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1685-07-22 — Lika joint raid (Posedarski, Janković, Bortulačić): Rebac, Ribnik, Medak (docs 86, 87, 89). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1685-09 — Bjelaj/Vakuf raid; brings 500 Orthodox musketeers from Srb to Venetian side (docs 97, 98). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-02 — Ill with podagra (gout) reaching neck, life-threatening; recovered (docs 122, 125, 129). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686 summer — Glamoč engagement, ~200 Turkish cavalry cut down (doc 138). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-07 — First Livno raid: ~5000 infantry + 1500 cavalry under four Kotar serdars; 400+ Turks killed, 1800 houses burned (doc 136). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-09 — Second Livno raid with Janković; Karalija and 2 captains killed on return (docs 141, 142). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1689 (post-mortem) — Widow Marica/Maricca and children Lazaro and Margarita named in family attestations.

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 103, 139, 144, 163, 165, 166, 184, 190, 255, 395.
Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs. 1, 19, 22, 27, 30, 32, 86, 87, 89, 97, 98, 122, 125, 129, 136, 138, 141, 142.

people/Son-of-Valier-b-Venice.title: son of Provveditor Pietro Valier
people/Son-of-Valier-b-Venice.content:
(Unnamed) son of Provveditor Valier
Unnamed son of Provveditor Pietro Valier. Present at the Sinj battle April 1685; last to leave the battlefield together with marchese Carlotti, doc 60 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 60.

people/Stanoje-Prijic-b-Marindol.title: desetnik (uskok)
people/Stanoje-Prijic-b-Marindol.content:
Stanoje Prijić
Recorded as desetnik in Marindol in the 1551 register of uskoci — among Prejić kin who fled to Bela-Krajina in the 1530s Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Stepan-sin-Radovana-b-Zrmanja.title: primićur
people/Stepan-sin-Radovana-b-Zrmanja.content:
Stepan, sin Radovana
Primićur of the new Vlasi Istre dzemat in “Zrmanja Istrija” in the 1550 register — 14 houses, none of whose names recur from 1540 (suggesting wholly new arrivals between 1540 and 1550) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Stephanus-Duich-b-Krmpote.title: starešina Vlaha Krmpoćana
people/Stephanus-Duich-b-Krmpote.content:
Stephanus Duich de Kernpothi (1681)
Starešina, registered as “Stephanus Duich de dicta Kernpothi itidem Rascianus” in the 1681 Dvorska komora zapisnik on Zrinski obligations Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Dabić 2000:107). Co-witness with Marko-Perpich-b????-Krmpote.
(See note on “Rascianus” interpretation in Marko-Perpich-b????-Krmpote.)

people/Stipan-Goreta-b-Sibenik.title: capo of the Šibenik territory Morlachi
people/Stipan-Goreta-b-Sibenik.content:
Stipan Goreta
One of the principal capi of the Šibenik-territory Morlachi, paired with Palikuća and Žinović (doc. 155). On the evening of 15 Nov 1686 came to Stojan Janković at Bribir with the news that the Šibenik-side men were about to flee, and despite Janković’s attempts to rally them, they bolted — forcing the abandonment of Bribir before the Bosnian pasha’s arrival Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Stipan-Soric-b-Gorica.title: don, župnik (1636–1647); harambaša de Morlacchi (1647–48); governator de Morlacchi (1648)
people/Stipan-Soric-b-Gorica.content:
don Stjepan Sorić (?– 17 July 1648)
The same Sorić appears across all three sources covering this period: 1636 župnik of Gorica/Vojnić Catholic Vlachs (Šarić 2008/2024), then 1647 vođa uskakanja of those same Vlachs into Venetian territory, then governator de Morlacchi and finally killed at Ribnik (Desnica 1950).
Pre-1646 (per Šarić)
Don, župnik in Gorica (parish of Tinj) in 1636, tending ~500 “Morlaka latinskog obreda” Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. In the 2008 article (Šarić), župnik of the župa Županovići in 1636 covering 6 villages (Gorica, Raštane, Prkos, Bubnjane, Lišane Tinjske, Brkljačina Polača) with ~1550 “duša” — Vojnić-area Catholic Vlach population Saric-2008-Bunjevci. In 1638 in dispute with Visovac Franciscans over jurisdiction.
1647–1648 (per Desnica)
Foscolo’s attestato of 1647-12-25 (doc. 19) traces his career from the start of the Candian War: previously paroco di Gorizza e ville adiacenti sotto Halil Begh dalla Vrana, Sanzaco di Lica, he opened a confidential channel to Foscolo through a brother who lived in Maidan di Bosna. He gave warning of Ibraim-paša’s army descending on Novigrad (1646), penetrated nightly to a Venetian galley moored at Pašman to deliver intelligence during the Ottoman attack on Zaravecchia. Wounded by Zagaja in the back during the rescue of Vezir’s nephew (which Foscolo’s narrative compresses incoherently). Promoted to governator delli Morlacchi — Foscolo’s terminacija doc. 26 (1648-04-20) recapitulates: razed Zvonigrad mills, helped take Drniš and Klis, captured the standard of paša Tekeli at Klis. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

1647-04 — Doc. 16, Foscolo on the deceptive Goričani uskakanje (Sorić’s own uskakanje with 20 families).
1648-04-18 — Doc. 25 — Pietro Paolo Roviglioni buys from “don Stefano Sorich governator delli Morlacchi” the Turkish slave-girl Rahe of Islam (notarial Skoci sv. 132, Šibenik).
1648-05-07 — Doc. 27 — Sorić personally vouches that the rob Mehmed Jelovac of Babodol was not paid by the State; signs bosanskom ćirilicom: “ja Pop Sorić potvrđujem gore rečeno.”
1648-06-21 — Leads the great raid on Udbina with Petar and Ilija Smiljanić — burns Mazin valley, Rudopolje (3 sela: Tomičić, Vodena Glava, Pancino selo), Klapavica, Mračaj, Bruno (doc. 32). Brings 70 Žegar families with 250 fighters into Venetian protection.
1648-06-20 — Senate sends him a gold chain (doc. 31), Foscolo to deliver it on his return.
1648-07-16/17 — Killed at Ribnik (doc. 37, 40, 41). Foscolo describes (doc. 40): captured wounded after valorosamente combattuto and ferito d’ arcobuggiata in a coscia; questioned by the Turks about his brother (i.e. they wanted to know whether his Bosnian-Maidan brother had betrayed them); when he answered the brother had been killed, the Turkish executioner stabbed him with a lance and finished him off. “È moro certo un bravo e valoroso soldato, ma dalla natione non molto ne obedito ne amato.”
1648-07-31 — His brother Mate Sorić elected by the Goričani as the new capo (doc. 41); the gold chain is later transferred to Mate (doc. 41 footnote: a parastos in Sv. Stošija Zadar with all morlački glavari present, 1648-08-19).

Family

Brother in Maidan di Bosnia — confidant, killed before pop himself (per the Turkish executioner’s question).
Brother Mate Sorić — capitan, succeeded him as Goričanski leader; received the gold chain.
(1683) Gregorio Sorić — implies him as a defunct — sues for relics: Margarita Ivančević is keeping the uščuvana ruka (preserved hand) of pop Stjepan Sorić as a relic; provveditore Donà orders her on 1683-09-02 to deposit the hand and his papers in the chancery (doc. 311). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Sources

Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre — pre-war (1636 župa Gorica).
Saric-2008-Bunjevci — pre-war (1638 dispute with Visovac).
Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — Candian War career, death, posthumous relic-cult — docs. 16, 19, 22, 25, 26, 27, 31, 32, 35, 36, 37, 40, 41, 311.

people/Stjepan-Posedarski-b.title: knez (or chaplain)
people/Stjepan-Posedarski-b.content:
Stjepan Posedarski
In 1519 a chaplain of Ivan-Karlovic-b????-Krbava under this name gave a dramatic anti-Ottoman speech before Pope Leo X in Rome, decrying Ottoman istimâlet tactics and intermarriage Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Šarić also lists a Stjepan Posedarski (knez) among 16th-c. cases of Vlach/noble defection to Islam — possibly the same person, possibly a kinsman.

people/Stojan-Jankovic-b1635-Zegar.title: harambaša → kavalier (1670) → kapo de Morlacchi (1681) → colonnello dell' regimento oltramarino (1686)
people/Stojan-Jankovic-b1635-Zegar.content:
Stojan Janković (c. 1635 – ?1687)
The most decorated kotarski uskok of his generation. Son of Janko-Mitrovic-b1605-Zegar. Born in Žegar (Ottoman zaleđe), came over with his father’s uskakanje in the late 1640s and lived in Posedarje. Captured in slavery by Ottomans 1666–1667 (14 months in Constantinople); released; named kavalier of the Collegio of San Marco 1670; capo de Morlacchi 1681. The dispatches of Foscolo, Foscarini, Dolfin, Cornaro, Priuli, Valier, Donato, and the dukal of Marc’ Antonio Giustinian (1684) document a near-continuous half-century of military service.
Timeline (events documented in this source — 1646 to 1684 only)

c. 1635 — Born in Žegar (estimated; not directly attested. Father’s age in 1649 doc. 49 suggests father was born c. 1614 → son c. 1635 is the conventional date).
1650-02-01 — As “Stojan, figlio di harambassa Gianco Mitrouich, in età tenera esistente,” granted 4 ducati/month (doc. 52). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1652-11-10 — peso di biscotto added to pay (doc. 65). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1653-08-01 — Pay raised to 6 ducati/month “seben in tenera età esistente” (doc. 73). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1666-04-05 — Captured by Turks at the Cetina rotta (battle near Obrovac na Cetini): “harambassa di Possidaria” missing, “il figliolo del Giancovich”; Cornaro’s letter from Split to Senate (doc. 148). 14 months as slave in Constantinople. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1666-05-06 — During his captivity, the Posedarje Morlachi unanimously elect Pavle Vukčević as their vice-harambaša (doc. 152). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1668-12-09 — Free again. Together with serdar Smoljan Smiljanić and governator Giovan Battista Soppe, he ambushed and crushed a 120-strong Turkish raiding party at the Bribir torrent — only 15 Turks escaped, all the rest killed (doc. 163, Priuli to Senate). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1669-01-02 — Senate approves Priuli’s distribution of golden rings to Soppe, Smiljanić and Mitrović (doc. 165). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1669-11-25 — Priuli’s attestato recapitulates his azioni: in person took the head of Reep-aga Filipović in Kotari, 70 heads + 30 schiavi at Cetina, 9 heads + 7 schiavi at Udbina, beheaded aga Velagić at Otres, beheaded aga Pajalitović at Kosovo polje (Kosulovo polje), 30 schiavi + 1 head at Gračac, copious herds at Rudopolje (doc. 168). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1670-01-15 — Stojan’s supplica to the Doge (doc. 170): names his uncles (the five Mitrović brothers) and recapitulates his deeds; requests cavaliere status. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1670-03-13 — Senate makes him kavalier nel collegio di San Marco, golden chain + medaglia + dolama (doc. 171). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1670-08-10 — Provveditore Barbaro grants him the houses of Jusuf-aga Tunić in Islam + 400 gognali of land (doc. 173 — original investitura in Arhiv B. Desnice u Obrovcu). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1674-04-23 — Birth of son Zorzi-Alvise, baptised Sv. Ilija Zadar by sacromonaco Athanasio Troilo. Mother donna Vinca (his first wife). Compare: signor Battista Sopino. (Doc. 207). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1675-01-17 (st. v.) — Sister Janja Janković marries Dimitri Nikolić (Bajo Pivljanin’s brother) at Sv. Ilija (doc. 210). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1675-08-24 — Senate orders Janko (= one of his brothers, perhaps Zaviša or Ilija; the patronymic confused the chancery) and his son Nikola enrolled in cavalry (doc. 215). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1676-08-16 (st. v.) — Wife Vinka/Vuka having died, marries Antonia Reci (Greek of Latin rite of Zadar), at Sv. Ilija (doc. 228). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1677-09-30 (st. v.) — Birth of son Josip Janković (mother Antonia) baptised Sv. Ilija (doc. 235). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1679-02-09 — His son Konstantin named capitano of the company of 50 fanti raised by Stojan (doc. 255). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1681-06-26 — Senate names him capo di tutti i Morlacchi with 25 ducati/month, replacing the deceased Zorzi Posedarski (doc. 275 — original ducal on parchment in Arhiv B. Desnice u Obrovcu). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1683-09-17 — Provveditore Donà interns Stojan and his brother Zaviša to Venice “per degni rispetti” (doc. 315). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1683-12-09 — Returns from Venice; immediately deployed by Donà to suppress the Vrana uprising; intercepts the senjska četa under Vukanović and his brother Ilija at Kruševo (doc. 348). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1684-02-08 — Pay raised to 40 ducati/month (doc. 369, ducal of Doge Marc’Antonio Giustinian). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1684-03-01 — Donà appoints him sopraintendente of the upper-Kotari villages (Ljuba, Ražanac, Radovin, Castel Venier, Posedarje, Budin, Bagnj, Starigrad) — doc. 381. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Timeline (continued — 1684 to 1687, from Desnica II)

1684-05-13 — Daughter Magdalena dies, buried at Sv. Ilija (Zadar) in rito greco (doc 3). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1684-06-02 — Battle near Knin: leads ~2000 Kotari Morlachs with Smiljanić and Bortulačić; ~120 Turks killed, 90 horses taken; lightly wounded in hand (doc 9). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1684-06-02 — Receives 13 brazza of crimson damask from Mocenigo’s fiscal chamber (doc 10). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1684-07-13 — Mocenigo assigns him sopraintendenza of I due Obrovazzi — Stari Grado — Budin e tutte le genti…ultimamente capitate alla divotione de Morlacchi (doc 19). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1684-07-15 — Mocenigo’s terminacija granting brother Ilija 15 ducats/month references “valorose attioni” of father Janko and Stojan’s own continuing service (doc 20). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1684-07-28 — Co-signs petition (with Posedarski, Bortulačić, Smiljanić) protesting Mocenigo’s appointment of four “new” capi (doc 22). Senate ruled in their favor (doc 23). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1684-08 — Glamoč–Grahovo campaign: ~5000 Morlachs raid Glamoč (palaces of alajbeg Filipović burned), then ambush Mazut-paša at Grahovo on return (doc 27, 30, 32). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1684-08-31 — Awarded 10 ducats/month durante bello (doc 29). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1685-01 — Cavalry pay; recruits 50-man Oltremarini company through brother Zaviša (doc 44, 51). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1685-04-07 — Battle of Sinj: Venetian disaster; Stojan one of few Morlach capi who fought through with bravery (doc 60, 61). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1685-05 — Brings 70 families / 900 souls from Lika under Polo Michiel (doc 70). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1685-06 — Settles 316 families / 2,561 souls from Lika at the territory between Kožulovo polje and Ostrovica (doc 73, 90). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1685-07-22 — Lika joint raid: with Posedarski, Smiljanić, Bortulačić; sacks Rebac, Ribnik, Medak, Parčići, Tepsincich, Pavlocich, Komić; ~300 Morlach houses transferred to Venetian side (doc 86, 87, 89, 90). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1685-07-25 — Son Janko dies, buried at Sv. Ilija (Zadar) (doc 94). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1685-09 — Bjelaj/Vakuf raid with Pietro Tartaglia + Geliseo + Razzetini; brings ~500 musketeer-strong Orthodox community from Srb (docs 97, 98). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1685-09 (after) — Sardar Ilija “Peraica” (of the Cetina migration) killed at Rogoznica by Turkish corsair fusta; pension passed to his brother Frane Peraica (doc 104, 112). Older readings identified this Ilija with Stojan’s brother Ilija Mitrović of Žegar; this wiki treats them as separate persons. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-01 — Lapac raid with 1,250 Morlachs; burns Pašić palazzo near Boričevac, captures Idris-aga of Bihać (doc 118). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-01 — Posts bail for Lika settler Ostoja Gagić (doc 124). Confirmed illiterate; Ivan Bortolazzi signs for him. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-02-01 — Anonymous Lapac complaint by new-settler Morlachs accuses him and Bortulačić of extortion, Turkish bribery, killing 15+ men, monopolising Kožulovo polje (doc 126). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-02-02 — Daughter Marietta dies, buried Sv. Ilija (Zadar) in rito greco (doc 127). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-06 — Destroys ~25–29 Krka watermills + tower (doc 135). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-07-30 — Receives the Iljanović letter from Vienna (doc 139), claiming descent from “signori de Illyanova” — flagged by Cornaro and reviewed by State Inquisitors as Ragusan intrigue (docs 147, 154). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-08-23 — Son Liberal dies, buried Sv. Ilija (Zadar) in rito greco (doc 140). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-09 — Second Livno raid (with Smiljanić); famous četobaša Karalija killed on return (doc 141, 142). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-09-23 — Buys redemption-right of house at S. Simeone (Zadar) from Caterina Grizogono (doc 143). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-11-07 — Doge Marc’Antonio Giustinian authorises a 500-man oltramarino regiment under his command, son Nikola as colonnello, son Konstantin to lead a cavalry company (doc 148). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-11-12 to 19 — Bosnian pasha invades Kotari with 16,000 Turks under 5 pashas; Stojan commands Bribir defence (doc 149–157); Bribir abandoned by ~700 men in panic; Vrana and Perušić successfully defended.
1687-01-29 — Wife Antonia dies, buried Sv. Šime (Zadar) (doc 166). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1687-04 — Sinj relief from Atlagić’s siege with Cornaro and Zen (doc 169). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1687-08-23 — Killed at Duvno, struck down by musket and sword while only 8–10 companions followed; the larger Morlach body refused to advance (doc 174). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Family

Father: Janko-Mitrovic-b1605-Zegar (d. 1659).
Brothers: Sabba (m. Maria Lase 1676-08-17, doc. 229); Ilija Mitrović (the bandit).
Sister: Janja (d. 1680-01-09 by fall, broke neck — Desnica’s footnote on doc. 211; Janja was 25, so b. ~1655; m. Dimitri Nikolić-Pivljanin).
Wife 1: Vinka (also documented as Vuka, doc. 211 fn.). Acted as kuma at the baptism of Bojana Novaković 1672-11-28 (doc. 203). Last attested (alive) Feb 1675. Children with V: Zorzi-Alvise (1674), Anastazija (1675), Nikola.
Wife 2: Antonia Reci (m. 1676-08-16, doc. 228). The Reci/Rezzi were Greci of Latin rite resident in Zadar (Desnica’s footnote). She was the daughter of donna Nicolotta and the q. Apostolo Rezzi. Children with A: Josip (1677), Konstantin (named capitan 1679 in tenera età).

Notes

His pay-roll, original terminacije on parchment, and the family genealogical Trassunto survived in Boško Desnica’s family archive in Obrovac — Desnica is Stojan’s lateral descendant.
The legend of “Stojan Janković” in epic poetry collapses Janko (father, d. 1659), Stojan (son, d. 1687), and the brigand Ilija into a single figure. The dispatches separate them clearly; on the kotarska epopeja Desnica preface §I treats this conflation explicitly.

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 52, 65, 73, 148, 152, 163, 165, 168, 170, 171, 173, 203, 207, 210, 211, 215, 228, 235, 250, 255, 275, 315, 348, 369, 381.
Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs. 3, 9, 10, 19, 20, 22, 27, 29, 30, 32, 44, 51, 60, 61, 70, 73, 86, 87, 89, 90, 94, 97, 98, 104, 112, 118, 124, 126, 127, 135, 139, 140, 141, 142, 143, 147, 148, 149–157, 154, 166, 169, 174.

people/Strahinja-Bratic-b-Unac.title: vojvoda
people/Strahinja-Bratic-b-Unac.content:
Strahinja Bratić
Vojvoda of nahija Unac. Held a shared timar in nahija Zrmanja with knez Radič, total revenue 1,135 akči split equally Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Tadija-Vrancic-b-Sibenik.title: kapetan (1648)
people/Tadija-Vrancic-b-Sibenik.content:
Tadija Vrančić
Sister’s son of Vuk Mandušić. 1648-08-03 — Foscolo names him capitan of his uncle’s vacated 50-man company “privo d’ altri più congiunti” (doc. 45) — i.e. Vuk had no closer relatives. By 1652 the family-name is recorded as Mandušić alias Vrančić (doc. 60, 4 ducati + peso di biscotto/month for him and his father Žorži Mandušić-Vrančić). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

people/Tartaglia-officer-b.title: officer
people/Tartaglia-officer-b.content:
Tartaglia (officer)
Officer assigned defense of Duare (Zadvarje) after the Sinj defeat April 1685, doc 60 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 60.

people/Tenente-Canagetti-b.title: tenente collonello (lieutenant-colonel)
people/Tenente-Canagetti-b.content:
Tenente collonello Canagetti
Lieutenant-colonel volunteer with Marin Michiel on the Knin reconnaissance tour February 1685, doc 51 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 51.

people/Theodorus-Bunyevcsevity-b-Stapar.title: pravoslavni svećenik
people/Theodorus-Bunyevcsevity-b-Stapar.content:
Theodorus Bunyevcsevity (1780)
Pravoslavni svećenik in Stapar near Sombor (Bačka), 1780 (Erdeljanović 1930:306) Saric-2008-Bunjevci — example of the Bunjev[a]c surname adopting in Orthodox Vlach milieux, paralleling the Lika Bunjevčević cases at Krš (Kosinj).

people/Tomas-Milovanic-b-Medvidja.title: knez
people/Tomas-Milovanic-b-Medvidja.content:
Tomaš Milovanić
Knez, brother of Petar-Milovanic-b????-Medvidja, resident in Medvidja in the 1528–1530 register Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Tomas-Ruzic-b-Sibenik.title: knez
people/Tomas-Ruzic-b-Sibenik.content:
Tomaš Ružić (Tomaso Rozic)
Born in the Sibenik area; served as a soldier in Klis and Senj (kraljevski Vlasi); fled to Vodice na Krasu 1518 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1524: contacted Gazi-Husrev-beg proposing to lead 100 Vlach families to Ottoman territory; captured by Venetians (Zuane-Minoto-b????-Venice) on Habsburg-Venetian border. Subsequently led his kindred back to nahija Kličevac (Miranje, Jagodnja, 26 houses) by 1528. After 1538/40 returned to Šibenik area.

people/Tomaso-Tubic-b-Zaravecchia.title: captain
people/Tomaso-Tubic-b-Zaravecchia.content:
Tomaso (Toma) Tubić
Captain of Zaravecchia (Biograd na Moru). Originally banished for participation in the Bortolazzi murder (~1690s); later pardoned. By 1704 commanded a galeotta serving the Inquisitori sopra dazi (doc 357) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Friend or kinsman of Mattio Žabetić.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 357.

people/Tomo-Sinovcic-b-Novigrad.title: Tomo-Sinovcic-b????-Novigrad
people/Tomo-Sinovcic-b-Novigrad.content:
Tomo Sinovčić (Tomas Sinovcich)
From Novigrad. Rewarded by Mocenigo on 5 September 1684 for killing 5 Turks at Grahovo, including the kjehaja (lieutenant) of Mazut-paša, doc 32 footnote Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 32 (footnote).

people/Vice-Ragionato-of-Valier-b.title: vice ragionato (deputy accountant) of Provveditor Valier
people/Vice-Ragionato-of-Valier-b.content:
Vice ragionato of Valier
Unnamed deputy accountant of Provveditor Pietro Valier. Killed at the Sinj battle April 1685 carrying 300 cecchini, doc 60 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 60.

people/Vicko-Zirovac-b-Kistanje.title: vojvoda i knez
people/Vicko-Zirovac-b-Kistanje.content:
Vičko Zirovac
Vojvoda and knez of a (likely orthodox) Vlach dzemat on the former Zecevo nahija lands in 1550 — among the new vlach groups replacing the Vlasi Istre Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Vid-Katalinic-b-Starigrad.title: capitano of Starigrad
people/Vid-Katalinic-b-Starigrad.content:
Vid (Francesco) Katalinić
Capitano of Starigrad on the Velebit (Morlacca) coast. Reported on Karlobag developments to Molin in January 1690 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 228). Appointed captain of a new 50-man Starigrad company by Dolfin in November 1696 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 290–291, 294).
Notes

Likely the same “Frane Katalinić” attested as knez of Starigrad in 1678 (succeeding his father Žorži, Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I doc. 253) — the volume-II “Vid” / “Francesco” appears to be the same person; no daughter/son fork in the source.

people/Vid-Petrovic-b-Kosovo.title: Vid-Petrovic-b????-Kosovo
people/Vid-Petrovic-b-Kosovo.content:
Vid Petrović (Kosovo near Sinj)
Haiduk leader on Mt. Prolog. In 1702, with Jovan Sinobad’s nephew and 60 men, attacked Ottoman travellers and a village near the Atlagić tower (doc 346) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Repeatedly described in source as “scellerato Vido Petrouich” — a notorious bandit at the confines.
In 1706 raided Ottomans carrying a public flag (his ensign was captured). Sought to avenge the death of a Kresović famous bandit and to oppress the Rasković family (doc 365) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Killed in ambush by conte Antonio Canagetti at Bruvno in 1707, together with a son of conte Obradović of Bruvno (doc 365).
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 346, 363, 365.

people/Vincenzo-Forza-b.title: vikar zadarskoga nadbiskupa
people/Vincenzo-Forza-b.content:
Vincenzo Forza
Vicar of the Zadar archbishop, 1636. Documented the orthodox Vlach population of c. 3,200 souls in Žegar, Krupa, Mokropolje, Plavno, Pađene, Žagrović, Butišnica, Kistanje, and Miranje, attached pastorally to Visovac monastery but oriented to Krka and Krupa orthodox monasteries Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Called Bukovica “jedna od najvećih planina Morlakije”.
Forza on Bunjevac populations
The same 1636 vizitacija reports for Catholic (“rito Latino”) “Christiani del rito Latino” — the Bunjevac populations Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Jačov 1986:268–271):

župa Županovići — 6 villages (Gorica, Raštane, Prkos, Bubnjane, Lišane Tinjske, Brkljačina Polača); ~1,550 souls; župnik Stipan-Soric-b????-Gorica.
župa Bukovica — managed by franjevac Ivan Visovački (“fra Zuanne da Vissovaz”); ~1,180 souls in Krmpote, Popovići, Ervenik, Parčić, Žužule.
selo Krmpote (=Medvidja) ~400 stanovnika alone.
51 mjesta + 6 župa total — ~13,700 catholic Ottoman subjects in the Zakrčje/Morlakija area.

Names additional villages in the broader Bunjevac vlach milieu: Bubnjane, Lišane Tinjske, Brkljačina Polača, Kamenjane, Podbrđani, Starošane Gornje i Donje, Veliki Prkos, Kašić, Biljane, Korlat, Bukvić, Kršulović, Kolarina, Bulić, Vukšić, Doljane, Međari, Plastovo, Rupe, Ceranje, Veliki and Mali Pristeg, Dobra voda, Stankovci, Banjevci, Popovići, Krmpote, Parčić, Ervenik.

people/Vincenzo-Vendramin-b-Venice.title: provveditor general di Dalmazia
people/Vincenzo-Vendramin-b-Venice.content:
Vincenzo (Vićenco) Vendramin
Venetian provveditor general of Dalmatia 1709–1711. Named Marko Smiljanić (minor son of Lazar) reserved serdar of Lower Kotari (1709), and Vujanović provisional serdar after Lazar Smiljanić’s death; granted Sinobad lands in Kašić Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 367, 368, 369, 370, 389.

people/Visarion-Borilovic-b-Cetinje.title: vladika of Cetinje
people/Visarion-Borilovic-b-Cetinje.content:
Vladika Visarion Borilović
Vladika of Cetinje. Awarded 10 ducats/month by Alessandro Molin in February 1690 for promoting Venetian interests among the Montenegrin clans Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 232).

people/Vittorio-Barbadico-b-Venice.title: zadarski knez
people/Vittorio-Barbadico-b-Venice.content:
Vittorio Barbadico
Zadarski knez. 24 June 1528: reported to the Venetian Senate on the Vlach return migration to Ottoman territory in the Zadar hinterland — the first unambiguous record of Vlasi-Istre presence Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Vladimir-vojvoda-b-Hercegovina.title: vojvoda
people/Vladimir-vojvoda-b-Hercegovina.content:
Vladimir, vojvoda
Vlach vojvoda west of the Neretva who concluded an istimâlet contract in 1477 with Hamza-beg-b???? and Sinan-beg-b????-Mostar, returning Vlachs to Mostar/Hum nahija (Blato, Brotnja, Veljaci, Imotski, Radobilja) — received baštine and mlinove around Mostar, Ljubuški, Imotski Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Together with vojvoda Radoje / Dadoje-vojvoda-b????-Hercegovina in nahija Humska zemlja, head of the knežinska aglomeracija that included the Vojnić katun (Vukasin-sin-Vojihne-b????-Mostar) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

people/Vlatko-Bunislavic-b1406.title: katunska glava
people/Vlatko-Bunislavic-b1406.content:
Vlatko Bunislavić (1406)
Vlach katunska glava in eastern Hum, 1406 Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Hrabak 1981:188). Attested example of the medieval Bun-stem vlach onomastic family. Descendant of a Bunislav, indicating use of Bun-derived personal names in 14th–15th c. Hercegovinian Vlach society — onomastic evidence for the etymology of the etnik Bunjevac.

people/Vojo-Firultic-b-Tornik.title: Vojo-Firultic-b????-Tornik
people/Vojo-Firultic-b-Tornik.content:
Vojo, sin Firultića
Resident of Tornik in nahija Podgorje (1528) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Vranes-Ivanovic-b-Kaloca.title: knez
people/Vranes-Ivanovic-b-Kaloca.content:
knez Vraneš Ivanović (1581)
Vlach knez recorded with his knežina in the area of Kaloca in 1581 (Fermedžin 1892:319) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
One of the earliest concrete attestations of dinarska sociokulturna structure in the Segedinski/Budimski beglerbegluk after the 1530s deportations. The personal name Vraneš is itself characteristic of the Hercegovinian-vlach onomastic stock.

people/Vucen-Stojisavljevic-b-Vrlika.title: Vucen-Stojisavljevic-b????-Vrlika
people/Vucen-Stojisavljevic-b-Vrlika.content:
Vučen Stojisavljević
Son of quondam Novko Stojisavljević; from a village under Vrlika. Married Marija Mitrović (daughter of Ilija Mitrović). Father of Petar, who after Vučen’s death was raised in the Mitrović household and assumed the Mitrović cognomen — discovered in 1729 investigation (doc 379) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 379.

people/Vucic-Oluic-b-Bilisani.title: Morlach nuovo habitante
people/Vucic-Oluic-b-Bilisani.content:
Vučić Oluić
New Morlach settler at Bilišani, above Obrovac. In late January 1686 (doc. 123) he comes to Stojan Janković at Zadar and reports that the Croatian ban (Erdődy) has crossed into Bosnia four days earlier with great destruction, and that 600 Morlach families have been moved by the ban to Croatia. He had been on a četa expedition to Sitna Gora (Siva Gora) on the Lika–Krbava montagne when this news reached them through the smoke of burning villages Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Vuk-Frletic-b-Dracevac.title: uskok
people/Vuk-Frletic-b-Dracevac.content:
Vuk Frletić
Senj uskok of the late 16th c., brother of Andrija-Frletic-b????-Dracevac Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Vuk-Mandusic-b-Sibenik.title: harambaša / kapo de Morlacchi di Šibenik
people/Vuk-Mandusic-b-Sibenik.content:
Vuk Mandušić (d. 1 August 1648)
The “Vuk Mandušić” of the kotarski epic. Senior harambaša of the Šibenik Morlachi. Foscolo’s encomium (doc. 46): “era veramente bravo soldato, discreto e disinteressato capitanio, conditione che non ritrovasi che di rado in queste genti, che per lo più chiamar si possono di rapina; ma quanto li veniva fatto di bottinare, tutto compartiva a soldati, che però lo amavano, lo stimavano l’ obedivano altrettanto, quanto era temuto da Turchi.”
Timeline

1648-06-02 — Returns from raid on Ključ (300 houses, near Banja Luka): killed >200 Turks, took 46 schiavi; on retreat ambushed at Glamoč, beat off the cavalry (doc. 30). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1648-07-11 — Foscolo proposes to give him the gold chain originally destined for pop Sorić — “essendo sopra tutti stimato in paese” (doc. 35). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1648-08-01 — Killed at Zečevo combatting an Ottoman raid that had pillaged Zaravecchia. The Battle of Zečevo (doc. 42, Ilija Smiljanić’s deposition; doc. 43, Matija Mihaljević of Drniš’s deposition): Vuk taken alive after killing four Turks himself, kept alive a few hours, beheaded; Ilija Smiljanić helped bury his torso. The 22-document forensic inquest (docs. 42–46) is the most detailed military narrative in the volume. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Family

Sister’s son Tadija Vrančić = his nearest male kin (no closer relations). Provveditore Foscolo named Tadija capitan of his 50-man company on 1648-08-03 (doc. 45). The family’s later style is Mandušić alias Vrančić (cf. doc. 60, 1652).
Father of harambaša Žorži Mandušić-Vrančić = Tadija’s father (doc. 60).

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 30, 35, 40, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 60.

people/Vuk-Popovic-b.title: vojvoda (uskok)
people/Vuk-Popovic-b.content:
Vuk Popović, vojvoda
Uskok vojvoda. Led migrations of Vlasi-Uskoplja from the Knin/Plavno area through Bihac toward Zumberak and Bela krajina in the 1530s Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Šarić proposes that “Vuk vojvoda Vlaha Uskoplja” of the 1528 Ottoman defter and the Habsburg-side “vojvoda Vuk Popović” are the same person.

people/Vukadin-Mitrovic-b-Zegar.title: harambaša
people/Vukadin-Mitrovic-b-Zegar.content:
Vukadin Mitrović (d. 1653)
Žegarski harambaša; “basso, occhi varii, pel nero, barba castagna, d’ anni 40 in circa” (doc. 51, 1650-01-08 — i.e. b. c. 1610) Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

1650-01-08 — 4 ducati/month pay; from Žegar (doc. 51).
1652-11-10 — peso di biscotto added (doc. 65).
1653 — Died defending the post of Novigrad against Ottoman attack: “toccò gloriosamente lasciar la vita” (doc. 74, 1653-08-01). Pay transferred to son Jakov Mitrović, who had earlier been enslaved (doc. 74, 274).

Likely brother or cousin of Janko (the kin-cluster is one uskakanje from Žegar).
Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 51, 65, 74, 274.

people/Vukasin-Rosic-b-Citluk-Licki.title: harambaša
people/Vukasin-Rosic-b-Citluk-Licki.content:
Vukašin Rošić
Harambaša. In February 1685 led 20 Morlak families from Čitluk near Novi (Lika) to the Starigrad (Velebit) area on the Venetian side; petitioned for the Perušić castle as residence, doc 45 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 45.

people/Vukasin-sin-Vojihne-b-Mostar.title: glava džemata
people/Vukasin-sin-Vojihne-b-Mostar.content:
Vukašin sin Vojihne (1477)
Head of the Vojnić katun in the 1477 Hercegovina defter, nahija Mostar. 10 houses + 3 unmarried (Aličić 1985:84) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Wintered/summered jointly with vojvoda Vladimir-vojvoda-b????-Hercegovina’s katun across W. Hercegovinian planinas and župas. Eponymous founder figure for Vojnic (Vojnići), and for selo Vojnici-Ljubuski in W. Hercegovina (~35 km west of Buna).
Earlier attestation of the lineage: 1408 — Bosnian king Stjepan Ostoja’s charter mentions Vlasi Vojihnići, subjects of the Radivojević-Vlatković Hum nobility.

people/Vukic-Krmpotic-b-Hercegovina.title: glava džemata
people/Vukic-Krmpotic-b-Hercegovina.content:
Vukić Krmpotić (1477)
Head (džematska glava) of the Krmpote katun in the 1477 Hercegovina defter, nahija Humska zemlja. Defter records 11 houses (poreznih jedinica). Aličić 1985:130–131 Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Defter notation: “od ranije su to bile njihove baštine pa su ponovo došli pod tim uvjetom” — the katun had returned from refuge under istimâlet protection (paralleling vojvoda Vladimir-vojvoda-b????-Hercegovina in the same defter).
Pasture range:

Winter (zimišta): Buhovo, Borajna, Ledinac, Veseli-Vstak (W. Hercegovina, ~22 km from Buna).
Summer (ljetišta): Cvrsnica, Vran, Ljubusa.

Founder figure of the Krmpotić lineage that dominates Bunjevac migration history. The katun name persists across the entire Tromeđa: Medvidja (Krmpote), Krmpote-Senj, etc.

people/Vuko-Vojkorsic-b-Citluk-Licki.title: harambaša
people/Vuko-Vojkorsic-b-Citluk-Licki.content:
Vuko Vojkorsić (Vuco Voicorsich)
Harambaša of Čitluk Morlaks. Came over to Venetian devotion with his family circa March 1685; awarded 2 zecchini, doc 54 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 54.

people/Vukon-Cvitanovic-b-Sibenik.title: Vukon-Cvitanovic-b????-Sibenik
people/Vukon-Cvitanovic-b-Sibenik.content:
Vukon Cvitanović (Vuconie Zuitanovich)
Morlach harambaša dispatched (with Nakić) on 12 Nov 1686 by Stojan Janković from Bribir to traverse the whole Zadar contado, alerting villages to the imminent Bosnian-pasha raid: each household to send one armed man to Bribir, the families and animals to be moved to safety (doc. 155) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Vukosav-Kosic-b-Starigrad.title: Vukosav-Kosic-b????-Starigrad
people/Vukosav-Kosic-b-Starigrad.content:
Vukosav Kosić
Lika-born Morlach who uskočio in 1684 and settled at Starigrad under Velebit. Carried Valier’s and Janković’s letters to Habsburg general Herberstein (camp at Jasenica) in summer 1685; on his return interrogated 8 Aug 1685 in Zadar, gave detailed information on the imperial army’s strength and on conditions in Ottoman Lika — biades and orzi abundant but not yet harvested, fortifications wood-trinciere takeable without cannon, no more than 1,000 fighting men in the cities, all “impauriti et avvilliti” (doc. 92, attached to Valier’s dispatch of 13 Aug 1685) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Vukoslav-Carapotic-b-Krusevo.title: Vukoslav-Carapotic-b????-Krusevo
people/Vukoslav-Carapotic-b-Krusevo.content:
Vukoslav Carapotić (Krmpotić?)
Ottoman-subject Vlach from Kruševo (likely Krusevo kod Obrovca), recorded as a debtor in Sibenik in 1554 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Likely a Krmpotic (Catholic Bunjevac) family member.

people/Vukota-Buncic-b1419.title: katunska glava
people/Vukota-Buncic-b1419.content:
Vukota Bunčić (1419)
Vlach katunska glava in eastern Hum, 1419 Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Hrabak 1981:188). The patronymic Bunčić = “son or descendant of Bun” — concrete evidence of the medieval Bun-stem onomastic family from which the etnik Bunjevac ultimately derives.
Likely connected to selo Buncici in Bilećke Rudine, where a stećak names Bunac-Rusovic-b????-Buncici — the latter probably a starešina from the Vlasi Banjani aglomeracija to which the Bunčići belonged.

people/Zaccaria-Valaresso-b-Venice.title: senator
people/Zaccaria-Valaresso-b-Venice.content:
Zaccaria Valaresso
Venetian senator. Signed Senate decree of July 1684, doc 22 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 22.

people/Zakman-Gledjevac-b-Karin.title: vojvoda
people/Zakman-Gledjevac-b-Karin.content:
Žakman Gleđevac
Vojvoda of the Karin Vlasi Istre dzemat (53 houses) in 1528–1530, residing at “Dasidžmani” with four other Gleđevac houses Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Held a shared timar in Vrbljani near Ostrovica with Marko-sin-Lipovica-b????. 1538: led migration to Venetian territory, settled in Podnovje (novigradski distrikt) as comes Murlacorum (vlach knez) in stipendiati military service; tracked in sources to 1559. Name “Žakman” is a variant of Šikman.

people/Zavisa-Jankovic-b-Zegar.title: kapitan Oltremarini → kapitan of Obrovac (1685–1688) → serdar
people/Zavisa-Jankovic-b-Zegar.content:
Zaviša / Sabba Janković
Brother of Stojan. Recorded as Sabba in the Sv. Ilija registers.

1676-08-17 (st. v.) — Married Maria Lase at Sv. Ilija Zadar; compare: illustrissimo signor Simon Bortolazzi (doc. 229). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
1683-09-17 — Interned to Venice with Stojan by Donà (doc. 315). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Timeline (continued — 1684 onwards, from Desnica II)

1684 — Mediates Novigrad-Obrovac robbery dispute; orders restitution of plundered goods (doc 15). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1685-02 — Recruits 50-man Oltremarini company (advance 150 ducats + 2,000 biscuits) on behalf of brother Stojan (doc 51). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1685–1688 — Capitano of Obrovac. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1686-04 — Captures the Udbina capitano (overseeing his fields), the disdar Ibrahim-aga, the spahija Muhamed-beg of Udbina (nephew of Ibrahim Pašić of Ripač), and Aga Kumalić; bought Muhamed-beg at auction for 650 reali, Ibrahim-aga for 260 reali (docs 79, 124, 126, 133, 134). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1687-06 — Raids Rebac with 500 men: 20 horses, 200 cattle, 8 captives (doc 170). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1687-09 — Wounded in Varcar Vakuf raid; 4,000 Morlachs penetrated 6 days into Bosnia (doc 179). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1689 — Attestation by Cornaro (doc 225). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1693–96 — Documented raids on Bilaj, Skopje (Vakup), Mostar (bridge), Goražde, Gabella, Cyclut, Klivno, Kupres, Bihać/Ripač (1696 attestation). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
1697 — Doge Silvestro Valier raises his pay to 50 ducats/month (doc 303). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
post-1700 — Redeployed during War of Spanish Succession to Italy. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 229, 315.
Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 15, 51, 79, 124, 126, 133, 134, 170, 179, 225, 303.

people/Zelel-aga-Babahmetovic-b.title: aga
people/Zelel-aga-Babahmetovic-b.content:
Zelel-aga Babahmetović
Former Venetian state slave; exchanged for conte Sabbini during the last (Cretan/Candian) war. His daughter (a widow returning to him) was in Mehmed-beg Durakbegović’s escort during the March 1685 ambush, doc 56 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Family

Daughter: unnamed widow, returning to her father in 1685 (in Durakbegović’s escort).

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — doc 56.

people/Zinovic-b-Sibenik.title: capo Morlach of Šibenik–Skradin
people/Zinovic-b-Sibenik.content:
Žinović (Xinovich)
One of the three capi of the Šibenik–Skradin Morlachs (with Goreta and Palikuća), paired with them in the November 1686 Bribir abandonment (doc. 155) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

people/Zuan-Moro-b-Venice.title: udinski providur
people/Zuan-Moro-b-Venice.content:
Zuan Moro
Udinski providur. 18 July 1528: reported on Christian defections from Habsburg Istria to Ottoman territory under the istimâlet offer of “blagoslovljeni većom sigurnošću i boljim životnim uvjetima” Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Zuane-Minoto-b-Venice.title: potestat i kapetan Kopra
people/Zuane-Minoto-b-Venice.content:
Zuane Minoto
Venetian potestat and capitano of Koper, 1524. Lured the Habsburg subject Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik onto Venetian territory and had him imprisoned and tortured to prevent a Vlach uprising on the border Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

people/Zuanne-Alberti-b-Split.title: governator; sub-leader for Novigrad–Karin–Bađun–Pridraga–Klošter (1684)
people/Zuanne-Alberti-b-Split.content:
Ivan (Zuanne) Alberti
Split nobleman (splitski plemić); governator; one of four “new” sub-leaders Mocenigo appointed in 1684 for the Kotari sub-region Novigrad–Karin–Bađun–Pridraga–Klošter, doc 19 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Timeline

1684 — Appointed sub-leader (doc 19); position abolished by Senate (doc 23) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685-04-07 — Captured at the Sinj battle by the Bosnian Pasha as personal slave (docs 60–62, 65) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685 — Wrote ransom letter from Klis (Livno) to Venice (doc 65) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1685 — Named successor to conte Marianović (doc 65) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 19, 23, 60–62, 65.

people/Zuanne-Rados-b-Zadar.title: conte; cavalier; sergente maggior di battaglia
people/Zuanne-Rados-b-Zadar.content:
Ivan (Zuanne) Radoš
Conte cavalier; sergente maggior di battaglia. Submitted petition for a cavalry company in 1684 (doc 5) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Member of the consortium owning the slave Hasan-beg/Ivisa Mandić (son of Šain-aga Mandić of Sinj), with ransom demand of 2,000 reali plus 4 horses (800 paid) (docs 65, 68). His brother — colonel/governator Radoš — killed or missing after the Sinj battle April 1685 (docs 60, 61); another brother held captive in Constantinople (doc 65).
Family

Brother: governator / colonnello Radoš — killed/missing at Sinj April 1685.
Brother: unnamed, captive in Constantinople (1685).

Sources

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II — docs 5, 33, 60, 61, 65, 68.

places/Alba-Real.title: Alba-Real
places/Alba-Real.content:
Alba Real / Székesfehérvár
Hungarian town. Atlagić formerly held this bassallaggio (doc 217) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Backa.title: Backa
places/Backa.content:
Bačka
Pannonian region between the Danube and Tisa; one of the four main Bunjevac branches (“podunavski / ugarski”) according to Šarić’s framework Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Bunjevac settlement

c. 1530s — earliest recorded Ottoman deportations of buntovni Vlachs from Vilajet-Hrvati.
1606+ — main wave (see Bunjevac-Migration-to-Backa-c1606).
1622 — first explicit “parochia Bunievczi” in the Kalocsa archdiocese, requested by don Simun-Matkovic-b????.
1633 — barski nadbiskup reports “parochia di Backa” with 400 zaselaka, “lingua illirica.”

Identity formation
In Bačka the Bunjevac name acquired a legitimating rather than depreciative meaning, in contrast to Dalmatia. By 19th c. it became central to the cultural revival under Ivan-Antunovic-b1815-Backa and Boza-Sarcevic-b????-Subotica in Subotica Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Settlement names of clearly Dinaric origin appearing along the Krivaja near Subotica by mid-17th c.: Kupuszina, Stanišić, Zobnatica.

places/Badjun.title: Badjun
places/Badjun.content:
Bađun
Village in Alberti’s sub-region (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Banadego.title: Banadego
places/Banadego.content:
Banadego (Banska Zemlja)
Older Venetian and Croatian designation for the lands of the Croatian Ban — pre-Ottoman northern Dalmatia and adjacent regions Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Preserved as a place-name in 16th-c. Venetian sources (“territorio turchesco” formerly Banadego) describing former Croatian holdings now under Ottoman rule.

places/Banja-Luka.title: Banja-Luka
places/Banja-Luka.content:
Banja Luka
Ottoman Bosnian frontier city; staging area for Topal Pasha 1688; convoy for Knin assembled here (docs 179, 190, 213) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Near  Mrkonjić-Grad.

places/Banjci.title: Banjci
places/Banjci.content:
Banjci
Village under Vrana pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Banjevci.title: Banjevci
places/Banjevci.content:
Banjevci
Village under Ostrovica pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Baranja.title: Baranja
places/Baranja.content:
Baranja
Region between the Drava and Danube; under Ottoman Sandzak-Mohac from 1543. Receiver of Bunjevac and Orthodox vlach migrations from Sandzak-Klis / Sandzak-Krka in the 16th–17th c. (see Bunjevac-Migration-to-Backa-c1606).
Notable settlement: Grabovac — Orthodox monastery founded 1585 by monks from manastir Dragović near Cetina. In 1619 reinforced by Klis-area Orthodox Vlachs Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Bela-Krajina.title: Bela-Krajina
places/Bela-Krajina.content:
Bela Krajina
Habsburg region in southern Kranjska. Reception area for Vlach uskok refugees from the 1530s onward, including settlement at Marindol kod Crnomelj (1551 register names Stanoje-Prijic-b????-Marindol as desetnik) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Belgrade.title: Belgrade
places/Belgrade.content:
Beograd / Belgrade
Bosnian Pasha’s destination 1684 (doc 1) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Jegen Pasha’s seat 1688 with 12,000 men (doc 211). 12,000 Imperial troops near here Aug 1688. Bishop Simeon Prešević of Belgrade.

places/Benkovac.title: Benkovac
places/Benkovac.content:
Benkovac
Town in Ravni-Kotari. Vlach nahija Benković (30 houses, 4 villages) in 1528–1530 led by primićur Petar-sin-Jancica-b????-Ostrovica; included Hotešteva, Obatija (Kula Atlagića), Polaca, Korlatović, Mirani-Jagodnja Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Nahija dissolved by 1540 (villages absorbed into Husrev-beg vakuf Kozulova-Polje).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Under Nadin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 329, 330, 377). Zaviša Janković’s holdings nearby (Bjeline / Biljane, Korlat, Kožulovo polje, Erunik / Ervenik, Kolarine, Perušić, Lisičić).

places/Bibinje.title: Bibinje
places/Bibinje.content:
Bibinje
Coastal village south of Zadar in Smiljanić sub-region (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Zemunik pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga. Captain Marlatić there (doc 316).

places/Bihac.title: Bihac
places/Bihac.content:
Bihać
Habsburg-era frontier town and captaincy seat in NW Bosnia. Way station for “uskok” Vlach migrations from Ottoman territory toward Zumberak in the 1530s, including the group of vojvoda Vuk-Popovic-b???? Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
By Desnica II era (Ottoman): Turkish frontier fort; 600 cavalry, 800 foot under Turks Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Zaviša Janković at Biač near Ripac (1696 attestation).

places/Bilisani.title: Bilisani
places/Bilisani.content:
Bilišane
Village near Obrovac Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 300). Settlement of Nicolò Budisalić (converted from Muslim Resep). Pop Mihailo Jagodić paroch (docs 385–387). Note: existing wiki has Bjeline; possibly the same.

places/Biljane.title: Biljane
places/Biljane.content:
Biljane
Village under Nadin pertinenza in the 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Sopot, Benkovac, Perušić near Benkovac, Kožulovac, Korlat, Kula-Atlagica, Cosulovo Polje, Ostrovica) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Zaviša Janković’s holdings (Bjeline = Biljane).

places/Bjelaj.title: Bjelaj
places/Bjelaj.content:
Bjelaj (Bilaj)
Main castle in Lika; in Turkish times provided 100 cavalry + 200 foot Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Ilija Janković’s June 1687 raid (800 men, 400 cavalry; killed Bilaj captain’s brother and son, doc 170). Conquered by Venetians c. 1692; population of ~5000 led to Venetian devotion 1692; tower of disdar stormed by Juka Vukmirović with bombs. 5000 souls migration with conti Đurić, Pirić, Zorić, settled Plavno, Zrmanja, Pađene, Mokro-Polje, Oton (1692-03-21). Sunaje village near Bilaj — Milovan Babić (doc 215). Christians from Bilaj area used Zarvovizza/Zrvnica mountains to ambush Turks Dec 1687.

places/Bjeline.title: Bjeline
places/Bjeline.content:
Bjeline
Village east of Benkovac. 1528: mezra “Stare Biline” with 2 non-Muslim houses, where Culina-sin-Milica-b????-Bjeline (knez, timar in Lika) resided Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1540: home of two “popovski sinovi” Nikola and Josif (Jusuf) — possible glagoljaški priest’s family. Old Catholic church Sv. Ivan (today orthodox Sv. Petka).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Bjeline / Bigliane (under Nadin pertinenza 1689) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Zaviša Janković’s holdings — 20 (later 40) ploughing oxen (docs 329, 330, 377). Note: Bilisani (Belissane / Nabelissane near Obrovac) is a distinct village despite similar name.

places/Blagaj.title: Blagaj
places/Blagaj.content:
Blagaj
Old fortress above the Buna spring; medieval seat of the Bosnian rulers, then of oblasni gospodari Sandalj Hranić and herceg Stjepan Vukčić Kosača (after whom Humska zemlja was renamed Hercegovina from 1448). After Ottoman conquest, seat of the nahija Blagaj in Sandzak-Hercegovina.
In Bosnian-Franciscan literary tradition, Buna under Blagaj came to function as a symbolic origin point of Hercegovina (“Blagaj šeher, a kasaba Mostar” — old proverb). Šarić: this symbolic charge underpins the constructed Buna-river origin legend of the Bunjevci, deployed by the Bosanska franjevačka provincija in 16th–17th-c. jurisdictional disputes with Dalmatian dioceses Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Blato.title: Blato
places/Blato.content:
Blato (Hercegovina)
Hercegovina/Mostar-area province from which 5000 souls migrated 1694 (with Brochno, Goranci) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Also a village in Mostar district where Rašić had property.

places/Bokanjac.title: Bokanjac
places/Bokanjac.content:
Bokanjac
Village in Julio Soppe’s sub-region (doc 19); under Zemunik pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Borajna.title: Borajna
places/Borajna.content:
Borajna
W. Hercegovina locality near the eastern edge of Bekija; 1477 Hercegovina defter winter pasture of the Krmpote katun (with Buhovo, Ledinac, Veseli-Vstak) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Boricevac.title: Boricevac
places/Boricevac.content:
Boričevac
Village in Lika / Bosanska Krajina border, mentioned in Desnica II Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Bosanska-Krajina.title: Bosanska-Krajina
places/Bosanska-Krajina.content:
Bosanska krajina
NW-Bosnian frontier with Habsburg Croatia. Šarić distinguishes two zapadnobosanski Bunjevac groups Saric-2008-Bunjevci:

“Stariji” — around Livno, Kupres, Glamoc (continuous from 16th c.).
“Noviji” — Bosanski Petrovac, Ključ, Sanski Most. These are actually lički Bunjevci who settled after the 1878 Austro-Hungarian occupation: predominantly Krnjeuša, Kolunić (Bosanski Petrovac), Velagići, Ramići (Ključ), Kljevci (Sanski Most). Many of these settlements were destroyed/displaced in WWII and the 1992–95 war.

The “stariji” component witnesses Catholic Vlach continuity in the prekoplaninska imigracijska zona of Sandzak-Klis; the 1743 vizitacija in Gornje Glamocko-Polje registers Catholic “Matheus Bunievza” as one such trace.

places/Brac.title: Brac
places/Brac.content:
Brač
Adriatic island (doc 55) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Cornaro’s galley off Brač (doc 172).

places/Brgud.title: Brgud
places/Brgud.content:
Brgud (kod Benkovca)
Village in Bukovica. 1528–1530: 15 non-Muslim houses; home of Samil-Jakovic-b????-Brgud (recorded in 1530 sumarni after conversion to Islam, absent from earlier mufassal) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1540 register: 16 non-Muslim houses. Old Catholic church on site of today’s orthodox Sv. Lazar.

places/Bribir.title: Bribir
places/Bribir.content:
Bribir
Castle, on confine with Zadar (docs 19, 51, 315) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Mikiel’s Knin tour 1685 included castle assessment.

places/Brochno.title: Brochno
places/Brochno.content:
Broćno
Hercegovina province from which 5000 souls migrated 1694 (with Blato, Goranci) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II; settled at Zadvarje and Vrgorac.

places/Brod.title: Brod
places/Brod.content:
Slavonski Brod
Sava crossing where Imperial army crossed 1688 (doc 211) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Imperial victory at Brod / crossing of Sava early Aug 1688 — Bosnian pasha defeated.

places/Bruska.title: Bruska
places/Bruska.content:
Bruška
Village NE of Benkovac. 1528: 7 non-Muslim houses. 1540: 6 non-Muslim houses — the only village remaining in vlach nahija Bukovica after the 1538 mass defection Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Bruvno.title: Bruvno
places/Bruvno.content:
Bruvno
Village in Lika Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 365). Conte Obradović from there. Vid Petrović killed at Bruvno 1707 by Canagetti.

places/Buda.title: Buda
places/Buda.content:
Buda / Budapest
Ottoman Buda eyalet capital until 1686 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 62). Captured Turkish caravan story (doc 62). Atlagić served at the siege of Buda (doc 217).

places/Budimski-Ejalet.title: Budimski-Ejalet
places/Budimski-Ejalet.content:
Budimski ejalet
Largest Ottoman administrative province of Hungary (Buda eyalet), 1541–1686. Comprised Sandzak-Mohac (Baranja), Backa, and other northern districts.
Receiver of two demographic waves relevant to Bunjevac history Saric-2008-Bunjevci:

1530s+ — Ottoman deportations of “buntovni vlaški element” from Vilajet-Hrvati.
1606+ — main Bunjevac wave from Sandzak-Klis / Sandzak-Krka after the Drniš revolt and other Klis-area unrest, settling the bajska/somborska/subotička nahija depopulated after the 1598 Pálffy migrations.

places/Budin.title: Budin
places/Budin.content:
Budin
Place where Sinobad-Vukčević-Mitrović Morlachs lived (doc 19, 30) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Islam pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga. Some families left Budin because of Sinobad-Mitrović feud 1684; Polo Michiel asked to mediate.

places/Budva.title: Budva
places/Budva.content:
Budva
Adriatic port “aperta e con poca difesa” — threatened by Skadar Sandžak May 1685 (doc 72) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Levant career station of Ottaviano Lazzari (doc 345).

places/Buhovo.title: Buhovo
places/Buhovo.content:
Buhovo
Western Hercegovina locality near today’s eastern edge of Bekija. Recorded in the 1477 Hercegovina defter as a winter pasture (zimište) of the Krmpote katun (alongside Borajna, Ledinac, Veseli-Vstak) — about 22 km west of the Buna river Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Aličić 1985:130–131).

places/Bukovica.title: Bukovica
places/Bukovica.content:
Bukovica
Karst region in northern Dalmatia between Zadar, Knin, and Velebit. Core settlement area of the Vlasi-Istre in the 16th c. Forms an Ottoman nahija in the 1528–1530 register (60 houses, 11 villages); reduced to a single village (Bruška) by 1540 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Later receives Hercegovinian Catholic Vlachs (Bunjevci) and Orthodox Vlach migrants.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Central focus throughout Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II; tax/herd zone. Smiljanić family origin. Pasha’s incursion April 1688 plundered it. Villages of Krmpote-Bukovica, Parčić, Modrino-Selo, Erveničani. Under Novigrad pertinenza 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Karin, two Obrovci, Krusevo, Žegar, Ervenik, Zelengrad, Drinjci, Otavac, Popovici, Lussichi). 1704 Bukovica Revolt (Pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža Uprising).

places/Buna.title: Buna
places/Buna.content:
Buna (river and place)
Short (~8 km) right-bank tributary of the Neretva in W. Hercegovina, rising at a karst spring beneath the old fortress of Blagaj. Place “Buna” stands on the river of the same name.
Significance for genealogy
Center of the Buna-river origin legend of the Bunjevci, first written down by Alberto Fortis (1778, Lika) and fra Marijan Lanosović (1794, Bačka). Šarić argues the legend is a 17th-c. Bosnian-Franciscan construct — using the Buna and Blagaj (medieval seat of Sandalj Hranić and Stjepan Vukčić Kosača) to symbolically anchor Bosnian Franciscan jurisdictional claims over Bunjevac populations against rival Dalmatian dioceses.
The 1477 Hercegovina defter for nahija Blagaj (which contained Buna) shows a different picture: among 36 vlach džemats, none can be identified as Bunjevac. The dominant figure is vojvoda Petar Hrabren (Donji Vlasi, manastirski ktitor), suggesting a predominantly Orthodox vlach population. The Neretva already in the 15th c. divided ikavski (W) from ijekavski (E) štokavski; the consistently-ikavski Bunjevci therefore cannot have originated east of the river Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
The closest core Bunjevac winter pastures (Krmpote zimišta Buhovo, Borajna) lay 22 km west by air; selo Vojnici-Ljubuski 35 km west.

places/Buncici.title: Buncici
places/Buncici.content:
Bunčići
Village in Radmilović-Dubrava near Bileća, Hercegovina. Site of a tall medieval stećak with Cyrillic inscription naming Bunac-Rusovic-b????-Buncici — likely a vlach starešina from the Banjani Vlach aglomeracija (Bešlagić 1971:390) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Connected to the medieval Bun-stem Vlachs (Vukota-Buncic-b1419 in the 1419 katun documents).

places/Bunjane.title: Bunjane
places/Bunjane.content:
Bunjane (Đakovica)
Village near Đakovica in Metohija; 1330 Dečanska povelja records 62 houses of agricultural (Serbian) population Saric-2008-Bunjevci. The toponym belongs to the medieval Bun-stem onomastic family of place- and clan-names (with Tudoricevci / Bunovići, Bunuševci of Vranjsko-Krajiste, Bunčići of Buncici).

places/Bunusa.title: Bunusa
places/Bunusa.content:
Bunuša
Village south of Leskovac. Toponymic relic of the medieval Vlasi Bunuševci of Vranjsko-Krajiste; result of territorialization of their katun Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Burgenland-Vlahija.title: Burgenland-Vlahija
places/Burgenland-Vlahija.content:
Burgenland Vlahija
Cluster of 12 Vlach-settled villages on the slopes of Kiseg gorje in southern Burgenland, on Batthyány and Erdődy estates Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. First mention 1541; settlement likely between 1517 and 1541 (perhaps c. 1538). Inhabitants were “libertini” (free peasants in military service); old Štokavian-Ikavian Croatian speakers, Catholic. Possibly drawn from same Vlach pool as the Vlasi-Istre migration cycle.

places/Buzet.title: Buzet
places/Buzet.content:
Buzet
Town in northern Venetian Istria. Buzetski Kras was a refuge for the Poropat kindred c. 1518–1528 before their return to Zrmanja Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Long-term concentration of Poropat (Poropatići) on the Venetian side at Trstenik, Dane, Lanišće.

places/Carigrad.title: Carigrad
places/Carigrad.content:
Carigrad / Istanbul
Ottoman capital (docs 53, 65) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. One Radoš brother held captive here 1685.

places/Cazin.title: Cazin
places/Cazin.content:
Cazin
Lika fortress (Bosanska Krajina), 150 horse + 300 foot Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Ceranje.title: Ceranje
places/Ceranje.content:
Ceranje
Village under Vrana pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga (Lerage o Ceragne) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Cetina.title: Cetina
places/Cetina.content:
Cetina
River and surrounding region. Forms the southeastern boundary of Vilajet-Hrvati. Site of the 1516 Ottoman capture of utvrda Nutjak, after which 9 vlach džemata defected from Poljica to Ottoman territory in Radobilja Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Cetinski Morlaci recorded by Domenico Negri (c. 1500) as speakers of “iskvarenim latinskim jezikom” — “Romani”.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Cetina campaign March–April 1685 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 28, 33, 42, 55, 59–61). Cetina Morlak migration March 1685: Ilija Peraica brought 600 armed men + families + 30,000 small animals + 10,000 cattle to Trogir territory. Atlagić retreated across Cetina April 1687; pasha at sorgente di Cettina April 1688. Cetinski-Most (Cetinski most / ponte di Cettina) — bridge mentioned docs 56, 59, 60. Vukovićev most / “ponte Vucovich” — docs 59, 61. Otok — island in Cetina where Turks camped before Sinj battle. Dragović — peninsula on Cetina with Greek-rite monastery, restored by Bušović 1694.

places/Cetinje.title: Cetinje
places/Cetinje.content:
Cetinje
Patriarch of Peć’s planned new seat 1686, with intent to send 100 cavalry to Janković (doc 160) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Seat of vladika Visarion Borilović. Bishopric of Cetinje 1707 (doc 366).

places/Cetinski-Most.title: Cetinski-Most
places/Cetinski-Most.content:
Cetinski most
Bridge over Cetina (docs 56, 59, 60) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Vukovićev most / “ponte Vucovich” also on Cetina (docs 59, 61).

places/Cicarija.title: Cicarija
places/Cicarija.content:
Ćićarija
Karst highland region between Habsburska-Istra and Mletacka-Istra, home to the bilingual Slavic-Romance “Ćići” Vlachs. Last preserved area of the Istro-Romanian / “vlaški” idiom, today only in Zejane and a handful of villages along Čepić polje Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Citluk-Licki.title: Citluk-Licki
places/Citluk-Licki.content:
Čitluk Lički
Village near Novi in Lika Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Origin of Vukašin Rošić’s 20 families (doc 45) and Vuko Vojkorsić’s family (doc 54).

places/Cres.title: Cres
places/Cres.content:
Cres
Adriatic island; Pokupić’s tartana from there Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Crna-Gora.title: Crna-Gora
places/Crna-Gora.content:
Crna Gora (Montenegro)
Region; parts joined Sandžak-beg of Skadar against Venetians 1685 (doc 72) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Crno.title: Crno
places/Crno.content:
Crno (Karno)
Village in Smiljanić sub-region (doc 19, 51); under Zemunik pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Cvrsnica.title: Cvrsnica
places/Cvrsnica.content:
Čvrsnica
Mountain in W. Hercegovina; 1477 summer pasture (ljetište) of the Krmpote katun (with Vran and Ljubusa) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Cyclut.title: Cyclut
places/Cyclut.content:
Čitluk (Hercegovina, near Mostar)
Ottoman fortress/town in Hercegovina near Mostar; defended in Morean War (first and second defense) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 358). Sinobad and Zaviša fought there. Distinct from Citluk-Licki (in Lika).

places/Dicmo.title: Dicmo
places/Dicmo.content:
Dicmo
Vallone near Sinj; Ali camped here April 1687 (doc 169); later place where settlers from Duvno + Rama placed; Orthodox enclave (docs 169, 184) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Diklo.title: Diklo
places/Diklo.content:
Diklo
Village in Julio Soppe’s sub-region (doc 19); under Lower Kotari (Milković serdarstvo) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Dobra-Voda.title: Dobra-Voda
places/Dobra-Voda.content:
Dobra Voda
Village under Ostrovica pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Dobruca-Vas.title: Dobruca-Vas
places/Dobruca-Vas.content:
Dobruča Vas (Dobrudža)
Village near Benkovac. 1528: 7 non-Muslim houses, residence of Petar-Najcinovic-b????-Dobruca-Vas (knez, head of Benković dzemat) and his relative Nenad-Jancic-b????-Dobruca-Vas Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1574 vakuf register: 15 Christian houses on Husrev-beg vakuf. Najčinović returned here after 1540 (1533 Zadar grain contract).

places/Dracevac.title: Dracevac
places/Dracevac.content:
Dračevac (kod Jasenica)
Village in nahija near Jasenice. 1590: residence of Hasan-aga-Frletic-b????-Dracevac, Muslim convert and Venetian informant on the Novigrad-more frontier; also the home of the father of uskok Andrija-Frletic-b????-Dracevac Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Dragomirani.title: Dragomirani
places/Dragomirani.content:
Dragomirani
Settlement in Donji Karin area (today only the toponym Dragomirov bunar survives). 1528: 2 non-Muslim houses; 1540: 4 non-Muslim houses including pop Stipan Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Dragovic.title: Dragovic
places/Dragovic.content:
Dragović
Peninsula on Cetina with old monastery, restored by Bušović 1694 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 317). Calogeri di Dragovich; granted lands at Međupuće (50 kanapa).

places/Drnis.title: Drnis
places/Drnis.content:
Drniš
Town in Petrovo polje, Sandzak-Klis. Site of the 1608 Drniš revolt of muslim and Vlach population under drniški aga Mehmed-Terzibasic-b????-Drnis — its suppression triggered the transfer of 2,000 morlach houses across the Danube reported by the Šibenik knez to the Venetian Senate Saric-2008-Bunjevci (see Bunjevac-Migration-to-Backa-c1606).
Drniš/Petrovo polje was one of the documented emigration sources for Bunjevac flight to Bačka, alongside Vrlika and Livno.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Captured/contested area; staging point March 1685 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 51). Fenzi the governor; threatened multiple times; Selman pasha’s defeat here; 200 men from Šibenik to garrison. Tomaso Zavoreo governator (doc 314). Petrovo-Polje near Drniš. Petrova Crkva (Petrovo Crichva) — church near Drniš/Petrovo polje (doc 195).

places/Dugopolje.title: Dugopolje
places/Dugopolje.content:
Dugopolje
Village near Klis where frate Andrea hid 1687 (doc 182) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Duvno.title: Duvno
places/Duvno.content:
Duvno (Tomislavgrad)
Hercegovina town/region, scene of the 23 Aug 1687 raid where Stojan Janković was killed by musket and sword while only 8–10 companions followed (doc 174) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Zeno burned the mosque-fortress.

places/Erdelja.title: Erdelja
places/Erdelja.content:
Erdelja (Prikanci)
Vlach settlement on the Bosiljevsko vlastelinstvo of the Frankapan. Founded c. 1540s by a smaller Vlach group in libertini service to grof Frankapan Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Catholic / pokatoličeni Vlachs.

places/Ervenicani.title: Ervenicani
places/Ervenicani.content:
Erveničani
Village in Bukovica, possibly variant of Ervenik Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Ervenik.title: Ervenik
places/Ervenik.content:
Ervenik
Village in nahija Zrmanja. 1528: 5 non-Muslim houses (recorded as “Irvnenik”). 1540: residence of pop Radoje (one of two priests recorded among Vlasi Istre that year) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Old Catholic churches Sv. Mihovil and Sv. Nikola.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Under Novigrad pertinenza (Hrvenik) in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 329, 330, 377). Settled with Bjelajci 1692. Zaviša Janković’s holdings; Novac Vujanić captain 1704.

places/Esseco.title: Esseco
places/Esseco.content:
Osijek
Slavonian town. Vizier sent Hercegovina alaibeg from Osijek 1687 (doc 174 footnote) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Forte-Opus.title: Forte-Opus
places/Forte-Opus.content:
Forte Opus / Opuzen
Venetian fort near Neretva mouth, with malarial garrison (doc 213) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Mentioned doc 55 as Opuzen / Opus.

places/Gabela.title: Gabela
places/Gabela.content:
Gabela
Ottoman fortress at Neretva mouth (Hercegovina relazione, doc 7) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Zeno discussed possible diversion (docs 172, 175). Conquered with Zaviša Janković’s help (1000 men) — Zaviša’s 1696 attestation.

places/Glamocko-Polje.title: Glamocko-Polje
places/Glamocko-Polje.content:
Glamočko polje
SW Bosnian polje. 1524 Habsburg border reports describe a “dangerous settlement of 6,000 vlach houses” in Glamoc and Unac — origin point for raiding into Habsburg Croatia and Kranjska (Vasić 1963) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In 1743 a biskupska vizitacija of Gornji Glamoč registered a Catholic named “Matheus Bunievza” — late Bunjevac trace in the prekoplaninska imigracijska zona Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Erdeljanović 1930).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Glamoč–Grahovo Campaign (Aug 1684): 5000 Morlachs under Janković, Smiljanić, Bortulačić raided Glamoč; alajbeg Filipović’s palaces burned, 50 Turks killed Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II; on return, ambushed two Bosnian-Hercegovinian pashas at Grahovo. Burgo of Glamoč burned by Zaviša after Cuprez (1696 attestation). Site of Sinobad’s death 1715 (doc 372): Andrija/Jovan Sinobad killed there. Filipović came from here.

places/Glucje.title: Glucje
places/Glucje.content:
Glučje
Village in vlach nahija Karin, part of vojvoda Zakman-Gledjevac-b????-Karin’s dzemat. 1528: 13 non-Muslim houses, total revenue 576 akčes; residence of Pavel-Jancic-b????-Glucje, his brother Radul-Jancic-b????-Glucje, and Juraj-Jancic-b????-Glucje (relatives of Petar-Najcinovic-b????-Dobruca-Vas) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Golubic.title: Golubic
places/Golubic.content:
Golubić (kod Obrovca)
Village in Bukovica. 1540: 12 non-Muslim houses in nahija Karin; residence of pop Stipan area (with Dragomirani). Home of Rajko, son of pop, recorded same year Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Goranci.title: Goranci
places/Goranci.content:
Goranci
Hercegovina province from which 5000 souls migrated 1694 (with Brochno, Blato) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II; settled at Zadvarje and Vrgorac.

places/Gorazde.title: Gorazde
places/Gorazde.content:
Goražde
Town on Drina, burned by Zaviša Janković (1696 attestation) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Gorica-Vrana.title: Gorica-Vrana
places/Gorica-Vrana.content:
Gorica (kraj Vrane)
Village under Bože Milković; raid 1693; previously burned by Tiepolo Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Vrana pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.
Cross-reference
Distinct from existing wiki Gorica (a different Gorica village).

places/Gorica.title: Gorica
places/Gorica.content:
Gorica (Tinj)
Catholic Vlach Bunjevac village in the Vojnić-Tinj corridor. Pre-1647 was within Sandžak Klis, kadiluk of Halil-beg of Vrana. Pop don Stjepan Sorić was župnik here from at least 1636 (per Šarić 2024/2008).
Source-village of major uskakanje

1647-05-29 — knez Frano Posedarski receives Cordo, Filipac and other Goričani who have crossed; Foscolo writes to receive them (doc. 5 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).
1647-06-17 — Foscolo’s proclama protects “Morlacchi da Gorizza, Percos et altri luoghi circonvicini venuti alla devotione del prencipe” (doc. 12).
1647 onward — don Stjepan Sorić of Gorica leads the uskakanje of the Goričani Catholic Vlachs into Venetian territory; mass-raids on Udbina (1648); killed at Ribnik 1648-07-17.
1648-07-31 — After Sorić’s death the Goričani elect his brother Mate Sorić as their new capo (doc. 41).

People

Don Stjepan Sorić
Mate Sorić (brother)

places/Grabovac.title: Grabovac
places/Grabovac.content:
Grabovac
Orthodox monastery in Baranja, founded 1585 by monks from manastir Dragović on the Cetina in Sandzak-Klis. Reinforced 1619 by Orthodox Vlachs from Klis-area accompanying further Cetina-region monastics Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Documents the parallel Orthodox migration stream into Podunavlje alongside the Bunjevac (Catholic) wave (see Bunjevac-Migration-to-Backa-c1606).

places/Gradiska.title: Gradiska
places/Gradiska.content:
Gradiška
Sava fortress; besieged by Imperials Aug 1688 (docs 204, 211) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Grahovo.title: Grahovo
places/Grahovo.content:
Bosansko Grahovo
Site of the 26 Aug 1684 Morlak victory: 5000 Morlachs under Janković, Smiljanić, Bortulačić ambushed two Bosnian-Hercegovinian pashas; 150 Turks killed (incl. 30 court aga, 2 “Bugliuch bassé”) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 7, 27, 56). Mazut-paša’s kjehaja killed by Sinovčić (doc 32 footnote). Smiljanić lightly wounded in hand.

places/Grbalj.title: Grbalj
places/Grbalj.content:
Grbalj (Zuppa)
Contado near Kotor at risk 1685 (doc 72) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Gruhe.title: Gruhe
places/Gruhe.content:
Gruhe
Village in Julio Soppe’s sub-region (doc 19); under Zemunik pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Habsburska-Istra.title: Habsburska-Istra
places/Habsburska-Istra.content:
Habsburška Istra (Habsburg Istria)
Inland and northeastern Istria under Habsburg rule, including Pazinska-Grofovija and parts of Kras. Refuge for Croatian Vlach migrants c. 1518–1523 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Source area for the 1528 return migration to Ottoman territory and the 1570 Pazin revolt-driven defection.

places/Hadzi-Lukovo.title: Hadzi-Lukovo
places/Hadzi-Lukovo.content:
Hadži Lukovo
Village in Mostar/Zaupa province, given to Rašić Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Hercegnovi.title: Hercegnovi
places/Hercegnovi.content:
Hercegnovi (Castel Novo)
Bay-of-Kotor stronghold under Venetian siege 1687–88; captured during the Morean War (doc 175) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Spingaroli participated in the conquest. Vodmac vineyard at Podhumnica region (formerly Resul Aga Babović’s) granted to Bishop Simeon Prešević 1697 (doc 307).

places/Hercegovina.title: Hercegovina
places/Hercegovina.content:
Hercegovina
Region south of Bosnia. Origin point of major Vlach migration streams into 16th-c. Croatia. Renamed “Hercegovina” from Humska zemlja from 1448 (after herceg Stjepan Vukčić Kosača, seat at Blagaj).
1477 defter
The 1477 Ottoman defter records istimâlet contracts with Vlach voivodes Vladimir-vojvoda-b????-Hercegovina (nahija Mostar) and Dadoje-vojvoda-b????-Hercegovina / Sinan-beg Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. The defter shows three core katuns of the future Bunjevac population Saric-2008-Bunjevci:

Krmpote — Vukic-Krmpotic-b????-Hercegovina, nahija Humska zemlja, 11 houses; pastures Buhovo/Borajna/Ledinac/Veseli-Vstak (winter) and Cvrsnica/Vran/Ljubusa (summer).
Vojnići — Vukasin-sin-Vojihne-b????-Mostar, nahija Mostar, 10 houses + 3 unmarried; eponymous selo Vojnici-Ljubuski.
Sladovići — Milosav-sin-Sladica-b????-Mostar, nahija Mostar, 19 houses; villages Podaca/Igrane/Kozica.
