In the same defter, nahija Blagaj has 36 vlach džemats (none Bunjevac); the dominant figure is vojvoda Petar-Hrabren-b????-Hercegovina of Donji Vlasi — predominantly Orthodox population around the Buna river.
Migration source area
Source area of later Bunjevac (Catholic) and Orthodox Vlach migrations into Bukovica, Ravni-Kotari, Lika, Backa. Earliest Bun-stem onomastic attestations in the 1477 defter: only Bunjak-sin-Radovana-b????-Rudine (nahija Rudine) and Bunus-sin-Petra-b????-Bjelopavlici (nahija Bjelopavlići) among 7,822 households + their fathers — the romance Bun-stem is already archaic.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Full description by fra Mijo Radonić May 1684 (doc 7) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Ahmed-paša commanded Hercegovina troops at Sinj 1685. Sandžak alaibeg there; Selman pasha threatened Knin (~1696). Brochno-Blato-Goranci migration 1693–1694 (5000 souls) settled at Zadvarje and Vrgorac. Towns/regions enumerated: Trebinje, Stolac, Konjic, Prozor, Počitelj, Gabela, Ljubuški, Mostar, Blagaj, Ranza (Rama), Glamoč, Hliuno (Livno), Sinj, Drniš, Skradin, Knin, Vrlika, Sidraga, Vrana, Obrovac, Grahovo (Bos.), Novi, Nevesinje, Gacko, Imotski, Vrgorac, Makarska, Sandžak Hercegovina (existing).

places/Hreljin.title: Hreljin
places/Hreljin.content:
Hreljin
Zrinski estate in the Croatian coastal hinterland that received the 1605 first Krmpote migration settling at Lic. In 1681 a Dvorska komora inquiry recorded testimony from two Krmpote starešine concerning earlier obligations to the Zrinski family for Lic, Krmpote, and Ledenice residents — Marcus Perpich and Stephanus Duich, both registered as “Rascianus” (a Habsburg administrative attribution, not a self-identification with Serbian ethnicity in the modern sense) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Hungary.title: Hungary
places/Hungary.content:
Hungary
Ottoman objective for Bosnian troops 1684 (doc 1) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Atlagić’s Hungarian campaign (doc 185). Atlagić had previously held the bassallaggio of Alba Real / Székesfehérvár (doc 217). Rákóczi mission of Baron Vojnović 1706 — Croat noble’s transit through Zadar to Venice/France.

places/Hvar.title: Hvar
places/Hvar.content:
Hvar
Adriatic island (docs 39, 55) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Cornaro went to Hvar; Andrea Longo camerlengo here (docs 193, 217).

places/Igrane.title: Igrane
places/Igrane.content:
Igrane
Village on Biokovo. 1477 Hercegovina defter: “Igre”, part of the Sladović džemat (with Podaca and Kozica) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Imotski.title: Imotski
places/Imotski.content:
Imotski
Hercegovinian-Cetina-frontier fortress (docs 7, 55) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Torre di Varlicca near Imotski destroyed for diversion 1688 (doc 214).

places/Islam.title: Islam
places/Islam.content:
Islam
Village; pertinenza HQ from 1689 Cornaro Liga, including Poličnik, Stošije, Budin, Kašić, Veljani, Suhovare Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Mehmed beg’s name attached to the village. Under Zaviša Mitrović 1691 (doc 309). Captain Ilija Nanić of Kašić & Islam. Mitrović family had houses and 400 gognali there from 1670 (Barbaro investiture). Conflict with Posedarci (docs 311, 312, 329, 330, 358, 359, 377). Note: 70 Žegarski porodice settled at Islam after Sorić’s 1648 raid (per Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).

places/Izsep.title: Izsep
places/Izsep.content:
Izsép
Selo near Marok in Sandzak-Mohac. 1561 defter records “Martin Bunivac” — same individual as the 1554 attestation in Marok (see Marton-Bunavac-b????-Marok) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Jablanac.title: Jablanac
places/Jablanac.content:
Jablanac
Frankopan port; pays datio for sea transit Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. 1649 Diet of Bratislava (Posonia) art. 32 restored Jablanac and Starigrad to Frankopans.

places/Jagodnja.title: Jagodnja
places/Jagodnja.content:
Jagodnja
Village in Ravni-Kotari paired with Miranje as the dzemat of Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik (1528) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Old Catholic church (now site of orthodox Sv. Simeon).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Listed in Bortulačić’s sub-region (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Two Jagodne (Giagodne) under Vrana pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.

places/Kaloca.title: Kaloca
places/Kaloca.content:
Kalocsa (Kaloča)
Catholic archdiocesan see in southern Hungary. Locus of the first explicit “parochia Bunievczi” (1622), requested by don Simun-Matkovic-b???? of the Congregatio Propaganda Fide Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In 1581 in the Kaloča area, knez Vranes-Ivanovic-b????-Kaloca with his knežina is recorded — early evidence of a Dinaric vlach presence pre-dating the main Bunjevac wave to Bačka.
In 1870 Ivan-Antunovic-b1815-Backa launched Bunjevačke i šokačke novine from Kaloča.

places/Kanjiza.title: Kanjiza
places/Kanjiza.content:
Kanjiža
“Five long days into Bosnia”; Kotarci raided here April 1688 — 300 men under Kalinić from Korlat; took 50 captives, 4000 small animals, 500 large; defeated by Dukajtar’s 100 cavalry; 15-20 dead (doc 202) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Likely Bosanska Kanjiža/Kanjiža in Slavonia or Hungarian Kanjiža.

places/Karin.title: Karin
places/Karin.content:
Karin
Ottoman fortress and Vlach nahija (53 houses, 9 villages) in 1528–1530, headed by vojvoda Zakman-Gledjevac-b????-Karin Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Held a Franciscan monastery (Bezgrešnoga začeća BDM) tending Catholic Vlachs under Ottoman rule until c. 1538; reopened 1550 by Mato-iz-Kresevo-b???? from Visovac. Karin nahija retained territorial integrity through 1540 register (29 houses).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Hajra/Kosa Lakić’s birthplace (doc 56) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Land dispute with Novigrad (doc 15). Defended itself against pasha April 1688 (doc 198). Mills leased; under Novigrad pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga; mentioned in Obrovac confine 1696. Component of pertinenza.

places/Karlobag.title: Karlobag
places/Karlobag.content:
Karlobag
Adriatic coastal town under Velebit. Habsburg fortress rebuilt 1574, becoming a new flashpoint between the three powers Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Receiving area for Rudelic families relocating from Radovin in 1683.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
“Carlobago, ancient Scrisia” — fortress on Adriatic; 200 archibuggieri 1690, palace built; salt scale opened 1696 to compete with Obrovac Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Imperial subjects retreated here 1687 toward Senj (doc 186). Senj statute confine extends to Lukovo (10 Italian miles south). Karlobag people in encroachment dispute with Tribanj (2 miles from Starigrad). 1592 Senj uskoks raided Karlobag/Pago → Venetian capture; 1615 Senj/Uskok War: Venetians destroyed Karlobag.

places/Karlovac.title: Karlovac
places/Karlovac.content:
Karlovac
Habsburg general’s seat; Erbestein’s command Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Imperial reconquest of Lika and Krbava launched from here 1689. Location of Vojnović feud, 1706 (doc 362).

places/Kasic.title: Kasic
places/Kasic.content:
Kašić
Village under Islam pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 309, 370, 377). Ilija Nanić captain of Kašić & Islam. Gvozden Radasović had property there.

places/Kastela.title: Kastela
places/Kastela.content:
Kaštela
Coastal villages between Trogir and Split. 7 April 1685: 3000 Turkish cavalry under Ahmed-paša of Hercegovina attacked Kaštela; defeated by 3000 castellani + Morlachs; Mustafa Jasko captured (docs 56, 62) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Kaštelani also raided Mostar district 1687.

places/Kistanje.title: Kistanje
places/Kistanje.content:
Kistanje
Village in Bukovica under Ostrovica pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 317, 377). Radin Bunar area near Kistanje.

places/Klicevac.title: Klicevac
places/Klicevac.content:
Kličevac
Ottoman Vlach nahija (16 villages, 120 houses) in 1528–1530 — the largest by households. Included villages Miranje, Jagodnja, headed by Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik (26 houses) and Radič (123 houses) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Dissolved by 1540, villages absorbed into Kozulova-Polje vakuf.

places/Klis.title: Klis
places/Klis.content:
Klis
Croatian fortress above Split, last major Croatian stronghold south of Velebit until taken by Ottomans in 1537. Gives name to the Sandzak-Klis; first sanjakbeg Murat-beg-Gajdic-b????-Sibenik Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik served here as a soldier before his 1518 flight to Istria.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Fortress; sub-region for various ops Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 38, 42, 51, 60, 61). Cornaro’s camp April 1687.

places/Klisa-Una.title: Klisa-Una
places/Klisa-Una.content:
Klisa (kraj Une)
Town near Una river, Ripac area; raided by Morlachs Holy Thursday April 1688 (doc 201) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Kloster.title: Kloster
places/Kloster.content:
Klošter
Village in Alberti’s sub-region (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Knin.title: Knin
places/Knin.content:
Knin
Strategic Croatian fortress town. Pre-Ottoman seat of the Knin diocese (reduced to titular see after 1522). Later seat of Sandzak-Krka Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Surroundings absorbed Vlasi-Uskoplja settlement c. 1528; later receives Vlachs Bjelajaca from Bosnia 1690.
Per Desnica (1646–1684)
Throughout the corpus the operational base of the Krčki sandžak-beg (Durakbegović 1670s–80s), the kapetan (Atlagić, then Firdusović 1680s+), and the disdar (Mehmed-aga). Recurring base of Ottoman counter-raids against the Kotari.

1648-04 — Conquered by Foscolo’s force after Klis (doc. 26); held only briefly.
1653-10-22 — Stojan Janković under Knin’s walls beheads aga Asan Cuna (Grgur Galiotović as alfier; doc. 77).
1666-04-05 — Knin Turks form the chief Ottoman muster behind the Cetina rotta.
1675-08-29 — Mehmed-beg Atlagić’s letter in Bosnian Cyrillic (doc. 214).
1683-12-16 — Pađen battle: 24 Kotarska zastave under Knin’s walls (docs. 353, 355). 10 Turks killed; 3 Kotarci dead/missing (Martin Suskovich da Budin, Bose Sudanović Bužanin, one from Ljuba).
1683 (Christmas) — Turks abandon Knin briefly, return; 1500-strong Ottoman base by Feb 1684 (doc. 384).

People (Ottoman side)

Mehmed-beg Atlagić — kapetan kninski.
Mustaj-beg Firdusović — kapetan kninski 1683 (doc. 380).
Mehmed-aga — disdar.
Asan Cuna — aga, beheaded 1653.
Omer-aga Vidimlić — 1679 (doc. 261).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Major fortress, multiple raids and skirmishes 1684–1685 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Mehmed-beg Durakbegović sandžak-beg until early 1685. Sandžak-beg Mehmed Beg Cernicich (sangiacco of Krka, Lika, Krbava); his son Mahmut Beg disdar/castellan of Knin fortress.
Knin Battle 2 June 1684 (doc 9): 2000 Kotari Morlachs under Janković, Smiljanić, Bortulačić; victory; ~120 Turks killed; 90 horses captured; Janković lightly wounded.
Mikiel’s reconnaissance (Feb 1685, doc 51): Mikiel + Janković + Smiljanić, 600-strong; burned Knin’s outlying houses; 4 Turks captured.
Knin Conquest (29 August – 11 September 1688) [docs 213–220]: Cornaro’s 15-day siege; assault Sep 2 (city); siege of inner fortresses; surrender Sep 11 by Atlagić to discretion. First/second recinto; fortress on Grebano; mosque converted to Catholic church; 11 bronze cannons captured; 600+ defenders, 300 perished, 1000 souls left, 150 Venetian subjects in chains freed. Atlagić, his son Mehmed Beg, nephew Alibeg captured. Convoy from Banja-Luka failed to relieve.
Krajina post-conquest: Sinobad governor/sopraintendente; Bulin Most + Aqua Radeglievaz lands; many Turkish houses (Hadži-Kurtović, Hadži-Emorić, Acmet-aga Livaković); Cossovo plain (Kosovo-Polje-Knin) full of new subjects; Juka Vukmirović Morlach habitant. Cadi-grande of Knin oversaw Skradin, Krka river, Strmica, Bošnjake, Komazlić, Golubić, Starčević, Otton, Pađene, Mokro-Polje, Bribir, Ivosenze, Barivode, Radučić, Zegar (doc 315). 1689 conquest details: Bjelajci settled with Pirić in Durakbegović tower; Selman pasha threatened Knin from Mostar.

places/Konjsko.title: Konjsko
places/Konjsko.content:
Konjsko
Campsite near Sinj/Klis; Zeno camped here before joining Cornaro April 1687 (doc 169) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Koper.title: Koper
places/Koper.content:
Koper (Capodistria)
Venetian Istrian seat. Potestat and capitano in 1524: Zuane-Minoto-b????-Venice — captured the Habsburg-subject Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik over Ottoman dealings Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Korcula.title: Korcula
places/Korcula.content:
Korčula
Adriatic island (doc 55) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Cornaro went here (doc 193). Peri’s origin.

places/Korlat.title: Korlat
places/Korlat.content:
Korlat
Village near Benkovac (1528: “Korlatović” with mezra Tihlić, 5 non-Muslim houses) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Old Catholic churches Sv. Nediljica, Sv. Jere, Uznesenja BDM. Adjacent Tihlić = today’s Kula-Atlagica.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Under Nadin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Biljane, Sopot, Benkovac, Perušić, Kozulovac, Kula-Atlagica, Cossulovo Polje, Ostrovica) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Zaviša Janković’s holdings (oxen 1699/1700). 300 men under Kalinić from Korlat raided Kanjiža April 1688 (doc 202).

places/Kosinj.title: Kosinj
places/Kosinj.content:
Kosinj
Lika locality. 1691 grant location for the Rukavina family Saric-2008-Bunjevci. 1712 popis: Donji Kosinj parish (Otočac regiment) had Vukelić family presence; Bunjevčevići u Kršu kod Kosinja are documented as Orthodox c. 1700.

places/Kosovo-Polje-Knin.title: Kosovo-Polje-Knin
places/Kosovo-Polje-Knin.content:
Kosovo Polje (kraj Knina)
Dalmatian Kosovo polje near Knin (doc 19, in Soppe Fortezza’s sub-region) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Pianura full of new subjects post-1688 conquest. NOT the Kosovo of Serbia. Vid Petrović “da Cossouo” — Kosovo near Sinj area, not this Knin Kosovo nor Serbian Kosovo.

places/Kostajnica.title: Kostajnica
places/Kostajnica.content:
Kostajnica
Bosanska Krajina stronghold; 800 cav + 1500 foot Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Captured by Imperials 1688 (doc 214).

places/Kotor.title: Kotor
places/Kotor.content:
Kotor (Cattaro)
Bay of Kotor naval base and Venetian provveditore headquarters Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 72, 174). Threatened by Skadar Sandžak May 1685 (Grbalj/Zuppa contado at risk). Boka where Laližić was exarch 1695. Levant career station of Ottaviano Lazzari (doc 345).

places/Kozica.title: Kozica
places/Kozica.content:
Kozica
Village under Biokovo in Vrgoračka krajina. 1477 Hercegovina defter: part of the Sladović džemat (with Podaca and Igrane) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Kozino.title: Kozino
places/Kozino.content:
Kožino
Village in Julio Soppe’s sub-region (doc 19); under Zemunik pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Kozulova-Polje.title: Kozulova-Polje
places/Kozulova-Polje.content:
Kožulova Polje
Most fertile area of the Vilajet Hrvati between Klicevac and Ostrovica fortresses, named after the pre-Ottoman noble Vlach family Kožul (Kožulić) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Endowed as the vakuf of Gazi-Husrev-beg in 1531 (first as čiftluk, later nahija Kožulova). 1574 register lists 97 “Istarska raja” houses across ~20 villages and mezre. Today only the village Kožlovac east of Benkovac preserves the name.

places/Kozulovac.title: Kozulovac
places/Kozulovac.content:
Kožulovac
Mikiel’s tour, 4 miles south of Vrana (doc 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Nadin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Biljane, Sopot, Benkovac, Perušić, Korlat, Kula-Atlagica, Cosulovo Polje, Ostrovica). See also Kozulova-Polje (existing) for the polje.

places/Kranjska.title: Kranjska
places/Kranjska.content:
Kranjska (Carniola)
Habsburg duchy. Affected by 1570 peasant unrest (wine tax) extending to Pazinska-Grofovija; site of Pazin-Peasant-Revolt-1570. Includes Bela-Krajina (south) and Notranjska (inner) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Kras.title: Kras
places/Kras.content:
Kras
Karst plateau in the Habsburg-Venetian borderlands above the Adriatic. Major refuge for Croatian Vlachs fleeing Ottoman conquests c. 1518–1523 (Vlach-Migration-to-Istria-1518-1523). Source area of Vlasi-Istre return migration 1528. Includes settlements Vodice-na-Krasu (where Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik was attested 1524), Buzet, Rašpor Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Krbava.title: Krbava
places/Krbava.content:
Krbava
Karst plateau region, pre-Ottoman seat of the Krbavski princes (Ivan-Karlovic-b????-Krbava). Krbava-Modruš diocese. Ottoman conquest 1522–1527 destroyed the knežstvo; some inhabitants migrated north or were taken in Ottoman raids (3000 captives in 1514) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Mehmed Beg Cernicich was sandžak-beg Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 17, 33, 55). Stojan Janković destroyed the area Aug 1687. Imperial reconquest 1689 from Karlovac under Erbestein. Castles: Komic (Cornich), Bunich (Bunić), Bidach, Curiach (uninhabited per Peri), Coremill (Korenica per footnote), Suignaraz (only millet guard).

places/Krivi-Put.title: Krivi-Put
places/Krivi-Put.content:
Krivi Put
Settlement in the Senjska-Kapetanija hinterland in the Senjska Draga; Habsburg-side Krmpote colony cluster with Sv-Jakov, Ledenice, Senjska-Draga. Subject of the Živjeti na Krivom Putu (2008) zbornik in which Saric-2008-Bunjevci appears.

places/Krka-Manastir.title: Krka-Manastir
places/Krka-Manastir.content:
Krka (manastir Sv. Arhangela)
Greek-rite (Orthodox) monastery on Krka river, granted to Greek-rite monks 1690 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Bounded by Lačani (vignale), Migliaska (three mills), Karslac (boschetto), Atlum Greb, Biela Vlaha, Giama Colubinca, Skradin road, Zerveni stine od Celine — 100 fields total.

places/Krka.title: Krka
places/Krka.content:
Krka (river)
River; “cadi grande” of Knin oversaw the area (doc 315) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Krka monastery of San Michiel Arcangelo (Sv. Arhangel) granted to Greek-rite monks 1690; bounded by Lačani, Migliaska (three mills), Karslac, Atlum Greb, Biela Vlaha, Giama Colubinca, Skradin road. Šuplja Crkva (Supglacriqua) — ruined church near Krka, on road to Knin (doc 51).

places/Krmcina.title: Krmcina
places/Krmcina.content:
Krmčina
Village in Bortulačić’s sub-region (docs 19, 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Zaravecchia pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.

places/Krmpote-Bukovica.title: Krmpote-Bukovica
places/Krmpote-Bukovica.content:
Krmpote (Bukovica)
Village in Bukovica near Zelengrad; distinct from Krmpote-Senj Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 301). 15 houses settled by Mede Milcović 1693; later harassed Parčić. Mede Milicovich capo.
Cross-reference
Three Krmpotes documented in this wiki: (a) Krmpote near Senj (existing), (b) Krmpote-Senj, (c) this Krmpote-Bukovica near Zelengrad.

places/Krmpote-Senj.title: Krmpote-Senj
places/Krmpote-Senj.content:
Krmpote (Senj area)
Habsburg-territory village in the Senjska-Kapetanija, settled by Krmpote families starting in the 1605/1627 migrations from Hercegovinian/Ottoman Krmpote (today Medvidja). Center of the Sv. Jakov parish (Sv-Jakov), with adjacent settlement clusters Krivi-Put, Ledenice, Senjska-Draga Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Eponymous transfer of the Hercegovinian katun name onto a new homeland — characteristic of Krmpote toponymy throughout the Tromeđa.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Luka Njegovan formerly lived here; brought 40–50 families to Vinjerac in last war Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 186). Distinct from Krmpote-Bukovica (Bukovica village near Zelengrad).

places/Krupa.title: Krupa
places/Krupa.content:
Krupa (na Zrmanji)
Village in nahija Zrmanja. 1528–1530: 1 Muslim + 5 non-Muslim houses; residence of Husein-sin-Poropata-b????-Krupa (early Muslim convert) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Later site of orthodox manastir Krupa (Uspenja Bogorodice).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Krupa monastery decima collected 1704 (doc 355) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Krusevo.title: Krusevo
places/Krusevo.content:
Kruševo (kod Obrovca)
Village in nahija Obrovac (Donja, Gornja Kruševa, with subhamlets Hotišina = Otišina, Ribnice). 1528: ~15 non-Muslim houses Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1554 Šibenik record: Vukoslav-Carapotic-b????-Krusevo (likely Krmpotic) and Mate-Milkovic-b????-Krusevo as Ottoman-side debtors. Old Catholic churches Sv. Jure and Sv. Kuzma i Damjan (in Ribnica).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Under Novigrad pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Mattio Miljanić captain 1704. Inhabitants Đurđević (now Jurjević), Anić, Karamarko, Miljanić, Klanac, Buljat, Marinović still trace into modern Kruševo (per source footnote on 1696 Obrovac inhabitants).

places/Kula-Atlagica.title: Kula-Atlagica
places/Kula-Atlagica.content:
Kula Atlagića
Village near Benkovac. 1528: “Obatija” (= Opatija) with 11 non-Muslim houses; old church Sv. Nikola at “Tihlić”. 1574 vakuf register: paired with Korlat as “Korlatović i Pehlić” (6 Christian houses) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Residence of Fran-Prejic-b????-Opatija (1528).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Under Nadin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Biljane, Sopot, Benkovac, Perušić, Kozulovac, Korlat, Cossulovo Polje, Ostrovica) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Atlagić family lands referenced near attacked village.

places/Kupres.title: Kupres
places/Kupres.content:
Kupres
Battle where Ismael pasha defeated Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (Zaviša Janković attestation 1696). Burgo of Glamoč burned by Zaviša after Cuprez.

places/Lantana.title: Lantana
places/Lantana.content:
Lantana
Small islet ~3 miles from Zadar. Outgoing Provveditor Donà was here when Mocenigo arrived May 1684 (doc 1) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Lapac.title: Lapac
places/Lapac.content:
Lapac
Lika locality mentioned in Desnica II Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Ledenice.title: Ledenice
places/Ledenice.content:
Ledenice
Coastal hinterland village on the former Zrinski estate; one of the Krmpote Habsburg-side colony cluster villages alongside Lic, Krmpote-Senj, Krivi-Put, Senjska-Draga Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In the 1681 Dvorska komora inquiry into Zrinski obligations, Krmpote starešine (Marko-Perpich-b????-Krmpote and Stephanus Duich) testified about earlier Ledenice/Lič/Krmpote duties Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Ledinac.title: Ledinac
places/Ledinac.content:
Ledinac
W. Hercegovina locality; 1477 winter pasture of the Krmpote katun (with Buhovo, Borajna, Veseli-Vstak) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Lic.title: Lic
places/Lic.content:
Lič
Village in Gorski kotar on the former Zrinski estate of Hreljin. Primary Habsburg-side Bunjevac settlement nucleus in the early 17th c. — destination of two reconstructed Krmpote migration waves:

1605 — first migration: 24+ Krmpote families, 15 Vojnić families, 20 Sladović “Gvozdenovi ljudi”.
1627 — second migration: 16 reconstructed families incl. Pavelic, Starcevic, Vukelic, Tomljanovic, Prpic.

Family lists per Pavličević 1989, medium confidence Saric-2008-Bunjevci. From Lič and the Senj coast, these families further dispersed into Lika (1690+) and Bačka.

places/Lika.title: Lika
places/Lika.content:
Lika
Karst plateau region east of Velebit. Pre-Ottoman home of “kraljevski Vlasi” (royal Vlachs); post-conquest part of Ottoman territory with major yaylak pastures (Mazinska planina, Čemernica) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Place of timar holdings for Petar-Prejic-b???? and Culina-sin-Milica-b???? (1528–1530). Toponym “Istrijanska Glavica” near Raduč preserves memory of Vlasi-Istre summer grazing.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Major source of new Morlak immigrants 1684–1685 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 8: 152 families/2300 souls; doc 70: 70 families/900 souls). Lika migration May 1685: Janković brought 70 Lika families (900 souls) under Polo Michiel’s authority. Atlagić wanted to escape Hungarian campaign; raids on Bilaj, Rebac, Udbina. Imperial conquest 1689 from Karlovac under Erbestein. 1731 Lika border cordon difficulties — communication halted. Many fortresses: Bjelaj, Sotkolač, Krug, Ostrosach, Presnić, Trzac, Krekovica, Mutuica, Kurlić, Zudurovo, Peć (Lika), Posmid, Vranograč, Cazin, Bila Stena, Buzim, Sgodagraski, Korica, Pedalj, Mali/Veliki Gračac, Mali/Veliki Obrovac (Lika), Bihać, Pazarišta, Bilai, Grabenec, Široka Kula, Budach, Brlog, Rebac, Perušić, Udbina (300 cav + 800 foot). 1684 Venetian raid burned Medak and other villages.

places/Limska-Draga.title: Limska-Draga
places/Limska-Draga.content:
Limska draga
Karst valley in central Istria, in the area of medieval Dvigrad. 1622 — selo Jural in Limska draga received 14 Orthodox Crnogorac families from Mrkojevici under pop Jovan, and (briefly) 12 Catholic families under fra Franjo Poruba Saric-2008-Bunjevci. The Catholic families separated and complained to rašporski kapetan Contarini.

places/Lipica.title: Lipica
places/Lipica.content:
Lika upper Krajina micro-fortresses
Note placeholder for several Lika fortresses listed in Peri’s relazione Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (Sotkolač, Krug/Kruga, Ostrosach, Presnić, Krekovica, Mutuica, Kurlić, Zudurovo, Peć, Posmid, Vranograč, Bila Stena/Bjela Stijena, Sgodagraski, Korica, Pedalj, Široka Kula, Budach, Brlog/Berlet, Grabenec). Most were minor castles; not pursued individually pending source confirmation.

places/Livno.title: Livno
places/Livno.content:
Livno
Bosnian frontier town (docs 9, 16, 27, 28, 30, 33, 38, 40, 53, 56, 60–62, 65) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Atlagić based here. Ali pasha of Hercegovina arrived with cavalry 1688. Burned by Zaviša (Klivuc / Cliuz). Bosnian Pasha’s stop March 1685 (doc 53).

places/Ljuba.title: Ljuba
places/Ljuba.content:
Ljuba
Village in Ventura’s sub-region (doc 19); under Posedarje pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Ljubusa.title: Ljubusa
places/Ljubusa.content:
Ljubuša
Mountain in W. Hercegovina; 1477 summer pasture of the Krmpote katun (with Cvrsnica and Vran) Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Also documented in 1670–71 visitation by makarski biskup Marijan-Lisnjic-b???? noting “Morlak” pastors and fra Anto-Ripcanin-b????.

places/Ljubuski.title: Ljubuski
places/Ljubuski.content:
Ljubuški
Hercegovina town (docs 7, 55) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. See also Vojnici-Ljubuski (existing).

places/Lovinac.title: Lovinac
places/Lovinac.content:
Lovinac
Lika village; one of three core Bunjevac settlement nuclei (with Pazariste and Smiljan) from 1690 Lika-Bunjevac-Colonization-1690. 1712 župnik: Damjan-Zdunic-b????-Lovinac — the pop Zduna of folk tradition Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Lukovo.title: Lukovo
places/Lukovo.content:
Lukovo
Village 10 Italian miles from Karlobag; the Senj statute extends only to here Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Site of duel between Mesić and Mitrović (doc 364 footnote — likely Saviša Janković).

places/Mahurci.title: Mahurci
places/Mahurci.content:
Mahurci
Village under Nin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Maidan.title: Maidan
places/Maidan.content:
Maidan
Town/place where Bosnian Pasha gathered troops March 1685 (doc 53) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Makarska.title: Makarska
places/Makarska.content:
Makarska
Adriatic port and Riviera center, Hercegovina relazione (doc 7, 33) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Listed Sept 1687 with Almissa and Poljica for Morlach captain assemblies (doc 177). Receiving area for Ivan Rašić’s group 1692 (200 souls / 25 families settled at Zavojane, Stigli, Hadži Lukovo).

places/Malpaga.title: Malpaga
places/Malpaga.content:
Malpaga
Village south of Zadar near Sukošan/Bibinje, in Smiljanić’s sub-region (docs 19, 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Listed under Zemunik pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.

places/Marcana.title: Marcana
places/Marcana.content:
Marčana
Village in southern Istra settled 1583 by a group of Morlaci Istrijani (Zadar refugees and Morlaks) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Marindol.title: Marindol
places/Marindol.content:
Marindol (kod Črnomlja)
Uskok settlement in Bela-Krajina near Črnomelj. 1551 register of uskoci records Stanoje-Prijic-b????-Marindol as desetnik (among the Prejic kin who moved north from Ottoman territory) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Marok.title: Marok
places/Marok.content:
Márok
Selo in Sandzak-Mohac (mod. Baranya county, Hungary). 1554 defter records rajetin Marton-Bunavac-b????-Marok (“Márton Bunavácz”) — the earliest known written form possibly representing the surname/etnik “Bunjevac” Saric-2008-Bunjevci (caveats noted on the person page).

places/Medak.title: Medak
places/Medak.content:
Medak
Lika village burned by Venetian raid 1684 (doc 316) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Medvedgrad.title: Medvedgrad
places/Medvedgrad.content:
Medvedgrad
Castle near Zagreb, where Ivan Karlović died 1531 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Medvidja.title: Medvidja
places/Medvidja.content:
Medviđa
Village in Bukovica. 1528–1530: 6 non-Muslim houses, dzemat of Petar-Milovanic-b????-Medvidja (also home of his brother Tomas-Milovanic-b????-Medvidja) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1540 register: 5 non-Muslim + 1 Muslim houses. Later “Krmpotsko Selo” hamlet (today Staro Selo) added by Bunjevac Krmpotic settlers; old church Sv. Ivan Krstitelj “Usik”.

places/Miranje.title: Miranje
places/Miranje.content:
Miranje
Village in Ravni-Kotari. Settled 1528 with Jagodnja as the dzemat of Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik (26 houses, fertile land yielding 1143 akčes) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Donje and Gornje Miranje were also a joint timar of Ivanis-Poropat-b????-Mirko and Ivaniš sin Mirka (2000 akčes split). Later orthodox church of Sv. Mihajlo built on site of medieval Catholic predecessor.

places/Mletacka-Dalmacija.title: Mletacka-Dalmacija
places/Mletacka-Dalmacija.content:
Mletačka Dalmacija (Venetian Dalmatia)
Coastal Dalmatia under Venetian rule: Zadar, Sibenik, Trogir, Split, islands. Reception area for Vlasi-Istre crossing 1538 (~5,000 to Zadar contado, of whom ~1,000+ retained by Antonio-de-Mula-b????-Venice) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Border with Ottoman Klis sandžak unstable until late 16th c.

places/Mletacka-Istra.title: Mletacka-Istra
places/Mletacka-Istra.content:
Mletačka Istra (Venetian Istria)
Coastal and southern Istria under Venetian rule. Designated Scudo della Dominante (“shield of the Dominante”) for its strategic value protecting Venice. Major reception zone for Vlach refugees 1538 — ~2,000 families settled, declining to ~1,700 by 1554 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Settlements include Premantura, Marcana, Zbandalj, Sikici, plus older villages absorbing newcomers.

places/Mljet.title: Mljet
places/Mljet.content:
Mljet
Adriatic island; Cornaro’s galley at Polače in Mljet harbor (doc 176) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Modrino-Selo.title: Modrino-Selo
places/Modrino-Selo.content:
Modrino selo
Village in Bukovica near St. Peter’s church (doc 302) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Sinobad family ancestors lavorano under Turks here. House of Turco Modre granted to Sinobad 1692; later disputed.

places/Modro-selo.title: Modro-selo
places/Modro-selo.content:
Modro (Modrino selo)
Casale (rural settlement) in Bukovica near the parish church of Sv. Petar.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
The casale and surrounding lands were originally held by a Turk known only as “Modre” (eponym of the place). After 1692 the lands passed to the Sinobad family. In 1697, Radoš Kresović and his brother Sava Kresović took possession of the casale and refused to return it to Sinobad — a recorded land dispute (doc 302) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
People associated

“il Turco Modre” — original Ottoman owner
Sinobad family — successor proprietors after 1692
Radoš Kresović and Sava Kresović — 1697 occupiers in dispute

places/Mokro-Polje.title: Mokro-Polje
places/Mokro-Polje.content:
Mokro Polje
Village near Knin. Concentration of Orthodox Vlach population by 1636 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Settled by Vlachs Bjelajaca from Bosnia 1690.
Per Desnica

1670-08-12 — Barbaro stations a 25-soldier guard there under capt. Marko Grubišić of Novigrad (doc. 174).
1683-12-16 — Kotarci-Šibenčani raid Pađen sub-village; some return through Mokro Polje (doc. 353).
1684-01-11 — Vukadin Bjedov da Mokropoglie (10 houses) settled at Obrovac after the Vrana uprising (doc. 364).
1684-02-28 — 600 minute + 150 grosse animali plundered “christiani sotto Grazaz” by 130 Obrovac Morlachi joined with Novigrađani (doc. 379).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Cadi-grande of Knin oversaw Mokropoglie Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 315). Assigned to Bjelajci 1692 (along with Plavno, Zrmanja, Pađene, Oton). Đuro Popović harambaša 1693. Selman pasha raid ~1696 — Sinobad repulsed; killed 100 Turks, 100 enslaved; nephew killed.

places/Morlakija.title: Morlakija
places/Morlakija.content:
Morlakija
Cartographic-imagological region of the early modern eastern Adriatic hinterland, broadly overlapping with the Tromedja and Velebit Podgorje. Used by Venetian observers (e.g. Vincenzo-Forza-b???? 1636) to designate the Vlach-populated mountainous backlands Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. “Bukovica je jedna od najvećih planina Morlakije” — Forza.

places/Mostar.title: Mostar
places/Mostar.content:
Mostar
Hercegovinian fortress and nahija seat. 1477 istimâlet contracts here brought Vlachs led by Vladimir-vojvoda-b????-Hercegovina back to Mostar/Hum nahija under sandžakbeg Hamza-beg-b???? and vojvoda Sinan-beg-b????-Mostar Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Mehmed-beg-b????-Poljica (sandžakbeg of Hercegovina, early 16th c.) was a native of Poljica.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
District descriptions in fra Mijo Radonić’s Hercegovina relazione May 1684 (doc 7) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. District includes Rakitno; raided by Kaštelani / Splićani 1687. Rašić family origin (Rusić village, Mostar district); Selman pasha of Hercegovina threatened Knin. Ilija Janković distinguished himself “sotto Mostar” in Venetian campaign (doc 375).

places/Mrkojevici.title: Mrkojevici
places/Mrkojevici.content:
Mrkojevići
Vlach montenegrin region near Bar in Sandzak-Skadar. In 1622, pop Jovan iz Mrkojevića led 14 Orthodox Crnogorac families to selo Jural in Limska-Draga in Mletacka-Istra. They were accompanied by 12 Catholic families under fra Franjo Poruba — the Catholic group separated, citing “uiuer essi sotto il rito latino, et gli altri sotto il Greco; onde non stariano mai bene insieme” — an early concrete instance of intra-Vlach rite-based separation Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Bertoša 1986:169).

places/Muskovci.title: Muskovci
places/Muskovci.content:
Muškovci
Village near Obrovac — territorialized katun of the medieval Mušković Vlachs (catunar Dien Mušković, 1433 Lika royal-Vlach charter) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1544: 25 families from here fled Lika summer pasture into Habsburg Prilisce.

places/Nadin.title: Nadin
places/Nadin.content:
Nadin
Castello (capo di Morlacchi di Nadin: Šimun Bortulačić, doc 10) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Pertinenza HQ from 1689 Cornaro Liga; Zeno’s camp. Pertinenza included Biljane, Sopot, Benkovac, Perušić-Benkovac, Kožulovac, Korlat, Kula-Atlagica, Cosulovo Polje, up to Ostrovica. Cula Smilčić, Pristeg, Boista listed under Nadin.

places/Neretva.title: Neretva
places/Neretva.content:
Neretva (Narenta)
River; Hercegovina relazione fra Mijo Radonić (doc 7) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Forte-Opus near mouth; San Zorzi / Sv. Đurađ Venetian galley station near mouth (doc 55).

places/Nin.title: Nin
places/Nin.content:
Nin
Venetian-Croatian episcopal town. Resettlement zone for some Vlach defectors during Cyprus-War-1570-1573 (April 1572 group via Nikola-Klacic-b????) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Ninska biskupija extended pastoral care into Ottoman territory through arhiprezbiter Jure-Matasovic-b????-Nin (1579).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Pertinenza HQ from 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Zaton, Bevilacqua, Pontadura, Verche, Poljica, Dračevac, Mahurci) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Cassio governor; Sebastiano Ponte noble of Nin (Liga 1696). Žegarani Morlachs settled below Nin after Ribnik 1648 (per Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).

places/Norin.title: Norin
places/Norin.content:
Norin (Narona)
Lower Neretva location; ancient Narona Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Notranjska.title: Notranjska
places/Notranjska.content:
Notranjska
Habsburg Inner Carniola; reception area for Croatian Vlach refugees c. 1518–1523, alongside Habsburska-Istra and Kras Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Krsto I. Frankapan held lands here pre-1527.

places/Nova-Vas.title: Nova-Vas
places/Nova-Vas.content:
Nova Vas (kraj Poreča)
Istrian village near Porec. Origin of Grgur-Milohanovic-b????-Nova-Vas who in 1561 founded Miljacki at Zemunik Gornji and led the 1570 retreat to Žbandalj. One of the surviving “istrorumunjski” speech communities into the modern era Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Novi-Hercegovina.title: Novi-Hercegovina
places/Novi-Hercegovina.content:
Novi (Hercegovina)
Hercegovinian town (doc 7) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Distinct from Hercegnovi.

places/Novi-Vinodolski.title: Novi-Vinodolski
places/Novi-Vinodolski.content:
Novi Vinodolski
Vinodol coast town; Peri served as captain here Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Novigrad-Dalmatia.title: Novigrad-Dalmatia
places/Novigrad-Dalmatia.content:
Novigrad (Dalmacija)
Coastal castello on the Novigradsko more (docs 8, 15, 19, 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Novigrad Pertinenza HQ from 1689 Cornaro Liga, including Karin, two Obrovci, Kruševo, Žegar, Ervenik, Zelengrad, Drinjci, Otavac, Popovići, Lussichi (Lišani?) and “all of Bukovica.” Capitanio Papafava. Vukadin Mitrović died defending Novigrad 1653.

places/Nunic.title: Nunic
places/Nunic.content:
Nunić
Village east of Benkovac. 1528: 8 non-Muslim houses (with Gurincem); residence of Martin-Prejic-b????-Nunic Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Old Catholic church Sv. Antun Padovanski.

places/Obrovac-na-Cetini.title: Obrovac-na-Cetini
places/Obrovac-na-Cetini.content:
Obrovac (na Cetini)
Distinct from Obrovac (Obrovac na Zrmanji). Tower in the Cetina valley near Sinj. Tower burned by Morlachs April 1685 (doc 61) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Cross-reference
Two Obrovacs in Desnica II: this Cetina-valley one (Sinj area, doc 61), distinct from the Zrmanja-river Obrovac in Mitrović sub-region (docs 11, 15, 19, 51).

places/Obrovac.title: Obrovac
places/Obrovac.content:
Obrovac
Ottoman fortress and varoš on the Zrmanja. Site of the Vlach nahija Obrovac (6 villages + varoš, 20 houses) in 1528–1530, headed by primićur Pavel-Rudelja-b????-Obrovac Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Ottoman fleet built here under Murat-beg-Gajdic-b????-Sibenik (1530, Velebit timber). Captured by Venetians June 1538, sparking Vlasi-Istre-Migration-to-Venice-1538.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
In Mitrović sub-region (docs 11, 15, 19, 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Both Veliki and Mali Obrovac (Obrovaz superiore/inferiore) referenced; salt scale; Casanova governor; Vlasto governor 1693. Civic complaints; families Anić, Buljat, Marinović, Miljanić, Klanac etc. settled 1696 (continued in modern Kruševo per source footnote). Janko Mitrović as Obrovac harambaša (doc 288). Mills leased to Zaviša Janković + Ilija Mitrović. Captaincy held by Zaviša; later assigned to Filip Mitrović (1 April 1688). Tomadelli signed for the illiterate Zaviša from Obrovac. Salt scale of Karlobag opened 1696 to compete with Obrovac.
Cross-reference
Distinct from Obrovac-na-Cetini (the Cetina-valley tower burned April 1685, doc 61). The “I due Obrovazzi” of doc 19 may refer to Veliki + Mali Obrovac on the Zrmanja.

places/Olib.title: Olib
places/Olib.content:
Olib
Island near Zadar Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 336). Half-owned by conte Califfi family, half by Soppe Fortezza heirs; sold to Zaviša Janković 1701 for 8000 ducats (perpetual half-half between Zaviša’s male line and his deceased brother Ilija’s male line).

places/Omis.title: Omis
places/Omis.content:
Omiš (Almissa)
Cetina-mouth port. Listed Sept 1687 alongside Makarska and Poljica for Morlach captain assemblies (doc 177) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Ostrogon.title: Ostrogon
places/Ostrogon.content:
Ostrogon (Esztergom)
Hungarian fortress; captured Turkish caravan story (doc 62) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Ostrovica.title: Ostrovica
places/Ostrovica.content:
Ostrovica
Ottoman fortress and Vlach nahija (29 houses, 4 villages) in 1528–1530, with primićuri Petar-sin-Jancica-b????-Ostrovica, Grgur-Bratic-b????-Ostrovica, later Milan-sin-Radka-b????-Ostrovica (1540 — 154 houses). By 1550 a major hub (352 houses) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Site of villages Bjeline (Stara Bilina), Lišane Ostrovičke, Vrbljani (timar of Marko-sin-Lipovica-b????).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Repeated muster point Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 19, 51). Zaviša Janković sent here; Milković’s base. Pertinenza HQ from 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Vukšić, Morlat Polača, Zazvić, Žečevo, Kistanje, Šuplja Gornja, Piramatovci, Stankovci, Banjevci, Dobra-Voda). Vušić, Morlač, Zavišić, Dobropolje, Šuplja Crikva listed under Ostrovica pertinenza.

places/Otocac.title: Otocac
places/Otocac.content:
Otočac
Imperial-side town in Lika (doc 316) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Simon Bisaković native.

places/Otok-Cetina.title: Otok-Cetina
places/Otok-Cetina.content:
Otok (na Cetini)
Island in Cetina river where Turks camped before the Sinj battle (docs 60, 61) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Otres.title: Otres
places/Otres.content:
Otres
Bukovica village. Sites of:

1648-05-11 — Janko Mitrović and other harambaše assemble at Otres after the Unac raid (doc. 28).
1662-02-13 — Otreška pogibija: Morlachi defeated by superior Turkish force after vainly pursuing a 100-Lika raid; about 200 lost (docs. 119, 120). Ražanac parish godovna knjiga lists the named dead from Ražanac including Šime and Ivan Matak, Grubiša and Ivan Skulić, Jure Valičić, Šime Ugarković, Nikola Bunjevac, Juriša Dundović, Ivo Radobilić, Garga and Maraš Jović, Vučen Vlaković, Vid Lilić, Mate Sikirić, Bože Garkinić — and from Novigradska parohijska knjiga: D. Vičko Vlatković and others.
1683 (uskakanje) — One of the muster-points of the Vrana uprising (doc. 353).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Bukovica village; Morlachs failed to muster here April 1688 (doc 198) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Padene.title: Padene
places/Padene.content:
Pađene
Village near Knin. 1636 Forza report records ~3,200 “Morlaci del rito Greco” (orthodox) populating Pađene, Plavna, Žagrović, Butišnica, Žegar, Krupa, Mokropolje, Kistanje Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Settled by Vlachs Bjelajaca from Bosnia in 1690.

places/Pag.title: Pag
places/Pag.content:
Pag
Adriatic island; recipient of part of the 1647 Krmpote exodus under harambaša Harambasa-Njegovan-b????-Medvidja. Some Pag-settled families later switched to Habsburg subjecthood Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
100 men recruited Oct 1684 by Mocenigo (doc 37) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. 1592 raid by Senj uskoks. Salt traders (“Paghesani”) with intricate negotiations. Don Vincenzo Mersio’s origin (doc 341).

places/Pakostane.title: Pakostane
places/Pakostane.content:
Pakoštane
Village in Bortulačić’s sub-region (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Zaravecchia pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Krčina, Toretta, Sv. Filip i Jakov). Commune that with Biograđani plotted Bortulačić’s murder (1692-01-16, with Vrana commune). Pardoned 1694. Petar Banković from there 1701 (doc 332).

places/Parcic.title: Parcic
places/Parcic.content:
Parčić
Village in Bukovica near Zelengrad Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Settled by Mede Milcović with 15 houses 1693; later disputed with Krmpote-Bukovica. Cvitan Cvitignanić captain 1704 (doc 352).

places/Pastrovici.title: Pastrovici
places/Pastrovici.content:
Paštrovići
Coastal community south of Budva threatened by Skadar Sandžak May 1685 (doc 72) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Pavlocich.title: Pavlocich
places/Pavlocich.content:
Pavlocich
Locality mentioned in Desnica II; precise modern identification uncertain Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Pazariste.title: Pazariste
places/Pazariste.content:
Pazarište
Lika village settled in 1690 by Bunjevac families during the recolonization of Lika–Krbava. Core Bunjevac nucleus alongside Smiljan and Lovinac.
Founding settler: porkulab Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik, holding 168 štrikova zemlje per the 1712 popis (Kaser 2003) across Pazarište, Vaganac, and Veliki-Zitnik Saric-2008-Bunjevci. 1712 župnik: Juraj-Smolcic-b????-Pazariste.
The Starčević lineage based at Veliki-Zitnik (a sub-locality of Pazarište) produced four generations later Sime-Starcevic-b1784-Lika and Ante-Starcevic-b1823-Veliki-Zitnik.

places/Pazin.title: Pazin
places/Pazin.content:
Pazin
Seat of Pazinska-Grofovija. Captain in 1571: Gaspar-Mauric-b????; predecessor Jakob earlier provoked the Pazin-Peasant-Revolt-1570 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Pazinska-Grofovija.title: Pazinska-Grofovija
places/Pazinska-Grofovija.content:
Pazinska Grofovija (County of Pazin)
Inland Habsburg Istrian county, seat at Pazin. Captain in 1571: Gaspar-Mauric-b????. Site of the 1570 Pazin-Peasant-Revolt-1570 which led to ~2,000 “Ćići” subjects fleeing to Ottoman territory Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Hosted Vlach settlements at Tinjan, Milohanic-i, and others.

places/Perast.title: Perast
places/Perast.content:
Perast
Bay-of-Kotor town (doc 72) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Origin of ship captain Zuanne Matošević (doc 221).

places/Petrcane.title: Petrcane
places/Petrcane.content:
Petrčane
Village in Julio Soppe’s sub-region (doc 19); under Lower Kotari (Milković serdarstvo) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Petrovo-Polje.title: Petrovo-Polje
places/Petrovo-Polje.content:
Petrovo polje
Locale near Drniš/Knin; Mile Dragičević’s village (b. c. 1646) (doc 162) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Petrova Crkva (Petrovo Crichva) — church near Drniš/Petrovo polje (doc 195).

places/Piramatovci.title: Piramatovci
places/Piramatovci.content:
Piramatovci
Village under Ostrovica pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Plavna.title: Plavna
places/Plavna.content:
Plavna / Plavno
Region near Knin. Settled c. 1528 by Vlasi-Uskoplja; depopulated, then resettled 1540 with returning Vlasi-Istre under primićur Hlapac-sin-Radovana-b????-Plavna and vojvoda Dragisa-sin-Dragoja-b????-Plavna (forming new “Plavna Istrija” nahija) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Later receives Vlachs Bjelajaca from Bosnia 1690.
Cross-reference / open question
See also Plavno (Desnica II usage 1684–1694). May be the same place — historiographical question open.

places/Plavno.title: Plavno
places/Plavno.content:
Plavno
Field/village near Knin. Site of “torre di Durach Begovich” (Durakbegović tower); Žepina lost an arm here 1684; Plavanjci offered to defect June 1684 (docs 2, 13) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. After 1688/92 conquest assigned to Bjelajci alongside Zrmanja, Pađene, Mokro-Polje, Oton; tower of Muhamedbeg Durakbegović given to Pirić; Janko Vrsalj built fence sheltering 50+ families 1694.
Cross-reference / open question
May be the same place as Plavna — historiographical question open. Saric (2024) records the older “Plavna Istrija” nahija as resettlement of Vlasi-Istre 1540; Desnica’s “Plavno” 1684–1694 sits in the same broad Knin region. Treated here as distinct entry per source-name usage.

places/Pocitelj.title: Pocitelj
places/Pocitelj.content:
Počitelj
Hercegovina town on Neretva (doc 7) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Podaca.title: Podaca
places/Podaca.content:
Podaca
Village in Makarsko primorje. 1477 Hercegovina defter: one of the three constituent villages of the Sladović džemat (Podci = Podaca), alongside Igrane and Kozica Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Šarić argues this anomalous “by-villages” organization (rather than transhumant pastures) suggests either a vlahizirano peasant population given Vlach status, or a fully territorialized vlach katun.

places/Podgorje.title: Podgorje
places/Podgorje.content:
Podgorje
The Velebit foothills along the Adriatic. In 1528–1530 a Vlach nahija with 147 houses across 6 villages and the varoš of Obrovac — the most populous Vlasi Istre nahija, headed by Mate-Rojic-b????-Podgorje (80 houses) and Mikula-Rojnovic-b????-Podgorje (57 houses) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. By 1540 entirely depopulated; old villages listed as “puste mezre”. Major yaylak (summer pasture) for transhumant Vlachs into the late 16th c.

places/Podnovje.title: Podnovje
places/Podnovje.content:
Podnovje (kod Podgradine)
Settlement in novigradski distrikt where Venetian authorities resettled key Vlasi Istre starešine after the 1538 defection. Residences of Zakman-Gledjevac-b????-Karin (comes Murlacorum, stipendiati) and Petar-Najcinovic-b????-Dobruca-Vas (kapetan) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Polaca.title: Polaca
places/Polaca.content:
Polača
Village near Benkovac. 1528: 7 non-Muslim houses; record of “Ivan, sin Hrvata” and (in nearby Marijan Polača) “Radonja, sin Morlaka”. Župnik in 1591: Matej-Danilovic-b????-Polaca, whose deposition before the Nin bishop documented widespread konkubinat among glagoljaški priests in Banadego and Lika Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Old Catholic churches Sv. Cecilija, Sv. Kuzma i Damjan.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Under Vrana pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Morlat Polača under Ostrovica pertinenza.

places/Polesnik.title: Polesnik
places/Polesnik.content:
Polešnik
Village in Ventura’s sub-region (doc 19); under Islam pertinenza (doc 377) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Policnik.title: Policnik
places/Policnik.content:
Poličnik
Village under Islam pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Stošije, Budin, Kašić, Veljani, Suhovare) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Poljica-Brig-Vrana.title: Poljica-Brig-Vrana
places/Poljica-Brig-Vrana.content:
Poljica (brig Vrane)
Village in the Zadar contado near Vrana / Nin, in Posedarski’s sub-region (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Distinct from Poljica (Poljičko kneštvo, between Split and Cetina). Later listed under Nin pertinenza in Cornaro/Dolfin Liga (1689, 1696) alongside Zaton, Bevilacqua/Privlaka, Pontadura, Vrčevo, Dračevac, Mahurci.

places/Poljica.title: Poljica
places/Poljica.content:
Poljica
Autonomous principality (Poljičko kneštvo) under nominal Venetian then Ottoman authority. 1475 statute regulated relations with Ottoman martolosi; 1506 Ivanis-Nenadic-b????-Poljica and others fled to Ottoman territory; 1508 attempted defection; 1514 nominal submission to Sultan; 1540 final Ottoman incorporation as vlach nahija under Sandzak Hercegovina Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Birthplace of sandžakbeg Mehmed-beg-b????-Poljica.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Listed Sept 1687 alongside Makarska and Almissa for Morlach captain assemblies (doc 177) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Cross-reference
See also Poljica-Brig-Vrana (the Zadar-contado “Poglizza” near Vrana — distinct).

places/Pontadura.title: Pontadura
places/Pontadura.content:
Pontadura
Village in Posedarski’s sub-region (doc 19), under Nin pertinenza 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Popovici.title: Popovici
places/Popovici.content:
Popovići
Settlement; pasha stopped here April 1688 with 1500 cavalry (doc 198) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Listed under Novigrad pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.

places/Porec.title: Porec
places/Porec.content:
Poreč
Venetian Istrian town. Nova-Vas near Poreč was home of Grgur-Milohanovic-b????-Nova-Vas, who founded Miljacki at Zemunik (1561) and later Žbandalj (1570) near Poreč after retreat Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Posedarje.title: Posedarje
places/Posedarje.content:
Posedarje
Coastal village/county on Novigrad more, ancestral seat of the Posedarski (Benja-Posedarski) noble line. The principal Venetian-side settlement-village for the Žegar Mitrović uskakanje and a major staging-area for Morlachi assaults into Bukovica.
Genealogical/military summary (per Desnica 1646–84)

1647 — Knez Frano Posedarski (the Elder) is the local governator collaborating with Foscolo (docs. 5–10) on Morlachi receiving operations.
1648-05-15 — Janko Mitrović given judicial first-instance authority over Bukovački uskoci based at Posedarje (doc. 29).
1654-01-10 — Janko Mitrović’s home village from his uskakanje base; he repels a Turkish raid at the Posedarje guazzo; pay raised to 20 ducati (doc. 78).
1656-08-04 — Bigliane (a Posedarje sub-village) is where the Morlach harambaše signed the petition refusing Posedarski as colonnello (doc. 105).
1666-05-06 — During Stojan Janković’s slavery the Posedarci elect Pavle Vukčević as vice-harambaša (doc. 152).
1671-01 — Greek-merchant svaleggio in the Posedarje area: 2 Greek merchants killed/wounded; Stojan Janković investigates (docs. 186, 188).
1674 — Petar Ćivran investitures Posedarci with additional Budin lands (doc. 209). 36+8+44 families: Possedarja old + Erveničani + Budinjani.
1683 — Frane Posedarski the Younger (governator of Nin) one of the four direttori (doc. 395).

People

Janko Mitrović (resident at Posedarje from c. 1647)
Stojan Janković — harambaša di Possidaria
Pavle Vukčević
Frane Posedarski Elder
Žorži Posedarski
Frane Posedarski Younger

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Posedarski’s sub-region (doc 19) included Pontadura, Vrčevo, Zaton, Privlaka, Poljica (brig Vrane), Posedarje Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Pertinenza HQ from 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Ražanac, Castel Venier (Vinjerac), Starigrad, Radovin, Ljuba). Sinobad family birthplace (doc 331).

places/Pozzi.title: Pozzi
places/Pozzi.content:
Pozzi (Venetian state prison)
The lowest tier of the Venetian state prison in the Doge’s Palace complex — the pozzi (“wells”) were ground-floor cells, the harshest detention in the Republic. Distinct from (and lower than) the Piombi (lead-roofed upper cells) and the Camerotti (mid-level, often used for political prisoners awaiting transfer).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)

pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža — moved from the Camerotti to the Pozzi after several years of confinement; held there for the bulk of his ~40-year imprisonment following the 1704 Bukovica revolt; released 29 March 1746 at age 80, blind and deaf, by order of the State Inquisitors (doc 389) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Notes

Jagodić’s own deposition (doc 389) describes the conditions: “10 mesi” in the Pozzi initially, then transfer to “altre carceri ma sempre oscure” — “always dark,” with progressive loss of sight and hearing over four decades.

places/Premantura.title: Premantura
places/Premantura.content:
Premantura
Village south of Pula founded 1585 by Vlach colonists from Sandzak-Krka (Zvonigrad, Nadin, Velim) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Marks the inflection point from “Vlasi Istre” cycle to new Štokavian “dalmatinsko-transdinarska” migration streams in southern Istra (17th c.).

places/Pridraga.title: Pridraga
places/Pridraga.content:
Pridraga
Village east of Novigrad (doc 196 footnote) in Alberti’s sub-region (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Grbe / Garbe — small field in Pridraga, site of skirmish March 1688 (“zabeleška o pogibiji na Grbama”).

places/Prilisce.title: Prilisce
places/Prilisce.content:
Prilišće
Village on the ribničko vlastelinstvo of the Zrinski. 1544: settled by 25 Vlach Mušković families from Obrovac who fled summer pasture in Lika to Habsburg territory; granted hereditary libertini status by Nikola-Zrinski-b???? (deed 25 June 1544) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Catholic, čakavski (ikavski) speakers; likely from the Vlasi-Istre population.

places/Pristeg.title: Pristeg
places/Pristeg.content:
Pristeg
Village near Benkovac. Old Catholic church Sv. Frane. Within Uželice belonged to “Donji i Gornji Čerani s Ožalicom” (1528: 17 non-Muslim houses) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Under Nadin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga; also listed under Vrana pertinenza Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Privlaka.title: Privlaka
places/Privlaka.content:
Privlaka
Village in Posedarski’s sub-region (doc 19); under Nin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Prolog.title: Prolog
places/Prolog.content:
Prolog (Mt.)
Mountain pass between Cetina and Bosnia, route of Turkish reinforcements to Sinj (docs 60, 61) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. “Bukova Klavica” (Bucova Clauizza) is a location on Mt. Prolog where Vid Petrović and 60 haiduks ambushed Ottoman travellers 1702 (doc 346); also where Nikola Žanković was killed 1699.

places/Pula.title: Pula
places/Pula.content:
Pula
Major Venetian Istrian port. Reception zone for late-16th-c. Vlach colonization of southern Istra, including Premantura (1585), Marcana (1583), and the Sikici hamlet (1586) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Radovin.title: Radovin
places/Radovin.content:
Radovin
Village in Zadar district. 16th–17th c. concentration of Rudelic Vlachs absorbed into Catholic Bunjevac stream; in 1683 relocate to Karlobag and Šugarje in Podgorje, with some to Smiljan in Lika (1686 Pavo-Rudelic-b????-Smiljan) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
In Ventura’s sub-region (docs 19, 31) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II; under Posedarje pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.

places/Rakitno.title: Rakitno
places/Rakitno.content:
Rakitno
District of Mostar; 20 houses migrated to Venetian territory 1687 with 40 armed men (doc 183) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Rama.title: Rama
places/Rama.content:
Rama
River entering Neretva (doc 7) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Site of Sv. Petar in Rama Franciscan monastery; abandoned by friars Oct 1687; 80+ friars + 500 armed family members fled to Sinj/Dicmo, then to Sustipan abbey near Split (docs 181, 184).

places/Ravni-Kotari.title: Ravni-Kotari
places/Ravni-Kotari.content:
Ravni Kotari
Plain region in the Zadar hinterland, fertile and contested between Ottoman and Venetian powers in the 16th c. Includes Benkovac, Nadin, Polaca, Miranje and surroundings. Major settlement zone of the Vlasi-Istre returning 1528 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Razanci.title: Razanci
places/Razanci.content:
Ražanac
Village in Ventura’s sub-region (docs 19, 31); under Posedarje pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Luka Njegovan lived above Ražanac in Podgorje (doc 186) — Krmpote→Vinjerac→Ražanac trajectory.

places/Rebac.title: Rebac
places/Rebac.content:
Rebac
Lika castle. Zaviša Janković’s June 1687 ambush (500 men, 20 horses, 200 cattle, 8 captives; doc 170) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Battle site where Turks of Udbina defeated (doc 316).

places/Ribnik.title: Ribnik
places/Ribnik.content:
Ribnik
Lika locality. Two historical claims to fame:
1648 — Battle of Ribnik
Site of the catastrophic Kotarska defeat Battle of Ribnik (16/17 July 1648) — turning point of the early-Candian-War Morlach campaign. The Kotarska force of ~3000 (under don Stjepan Sorić, Petar Smiljanić, Janko Mitrović and a host of harambaše) attempted to take Ribnik on intelligence supposedly favourable; ambushed at the narrow exit-pass; pop Sorić captured wounded and beheaded by the Turks; Petar Smiljanić killed; their entire senior cadre fell.
Doc. 39 (1648-07-17) lists losses harambaša-by-harambaša with village of origin → settlement village — the single richest origin/settlement document in Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I. See Battle-of-Ribnik-1648.
1702 — Ribnička buna
Lika locality giving its name to the Ribnička buna of 1702 — the Bunjevac uprising sparked by the conflict between porkulab Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik and vojvoda Marko-Butorac-b????-Lika. 1712 popis: Rukavina, Franić, Jurjević, Rogić, Sekulić, Vranešić, Župan family presence Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Ricice.title: Ricice
places/Ricice.content:
Ričice
Lika locality. 1691 grant location for the Rukavina family Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Rijeka.title: Rijeka
places/Rijeka.content:
Rijeka
Habsburg Adriatic port (Fiume), reference point on migration routes between Habsburska-Istra and the Croatian coast.

places/Ripac.title: Ripac
places/Ripac.content:
Ripač
Castle near Bihać on the Una; Klisa raid Holy Thursday April 1688 (doc 201) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Mentioned in Lika report and Zaviša Janković’s deeds.

places/Rusic.title: Rusic
places/Rusic.content:
Rusić
Village in Mostar district; origin of Rašić Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Sandzak-Bosna.title: Sandzak-Bosna
places/Sandzak-Bosna.content:
Sandzak Bosna
Ottoman sandžak covering Bosnia. Sanjakbeg Gazi-Husrev-beg (active 1521–1541) administered the early conquests in Croatia via Vilajet-Hrvati Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Site of the 1528–1530 mufassal defter (TR-BOA-TTD No. 157) and 1530 sumarni defter that first record the Vlasi Istre.

places/Sandzak-Hercegovina.title: Sandzak-Hercegovina
places/Sandzak-Hercegovina.content:
Sandzak Hercegovina
Ottoman sandžak covering Hercegovina from c. 1470. 1477 Vlach defter records istimâlet settlement contracts (Vladimir, Radoje vojvode) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Source area for major Vlach migrations into Croatia, including Vlasi-Uskoplja and Catholic Bunjevac streams.

places/Sandzak-Klis.title: Sandzak-Klis
places/Sandzak-Klis.content:
Sandzak Klis
Ottoman frontier sandžak established 1537 after the conquest of Klis fortress, succeeding the Vilajet-Hrvati. Seat at Klis, later Knin. First sanjakbeg: Murat-beg-Gajdic-b????-Sibenik. Surveyed in opširni defteri of 1540, 1550, 1574, 1585 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Held the western Tromeđa frontier with Venice and Habsburgs.

places/Sandzak-Krka.title: Sandzak-Krka
places/Sandzak-Krka.content:
Sandzak Krka (Lika)
Ottoman sandžak with seat at Knin, created from western parts of Sandzak-Klis in the late 16th c. 1585 register here marks the disappearance of the Vlasi Istre name; surviving “raja” pay former Vlach filurija in reduced amounts Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Sandzak-Mohac.title: Sandzak-Mohac
places/Sandzak-Mohac.content:
Sandžak Mohač (Baranja)
Ottoman administrative unit covering today’s Baranja and northern Slavonia after 1543. Source for two key Bunjevac defter attestations Saric-2008-Bunjevci:

1554 defter, selo Marok: Marton-Bunavac-b????-Marok (“Márton Bunavácz”). Earliest possible written form of “Bunjevac”.
1561 defter, selo Izsep: same person as “Martin Bunivac” (Velics 1890).
Same registers also list raja designated “Hirvat” in selo Sukit (mađ. Szőkéd) and selo Ata (mađ. Áta) — Ottoman regional Croat designation for migrants from Vilajet-Hrvati.

places/Sarajevo.title: Sarajevo
places/Sarajevo.content:
Sarajevo
Major Bosnian city; Ottoman Bosnia capital. Departure of 80+ families fleeing to Constantinople 1688 (doc 211) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Senj.title: Senj
places/Senj.content:
Senj
Habsburg Adriatic port and base of the Senj uskoks (corsair-warriors targeting Ottoman territory). Captain in 1560: Ivan-Lenkovic-b???? Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Hosted Vlasi-Istre defectors among uskoks; notable were Andrija-Frletic-b????-Dracevac (“Andre kapetan” of epic tradition) and his brother Vuk. Many uskok captains were former Ottoman subjects.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Capitanio of Segna mentioned (doc 61) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Senj statute confine extends only to Lukovo (10 Italian miles south of Karlobag). Senjani occupied Frankopan estates. Sv. Juraj near Senj served as refuge for Bukovčani during the Candian war.

places/Senjska-Draga.title: Senjska-Draga
places/Senjska-Draga.content:
Senjska Draga
Senj hinterland valley; Habsburg-side Krmpote colony cluster (with Krmpote-Senj, Sv-Jakov, Krivi-Put, Ledenice) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Senjska-Kapetanija.title: Senjska-Kapetanija
places/Senjska-Kapetanija.content:
Senjska Kapetanija
Habsburg captaincy seated at Senj, on the Adriatic coast adjacent to the Tromedja. Base of the Senj uskoks. Captain in 1560: Ivan-Lenkovic-b???? Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Hosted Vlasi-Istre defectors among the uskoks, including Andrija-Frletic-b????-Dracevac and Vuk Frletić.

places/Senjsko-Modruska-Biskupija.title: Senjsko-Modruska-Biskupija
places/Senjsko-Modruska-Biskupija.content:
Senjsko-modruška biskupija
Catholic diocese covering the Senj and Modruš sees united in administration. Around 1700 covered four kapetanije of the Karlovački generalat (Senj, Otočac, Ogulin, Tounj) plus Lika and Krbava.
The only early-modern ecclesiastical institution to introduce “Bunjevac” into official record Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Sequence:

1702 — biskup Martin-Brajkovic-b????-Senj uses dvojni naziv catholici Valachi alias Bunievczi.
Subsequent biskupi continue: Benedikt Bedeković, Adam Ratkaj, Nikola Pohmajević, Ivan Anton Benzoni, Juraj Vuk Čolić — within years the vlaški part dropped, leaving only Bunievczi.
1733 — vojni svećenik Andrija-Josip-Mandal-b????-Lika no longer calls Bunjevci Vlachs but says they are similia in dress, customs, and life.

Šarić’s reading: senjska Crkva took the name from popular tradition because vlaški had become a synonym for Orthodox/Schismatic in adjacent dioceses (Zagreb, Ljubljana). It served as differentia specifica to mark Catholic Bunjevci off from Orthodox vlach krajišnici.

places/Sibenik.title: Sibenik
places/Sibenik.content:
Šibenik
Venetian Dalmatian city. Birth area of Murat-beg-Gajdic-b????-Sibenik and of Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik (before his flight to Istria 1518). Šibenik knez in 1532: Bernardo-Balbi-b????-Venice Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Hub for trade contacts of Vlasi Istre on the Ottoman side (e.g. Petar-Najcinovic-b????-Dobruca-Vas 1533).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Multiple staging events; recruiting area, pertinenza border Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 8, 16, 17, 25, 28, 38, 39, 48, 49, 50, 51). Battista Contarini conte. Vranjska zaseda 28–29 May 1684: Šibenik Morlachs ambushed Turkish raiding party returning from Šibenik area; 40 Turks killed. 500 picked men from Šibenik / Skradin / Velim raided Bilaj Dec 1687. 200 men from Šibenik to garrison Drniš. Crnice brothers died in prison there (doc 343). Bishop Calegari. Filip Smiljanić actually killed in Šibenik brawl (per source footnote, doc 320 — corrects the family supplica’s claim he died fighting Turks).

places/Sicevo.title: Sicevo
places/Sicevo.content:
Šićevo
Mountain between Glamoč and Grahovo crossed by Morlachs Aug 1684 (doc 27) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Sidraga.title: Sidraga
places/Sidraga.content:
Sidraga
Old medieval region name (doc 7) for the Bukovica/Biograd area Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Sikici.title: Sikici
places/Sikici.content:
Šikići
Hamlet near Pula founded 1586 by Morlach colonists Sime-Sikic-b???? and Mate-Sikic-b???? with their families. First “bunjevačka” stream into southern Istra Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Sinj.title: Sinj
places/Sinj.content:
Sinj
Cetina-valley fortress (docs 33, 38–42, 60–65) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Sinj attempt under Marcello (Oct 1684) — failed siege; led by Alvise Marcello + Bortulačić (doc 42). Sinj Battle 7 April 1685 — major Venetian disaster: Morlach panic, Italian infantry rout; Stojan Janković fought bravely, almost alone among capi; many officers killed/captured (Tanusi, Marušić, Macedonia, Palese, Rados-brother, Lombardo missing); Alberti captured by Bosnian Pasha. Sinj defenders: ~70 sejmena + 200 mestani = ~270. Sinj Relief (April 1687) — Cornaro and Zeno relieved Sinj from Atlagić’s siege; Atlagić withdrew across Cetina. Conquest finalized; Sinobad among first up the breccia. Site of bishopric.

places/Skoplje-Bosnia.title: Skoplje-Bosnia
places/Skoplje-Bosnia.content:
Skopje (Bosnia, near Klivuno)
Bosnian Skoplje, near Livno Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 181). 25 Knin Turks ambushed between Skopje and Klivuno Oct 1687. Distinct from Macedonian Skopje and from Hercegovinian Uskoplje. Seat of Jusuf aga Derviševčić in 1700 (doc 321). Burned by Zaviša Janković (Vakup superior + 300 houses; 1696 attestation).

places/Skradin.title: Skradin
places/Skradin.content:
Skradin
Ottoman fortress and seat of the kadiluk under which the nine Vlasi Istre nahijas were registered in 1528–1530 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Site of Ottoman fleet construction alongside Obrovac under Murat-beg-Gajdic-b????-Sibenik.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Repeated reference (docs 19, 28, 33, 37, 38, 50, 51, 58) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Cadi-jurisdiction subordinate to Knin. Staging area for Knin campaign Aug 1688 (bridge planned). Depopulated post-conquest; Dolfin ordered Morlachs to return; 50 fields granted. 500 picked men from Šibenik / Skradin / Velim raided Bilaj Dec 1687 (doc 184).

places/Skrobucani.title: Skrobucani
places/Skrobucani.content:
Skrobučani
Village near Skoplje (Uskoplje) raided by Primorci Nov 1687 (doc 182) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Slosella.title: Slosella
places/Slosella.content:
Slosella
Coastal village in the Šibenik area, mentioned in Desnica II Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Smiljan.title: Smiljan
places/Smiljan.content:
Smiljan
Lika village; major Bunjevac settlement nucleus from 1690 Lika-Bunjevac-Colonization-1690. 1712 župnik: Simun-Zdunic-b????-Smiljan Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Earlier attestation: Pavo-Rudelic-b????-Smiljan (Rudelić Smiljan, 1686) — pre-1690 Vlach presence noted in the Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre ingest.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Lika village within imperial reconquest 1689 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Smiljanić family origin (Bukovica branch — Bukovica).

places/Solin.title: Solin
places/Solin.content:
Solin (Salona)
Coastal locality near Split (docs 38, 39) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Sopot.title: Sopot
places/Sopot.content:
Sopot
Village under Nadin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Split.title: Split
places/Split.content:
Split (Spalato)
Major Venetian Adriatic port; base for many operations (docs 24, 35, 38, 40, 42, 54, 55, 57, 60–66) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Cosmi archbishop. Sustipan abbey (Sant Steffano) outside Split assigned as temporary refuge to Rama Franciscans 1687. Solin / Salona nearby.

places/Srb.title: Srb
places/Srb.content:
Srb
Lika/Una-area locality, mentioned in Desnica II Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Stankovci.title: Stankovci
places/Stankovci.content:
Stankovci
Village under Ostrovica pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Stari-Grad-Zaravecchia.title: Stari-Grad-Zaravecchia
places/Stari-Grad-Zaravecchia.content:
Stari Grad (kraj Biograda / Zara Vecchia)
Locality near Biograd na Moru / Zara Vecchia, distinct from Starigrad (Starigrad-Paklenica on the Velebit coast). Listed in the Mitrović sub-region with “I due Obrovazzi — Stari Grado — Budin” (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Cross-reference
The Mitrović jurisdictional list places “Stari Grado” alongside both Obrovacs and Budin, suggesting the southern (Biograd-area) toponym, not Starigrad-Paklenica.

places/Starigrad.title: Starigrad
places/Starigrad.content:
Starigrad
Coastal village on the Velebit coast that received Krmpote families during the 1647 migration under harambaša Harambasa-Njegovan-b????-Medvidja Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Velebit-coast Starigrad (Starigrad-Paklenica) listed under Posedarje pertinenza alongside Rasanze, Castel Venier (Vinjerac), Radovin, Ljuba (Cornaro Liga 1689, Dolfin Liga 1696) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Sibuljina/Tribanj 2 miles distant; encroachment dispute with Karlobag people; in Tribanj resettlement 1702/1704 some 25 families moved. 1649 Diet of Bratislava (Posonia) art. 32 restored Jablanac and Starigrad to Frankopans.
Cross-reference
Distinct from Stari Grad (Zara Vecchia) near Biograd (Mitrović sub-region, doc 19).

places/Stigli.title: Stigli
places/Stigli.content:
Stigli
Village in Mostar/Zaupa province, given to Rašić Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Stinica.title: Stinica
places/Stinica.content:
Stinica
Port near Karlobag, 5 miles from Lukovo, with church of Madonna; settled in 1696 by Bukovčani who fled to Sv. Juraj near Senj during the Candian war Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Stosije.title: Stosije
places/Stosije.content:
Stošije
Village under Islam pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Subotica.title: Subotica
places/Subotica.content:
Subotica
Northern Backa city. Major Bunjevac population center from the 17th-c. migrations onward.
In 1687 Vojnići are listed among Subotica graničari; the subotički Vojnići were ennobled by the Hungarian crown in 1741 (Sekulić 1986). Per Sekulić, they trace origin to Dalmatia — Šarić raises but does not resolve whether they descend from the Tinj/Županović Vojnići of Ravni-Kotari Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
19th-c. revival nucleus

1868 — Boza-Sarcevic-b????-Subotica launches the Bunjevački kalendar.
1870 — Ivan-Antunovic-b1815-Backa launches Bunjevačke i šokačke novine (Kalocsa).

This Subotica intellectual circle reaffirmed bunjevaštvo as a distinct cultural identity in response to Hungarian magyarization. Šarić frames this as a movement opposite to the Lika trajectory (where Bunjevac identity was being absorbed into Croatian) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Suhovare.title: Suhovare
places/Suhovare.content:
Suhovare
Village under Islam pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Sukosan.title: Sukosan
places/Sukosan.content:
Sukošan
Coastal village south of Zadar in Smiljanić sub-region (docs 19, 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Zemunik pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga (S. Bartolomeo).

places/Suplja-Gornja.title: Suplja-Gornja
places/Suplja-Gornja.content:
Šuplja Gornja / Šuplja Crkva
Ruined church near Krka, on road to Knin (doc 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Ostrovica pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.

places/Surozani.title: Surozani
places/Surozani.content:
Surožani
Village in nahija Zrmanja / Ostrovica. 1528: 7 non-Muslim houses (with Bliznjani and Dubnić). 1540: 12 non-Muslim + 2 Muslim (including Hasan-Prejic-b????-Surozani, with Novica) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Sustipan.title: Sustipan
places/Sustipan.content:
Sustipan
Abbey outside Split assigned as temporary refuge to Rama Franciscans (doc 184) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Sv-Filip-i-Jakov.title: Sv-Filip-i-Jakov
places/Sv-Filip-i-Jakov.content:
Sv. Filip i Jakov
Village in Bortulačić’s sub-region (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Zaravecchia pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Krčina, Toretta, Pakoštane).
Cross-reference
Distinct from Sv-Jakov (existing wiki page).

places/Sv-Ilija-Zadar.title: Sv-Ilija-Zadar
places/Sv-Ilija-Zadar.content:
Sv. Ilija (Zadar)
Greek-rite (Orthodox) church in Zadar. Burial place of Magdalena Janković (d. 13 May 1684), daughter of Stojan Janković (doc 3) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Center of the Croatian/Albanian (Vlach/Serb) cavalry confraternity disputed in Valier’s ruling 12 Feb 1685 (doc 47). Significant institutional marker of Janković/Mitrović family Orthodox identity. The text says “sepolta nella chiesa di sant’ Elia” while the source archive heading is “Parohijski arh. crkve Sv. Stošije” — the Greek-rite chapel was administratively under St. Anastasia’s jurisdiction but physically Sv. Ilija.

places/Sv-Jakov.title: Sv-Jakov
places/Sv-Jakov.content:
Sveti Jakov
Parish settlement coincident with Krmpote-Senj in the Senjska Draga area; central locus of the Krmpote Habsburg-side colony Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Sv-Juraj-Senj.title: Sv-Juraj-Senj
places/Sv-Juraj-Senj.content:
Sv. Juraj (kraj Senja)
Village near Senj, refuge for Bukovčani during the Candian war Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Later Bukovčani moved on to Stinica.

places/Sv-Mihovil.title: Sv-Mihovil
places/Sv-Mihovil.content:
Sveti Mihovil
Lika–Senj area locality. 1691 — among the estates granted to the Rukavina family during the Bunjevac colonization of Lika, with Sv-Rok, Vratnik, Ricice, Kosinj (Fras 1835) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Sv-Rok.title: Sv-Rok
places/Sv-Rok.content:
Sveti Rok
Lika locality. 1691 grant location for the Rukavina family (with Sv-Mihovil, Vratnik, Ricice, Kosinj) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Sv-Sime-Zadar.title: Sv-Sime-Zadar
places/Sv-Sime-Zadar.content:
Sv. Šime (Zadar)
Latin-rite church in Zadar. Burial place of Antonia, wife of Stojan Janković (d. 29 January 1687, age c. 30) (doc 166) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Lent its name to the S. Simeone contrada in Zadar.

places/Sv-Stosija-Zadar.title: Sv-Stosija-Zadar
places/Sv-Stosija-Zadar.content:
Sv. Stošija (Zadar)
Cathedral of Zadar (St. Anastasia). The Greek-rite Sv. Ilija chapel was administratively under Sv. Stošija’s parish archive (“Parohijski arh. crkve Sv. Stošije”), even though Magdalena Janković’s 1684 burial was physically at Sv. Ilija (doc 3) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Tepsincich.title: Tepsincich
places/Tepsincich.content:
Tepsincich
Locality mentioned in Desnica II; precise modern identification uncertain Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Tinj.title: Tinj
places/Tinj.content:
Tinj
Town. Conquered by Ottomans in Cyprus-War-1570-1573; uvakufio 1574 by Ferhat-beg-Sokolovic-b???? as the čiftluk Tinj (six villages including Lišane, Sikovo, Raštane, Gorica, Prkos) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. After 1585 settled with western-Hercegovinian Vojnić Vlachs (“Bunjevci”). 1636 Catholic župa under don Stipan-Soric-b????-Gorica. Region also known as “Županovići” after Zupanovic starešina family.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
“Castello di Thin” (docs 19, 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Vrana pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.

places/Topolje.title: Topolje
places/Topolje.content:
Topolje
Torre near Knin held by Mihail Sinobad before Zvonigrad appointment Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Toreta.title: Toreta
places/Toreta.content:
Toreta
Village in Bortulačić’s sub-region (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Zaravecchia pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.

places/Tornik.title: Tornik
places/Tornik.content:
Tornik
Village in Podgorje / present-day Zaton Obrovački. 1528: 22 non-Muslim houses, includes Borić Gladanović. Home to the sons of Firultić (later Frletic): Pavko-Firultic-b????-Tornik, Vojo-Firultic-b????-Tornik, Juraj-Firultic-b????-Tornik, Milovan-Firultic-b????-Tornik Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Travnik.title: Travnik
places/Travnik.content:
Travnik
Seat of the Bosnian valija Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 343, 346). Halil-paša wrote from there.

places/Trebinje.title: Trebinje
places/Trebinje.content:
Trebinje
Hercegovinian town Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Lands of Aga Mustibeg Ćerinagić assigned to Demetrio Pivljanin (Padglivie / Podglibje, in Trebigne) 1696. Prešević family lands 15+15 fields.

places/Tribanj.title: Tribanj
places/Tribanj.content:
Tribanj / Šibuljina
Krajnje dalmatinsko selo na Morlačkom kanalu prema Hrvatskom primorju Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 41 footnote 1). Šibuljina je zaselak. 131 souls newly settled (doc 41). 1702 Morlach families settled but ordered to disperse to Ražance/Starigrad; 25 families re-petitioned to resettle 1704 (docs 337, 354). 2 miles from Starigrad; encroachment dispute with Karlobag people. Decima collected from inhabitants (doc 355).

places/Trogir.title: Trogir
places/Trogir.content:
Trogir (Traù)
Venetian port and territory (docs 9, 16, 18, 51, 56, 59, 61) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Cetina Morlak migration March 1685: Ilija Peraica brought 600 armed men + families + 30,000 small animals + 10,000 cattle to Trogir territory. Castelli di Trau attacked by Turks 7 April 1685 (docs 56, 62) — defeated by 3000 castellani + Morlachs.

places/Tromedja.title: Tromedja
places/Tromedja.content:
Tromeđa / Triplex Confinium
The “tripoint” between Ottoman, Venetian, and Habsburg territories on the Eastern Adriatic. The legal-geopolitical Triplex Confinium was defined only by the 1699 Karlowitz peace, but a de facto tripartite borderland already formed in the 1520s in the contact zone of Novigradsko more, Karinsko more, and the Velebit channel — Šarić’s “original Tromeđa” Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Bounded approximately by Zadar, Knin, Senj. Tightly linked to the imagological region Morlakija.

places/Trst.title: Trst
places/Trst.content:
Trst (Trieste)
