Habsburg Adriatic port. Captain in 1523: Nikola-Rauber-b???? (administered eastern Rašpor villages including Jelovica and Vodice after their 1523 transfer to Habsburg control) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Tudoricevci.title: Tudoricevci
places/Tudoricevci.content:
Tudoričevci
Medieval vlach katun on the Dečansko vlastelinstvo (today’s Metohija). Recorded in the 1330 Dečanska povelja of Stefan Uroš III (hrisovulja for manastir Dečani). 29 ognjišta; the Bunovići were one of five major (proširene/zadružne) families in it — descendants of Bun-praotac-b????-Tudoricevci Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Ivanović 1951–52).
Summer pastures on Visitor near Dobra Rijeka and Andrijevica; winter “altinska zemlja” near Dečani. Onomastic relic: Bunova livada / Livadhi i Bon’s in selo Shaptej near Dečani (Gashi 1982).

places/Udbina.title: Udbina
places/Udbina.content:
Udbina
Lika–Krbava centre, capital of the kapetanija Udbina. Critical for Kotarska genealogy: the original home of the Smiljanić clan (per Desnica’s footnote on doc. 20: “Smiljanići poreklom iz Udbine, a ne kako se priča i veruje, iz Smiljana u Lici”).
The 1647 attestation reading “Pietro Smiglianich da Vavina” is a copyist’s error for Undina = Udbina.
Surnames originating in Udbina

Smiljanić — Petar (d. 1648), Ilija (d. 1654), Filip (d. 1656), Smoljan, Lazaro.

Other Desnica attestations

1648-06-21 — Sorić, Smiljanić, Mitrović raid Udbina, burning Mazin valley + Rudopolje sub-villages (doc. 32).
1648-08-19 — capitan d’ Udvina a senior Turkish military rank (alai-bei) of Udbina; one such captured at Otres (doc. 34); subsequently killed by an embittered harambaša whose brother had been killed (doc. 34).
1654 (Sept) — Stojan Janković and Ilija Smiljanić raid the village Ondič near Udbina (doc. 86) — Ilija is killed on retreat at Vučjak.

People

Petar Smiljanić
Ilija Smiljanić
Filip Smiljanić

places/Ulcinj.title: Ulcinj
places/Ulcinj.content:
Ulcinj
Adriatic port; origin of “Fuste Dalcignotte” pirates threatening the Adriatic (doc 373) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Dolfin at Ulcinj while Selman pasha raided Mokro Polje (~1696).

places/Uskoplje-Hercegovina.title: Uskoplje-Hercegovina
places/Uskoplje-Hercegovina.content:
Uskoplje (Hercegovina)
Area whence prete Zorzi led 26 families + 50 armed men to Venetian land Nov 1687 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 183). Explains Orthodox enclaves at Dicmo, Biletić, Broćanac in Cetina region. Distinct from Macedonian Skopje and Bosnian Skoplje. Linked to existing Vlasi-Uskoplja surname.

places/Vaganac.title: Vaganac
places/Vaganac.content:
Vaganac
Lika locality where porkulab Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik held part of his 168 štrikova zemlje per the 1712 popis Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Distinct from the Vaganac in Ogulinska regimenta (Ogulin parish), which had Rukavina settlers (1712 popis).

places/Vakuf.title: Vakuf
places/Vakuf.content:
Kulen Vakuf
Ottoman town captured during the Morean War; Saviša wounded there Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 344, 358). Vakup superior + 300 houses burned by Zaviša at Skopje area; Resep Bairamović from Vakup. See also Varcar-Vakuf (Mrkonjić-Grad).

places/Valtura.title: Valtura
places/Valtura.content:
Valtura
Village near Pula in southern Istria. Settled in 1647 by a Vojnić group under knez Filip-Zupanovic-b????-Tinj during the Candian War — separating the Vojnići from the Tinj/Županovići area as Ottoman territory Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Sister settlement to Premantura and Marcana in the broader 16th–17th-c. Vlach colonization of S. Istria.

places/Varcar-Vakuf.title: Varcar-Vakuf
places/Varcar-Vakuf.content:
Varcar Vakuf (Mrkonjić-Grad)
Large town near Banja-Luka; raided Sep 1687, Zaviša wounded (doc 179) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Bošnjak Janković Migration: 4000 Morlachs penetrated 6 days into Bosnia.

places/Velebit.title: Velebit
places/Velebit.content:
Velebit
Mountain range separating Lika from the Adriatic coast and Podgorje. Site of major yaylak summer pastures (Veliko/Malo Rujno, Oglavinovac, Javornik, Štirovac, Bunjevac, Sveto Brdo, Veliki/Mali Golić, Libinje, Male/Duboke jasle) used by Vlasi-Istre and other transhumant Vlachs Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Timber from these slopes was used for the Ottoman Obrovac fleet 1530.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
“Morlacca / Velebich” — Vinjerac villagers guarded passes here in last war Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 173).

places/Velika-Kladusa.title: Velika-Kladusa
places/Velika-Kladusa.content:
Velika Kladuša
Lika/Bosanska Krajina fortress Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. With Mala Kladuša mentioned together.

places/Veliki-Zitnik.title: Veliki-Zitnik
places/Veliki-Zitnik.content:
Veliki Žitnik
Sub-locality of Pazariste in Lika. Family seat of the Bunjevac Starcevic lineage from 1690. Birthplace of Ante-Starcevic-b1823-Veliki-Zitnik (1823–1896), founder of the Hrvatska stranka prava Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Velim.title: Velim
places/Velim.content:
Velim
Village; 500 picked men from Šibenik / Skradin / Velim raided Bilaj December 1687 (doc 184) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Veljani.title: Veljani
places/Veljani.content:
Veljani
Village under Islam pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Radovan Radosav captain 1704.

places/Veseli-Vstak.title: Veseli-Vstak
places/Veseli-Vstak.content:
Veseli vštak
W. Hercegovina locality; 1477 winter pasture of the Krmpote katun (with Buhovo, Borajna, Ledinac) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Vienna.title: Vienna
places/Vienna.content:
Beč / Vienna
Capital of the Habsburg Monarchy. “Guerra sotto Vienna” (1683 siege) is the political backdrop for the entire 1684–1699 Morean War / Holy League conflict that frames Desnica II Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 36, 315). 1731 Lika border cordon difficulties — Imperial commander dependent on Vienna for resources.

places/Vilajet-Hrvati.title: Vilajet-Hrvati
places/Vilajet-Hrvati.content:
Vilajet Hrvati (Vilâyet-i Hirvat)
Provisional Ottoman military-administrative unit on the western frontier of Sandzak Bosna, covering ~12,000 km² from the lower Cetina to Lika and Krbava, including SW Bosnian karst polja and upper Pounje Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Created after Ottoman conquest 1522–1527; replaced 1537 by the Sandzak-Klis. First subaša/voivode: Murat-beg-Gajdic-b????-Sibenik, under Bosnian sanjakbeg Gazi-Husrev-beg. ~4,220 taxable households in 1530.

places/Vinjerac.title: Vinjerac
places/Vinjerac.content:
Vinjerac (Castel Venier)
Coastal village/castle on Novigrad more, Italian name Castel Venier from the patrician Venier family.
1647 — Krmpote re-settlement
Harambaša Harambasa-Njegovan-b????-Medvidja settled 40–50 Krmpote families in 1647 after their final exodus from Ottoman Medvidja (selo Krmpote in nahija Obrovac) during the Candian War — see Krmpote-Migration-Vinjerac-1647 Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Per Desnica (1647–84)

1656-03-04 — Janko Mitrović orders castel-Venier villagers to assemble at the Obrovac superiore pass-guard (doc. 101 footnote: “Stanovnici Krmpota u Bukovici, koji su 1648 uskočili u kraj između Posedarja i Vinjerca” — i.e. the Krmpoćani settled in the district between Posedarje and Vinjerac).
1663-02 — kapetan Ivan Čačić of castel-Venier killed Murat-aga Salihagić (Perušić disdar) and exhibited his head on Vinjerac walls (doc. 127).
1664-05-21 — Ivan Čačić named serdar (doc. 137).
1678 — Sv. Juraj uskoks contested for montagna lands with castel-Venier residents (docs. 239, 240).
1684-03-01 — Jovo (Giuco) Garguricić named capitano (doc. 381).
The kotari knez Tadić owned a malin near Vinjerac (the Malin del conte Tadijch of doc. 258).

People associated

Janko Mitrović (post-1647 partly stationed here)
Ivan Čačić — kapetan / serdar

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Village of 80 houses Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 173, 203). Grguričić captain, Knežević judge; 6 robbers of Zagreb Bishop included 2 from here. Stefano Knežević resident; under Posedarje pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga. Tadia Knežević captain 1700 (doc 321). Luka Njegovan brought 40–50 families from Krmpote-Senj to Vinjerac in last war (Cretan War era). Velebit (Morlacca / Velebich) — Vinjerac villagers guarded passes here in last war.

places/Visnjani.title: Visnjani
places/Visnjani.content:
Višnjani
Village near Skoplje (Uskoplje) raided same time as Skrobučani Nov 1687 (doc 182) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Vodice-na-Krasu.title: Vodice-na-Krasu
places/Vodice-na-Krasu.content:
Vodice na Krasu
Village in the Kras / Ćićarija. Refuge of Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik from 1518; site of his 1524 contact with Gazi-Husrev-beg and subsequent capture by Venetians Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Part of the Rašpor estate transferred to Habsburg control in 1523, administered by Nikola-Rauber-b???? from Trst.

places/Vojnici-Ljubuski.title: Vojnici-Ljubuski
places/Vojnici-Ljubuski.content:
Vojnići (Ljubuški)
Eponymous origin village of the Vlasi Vojnići, NW of Ljubuški in W. Hercegovina — the result of territorialization of the original 1477 katun (džemat of Vukasin-sin-Vojihne-b????-Mostar). Located ~35 km west of Buna Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Earlier attestation: 1408 charter of Bosnian king Stjepan Ostoja mentions Vlasi Vojihnići, subjects of the W. Hum noble line Radivojević-Vlatković (Dinić 1940).

places/Vran.title: Vran
places/Vran.content:
Vran
Mountain in W. Hercegovina / SW Bosnia; 1477 summer pasture of the Krmpote katun (with Cvrsnica and Ljubusa) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Vrana.title: Vrana
places/Vrana.content:
Vrana
Old Croatian district by Vransko jezero. After 1540 partly retained by Venice; 1549 settler Rade-Siljanovic-b???? led peasants here as zakup Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Old Catholic church Gospa od Karmela. Conquered by Ottomans during Cyprus-War-1570-1573 along with Tinj and Zemunik.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Major site (docs 8, 13, 16, 22, 34–36, 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Vrana — Morlak settlement and uprising (1683–1684): Vrana Morlachs expelled their Sanjak-beg (refusing to fight at Vienna), then sought Venetian protection; fra Grgur Šutić convinced them to seize Vrana and start war on Turks. Morpolača (torre de Morlacchi Palazzo) — tower 3 miles before Vrana (doc 51 footnote). Bortulačić governor; killed at Vrana 1692-01-16 by Biograđani and Pakoštanci. Spingaroli later sopraintendente. Pertinenza HQ from 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Banjci, Polača, two Jagodne, Vrčevo, Tinj, Lerage o Ceragne, Banjana, Pristeg, Radasinovac, Raštane, Gorizza). Bunjevac/Vrana petition for Smiljanić as capo and Radašinović as captain (Sept 1684, in Cyrillic — “idioma illirico”, “caratteri illirici”; docs 34–35). Bili Vučić, Francesco Mirčetić, Ilija Radašinović, Đure Đekić, Mattio Pop, Grgur Lepur, Radivoj Najerlović, Mattio Pančić, Mattio Bajčić, Parišić — all Vrana harambase/knezovi acting collectively 1684.

places/Vranjsko-Krajiste.title: Vranjsko-Krajiste
places/Vranjsko-Krajiste.content:
Vranjsko krajište
Eastern frontier krajište of the medieval Serbian state, in the upper Južna Morava drainage (Vranje, Inogošta, Preševo, Dubočnica, Znepolje). Disintegrated after the Battle of Rovine (1395). Home to the Vlasi Bunuševci in the 14th c. — one of the medieval Bun-stem Vlach groups Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Blagojević 1989).
The Bunuševci performed border-guard service to a krajiški vlastelin. Toponymic remnant: village Bunusa south of Leskovac, formed by territorialization of their katun.

places/Vratnik.title: Vratnik
places/Vratnik.content:
Vratnik
Senj hinterland locality. 1691 grant location for the Rukavina family Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Vrcevo.title: Vrcevo
places/Vrcevo.content:
Vrčevo
Village in Posedarski’s sub-region (doc 19); under Vrana pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga (also Nin pertinenza 1689 listing) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Vrgorac.title: Vrgorac
places/Vrgorac.content:
Vrgorac
Hercegovinian-frontier fortress (doc 7) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. New settlers from Brochno/Blato/Goranci alloggiati here 1694 (5000 souls migration).

places/Vrlika.title: Vrlika
places/Vrlika.content:
Vrlika
Cetina-area fortress (doc 7) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Surrendered Sep 1688 to Fenzi without a shot; commands “fertile vastissime campagne” (docs 214, 216, 220). Bože Cerniza placed garrison there. 1697 Crnice brothers from there. 1700 governator Franćeski. 1729 Stojisavljević family origin (Vučen Stojisavljević married Marija Mitrović).

places/Vrpolje.title: Vrpolje
places/Vrpolje.content:
Vrpolje
Village in the Šibenik / Krka area, mentioned in Desnica II Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Vucjak.title: Vucjak
places/Vucjak.content:
Vučjak
Mountain pass on the Lika–Dalmatia border, on the route between Krupa and Gračac (per Desnica’s footnote on doc. 86). Site of the death of Ilija Smiljanić (8 September 1654, return from raid on Ondič near Udbina, ambushed by Turks waiting in the boscage).

places/Vuksic.title: Vuksic
places/Vuksic.content:
Vukšić
Village in Kozulova-Polje vakuf. Old Catholic churches Sv. Mihovil and Sv. Kata; the village is mentioned in connection with the Sv. Mihovil fair whose revenues went to the vakuf Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
“Ussich” — castle 4 miles south of Vrana (doc 51 footnote 2 identifies as Vukšić) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Ostrovica pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.

places/Zacadje.title: Zacadje
places/Zacadje.content:
Začađe
Village in nahija Zrmanja, exact location not identified. 1528–1530: 2 non-Muslim houses + 2 baštine; residence and dzemat seat of Jakov-Poropat-b????-Zacadje Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1540: 6 non-Muslim houses, including Ivan sin Prejića.

places/Zadar.title: Zadar
places/Zadar.content:
Zadar
Major Venetian Adriatic port and seat of the Zadar contado. Reception zone for Vlasi-Istre migrations 1538 and 1540 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Documented Venetian rectors include Vittorio-Barbadico-b????-Venice (1528), Antonio-de-Mula-b????-Venice (1540), Antonio-Michielo-b????-Venice (1557). Hub of notarial records, Senate correspondence, and franjevački pastoral activity.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Administrative center throughout Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Base of Mocenigo, Pasqualigo, Valier as provveditori generali. Parishes: Sv. Stošija cathedral; Greek-rite Sv. Ilija church (Magdalena Janković burial 13 May 1684 — doc 3; Croatian/Albanian-Vlach cavalry confraternity dispute 12 Feb 1685 — doc 47); Latin-rite Sv. Šime (Antonia Janković burial 29 Jan 1687 — doc 166). Site of Janković regiment recruitment 1686 (300+ oltramarini sent to Venice). Kotari Pertinenze Reform 11 March 1689 (doc 224) divided Zadar territory into 9 administrative pertinenze (Nin, Posedarje, Islam, Novigrad, Nadin, Zemunik, Vrana, Ostrovica, Zaravecchia). 1689 census: 16,273 souls; 4,470 fit for arms (893 cavalry); 28 working mills.

places/Zadvarje.title: Zadvarje
places/Zadvarje.content:
Zadvarje (Duare)
Cetina-valley fortress (docs 1, 40, 55, 60) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Cavalry sent here April 1687 (docs 169, 172). New settlers from Brochno/Blato/Goranci alloggiati 1694 (5000 souls).

places/Zagreb.title: Zagreb
places/Zagreb.content:
Zagreb
Habsburg Croatian center Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Bishop of Zagreb robbery May 1688: 6 Kotarci + 2 from Vinjerac ambushed Bishop returning from Rijeka, took money + 3 horses, killed 1 of his retinue (doc 203). Karlović died at nearby Medvedgrad 1531.

places/Zaostrog.title: Zaostrog
places/Zaostrog.content:
Zaostrog
Coastal village on the Makarska Riviera, mentioned in Hercegovina relazione 1684 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Zaravecchia.title: Zaravecchia
places/Zaravecchia.content:
Biograd na Moru (Zaravecchia)
Venetian commune on the coast south of Zadar Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Pertinenza HQ from 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Krčina, Toretta, Sv. Filip i Jakov, Pakoštane). Mattio Žabetić captain; site of 1704 unrest. Commune that with Pakoštane plotted Šimun Bortulačić’s murder 1692; pardoned 1694. Distinct from Stari Grad also called Zara Vecchia in some texts.

places/Zaton.title: Zaton
places/Zaton.content:
Zaton (kraj Nina)
Village in Posedarski’s sub-region (doc 19); under Nin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Zavojane.title: Zavojane
places/Zavojane.content:
Zavojane
Village in Mostar/Zaupa province, Catholic, with church of Madonna; given to Rašić 1692 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (200 souls / 25 families settled at Zavojane, Stigli, Hadži Lukovo).

places/Zbandalj.title: Zbandalj
places/Zbandalj.content:
Žbandalj
Village near Porec settled 1570 by 40 families led by Ivan-Filipini-b????, including Grgur-Milohanovic-b????-Nova-Vas returning from Miljacki (Zemunik Gornji) after Ottoman conquest Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Zecevo.title: Zecevo
places/Zecevo.content:
Zečevo
Two distinct historical claims:
16th c. — Vlach nahija
Ottoman Vlach nahija (50 houses, 11 villages) in 1528–1530, headed by primićur Mikula-Blazic-b????-Zecevo Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Dissolved by 1540, lands absorbed into Kozulova-Polje vakuf and Ostrovica nahija.
17th c. — Battle ground (Desnica)
Site of two pivotal battles in the Candian War:
Battle of Zečevo I (1 August 1648)
Vuk Mandušić killed defending the small castle of Zečevo against an Ottoman raid that had pillaged Zaravecchia. Vuk taken alive after killing four Turks himself, kept alive a few hours, beheaded; Ilija Smiljanić helped bury his torso. 50 Turks dead, ~20 of naših including Vuk, harambaše Ščandić, kapetan Pero Aričić, harambaša Ilija Cverljević, harambaša Zuanne Kraljević, both Galiotović brothers, one captured. Documented by ~5 forensic depositions (docs. 42–46).
Battle of Zečevo II (1 May 1666)
Filipjakov glagolska zabeleška (doc. 151): “Taj isti dan poginuše Kotarani na Zečevu i tote poginu ljudi niko od 73 čovika među kojima poginu dobri junak Vučko Močivuna. Iz samoga Filipjakova poginu ljudi 16. Pisa ja Nikola Kužinović budući žalan i vele žalostan za našom lipom braćom bog im dušu pomilova.” — 73 Kotarani killed including Vuk Močivuna; o. Filip Kučić (sepolto al duomo) also fell — Cornaro’s report doc. 153.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Castle with advance guards near Skradin (doc 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Defensive position in Bukovica May 1688. Under Ostrovica pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.

places/Zegar.title: Zegar
places/Zegar.content:
Žegar (na Zrmanji)
Village in nahija Zrmanja (Bukovica). 1528: 7 non-Muslim houses Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Later concentration of Orthodox Vlach population (1636 Forza report).
Source-village of major uskakanja (per Desnica)

The Mitrović clan (Janko, Giovanni, Stefan, Pavle, Andrija) — five brothers — uskočili with ~70 households / ~150 fighters into Venetian Ravni Kotari c. 1647 (Stojan’s 1670 supplica, doc. 170). Janko becomes the first serdar de Morlacchi (1656).
Vukadin Mitrović also from Žegar (doc. 51, 1650 — d. defending Novigrad 1653).
Žegarani Morlaci (200 pješaka) — settled below Nin after Ribnik 1648 (doc. 39, harambaša Mileta Vukčević).
70 Žegarski porodice — brought by Sorić’s 1648-06 raid on Udbina, settled at Islam and Žemunik (doc. 32).

1683 retaliations

1683-12-07 Senjski raid + 400 Kotarci led by Bajo Pivljanin and Ilija Mitrović plundered Morlachi di Segar — 700 cavalli/manzi, 1 Senjanin and 5 Žegarci killed (docs. 345, 348) — the raid attacked the very village from which the Mitrovići had originated 36 years earlier.

People associated

Janko Mitrović
Vukadin Mitrović
Stojan Janković
Zaviša Janković
Ilija Mitrović

places/Zejane.title: Zejane
places/Zejane.content:
Žejane
Village on Cicarija. One of the last remaining communities of the Istro-Romanian / “istrorumunjski” idiom into the modern era — last relict of the bilingual Slavic-Romance Vlach speech of the Vlasi-Istre Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Zelengrad.title: Zelengrad
places/Zelengrad.content:
Zelengrad
Pre-Ottoman fortress in Zadar district. Petar-Milovanic-b????-Medvidja is attested 1518 in a Zadar deed as catonarius districtus Zelengradi — the earliest dated record for the Milovanić Vlach lineage Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Under Novigrad pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Bukovica villages Krmpote-Bukovica and Parčić near here.

places/Zemunik.title: Zemunik
places/Zemunik.content:
Zemunik
Town in Zadar contado. Lost to Ottomans in Cyprus-War-1570-1573; subsequently uvakufio for Ferhat-beg-Sokolovic-b???? vakuf (Zemunik mosque + mekteb) and Hrvace Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Selo Miljacki (Zemunik Gornji) was founded 1561 by returnee Grgur-Milohanovic-b????-Nova-Vas.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Pertinenza HQ from 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Gruhe, Malpaga,  S. Bartolomeo, Bibinje, Cerno, Kristagna, Bokanjac, Kozino, Gunpuri, Porto Schiavina) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 51, 56). Hassan Durakbegović killed there earlier. Assembly point for cavalry. Captain Marlatić (Bibinje, doc 316).

places/Zrmanja.title: Zrmanja
places/Zrmanja.content:
Zrmanja
River and surrounding region between Velebit and Bukovica. Ottoman nahija under the Vlasi Istre (131 houses, 22 villages, 1528–1530), led by primićuri Jakov-Poropat-b????-Zacadje and Slade-Livoja-b????-Zrmanja Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Maintained territorial integrity into 1550 register (as “Zrmanja Istrija”). Includes settlements Krupa, Zegar, Ervenik, Bilisani.

places/Zumberak.title: Zumberak
places/Zumberak.content:
Žumberak
Habsburg-side mountain region; major reception zone for “uskok” refugees from Ottoman territory in the 1530s and after, via Bihac Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Associated with vojvoda Vuk-Popovic-b????.

places/Zvonigrad.title: Zvonigrad
places/Zvonigrad.content:
Zvonigrad
Fortress on the Zrmanja in Zadar contado Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 304, 315, 316, 318, 321). Mehmed aga as disdar pre-conquest. Devastated by Venetian arms; Jovan Sinobad governor 1690; Filip Sinobad 1691; Mihail Sinobad 1694 (d. 1697).

sources/Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.title: Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
sources/Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.content:
Boško Desnica, Istorija kotarskih uskoka 1646–1684, sveska I (1950)
Citation
Desnica, Boško. Istorija kotarskih uskoka 1646—1684. Sveska I. Srpska akademija nauka, Zbornik za istoriju, jezik i književnost srpskog naroda, treće odeljenje, knjiga XIII (Historia Uscoccorum Cotarensium 1646—1684, Fasciculus I). Beograd: Izdavačko preduzeće Narodne Republike Srbije, 1950. Edited by Svetozar Brkić. 359 pp.
Compiler: Dr. Boško Desnica of Obrovac (1886–1945) — Serbian Dalmatian historian, last bearer of the Janković-Mitrović line through his maternal lineage; the family archive in Obrovac is one of the source-fonds for this volume.
Period covered
1646 — 1 May 1684. From Foscolo’s correspondence at the start of the Candian War (rat 1645–1669) through the post-Karlovački-mir interbellum to the outbreak of Vrana uprising and the eve of the Morean War.
Form, language, transmission

Form: primary archival anthology — 399 numbered documents transcribed (per Desnica’s preface, intentionally) “tačno onako kako stoje u originalu, bez ikakvih bilo gramatičkih bilo ortografskih ispravaka ili izmena.”
Languages: Italian (most provveditorial dispatches and terminacije), Latin (ducali), Croatian/Serbian (a minority of letters from Krajiški Turci and Morlachi, both in bosanska ćirilica and latinica), Turkish-via-translation (a few sandžak letters in Italian translation; one Bosnian-Cyrillic original from Mehmed-beg Atlagić).
Document types: dispatches of the provveditore generale to the Senate; terminacije (decrees) granting pay/land; patenti and dukali; lettere of the conti of Nin, Šibenik, Trogir, Split, Klis, Novigrad; notarial instrumenti (Šibenik, Zadar); parish registers (Sv. Stošija and Sv. Ilija in Zadar, Sv. Zulijan in Šibenik, Filipjakov, Novigrad, Ražanac, Posedarje); inquisitions/preslušavanja of harambaše and confidenti; letters from Krajiški Turci (Atlagić, Filipović, Durakbegović, Mehmed-aga); reports of confidenti spying in the Ottoman zaleđe.

Archival fonds drawn upon

Mletački državni arhiv (Venice State Archive): Senato — Dispacci provveditore generale in Dalmazia, filze 50–111 (the spine of the volume — almost every dispatch is appended with multiple in-document originals).
Zadarski stari arhiv (Zadar State Archive): Spisi of provveditori Foscolo, Foscarini, Dolfin, A. Zen, Bernardo, Cornaro (Andrea & Caterino), Contarini, Priuli, A. Barbaro, Morosini, Civran, Grimani, Valier, Cornaro G., Donato; the Arhiv mletačkog dragomana (filze for Turkish-language correspondence).
Šibenski bilježnički arhiv (held with the Šibenik Okružni Sud): notarial protocols of Bernardo Skoci and Petar Verancio.
Family archives:

Posedarski Zbornik in the Arhiv kneza Antona Benje-Posedarskog u Zadru (the Posedarski “zlatna knjiga”).
Šurićev zbornik in the family of P. Šurić in Split.
Smiljanić zbornik (“Summario di ducali, pubbliche fedi ed attestazioni meritate dall’antica, benemerita famiglia Smiglanich”, 1786) in the Bihać society in Split.
Janković-Mitrović archive (“Trassunto delle benemerenze della famiglia Mitrovich”) in the possession of B. Desnica, Obrovac — including original terminacije on parchment.


Parish/church archives: Sv. Stošija (cathedral) Zadar, Sv. Ilija (Greek-rite Orthodox) Zadar, Sv. Zulijan (Greek-rite) Šibenik, parohijska crkva u Filipjakovu (with Kašićev Ritual), and minor records of Novigrad, Ražanac, Posedarje.
Library archives: Zadarska gradska biblioteka Paravia, Biblioteka Papafava (Zadar), Biblioteka kninskog muzeja (for the Kašićev Ritual with the glagolska zabeleška about Močivuna).

Reliability and biases

Primary: original Venetian administrative correspondence; near-real-time dispatches generally written within hours/days of events.
Strengths:

Provides exact dates of births/marriages/deaths for the central families (Janković, Smiljanić, Sorić, Mandušić, Šarić, Močivuna, Pivljanin, Posedarski) via parish-register transcriptions otherwise lost or hard to access.
Preserves 14 mass-rosters of harambaše with village of origin → settlement village, the single richest documentary base for late-17th-c. uskočka migration mapping in Ravni Kotari and Bukovica.
Includes the cardinal genealogical correction in doc. 20 (footnote): “Smiljanići poreklom iz Udbine, a ne kako se priča i veruje, iz Smiljana u Lici.”


Biases:

Venetian-administrative perspective. The Morlachi are described from above, by their Venetian patrons; their own voices appear chiefly in mediated costituti (interrogations).
Numbers (Turkish casualties, captured animals) are partisan and often inflated by the harambaše who depose them — Desnica frequently flags this in footnotes.
Desnica’s own footnotes are interpretive (e.g., on the Smiljanić origin, on the Pivljanin–Janković kinship, on toponym identifications). Treat the document body as primary; treat Desnica’s footnotes as carefully-argued secondary commentary.
Place-name identifications in footnotes are usually solid; a few (“Notina”/Popina, “Vavina”/Udbina) are explicit conjectural emendations.


Reliability: high for the bare facts (names, dates, places, kin-links, attestations); medium-high for numerical claims; high for the chains of kinship Desnica reconstructs in his footnotes (he had access to family archives no longer in private hands).

Key facts extracted (summary)

Persons added or substantially expanded: ~140 (major Janković-Mitrović and Smiljanić clusters, harambaše of every named uskočka grupa, Venetian provveditori 1646–84, key Krajiški Turci).
Surnames added or expanded: ~150, with place-attestation for every single-mention bearer.
Places added or updated: ~80 — the full geography of Ravni Kotari, Bukovica, Lika–Krbava perimeter, Šibenski zaleđe, Bosanska Krajina edge cities (Knin, Drniš, Banja Luka, Livno, Glamoč, Sinj).
Events documented: Battle of Ribnik (Jul 1648), Battle of Zečevo I (Aug 1648), Battle of Zečevo II (May 1666), Conquest of Klis (1648), Cetina rotta (Apr 1666), Bribir ambush (Dec 1668), Vrana uprising (Oct 1683 – May 1684), Grusi krajiški statut (5 Aug 1654).
Critical genealogical corrections: Smiljanići from Udbina, not Smiljan.

sources/Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.title: Istorija kotarskih uskoka 1684–1749, sveska II
sources/Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.content:
Boško Desnica, Istorija kotarskih uskoka 1684–1749, sveska II (1951)
Citation
Desnica, Boško. Istorija kotarskih uskoka 1684—1749. Sveska II. Srpska akademija nauka, Zbornik za istoriju, jezik i književnost srpskog naroda, treće odeljenje, knjiga XIII (Historia Uscoccorum Cotarensium 1684—1749, Fasciculus II). Beograd: Izdavačko preduzeće Narodne Republike Srbije, 1951. Redigovao Svetozar Brkić.
Companion to Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I (1646–1684); together the two volumes form the canonical primary-source base for ravnokotarska genealogy 1646–1749.
Period covered
6 May 1684 — 9 April 1749 (65 years). Document density is heaviest in 1684–1700 (Morean War years); the long 1700–1749 tail covers administrative aftermath, the 1704 Bukovica revolt, the War of Spanish Succession redeployments, and final Venetian-Habsburg border arrangements.
Form, language, transmission

Form: 392 numbered documents transcribed in the same fidelity policy as Sveska I — original orthography preserved.
Languages: Italian (overwhelming majority), Latin (dukali), Croatian/Serbian (a few letters from Morlach harambaše and Bosnian agas, both ćirilica and latinica), one Bosnian-Cyrillic letter from vojvoda Ivan Marušić (in captivity, doc 110).
Document types: dispatches of the provveditore generale to the Senate (Mocenigo, Valier, Cornaro, Molin, Dolfin, Mocenigo II, Vendramin, Riva, Zane, Diedo); terminacije; patenti and dukali; ducali of doges Marc’Antonio Giustinian, Silvestro Valier, Alvise Mocenigo II; reports of inquisitori di stato; parish registers (Sv. Ilija and Sv. Šime in Zadar); inquisitions/preslušavanja; letters from Atlagić, Filipović, Mandić, Pašić; family attestations from the Janković-Mitrović archive.

Archival fonds drawn upon

Mletački državni arhiv (Venice State Archive): Senato — Provveditor general dell’ armi (in Dalmazia), filze 112/521 onwards through ~155, the spine of the volume; also Inquisitori di Stato, busta 47 and busta supplicahe.
Zadarski stari arhiv (Zadar State Archive): Spisi of provveditori Mocenigo, Valier, Cornaro, Molin, Dolfin (multiple), Mocenigo II, Vendramin, Riva, Zane, Diedo, Erizzo.
Family archives:

Janković-Mitrović archive (“Trassunto delle benemerenze della famiglia Mitrovich”) in the possession of B. Desnica, Obrovac.
Posedarski Zbornik in the Arhiv kneza Antona Benje-Posedarskog u Zadru.
Smiljanić zbornik (“Summario di ducali…”, 1786) in the Bihać society in Split.


Parish/church archives: Sv. Ilija (Greek-rite) Zadar; Sv. Šime Zadar; matica umrlih of pravoslavna crkva Sv. Ilije in Zadar (used for Janković-family deaths and for pop Petar Jagodić’s death notice 9 April 1749).

Reliability and biases

Primary: original Venetian administrative correspondence; near-real-time dispatches.
Strengths:

The single densest source for the Janković-Mitrović family in its prime: Stojan’s regiment authorisation (7 Nov 1686), his death at Duvno (Aug 1687), the deaths of his wife Antonia (Jan 1687) and four of his children, his sons Nikola and Konstantin, the long aftermath through brother Zaviša and nephew Filip Mitrović.
Comprehensive lists of new Morlach migrations: 152 families/2,300 souls from Lika (1684); 70 families/900 souls (May 1685); 316 families/2,561 souls (June 1685); aggregate 3,051 families / 10,290 fighters (1685 census, doc 107); 5,000 souls from Bjelaj region (March 1692, doc with serdari Đurić, Pirić, Zorić); 5,000 souls from Brochno-Blato-Goranci (1693–94, settled at Zadvarje and Vrgorac); 26 families with Orthodox priest Đurađ from Skoplje/Vakup (Nov 1687); 15 Franciscan friars + 500 family members from Rama (Oct 1687, settled Sustipan).
The Kotari Pertinenze reform of 11 March 1689 (doc 224) — Cornaro’s ordinance dividing the Zadar contado into 9 administrative units, with named governors, judges, descrizione rules, militia rolls.
The Knin conquest of 29 August – 11 September 1688 (docs 213–220) in unprecedented detail.
Hundreds of single-mention surnames with place attestation, for example: Žepina (Plavno, doc 2), Brkljača/Bistrić/Boljač (Radovin/Vinjerac, doc 31), Avramović (doc 49), Vojkorsić (Čitluk, doc 54), Lakić (Karin, doc 56), Sinovčić (Novigrad, doc 32), Kosić (Starigrad, doc 92), Sudarović (Parčići in Lika → Žegar, doc 114), Tepšić, Gagić (Biljane, doc 124), Cona, Cvitanović, Tintor, Goreta, Palikuća, Žinović (Šibenik-Skradin capi, doc 155), Salomonić, Iljanović, etc.


Biases:

Venetian-administrative perspective dominates; Morlach voices appear in mediated petitions and depositions.
Numerical claims (Turkish casualties, captured animals) are partisan; Desnica flags inflations in footnotes.
The Iljanović letter (doc 139, 30 July 1686) purporting to derive Stojan Janković from Hercegovinian dukes was flagged by State Inquisitors as a Ragusan intrigue (docs 147, 154); record but treat as low-confidence.
The Lapac complaint (doc 126, 1 Feb 1686) anonymous accusation against Stojan Janković and Šimun Bortulačić of extortion and unlawful killings — record but no resolution in source.
Desnica’s footnotes are interpretive secondary commentary; treat document bodies as primary.


Reliability: high for names/dates/places/kin-links; medium-high for numerical claims; high for cross-references to family archives no longer privately held.

Key facts extracted (summary)

Persons added or substantially expanded: ~400 (the full Janković-Mitrović family in its 1684–1749 prime, the four Kotari capi, all named Venetian provveditori and inquisitori, named Ottoman beys/agas at Knin/Sinj/Livno/Bihać, every harambaša named in deposition or migration roster, every named bearer in the 1689 pertinenze reform).
Surnames added or expanded: ~220, including all single-mention bearers with place attestation (per user’s directive: capture every surname).
Places added or updated: ~80 — the wider geography extends north into Lika–Krbava (Lapac, Boričevac, Ripač, Bjelaj, Vakuf, Srb, Komić), east into Bosanska Krajina (Livno, Glamoč, Grahovo, Banja Luka, Kupres), into Hercegovina (Mostar, Gabela, Stolac, Počitelj, Trebinje, Nevesinje, Gacko, Vrgorac), south to Kotor / Pastrovići / Budva / Cetinje, plus a tail of new pertinenze unit names (Pridraga, Polešnik, Bađun, Klošter, etc.).
Events documented: Sinj battle (Apr 1685), Bjelaj raid (Sep 1685), Cetina migration of Peraica’s people (Mar 1685), Zadvarje siege relief (June 1685), Vrana attempt (Oct 1684), 1685 Lika census, 1686 Sinj conquest, Stojan Janković’s death at Duvno (Aug 1687), Rama Franciscan migration (Oct 1687), Skoplje migration (Nov 1687), Pasha’s April 1688 Kotari raid, Knin conquest (Aug–Sep 1688), Vrlika capitulation (Sep 1688), Kotari Pertinenze reform (11 Mar 1689), Šimun Bortulačić’s murder at Vrana (16 Jan 1692), Bjelaj migration (March 1692), Brochno-Goranci migration (1693–94), Mitrović–Sinobad / Mitrović–Milković reconciliations (1692), Ilija Mitrović’s death (1693), 1704 Bukovica revolt under pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža.

Editorial note

Compiler: Dr. Boško Desnica of Obrovac (1886–1945) — see Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I for full biographical note. The volume was published posthumously six years after his death.
Redactor: Svetozar Brkić, asistent Univerziteta.
Manuscript accepted at the VI session of the SAN Odeljenje društvenih nauka, 24 September 1948; printed 1951 by Vuk Karadžić press, pogon Zadružna štamparija, Beograd.

sources/Saric-2008-Bunjevci.title: Bunjevci u ranome novom vijeku: Postanak i razvoj jedne predmoderne etnije
sources/Saric-2008-Bunjevci.content:
Šarić 2008 — Bunjevci u ranome novom vijeku
Summary
Synthesizing scholarly study of the Bunjevci as an early-modern (“predmoderna”) ethnic community: Catholic Vlach katuns from western Hercegovina (the 1477 katuns of Krmpote, Vojnići, Sladovići and others), colonized by Ottoman authorities into the vilajet Hrvati / Klis sandjak in the early 16th c. Their identity crystallized through the bunjevci ↔ rkaći dichotomy with Orthodox Vlachs around mid-16th c.
The article disentangles four branches that emerge by the 17th c. — western-Bosnian (Ottoman), Dalmatian (Venetian), Lika–Primorje (Habsburg), and Danubian/Bačka (Hungarian) — and traces their reversible cyclical migrations. It establishes that the Buna-river origin legend is a 17th-c. Bosnian-Franciscan legitimating construct, and argues the etymon is the Vlach anthroponym Bun/Bunj (< Latin Bonifacius via Balkan-Romance vocalism), with patronymic suffix -evac/-evci — a parallel formation to medieval Vlach groups Bunčići, Bunovići, Bunuševci.
Citation
Šarić, Marko. “Bunjevci u ranome novom vijeku: Postanak i razvoj jedne predmoderne etnije.” In Živjeti na Krivom Putu (zbornik radova). Zagreb, 2008, pp. 15–43.
Reliability and biases

Form: scholarly synthetic article; companion piece to Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre and same author’s master’s thesis (Šarić 2005, Dinarski Vlasi…).
Author: Marko-Saric-b????-Zagreb, FFZG, leading specialist on early-modern Dinaric Vlach studies.
Source type: secondary, but draws on a wide spread of primary registers (Ottoman defters 1477/1554/1561, Lika–Krbava 1712, Venetian commissiones, Bosnian Franciscan reports).
Strengths: explicitly anti-presentist methodology; rejects both Croat-only and Serb-only readings of Bunjevci as projections of modern nationality onto a pre-modern community. Comparative onomastic, lingusitic, and ethnographic argumentation.
Limitations for genealogy:

Earliest 16th-c. attestations are at the level of Vlach group names (Krmpote, Vojnići), not individual surnames.
Bunjevac surnames stabilize across the 17th c.; before that bearers appear under patronymic + village.
Article is interpretive — for individual genealogies, the underlying primary sources (Aličić 1985 defter; Kaser 2003 Lika 1712 census; Pavličević 1989 on Krmpote migrations) are authoritative.
The 1605 and 1627 Lič settlement family lists come via Pavličević (compiled from later 18th-c. records and inferred for 1627); treat as plausible but not register-direct.



Snapshot data points











































































YearSourceDatum1408Bosnian charterFirst mention of “Vlasi Vojihnići”1477Hercegovina defterVukić Krmpotić katun 11 houses; Vukašin sin Vojihne 10 houses; Milosav sin Sladića 19 houses1530Ottoman policySpecial Vlach status abolished → mass migrations1554/61Mohač/Baranja defter”Marton Bunavac” — earliest possible written form of “Bunjevac”1605LičFirst Krmpote migration (~24 named families)1622don Šimun MatkovićFirst explicit “parochia Bunievczi” (Kalocsa archdiocese)1627LičSecond Krmpote migration (~16 families incl. Starčević, Pavelić)1636Vicenzo Forzažupa Županovići: 6 villages, 1550 souls; župa Bukovica: 1180 souls1647Candian WarLast Krmpote migration (harambaša Njegovan → Vinjerac, Starigrad, Pag); Vojnići → Valtura (Pula)1690Lika colonizationBunjevac influx to Pazarište, Smiljan, Lovinac1699Karlovački mirMarsigli’s “Meerkroaten”1702Ribnička bunaMiloš Starčević vs. vojvoda Marko Butorac1712Lika–Krbava popis~158 Bunjevac surnames; 37 shared with Orthodox Vlachs
Key concepts introduced

bunjevci ↔ rkaći — confessional-onomastic dichotomy (Catholic vs. Orthodox Vlach), forming mid-16th c. on the Tromeđa.
etnokonfesionalizam — fusion of ethnic and confessional identity in 16th-c. Vlach society, driven by Pećka patrijaršija (renewed 1557) and post-Tridentine Catholic renewal.
Buna-river legend — first recorded by Fortis 1778 (Lika), Lanosović 1794 (Bačka). Šarić argues it is a Bosnian-Franciscan construct legitimating their pastoral jurisdiction over Dinaric Catholic Vlachs against Dalmatian dioceses.
Bun/Bunj anthroponym — Vlach personal name from Latin Bonifacius via Balkan-Romance vocalic shift o > u; cf. medieval Bunčići, Bunovići (Tudoričevci, Dečani), Bunuševci (Vranje), Bunislavići (1406 east Hum).
“krajinska etnija” — frontier-shaped ethnicity; Bunjevci formed in Ottoman serhad conditions and shaped by reversible cross-border migrations.
Meerkroaten / Catholische Walahen / Rasciani catholici — administrative names used by Habsburg/Hungarian authorities; “Bunjevac” itself rarely used in official records before mid-18th c.
Senjsko-modruška biskupija — first ecclesiastical institution to introduce “Bunjevac” into official usage (biskup Martin Brajković, 1702: catholici Valachi alias Bunievczi).

Notes for the wiki

This is the spine for Bunjevac genealogy and identity formation. Pair with Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre for the early-16th-c. Vlach context. Where they overlap (Krmpotić, Vojnić, Sorić, Matković origins), cite both.
The Buna-legend question is now settled (this article): file the legend under symbolic/etymological-cultural origin, not as a historical migration claim.
Cite as [[Saric-2008-Bunjevci]]. Where the article in turn cites a register or primary source, mention the register year + author in body prose, then attribute via this article.
For the 1605 / 1627 Lič settler-family lists, mark confidence: medium — these are reconstructions via Pavličević 1989, not direct register attestations.
The article’s footnote 44 lists ~70 Bunjevac surnames across 23 Lika/Otočac/Ogulin parishes from the 1712 popis — substantial source for breadth-first surname pages.

sources/Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.title: Osmanski Vlasi Istre na izvornoj Tromeđi: nestabilna podaništva i ambivalentne lojalnosti na imperijalnom višegraničju u Hrvatskoj 16. stoljeća
sources/Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.content:
Šarić 2024 — Osmanski Vlasi Istre na izvornoj Tromeđi
Summary
Scholarly analysis of the “Vlasi Istre” (Ottoman: Eflâkân-i Istryia; Venetian: Morlachi istriani) — a 16th-c. Vlach group that fled Croatian lands ahead of Ottoman conquest c. 1518–1523, settled in Habsburg NE Istria and Kras, then returned in 1528–1530 to the Klis Sanjak under Ottoman istimâlet (winning-over) policy. The article traces their reversible cyclical migrations across Ottoman, Venetian, and Habsburg territories until they disappear as a recognizable group c. 1585.
Citation
Šarić, Marko. “Osmanski Vlasi Istre na izvornoj Tromeđi: nestabilna podaništva i ambivalentne lojalnosti na imperijalnom višegraničju u Hrvatskoj 16. stoljeća.” Povijesni prilozi 67 (2024): 179–236. DOI: 10.22586/pp.v43i67.30587.
Reliability and biases

Form: peer-reviewed scholarly article (izvorni znanstveni rad).
Author: Marko Šarić, Department of History, Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, University of Zagreb. Specialist in 16th–17th c. Vlach/Morlach studies and the Triplex Confinium.
Source type: secondary. The article analyzes but does not fully transcribe the underlying primary registers. Claims drawn from registers should cite “Šarić 2024” with the underlying register noted in the body, not as if the register were directly read.
Strengths: extensive use of Ottoman tax registers (defters) cross-referenced with Venetian state correspondence and Habsburg records. Engages with prior literature (Buzov 1990, Juran 2022, Roksandić 2003, Caciur 2015–16, Bracewell 1997).
Limitations for genealogy:

Most register-only individuals appear with patronymic only (e.g. “Petar, sin Milovana”) — fixed surnames had not yet stabilized in 16th c.
Many village locations marked “nepoznato” (unknown) — toponymic gaps from later depopulation and resettlement.
Confessional identity (Catholic / Orthodox) is hard to determine from given names alone in this period.
Ottoman registers list household heads; women, children, and dependents are aggregated.



Snapshot data points









































YearRegisterHousesNotes1528–30mufassal/sumarni, sandžak Bosna640 (632–640)9 nahijas, 16 dzemats, peak1540opširni Kliški sandžak322 (in 5 nahijas)post-war collapse, ~52% drop1550opširni Kliški sandžak~190 (incl. vakuf)~52% further drop1574vakuf Gazi Husrev-bega97re-classified as “Istrian raja”1585sandžak Krka0name “Vlasi Istre” gone
Key concepts introduced

istimâlet — Ottoman strategy of winning over local populations through privileges, exemptions, and accommodations rather than coercion.
Tromeđa / Triplex Confinium — the original tripoint between Ottoman, Venetian, Habsburg territories, focused around Novigradsko more, Karinsko more, and the Velebit channel.
dzemat / katun — Vlach community/lineage unit, often headed by a knez or vojvoda and primićur.
filurija — Vlach household tax (replacing other dues).
timar — Ottoman benefice; granted to some Vlach starešine.
Morlaci Istrijani — Venetian-side counterpart to the Ottoman Vlasi Istre, on the Zadar contado from c. 1540.
Ćići / Ćiribirci — bilingual (Slavic + Balkan-Romance) Vlachs, last attested speakers in Istria/Kras (modern Istro-Romanian).

Notes for the wiki

This source is the spine of wiki coverage for 16th-c. Vlach migrations in the original Tromeđa.
When citing a register-attested fact, record the register year (1528–30 / 1540 / 1550 / 1574 / 1585) in the body, then cite this article: [[Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre]].
The label “Vlasi Istre” is exogenous — an Ottoman administrative classification, not a self-identifier.
For each register-only person where surname is uncertain, the patronymic stem (e.g. “Milovan” → “Milovanić”) may have stabilized as a surname later; treat as the canonical surname when the article confirms continuity, otherwise file under the patronymic-derived form.

surnames/Agostini.title: Agostini
surnames/Agostini.content:
Agostini
Bearers in Desnica II

Agostini — public agrimensor (surveyor); 1696-09-02 surveyed Vodmac lands near Hercegnovi (doc. 307) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Alberghetti.title: Alberghetti
surnames/Alberghetti.content:
Alberghetti
Italian engineer-family in Venetian service.
Bearers in Desnica II

Alberghetti (engineer) — Venetian military engineer at Dalmatian fortifications Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Giust’Emilio Alberghetti — brother Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Alberti.title: Alberti
surnames/Alberti.content:
Alberti
Bearers

Ivan (Zuanne) Alberti — Zadar plemić; guvernadur (governor) and capitano paired with kapetan Frane Ventura in 1684 directives (line 981); Cornaro’s 1689 pertinenze reform later names governator Zuanne Alberti over Novegradi–Charin–Bađun–Pridraga (line 1045) — same individual, abile Zaratino, d’anni 60 (line 14918) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Zuanne Alberti of Split — Splitski plemić, captured by the Turks beneath Sinj at the April 1685 defeat; held by the bassa di Bosna; his letters survive (lines 3359, 3373, 3438). He is “preso per schiavo proprio dal bassa di Bosna” — distinct from the Zadar Alberti Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
agente Gerolimo Alberti, interprete — Venetian agent and interpreter (line 4282) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
sopraintendente Alberti — at the 1688 Knin conquest commanded the natione oltramarina with Zadar borghesani (line 10494) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Alemin.title: Alemin
surnames/Alemin.content:
Alemin
Bearers in Desnica II

Turco Alemin — late Turk; tower (cula) in Modrino selo (Bukovica) (doc. 259) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Anic.title: Anic
surnames/Anic.content:
Anić
Family settled in Obrovac during the Morean War, listed among 1696 inhabitants.
Bearers in Desnica II (doc. 284, 1696)

Vido Anić — Obrovac.
Andrea Anić — Obrovac.
Simon Anić — Obrovac.
Mattio Anić — Obrovac.
Martin Anić — Obrovac.

Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Notes

The Anić family is among those Desnica’s footnote notes as still living in Kruševo near Obrovac (continuity to modern times) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Antunovic.title: Antunovic
surnames/Antunovic.content:
Antunović
Bunjevac surname of Backa. Foremost member: Ivan-Antunovic-b1815-Backa (1815–1888), naslovni biskup, central figure of the 19th-c. Bunjevac narodni preporod through the Razprava (1882) and the Bunjevačke i šokačke novine (1870) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

surnames/Arzovic.title: Arzovic
surnames/Arzovic.content:
Arzović
Bearers in Desnica II

harambaša Simon Arzović (Šimun Arzović) — Goranci 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Atlagic.title: Atlagic
surnames/Atlagic.content:
Atlagić
Bosnian beg family centered in Knin; “Kula Atlagića” is a major locality on the Knin–Drniš edge.
Bearers

Mehmed-beg Atlagić kapetan kninski — 1675-end-Aug forwards letters of the Bosnian teftedar Omer-paša and the Venetian bailo to provveditor Marin Zorzi; objects to Sandžak-beg Durakbegović trying to collect travarina on Žemunik/Poličnik/Islam lands (doc. 214). Letter in Bosnian Cyrillic.
Atlaghich (“il Turco Atlagich”) — 1662-02-18 in the Ottoman raid party that struck the Kotari (doc. 121). Capitano-rank.
Atlaghich — captain of Knin 1677-02-26 sells castrati and grain to Zadar merchants Deanović, Ponte, Tomasoni for 500 cechini (doc. 234).
alaijmegh Atlagich — killed at the Cetina rotta April 1666 — “soggetto dal grido et auttorita ch’ é ben nota a questi confini” (doc. 148).
figliolo et nipote del Atlaghich con Omerizza suo di casa — 1682 came from Belgrade to Knin (doc. 280).
case dell’ Atlaghich near Cliuno — 1684 the Bosnian alaj-beg encamps there with 1000 spahi (doc. 384).
Kula Atlagića — Salihagini family attestation: 1680 Jussuf e Suglio Pervichio dalla Cula dell’ Atlaghich (doc. 263) — Pervichi being the residential Atlagić sub-line.

Notes

Despite being adversaries of the Janković, the Atlagići maintained corresponding-business and even sheep-fattening contracts with Zadar burghers in peacetime.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

bassa Atlaghich (paša Atlagić) — tried to bombard Zadar 1689; defeated by Zaviša Janković actions Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs. 224, 288).
Atlagić, commandant of Knin — pre-1690s, oversaw disdar Mehmed of Zvonigrad (doc. 321 — Jusuf aga Derviševčić’s testimony 1700) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Casa dei Atlaghich (tower) — 1702 referenced near a village attacked by haiduks of Vid Petrović and Sinobad’s nephew on Mt. Prolog Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 346).

surnames/Avramovic.title: Avramovic
surnames/Avramovic.content:
Avramović
Bearers

Dragić Avramović — Morlak suddito newcomer; petitioner February 1685 for help for the widow and children of his brother Dragoja, who killed Čejvan-aga Lopušić of Knin and was himself killed; awarded 1 peso of biscuit/month (doc 49) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Dragoja Avramović — brother of Dragić; killed Čejvan-aga Lopušić of Knin then died in the same skirmish (doc 49) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Babahmetovic.title: Babahmetovic
surnames/Babahmetovic.content:
Babahmetović
Bearers

Zelel-aga Babahmetović — former Venetian state slave, exchanged for conte Sabbini during the Candian War; his daughter (a widow returning to him) travelled in Mehmed-beg Durakbegović’s escort intercepted March 1685 (doc 56) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
figliola di Zelel-aga Babahmetović — unnamed widowed daughter of Zelel-aga, returning to him in the same March 1685 escort (doc 56) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Babovic.title: Babovic
surnames/Babovic.content:
Babović
Bearers in Desnica II

Resul Aga Babović — Turkish former owner of vineyard in Vodmac/Valmaz, Podhumnica region near Hercegnovi/Castelnuovo; lost it in war; vineyard granted to Bishop Simeon Prešević May 1697 (doc. 307) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Bacic.title: Bacic
surnames/Bacic.content:
Bačić
Surname recorded in Šarić’s continuity-list of Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with possible medieval roots. Some bearers absorbed into the “bunjevačka” Catholic Vlach population near Benkovac and Obrovac Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers (Desnica 1683)

harambaša Vid Bačić — 1683-11-09 with alfier Petar Radić, capo of the Boraja-Suhi Dolac-Labin-Prapatnica-Bristivica-Ljubitovica-Vrsno villages; presents petition to Donà for uskakanje of 1000 souls / 400 fighters (doc. 332). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

surnames/Bajcic.title: Bajcic
surnames/Bajcic.content:
Bajčić
Bearers

Mattio Bajčić — harambaša of Vrana; signatory of the 1684 Vrana petition (doc 36) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Bajcinovic.title: Bajcinovic

surnames/Balen.title: Balen
surnames/Balen.content:
Balen (Balenović / Balinović)
Bunjevac surname; founder family of the Krmpote katun. Šarić classifies the root as arbanaški (Albanian) stratum within the 1712 Bunjevac onomastic stock Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Attestations

mid-16th c. — Ivan-Balenovic-b????-Kijani sin Mihovilov, buried in selo Kijani near Gracac (Cyrillic stećak inscription).
1605 — Balinović (with original katun-aglomeracija) listed among the 24 Krmpote families joining the first Lič migration; also listed among the Sladović “Gvozdenovi ljudi” 1605 group of 20 (the surname appears in both lists).
1756 — Kačić Miošić in Razgovor ugodni names Balenovići among “vitezovi hrvatski” alongside Starcevic, Rukavina, Došen, Milinković Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

surnames/Banenovic.title: Banenovic
surnames/Banenovic.content:
Banenović

surnames/Banic.title: Banic
surnames/Banic.content:

Bearers

Benja (Begna)

Bearers

kavalier-corazze Begna — 1648-07-14 sent with Civaleli into the territory to console the post-Ribnik Morlachi (doc. 37).
knez Anton Benja-Posedarski — Zadar nobleman who in the 1930s held the family archive (custodian of the Posedarski Zbornik) — referenced extensively in Desnica’s fontes but not as a historical actor in the corpus.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Giulio Begna — appointed governor of pertinenza 5 (Nadin) by Cornaro in the 1689-03-11 Liga reform (doc. 224) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
don Gregorio Begna — late by 1693; recorded as debtor to Marija Smiljanić for 4 zecchini in her testament (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Bojicic.content:

surnames/Bolic.title: Bolic
surnames/Bolic.content:

Maria Bolić-Smiljanić (the younger) — wife of Lazaro Smiljanić; pregnant when he wrote will 1696-07-28 (doc. 289) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Boljac.title: Boljac
surnames/Boljac.content:

surnames/Bortulacic.title: Bortulacic
surnames/Bortulacic.content:
Bortulačić
Zadar-patrician (gradski) line, never on payroll, served as venturiere (volunteer/civil servant). Active throughout the 1666–1684 emergencies of the Kotari–Bukovica frontier.
Bearers

Frane (Francesco) Bortulačić q. Šimun — 1666-08-26 receives Korner’s instructions on managing the chain-of-fires fuochi/fumi signal system from Šibenik to Zadar (docs. 156, 157). Mentioned as q. Simon in 1678. Held position by 1678 (doc. 242, on the Liga oversight).
Šimun (Simon) Bortolazzi q. Girolamo — kavalier from a different Bortolazzi sub-branch; at Sv. Ilija 1676-08-17 stands as kompare at Zaviša/Sabba Janković’s wedding (doc. 229). Active in 1683–84 as one of the four direttori over the Morlachi (doc. 395). 1684-04-09 (doc. 392) named capo de Morlacchi essistenti alla Vrana with 20 ducati/month, on the express request of those very Morlachi who “nominarono precisamente D. Simon Bortolazzi.”
Jerolim (Girolamo) Bortolazzi — 1678 nominated to oversee the Liga (doc. 242).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
The murder of Šimun Bortulačić (already noted above as capo de Morlacchi alla Vrana) is documented at length in Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Šimun Bortulačić (Bortolazzi) colonnello, governor of Vrana — murdered 1692-01-16 in Vrana by Biograđani and Pakoštanci with arquebus, body covered with stones; aged ~31; buried in Sv. Stošija, Zadar (docs. 224, 242, 243, 247, 269, 271, 275). Primary instigator of the murder: Tomaso Antičić of Zaravecchia/Pakoštane, who escaped wounded from arrest in Zadar (doc. 269). Two main perpetrators captured and condemned 1693–94; Mattio Žabetić’s brother was squartato (quartered) for participation (doc. 357); Tomaso Tubić of Zaravecchia was banished then pardoned (doc. 357). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

surnames/Bracic.title: Bracic
surnames/Bracic.content:
Bračić

surnames/Brajkovic.title: Brajkovic
surnames/Brajkovic.content:
Brajković
Foremost bearer: biskup Martin-Brajkovic-b????-Senj of Senjsko-Modruska-Biskupija, 1702 — first to introduce the dvojni naziv catholici Valachi alias Bunievczi into ecclesiastical record Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

surnames/Brajnovic.title: Brajnovic
surnames/Brajnovic.content:
Brajnović (Brainović / Brajinović)
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Two distinct 17th-c. kin-groups appear in the corpus:

Petropolje Brainović — Franciscan clergy line.
Zadar Brajinović — settled Morlach family in the Spianata (Predgrađe Sv. Marka, future Borgo Erizzo / Arbanasi).

Bearers (Desnica)

fra Šimun (Simon) Brainović — 1647-12-17 capelan of Petropolje; signs the uskakanje contract on behalf of the conti (doc. 18).
fra Pavao (Paulo) Brainović — Šimun’s brother (doc. 18) — Petropolje pop.
fra Frane (Francesco) Brainović — Šimun’s brother, also Petropolje paroh (doc. 18).
q. Toma Brajinović — d. before 1664; his estate held in escrow.
q. Frane Brajinović (son of q. Toma) — first husband of Anka, who later remarried into the Smiljanić.
Anka — widow of q. Frane Brajinović; mother of Šimun and Marko Brajinović + Smoljan Smiljanić (uterine).
Šimun Brajinović (son of Frane & Anka, uterine half-brother of Smoljan Smiljanić) — 1664 was a slave (doc. 184); 1671 inheritance restored.
Marko Brajinović — Šimun’s brother (doc. 184).
Paolo Brainovich of Malpaga — 1673-05-01 in the bandits-list of those who plundered the Klis caravan (doc. 204).

Note on the Sv. Marko connection
The Brajinović house was on the Spianata behind Sv. Marko in Zadar — the same predgrađe later renamed Borgo Erizzo and now Arbanasi, named after the 1726 Albanian settlement. Pre-Albanian, this was the Bukovica-uskočka Morlach predgrađe.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Nikola Brajnović (Nicolo Brainovich) — Obrovac inhabitant 1696 (doc. 284) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Bucevic.title: Bucevic
surnames/Bucevic.content:

Raina Bucevich et fratello — 2 souls.

surnames/Budisalic.content:

surnames/Buncic.title: Buncic
surnames/Buncic.content:
Bunčić
Medieval vlach katun-name in eastern Hum (Hercegovina), 15th c. Concretely:

1419 — katun of Vukota-Buncic-b1419 (Hrabak 1981:188).
15th c. stećak — selo Buncici (Radmilović-Dubrava near Bileća), tomb of Bunac-Rusovic-b????-Buncici; the bearer probably a starešina of the Vlasi Banjani aglomeracija (Bešlagić 1971:390).

Onomastic evidence for the Bun-stem family of vlach personal/clan names from which the etnik Bunjevac ultimately descends (along with Bunovic, Bunuševci, Bunislavic) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

surnames/Bunislavic.title: Bunislavic
surnames/Bunislavic.content:
Bunislavić
Medieval vlach katun-bearing surname in eastern Hum, 15th c. Attested 1406 in Vlatko-Bunislavic-b1406’s katun (Hrabak 1981:188) Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Bun-stem onomastic family with Buncic, Bunovic, Bunuševci.

surnames/Bunjevac.title: Bunjevac
surnames/Bunjevac.content:
Bunjevac
The etnik-turned-surname at the heart of the wiki’s namesake population. Šarić’s argument: Bunjevac as etnik forms in Catholic Vlach milieu of the Tromeđa around 1550 and acquires its surname function precisely when bearers move into non-Bunjevac (typically Orthodox vlach or Hungarian-administered) environments, where neighbors mark them by the etnik Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Etymology
Bunj- stem (vlach anthroponym Bun/Bunj < Latin Bonifacius via Balkan-Romance vocalism o>u; later n>nj jotacija post-14th c.) + -evac/-evci patronymic suffix. Parallel to medieval vlach groups Buncic, Bunovic (Tudoričevci/Dečani), Bunuševci (Vranje), Bunislavic (1406 east Hum).

Confessional pattern
