surnames/Bunovic.title: Bunovic
surnames/Bunovic.content:
Bunović
Medieval vlach clan in the Tudoricevci katun on the Dečansko vlastelinstvo. Recorded in the 1330 Dečanska povelja (Stefan Uroš III’s hrisovulja for manastir Dečani) — one of five major (proširene/zadružne) families in a 29-ognjište katun Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Named ancestor: Bun-praotac-b????-Tudoricevci with sons Nikola, Tvrtko, Tvrde, Tudorica, brother Rade, Rade’s son Vojisil (Ivanović 1951–52:260). Onomastic relic: Bunova livada / Livadhi i Bon’s in selo Shaptej (Gashi 1982).
Together with Buncic and Bunislavic, a key 14th-c. attestation in the Bun-stem onomastic family from which the etnik Bunjevac derives.

surnames/Bunusevac.title: Bunusevac
surnames/Bunusevac.content:
Bunuševac (Bunuševci)
Medieval vlach katun-name in the upper Južna Morava drainage — eastern frontier of the medieval Serbian state. Attested in 14th c. as Vlasi Bunuševci of the Vranjsko-Krajiste (Blagojević 1989:33–36) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Performed čuvar-granice (border-guard) service to a krajiški vlastelin. Toponymic remnant: village Bunusa south of Leskovac (territorialization of the katun).
Possible link to selo Punoševci/Punoševići in Hum 1402 (Hrabak 1997:145), and to selo Ponoševac/Punashec near Đakovica (Gashi 1982:53) — though these are speculative.
Bun-stem onomastic family with Buncic, Bunovic, Bunislavic.

surnames/Busanic.title: Busanic
surnames/Busanic.content:
Bušanić
Single attestation: Spahia Radivoi Bussanich — 1653-01-16 co-signs Smiljanić proxy (doc. 70). The title Spahia indicates an Ottoman feudal landholder who uskočio with his land-rights.

surnames/Busljetic.title: Busljetic
surnames/Busljetic.content:
Bušljetić
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers (Desnica)

Giacomo Busletich con due fratelli — 3 souls in the 1671-12-17 Dračevac/Komorce repopulation roster (doc. 199, Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).

surnames/Busovic.title: Busovic
surnames/Busovic.content:
Busović
Bearers

Spahija Busović — 1648-05-11 uskočio with 30 Morlach houses to Janko Mitrović’s banner from Lika (doc. 28).
Dragosav Busović + Todora — 1663-04-21 parents of Đurđe (Zorzi) Busović, baptised at Sv. Zulijan Šibenik (doc. 129). Đurđe is the brother of vladika Nikodim Busović (per Desnica’s footnote: a separate baptismal record for Nikodim was published in Prilozi, knj. XVII, sv. 1).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

monsignor Nikodim Busović (Nicodemo Buscovich) — Greek-rite bishop (“vescovo del rito greco / vescovo di Stratonika”); native subject; ordained 1693-06-24 by Melentije bishop of Philadelphia (doc. 317 footnote). Petitioned 1694 to restore monastery of Dragović between two arms of the river Cetina (doc. 276). Sept 1699 received 50 kanapa of land at Međupuće for Dragović monks (doc. 317). Troubled Nikanor Stanković of Vrlika 1698 (doc. 308). 1701 pledged for Petar Banković of Pakoštane (doc. 332) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Butkovic.title: Butkovic
surnames/Butkovic.content:
Butković
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Andrija (Andrea) Butković — kavalier, captain (1698 commission member, doc. 312); colonnello di cavalleria croatta; appointed sopraintendente of Knin and Vrlika in July 1715 by provveditor Anđelo Emo, succeeding Jovan Sinobad killed at Glamoč (doc. 372) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Butorac.title: Butorac
surnames/Butorac.content:
Butorac (Butorčić)
Bunjevac surname. Originally Butorčić (patronymic) in the 1605 Lič migration, simplified to Butorac by 18th c. Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Attestations

1605 — among Krmpote families on the first Lič migration.
1702 — vojvoda Marko-Butorac-b????-Lika in Ribnik / Lika; antagonist of porkulab Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik in the Ribnička buna.

surnames/Cacic.title: Cacic
surnames/Cacic.content:
Čačić
Bearers

kapetan Ivan (Jovan) Čačić of castel Venier — 1663-02 attested by Contarini for beheading Murat-aga Salihagić, disdar of Perušić during a counter-pursuit (doc. 127). 1664-05-21 promoted to serdar by Contarini, replacing the killed Petar Gargurica (doc. 137).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Vučić Čačić (Vucich Ciaccich) — Obrovac inhabitant 1696 (doc. 284) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Calcina.title: Calcina
surnames/Calcina.content:
Kalčin (Calcina)
Bearers

kavalier dottore Grgur (Gregorio) Calcina — 1680-06-07 sopraintendent of the Liga at Visočani (doc. 270). 1682-11-06 sopraintendent at Zaravecchia Liga (doc. 295, 297).
Nicolo Calcina — 1682-11-06 also nominated (doc. 296).

Note

See also existing surname Kalčina entry for medieval-modern continuity background.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Pietro Calčina (Pietro Calcina / Petar Kalčina) — appointed governor of pertinenza 2 (Posedarje) by Cornaro in the 1689 Liga reform (doc. 224); reported defeat of Popržen to capitano Papafava (doc. 225). 1698 commission member (doc. 312). 1701 captain; claimed to have been invested 1675/1680 in cancelleria illirica, opposed Lomazzi’s appointment (doc. 327). Previously served as cavalier in Levant under generals. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
dottor cavalier Gregorio Calčina (Grgur Kalčina) — late by Feb 1694; cancelliere of Illyrian and Serbian letters in Zadar; succeeded by Lomazzi (doc. 272). Father of Pietro per doc. 327 (“il quondam signor kavalier Calcina”). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

surnames/Caldana.title: Caldana
surnames/Caldana.content:
Caldana
Bearers in Desnica II

don Andrea Caldana — curato of duomo of Zadar (Sv. Stošija); recorded death of Constantin Janković Feb 1692 and of Marko Smiljanić 1693-02-23; gave extreme unction to Marko; witnessed Marija Smiljanić’s testament opening 1694-04-13 (docs. 244, 264, 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Califfi.title: Califfi
surnames/Califfi.content:
Califfi
Italian/Venetian noble family resident in Zadar; held half-interest in the island of Olib.
Bearers in Desnica II

Conte Francesco Califfi — deceased by 1701; father of Giacomo. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Conte Giacomo Califfi (son of conte Francesco) — sold half-island of Olib to Mitrović family in 1701 for 8000 ducats with peculiar dynastic conditions: perpetual half-half ownership between Saviša Janković’s male line and his deceased brother Ilija’s male line. See Olib-Sale-1701. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

surnames/Camuccio.title: Camuccio
surnames/Camuccio.content:
Camuccio
Bearers

ingegner Camuccio — Venetian military engineer; designed siege works at Sinj April 1685 with 12 scaling ladders (docs 60, 61); supervised the 1686 Sinj-Salona campaign and continued through the Knin conquest 1688 (doc 144) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Canagetti.title: Canagetti
surnames/Canagetti.content:
Canagetti
Bearers

Canagetti — lieutenant-colonel volunteer Feb 1685 (doc 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Capelletto.title: Capelletto
surnames/Capelletto.content:
Capelletto / Kapelet
The italianized military epithet “Capelletto” (= soldier in the Cavalleria Capelletta, a Venetian Croatian-cavalry corps) became a hereditary surname for the family of Dragosav of Budin.
Bearers

Dragosav Capelletto da Budin — 1678 capitan; with kapetan Ivesko Jović of Ražanac among the four arbitri who divided the Sv. Juraj/Castel Venier lands (docs. 239, 240). 1679-05-16 — Vukčević matter: ordered not to harm Radojica Garković in retaliation for his slave Milovan being sold to Turks (doc. 247). Father of Vukadin and uncle of Bogoje Vukčević.

surnames/Capello.title: Capello
surnames/Capello.content:
Capello
Venetian patrician (provveditor de cavalli, secretario).
Bearers in Desnica II

Stefano Capello (Capelo) — provveditor de cavalli; 1693-11-06 reported to Dolfin in Šibenik on Gorica raid (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Giacomo Capello — Venetian secretary 1705 (doc. 360) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Carletta.title: Carletta
surnames/Carletta.content:
Carletta
Pag noble/patrician family active in salt trade.
Bearers in Desnica II

Nicolo Carletta — giudice of Pago; signer of Pago salt contract 1694 (doc. 279) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Giorgio Carletta — difensor of Pago; signer of same Pago salt contract (doc. 279) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Carlotti.title: Carlotti
surnames/Carlotti.content:
Carlotti
Bearers

marchese Carlotti — with Pietro Valier at the Sinj campaign April 1685 (doc 60) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Carsolov.title: Carsolov
surnames/Carsolov.content:
Carsolov / Karsolov
Single attestation: Antonio Carsolov — 1 soul in the 1671-12-17 Dračevac roster (doc. 199).

surnames/Casanova.title: Casanova
surnames/Casanova.content:
Casanova
Italian family.
Bearers in Desnica II

Cesare Casanova — capitan/governator of Obrovci, appointed by provveditor Molin Jan 1690; previously had a galleotta in the area; spent years in Spalato; died c. 1693, succeeded by Dimo Vlastò Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs. 226, 227, 256, 260).

surnames/Casotti.title: Casotti
surnames/Casotti.content:
Casotti
Bearers

govvernator Casotti — governor in the Trogir Castelli; at line 4542 commanded granatieri together with Geliseo and Razzetini against the Turks (1685) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Casseretti.title: Casseretti
surnames/Casseretti.content:
Casseretti
Bearers in Desnica II

Casseretti — commissario of Marija Smiljanić’s 1693 will (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Cassio.title: Cassio
surnames/Cassio.content:
Kašić (Cassio)
Bearers

dr. Ivan (Giovanni) Kašić — 1678-04-15 named by Valier among the four sopraintendentini (Sope, Bortulačić, Kašić, Pasini) of the Liga (doc. 242).

Notes

The Kašićev Ritual at the Filipjakov parohijska crkva (now in Knin museum) is annotated with a 1666 glagolska zabeleška by Nikola Kužinović about the death of Vučko Močivuna at Zečevo (doc. 151).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Francesco Cassio — Zadar/Nin noble; appointed governor of pertinenza 1 (Nin) by Cornaro in 1689 Liga reform; later one of Liga giudici under Dolfin 1696 (docs. 224, 286) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
dottor Cassio — father of Ellena, who received a diamond ring bequest in Marija Smiljanić’s 1693 testament (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Giovanni (Ivan) Cassio dottore — witness alongside alfier Antonio Bardi to the 14 September 1686 Stojan-Janković purchase contract for the San Simeone-parish house in Zadar (doc 143, line 6305) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Catalinic.title: Catalinic
surnames/Catalinic.content:
Katalinić
Bearers

Žorži (Zorzi) Katalinić — knez of Starigrad; killed 1678 defending Morlach animals against a Lika Turkish raid (doc. 253).
Frane (Francesco) Katalinić — 1678-11-10 son of Žorži; named knez of Starigrad to succeed his father by Valier (doc. 253).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Frane (Francesco) Cattalinich (Vid Katalinić) — capitano of Starigrad (under Velebit/Morlacca); reported on Karlobag developments to Molin Jan 1690 (doc. 228); appointed captain of new 50-man Starigrad company by Dolfin Nov 1696 (docs. 290, 291, 294); 1696 testified with Šimun Vukosalkić about Stinica being inhabited by Bukovčani who fled to Sv. Juraj near Senj during Candian War (doc. 291) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Cengic.title: Cengic
surnames/Cengic.content:
Čengić
Famous Bosnian beg-family.
Bearers (Desnica)

alaj-beg Čengić (Cengligch) — 1662-02-18, in the raid party that struck the Kotari (doc. 121).
Cinghic — 1666-04-05 mortally wounded at the Cetina rotta (doc. 148).

surnames/Ceprnja.title: Ceprnja
surnames/Ceprnja.content:
Čeprnja
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

surnames/Cerinagic.title: Cerinagic
surnames/Cerinagic.content:
Ćerinagić (Kerimagić)
Hercegovinian beg family.
Bearers in Desnica II

Aga Mustibegh Ćerinagić (Mustajbeg) — Turkish aga of Trebinje; lands and ruined tower in Padglivie/Trebinje taken; in 1696 the 12 fields and ruined tower were granted to Demetrio (Dmitar) Pivljanin, brother of late Bajo Pivljanin Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 287).

surnames/Cernicic.title: Cernicic
surnames/Cernicic.content:
Černičić (Cernicich)
Ottoman beg family of Knin/Krka/Lika.
Bearers in Desnica II

Mehmed-beg Černičić — sangiacco of Krka, Lika and Krbava (late 17th c.) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 224 context).
Mahmut-beg Černičić — son of Mehmed-beg; disdar of Knin Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Notes

Distinct from the Crnica (Cernizza) of Tinj — the Ottoman Cernicich sangiacco line is a different family despite spelling overlap.

surnames/Cernizza.title: Cernizza
surnames/Cernizza.content:
Crnica
Bearers

col. Vuk Crnica — colonnello, served from start of Candian War. 1655-02-25 ducal of Doge Molino orders his arrest with Žorži Posedarski, Petar Šope, Vasilij Slaven for fleeing the Knin battle (doc. 92, 93). 1671-02-01 — investitured by Barbaro with 400 kanapa in Tinj/Bubnjane/Lišani plus the ruined tower of Ferhat-pašić (doc. 182). Died 1671-04-29 per Sv. Stošija matica umrlih (Desnica’s footnote on doc. 182). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
kavalier Marko Crnica — son of Vuk; co-investitured with father (doc. 182). 1682-11-06 elected sopraintendent of the Liga from Nin (doc. 295, 297). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
kapetan Žorži (Zorzi) Crnica — 1678-06-29 patron of a galiotta posted at Zaravecchia (doc. 249). 1684 — surnamed capitan Vuco Cernizza (different person? — same as Vuk?) is at Sukošan dispatching the galiotta to Morlacca (doc. 241).

Notes

The 1671 investitura is aspirational: Desnica’s footnote notes that “Sve su Barbarove investiture ostale mrtvo slovo, jer je kopnena Dalmacija kod razgraničenja od 1671 g. opet pripala Turcima. Ipak su neke od ovih infeudacija posle konačnog izgona Turaka bile oživele.”
Vuk’s tower (the kula begova Ferhat-pašića) survived in Tinj until ~1934, when local villagers blew it up with mines (Desnica’s footnote on doc. 182).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Bože (Boze) Cernizza — at garrison of Vrlika 1688; captain (referenced 1688). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Two Crnice (Cernizza) brothers — rebels from Vrlika; abandoned Vrlika garrison and went over to Ottomans 1697; later recalled and died in Šibenik prison (doc. 305) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Cheuro.title: Cheuro
surnames/Cheuro.content:
Cheuro (Ćuro / Ker)
Single attestation: Tommaso Cheuro con tre figli e nipote — 5 souls in the 1671-12-17 Dračevac roster (doc. 199). Croatian transliteration uncertain — possibly Ćuro, Ker, Hor. Cf. Petar Chieur in another doc.

surnames/Cipic.title: Cipic
surnames/Cipic.content:
Čipić (Mihelić-Čipić)
Petropolje knez sub-line. Doc. 18 (1647-12-17): “conte Giacomo Michelich conte di conti di tutte le ville de cristiani di Campo Piero, che sono il numero di tredici” — and (separately) “conte Giacomo Gargich detto Cipich conte di Cipich che non havendo potuto venire ha mandato il proprio anello.”
Bearers

conte Jakov (Giacomo) Mihelić — knez nad knezovima of all 13 Petropolje villages.
conte Jakov Gargić rečeni Čipić — knez of Čipići.

surnames/Cirjak.title: Cirjak
surnames/Cirjak.content:
Čirjak
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

surnames/Cittadella.title: Cittadella
surnames/Cittadella.content:
Cittadella
Bearers

kavalier Cittadella — present on Korponež’s galeotta beneath the Pastrovići towers March 1686 (doc 131); at the 1686 Sinj campaign distinguished himself among the first to attack though not commanded (line 6470) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Civalelli.title: Civalelli
surnames/Civalelli.content:
Civaleli
Zadar patrician house. Active throughout the corpus as Venetian envoys/colonelli.
Bearers

Gregorio Civaleli — 1647-07-21 already with command-rank — Foscolo cites him among the capitani de Crovati et Albanesi killed at the Diklo–Bokanjac fight (doc. 13). Surviving Civaleli active 1648-07-14 sent with kapetan Begna to console the Morlachi after Ribnik (doc. 37).
col. Civaleli — 1658-06-28 sent by Bernardo to Petar Zrinski (doc. 106).
Civalelli — 1655 witness to Smiljanić-Zubičević dote (doc. 97).

surnames/Civran.title: Civran
surnames/Civran.content:
Civran
Venetian patrician.
Bearers

Andrea Civran — captain of the Gulf 1615; recorded oral tradition of the Krmpote/Bunjevci Hercegovinian origin (see Krmpotic).

surnames/Cloder.title: Cloder
surnames/Cloder.content:
Cloder
Bearers

mistro Claudio Cloder, detto Zampagna — quondam by 1686; his heirs received an annual livello affrancabile of 17 ducats on the San Simeone-parish house Stojan Janković purchased from the Pierantonii–Gioachini chain (doc 143, 14 Sept 1686) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Colic.title: Colic
surnames/Colic.content:
Kolić / Čolić
Single attestation: Cvitco Colich — 1 soul in the 1671-12-17 Dračevac roster (doc. 199).

surnames/Cona.title: Cona
surnames/Cona.content:
Cona
Bearers

Lazaro Cona — sent by Stojan Janković from Bigliane (Biljane) to find the commissario (Marin Michiel) at Malpaga at the start of the November 1686 Bosnian Pasha incursion (doc 155, Stojan Mitrović’s deposition of 16 Nov 1686, Skradin) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Contarini.title: Contarini
surnames/Contarini.content:
Contarini
Venetian patrician house.
Bearers

Battista Contarini — Conte (count/governor) of Šibenik (docs 25, 48) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Cordic.title: Cordic
surnames/Cordic.content:
Kordić
Single attestation: Tiomir Kordić iz Kruševa — 1684-01-11 settled in Obrovac with 10 houses (doc. 364).

surnames/Cornaro.title: Cornaro
surnames/Cornaro.content:
Cornaro
Venetian patrician.
Bearers in Desnica II

Girolamo Cornaro (Đirolamo Kornaro) — provveditor generale in Dalmatia 1689; issued attestation for Zaviša Janković doc. 225; issued the 1689-03-11 Liga regulation dividing Kotari into 9 pertinenze with governators and judges (doc. 224). Was at conquest of Knin (doc. 321) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Alessandro Corner — Turk-converted Christian from Knin; witness 1700 in Sfakioto’s Grimani-commission protocols (doc. 321) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Corner.title: Corner
surnames/Corner.content:
Corner / Cornaro
Venetian patrician house. The same family appears in Italian sources as Corner and Latinized as Cornaro.
Bearers

Nicolò Corner — Venetian senator, signatory of doc 22 (1684) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Zorzi Corner — Venetian senator (doc 144 / line 4509) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Girolamo Cornaro kavalier — Provveditor general in Dalmazia et Albania from 1686; conducted the 1686 Sinj campaign and the 1688 Knin conquest; correspondent of dozens of docs from 1686–88; brother of the late kavalier Catterino Cornaro (doc 138) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Crekat.title: Crekat
surnames/Crekat.content:
Crekat
Single attestation: harambaša Zuanne Crecat — 1663-05-08 leads the guard at the Bilisane pass with men of Ražanac and Jesenice (doc. 130).

surnames/Crestich.title: Crestich
surnames/Crestich.content:
Crestich
Bearers in Desnica II

harambaša Crestich — Blato 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Crnojevic.title: Crnojevic
surnames/Crnojevic.content:
Crnojević
Bearers in Desnica II

Patriarch Arsenije III Crnojević (Arsenio Zarnoevich) — Serbian Patriarch; sheltered in Habsburg lands; in 1693 appointed Teodosije Mitrović his exarch and vicegerent (docs. 262, 266); letter issued 1693-01-10 (old style) at Lepavina monastery Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Culina.title: Culina
surnames/Culina.content:
Čulina (Čulinović)
Vlach lineage attested on the original Tromeđa in 16th–17th c. Possibly continuous with the 1528-attested Culina-sin-Milica-b????-Bjeline (knez, timar in Lika), though Šarić leaves the link uncertain Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Mid 16th c.: living at Pridraga (novigradski distrikt) and Ljubač (1608: 2 houses); some moved to Ledenice in Senjska-Kapetanija.
Bearers in this wiki

Culina-sin-Milica-b????-Bjeline — knez (1528)

surnames/Cvitanovic.title: Cvitanovic
surnames/Cvitanovic.content:
Cvitanović
Bearers

Vuconie (Vukon) Cvitanović — Šibenik-territory rider; in November 1686 Stojan Janković dispatched him with karambassà Nakić from Bribir to alert the Zadar contado of the Bosnian Pasha’s irruption (doc 155) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Matteo Cvitanović — captain in Split; in 1700 in horse-trade litigation with tenente colonnello Frano Franćeski (Franceschi), governor of Vrlika, who had fallen from a stallion riding alka on the Split quay during carnival; horse died, valued at 40 reali (doc 324) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Cvitkovic.title: Cvitkovic
surnames/Cvitkovic.content:
Cvitković
Bearers in Desnica II

harambaša Doimo Cvitković (Dujam Cvitković) — Goranci 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Danilovic.title: Danilovic
surnames/Danilovic.content:
Danilović
Don Matej-Danilovic-b????-Polaca was župnik in Polača in 1591; his deposition before the Nin bishop documented widespread konkubinat among glagoljaški priests in Banadego and Lika Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Matej-Danilovic-b????-Polaca — don, župnik (1591)

surnames/Detrico.title: Detrico
surnames/Detrico.content:
Detrico (Detrešić)
Zadar patrician house. The provveditori entrust them with confidential paciatorial work on the Krajina.
Bearers

Gregorio (Grgur) Detrico — 1671-02-26 (Split) Barbaro entrusts him with all cavallaria pagata and direction of the Kotarci, with secret instructions (doc. 191). 1671-07 leads 60 cavallaria to receive the Bosnian basha for the razgraničenje. 1675-01-17 stands as compare at the baptism of Stojan Janković’s daughter (doc. 207-related). 1678-06-29 in Šibenik instructed by Valier on the post-Žemunik reconciliation, with secret authority to commission private assassinations of named perpetrators (doc. 249).

surnames/Devic.title: Devic
surnames/Devic.content:
Dević
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers (Desnica)

Milinko Dević — harambaša of Miranje 1646-03-26 (doc. 2 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I) — co-petitioner with pop Petar Popović and Petar Grudarović for uskakanje of 20 families.
Ivan Dević — harambaša 1663-05-08, posted with villagers of Bogoselci, Bibinje, Kolarin, Brkljača, Sukošan at the Margitina Voda pass-guard (doc. 130).
Stevan Deović — 1664 Zadar burgher (doc. 140); kreditor of Vuk Močivuna; held a Turk slave Oman Miličević for debt-recovery.

surnames/Diedo.title: Diedo
surnames/Diedo.content:
Diedo
Venetian patrician family.
Bearers in Desnica II

Diedo — Provveditor Generale in Dalmatia; correspondent in the long administrative tail of Desnica II. Simple record per directive. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

surnames/Dikic.title: Dikic
surnames/Dikic.content:
Đikić
Bearers in Desnica II

Salin-aga Đikić (Saliaga Gichich) — late Turkish bey near Mostar/Zavojane (Zaupa); his abandoned villages and lands were assigned to Ivan Rašić in 1692 (doc. 258) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Djekic.title: Djekic
surnames/Djekic.content:
Đekić
Bearers

Giure (Đure) Đekić — Vrana harambaša; signatory of the 1684 Vrana petitions to Mocenigo (doc 35) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Djervescovic.title: Djervescovic
surnames/Djervescovic.content:
Đerverščović
Demonymic surname (= “of/from Đevrske”). Possibly the same as Smoljan Miković of Đevrske (cf. Mikovic) under a different patronymic.
Bearers

Smoljan Đerverščović da Đevrske (Smoglian Gerverscovich) — 1653-01-16 co-signs Smiljanić proxy (doc. 70). 1671-06-21 with Milisav Močivuna and Luka Kožulović represents the pravoslavni Morlaci over the Sv. Ivan church in Spianata (doc. 193).

surnames/Djurdjevic.title: Djurdjevic
surnames/Djurdjevic.content:
Đurđević (Jurjević)
Footnote in Desnica explicitly: “Gjurgjević (sada Jurjević)” — the family is the same line as the modern Jurjević of Obrovac/Kruševo Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Bearers in Desnica II

Vido (Vid) Đurđević — alfier (ensign) under serdar Zaviša Mitrović; resident of Obrovac; witness to doc. 265 (1693); subject to surety bond by Zaviša 1694-01-13 (docs. 265, 270, 284). 1702 commanded Janković company at Obrovac after Zaviša’s death; volunteered to lead cavalry company to Italy; declared harambasa of Obrovac March 1702 (doc. 351); 1704 his animals seized at Obrovac during Bukovica revolt (doc. 352); 1703 called to Split to raise paesana company Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Martin Đurđević (Jurjević) — Obrovac inhabitant 1696 (doc. 284) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Djuric.title: Djuric
surnames/Djuric.content:
Đurić
Bjelaj-area capi family that led the 1692 mass migration of ~5000 souls into Venetian state.
Bearers in Desnica II

Conte Paolo Đurić (Paolo Giurich) — capo of Bjelaj province; led ~5000 souls to Venetian devotion; awarded 10 ducats + biscuit/month June 1692; settled in Zrmanja, Plavno, Pađene, Mokro Polje, Oton; killed in clash with Turks; pension transferred to brother Vuk 1693-08-11 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs. 251, 252).
Conte Vuk Đurić (Vuk Giurich) — brother of Paolo; received Paolo’s 10 ducats/month pension after his death 1693 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (footnote of doc. 251).

surnames/Dobric.title: Dobric
surnames/Dobric.content:
Dobrić
Bearers

harambaša Jovan Dobrić — 1648-07-17: “Uskoci iz Dobropoljaca naseljeni u Ljubču od 60 ljudi izgubili dvojicu” at Ribnik (doc. 39).
harambassà Ivan Dobrievich — 1663-05-08 leads the guard with men of Parčić, Žemunik, Bokanjac and Malpaga at the Otres pass (doc. 130).
Milja Dobrić — 1684-03-01 named capitano of Radovin by Donà (doc. 381).

surnames/Dolfin.title: Dolfin
surnames/Dolfin.content:
Dolfin
Venetian patrician.
Bearers in Desnica II

Daniel Dolfin — provveditor generale di Dalmazia from Feb 1692, succeeding Alessandro Molin; “kavalier provveditor”; reconciled the Mitrovići and Milkovići 1692 (doc. 247); ratified many decisions through 1696 (docs. 243 onwards). Gave 1697 relazione to Senate (doc. 305) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Daniel Dolfin (the 4th, “quarto”) — provveditor general of Dalmazia 1737–1738; handled pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža’s correspondence (docs. 386, 387, 388) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Alvise Dolfin — Venetian consigliere 1705 (doc. 358) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Nicolo Dolfin — Venetian senator 1727 (doc. 378) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Dominis.title: Dominis
surnames/Dominis.content:
Dominis
Bearers in Desnica II

Angiolina Dominis — mentioned in scritto of Marija Smiljanić’s 1693 will (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Donado.title: Donado
surnames/Donado.content:
Donà / Donado
Venetian patrician house.
Bearers

Lorenzo Donà / Donado — outgoing Venetian Provveditor General May 1684; ill, in bed at the scoglio del Lantana when Mocenigo arrived to relieve him (docs 1, 36) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Dorimic.title: Dorimic
surnames/Dorimic.content:
Dorimić
Bearers in Desnica II

harambaša Steffano Dorimić (Stjepan Dorimić) — Blato 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Dragojl.title: Dragojl
surnames/Dragojl.content:
Dragojl (knez)
Single attestation: knez Dragojl iz Miljevaca — 1648-10-08 “sismatico, basso, barba grisa folta, pello nero” — 4 ducati/month assigned by Foscolo (doc. 47). Sismatico = “schismatic” = Orthodox.

surnames/Dragovic.title: Dragovic
surnames/Dragovic.content:
Dragović
Single attestation: pop (sveštenik rito greco) Lazar Dragović — 1683-12-26 envoy of 1500 Morlach families from Kolasaz, Parčić, Krmpote, Rodaljica, Kosulovo Polje, Skradin, Kistanje, Perušić, Benkovac, Brkljača Polača, Mor Polača who had occupied the kašteli Raslina, Račevica, Dobri Dolac, Dejanović, Putičane, Skonotić, Vrana. Asks Donà to assign them a director (doc. 358). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

surnames/Ducanevic.title: Ducanevic
surnames/Ducanevic.content:
Ducanević
Bearers in Desnica II

Miho Ducanević — Brochno only-bread recipient 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Dugarsevic.title: Dugarsevic
surnames/Dugarsevic.content:
Dugaršević
Bearers in Desnica II

Zorzi Dugaršević (Đorđe Dugaršević) — serdar of Brochno superior; led migrations 1694; awarded 10 ducats/month (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Duhakovic.title: Duhakovic
surnames/Duhakovic.content:
Duhaković
Bearers in Desnica II

Michel Duhaković — Brochno only-bread recipient 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Dukajtar.title: Dukajtar
surnames/Dukajtar.content:
Dukajtar
Single Ottoman-side attestation in chunk 3 of Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Stub page.

surnames/Dundovic.title: Dundovic
surnames/Dundovic.content:
Dundović
Single attestation: Juriša Dundović of Ražanac, killed 1662-02-13 at Otres (Ražanačka godovna knjiga, doc. 119).

surnames/Dupor.title: Dupor
surnames/Dupor.content:
Dupor
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

surnames/Durakbegovic.title: Durakbegovic
surnames/Durakbegovic.content:
Durakbegović
Bosnian beg family that held the Vrana zijamet and the Sandžak of Krka (Cetina) on the Dalmatian frontier from before 1671 to the Vrana uprising 1683.
Bearers

Durak-beg (Durac bei) Durakbegović — sandžak-beg of Krka. Active 1671–1684. The post-1671 razgraničenje granted Vrana back to “li figlioli di Durag begh antichi padroni di quella” (doc. 196, 1671-07-20). His wife (la moglie del sangiacco) lived at Vrana then Plavno (doc. 316, 367). His son Allilbeg Duracbegovich was beheaded by Stojan Janković per Stojan’s 1670 supplica (doc. 170).
Muhamed-beg (Mohamed-beg) Durakbegović — sandžak-beg of Krka. Letters in Bosnian Cyrillic 1675-08-09, 1675-08-12, 1675-09-x, 1682-01-02, 1684-02-22 (docs. 212, 213, 216, 277, 377). Father (1682) is a confidant of the Posedarski; mediates between Knin Turks and Venice. By 1684 ex-sandžak (passato sangiacco), called by the Bosnian basha to dissuade the Morlachi from defection (doc. 377).
Mehmed-beg Durakbegović — also referred to (in 1684 he is alive and resident; 1684 has wife and son who flee to Plavno then Blagaj — doc. 367).
Hasan-beg Durakbegović — brother of the sandžak; 1670 the casa di Assan Begh in Vrana investitura’d to the Vasallo brothers (doc. 178). 1679 with Krčki kadi at Žemunik, conferring with Soppe (doc. 261). Implicated in the August 1682 Žemunik affair where Hassan begh led an unauthorized force against the Morlachi cultivating the Žemunik fields (doc. 300, retrospective).
Durakbegovica (anonymous wife of the sandžak) — 1683-09-29 levaling Vrana, retreats to Plavno (doc. 316). 1684-01-28 with son retreats further to Blagaj in Hercegovina (doc. 367).
Allilbeg Duracbegovich — son; beheaded by Stojan Janković.

Notes

Mocenigo (after the source’s end-date) made Mehmed-beg Durakbegović sandžak of a place “verso Canisa” — survives the Vrana uprising (doc. 350).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Muhamed-beg Durakbegović — Turkish bey of Plavno; his tower (cula) at Plavno was assigned to Nicolò Pirić in 1692 when 5000 souls of the Bjelaj region settled with conti Đurić, Pirić and Zorić (docs. 251, 252, 253) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Emo.title: Emo
surnames/Emo.content:
Emo
Venetian patrician house.
Bearers

Angelo Emo — Conte (count/governor) of Zadar 1684 (doc 33) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Emoric.title: Emoric
surnames/Emoric.content:
Emorić
Bearers in Desnica II

Hadži (Agia) Emorić/Omeragić (Emorich) — late Turk; house in Knin granted to Sinobad in 1691 (doc. 241) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Erbestein.title: Erbestein
surnames/Erbestein.content:
Herberstein (Erbestein)
Habsburg general.
Bearers in Desnica II

General Herberstein/Erbestein — Habsburg general of Karlstadt (Karlovac), county of Senj; was provisioning a large ship with cannons to bring Barletta salt to Karlobag and supply Lika/Krbava forts in 1690; died before executing his plans Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs. 228, 281). Came to Lika after Venetians ~1689 to consolidate Imperial gains (doc. 316).

surnames/Erizzo.title: Erizzo
surnames/Erizzo.content:
Erizzo
Venetian patrician.
Bearers in Desnica II

Nicolò Erizzo II — provveditor estraordinario of Cattaro; terminacija 1653-03-15 (doc. 280) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Niccolò Erizzo (Nikolo Erico) — provveditor general of Dalmazia 1725–1726; appointed Petar Mitrović-Stojisavljević serdar of Knin 1726-02-23 (docs. 376, 379) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Erlic.title: Erlic
surnames/Erlic.content:
Erlić (Harlić)
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

surnames/Fanfogna.title: Fanfogna
surnames/Fanfogna.content:
Fanfonja (Fanfogna)
Zadar patrician land-owning house.
Bearers

Frane (Francesco) Fanfogna — 1671-12-17 holds most lands adjoining Dračevac/Komorce; settles 20 Morlach families there for repopulation (doc. 199). Zaviša Ivancevich, Tomaso Cheuro, Antonio Carsolov, Tommaso Gelusich, Andrea Gelusich, Mate-Marco-Antonio-Zorzi-Mattio Harlich, Giacomo Buslević, Mate-Vido-Toma-Mattio-Michel-Raina Bućević, Pero Pugnić, Cvitko Colić — all listed as 43 souls.
Pietro Fanfogna — 1653-01-16 giudice esaminatore della corte di Zara signing the Smiljanić proxy (doc. 70).
Anđeo (Anzolo) Fanfogna — 1680-06-07 sopraintendent of the Liga at Visočani (doc. 270).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

conte kavalier Francesco Fanfogna — 1696 one of Liga giudici under Dolfin (doc. 286); 1698 commission member; age 61 in 1699 (b. ~1638), sergente maggiore di battaglia, witness in Sfakioto’s Grimani-commission protocols re Morlacca possessions (docs. 312, 315) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
conte Anđelo (Angelo) Fanfogna — 1698 commission member Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 312).
conte Simon Fanfogna — nobleman, leased Kotari decima for 7800 reali via proxy Ilija Vrbnjčanin in 1704; targets of Bukovica revolt violence (doc. 352) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
colonnello Fanfogna — 1707 helped pop Petar Jagodić approach provveditor Da Riva (doc. 389) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Fenzi.title: Fenzi
surnames/Fenzi.content:
Fenzi
Single attestation: colonel in Venetian Dalmatian service Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Stub page.

surnames/Filipovic.title: Filipovic
surnames/Filipovic.content:
Filipović
Franjo-Filipovic-b????-Zagreb, canon of Zagreb, converted to Islam in 1578 — cited by Šarić alongside other 16th-c. cases of noble or clerical defection across the Tromeđa Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. By the mid-17th c. the Filipovići appear as a senior Bosnian beg-family; whether they descend from the 1578 Zagreb canon is conjectural but not implausible.
Bearers

Franjo-Filipovic-b????-Zagreb — Zagreb canon, Muslim convert (1578).
Jusuf alaj-beg Filipović — Bosnian alaj-beg; 1652-12 captured by Šibenik Morlachi at Duare (docs. 68, 69 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I); ransomed 1659 in Danilo via baratto for the Venetian patrician Daniele Morosini (doc. 264 footnote — establishing the Filipović–Morosini friendship). Later beheaded by Stojan Janković: per Stojan’s 1670 supplica “Recep aga Filipovich” cut down in Kotari (docs. 168, 170).
Reep-aga Filipović — alternative spelling of the same beheaded individual (Stojan’s 1668 attestato, doc. 168).
Mehmed-beg Zain Filipović — 1680-05-07 writes to provveditor Korner from Glamoč asking help to find his grandson, son of Jusuf (doc. 264). Father of Jusuf.
Mehmed-beg Filipović — 1682-03 writes from Glamoč about a man captured on the Sukošan road (doc. 281).
Filipovich kuće (kod Cliuna) — 1684 Bashas of Bosnia lodge there before the campaign against the Morlachi (docs. 372, 384).
Ferhat-paša Filipović — 1648 paša prior to the post-Klis-fall attack on Kotari (doc. 19).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

alaj-beg Filipović of Glamoč — 1684 his palaces and ten surrounding villages are burned by Janković and Smiljanić in the August 1684 Glamoč raid (docs 27, 28) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
alaj-beg Filipović of Bosnia — September 1686 newly named alajbeg of Bosna (with title capigi); arrived at Livno together with the new Zvornik pasha Bastić to repair the houses and towers burned in the first Livno raid; Janković and Smiljanić then carried out the second Livno raid burning everything within 50 miles (doc 141, 7 September 1686) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Firdusovic.title: Firdusovic
surnames/Firdusovic.content:
Firdusović
Bearers

Mustaj-beg Firdusović — capitano di Chnin. 1662-02-18 attested as kapetan kninski (doc. 121). 1684-02-end coauthor with Mehmed-aga (kninski disdar) of letter to the rebel knezovi promising amnesty if they return to Ottoman submission (doc. 380).

surnames/Foscarini.title: Foscarini
surnames/Foscarini.content:
Foscarini
Venetian patrician house.
Bearers

Zuan Paulo Foscarini — capitanio of Zadar (line 10323, 1688) at the Knin conquest Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Frankapan.title: Frankapan
surnames/Frankapan.content:
Frankapan (Frankopan)
Croatian-Hungarian magnatial house. Krsto-I-Frankapan-b???? held estates in Istria, Kras, and Notranjska; lost them spring 1527 after siding with Ivan Zápolya against Ferdinand Habsburg. The dispossession of his Vlach subjects was a possible trigger for the 1528 return migration to Ottoman territory Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Bosiljevsko vlastelinstvo (later Frankapan) hosted a smaller Vlach libertini settlement at Erdelja.
Bearers in this wiki

Krsto-I-Frankapan-b???? — magnate; lost Istria/Kras/Notranjska estates 1527

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
The Frankapan estates of Jablanac and Starigrad on the Velebit Podgorje feature in Giacinto Peri’s 1695 report on Lika/Krbava/Turkish Croatia Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 281):

Toni Francesco Sokolić — still alive at time of Peri’s report 1695; collected dues at Starigrad and Jablanac during last Frankopans’ time (doc. 281).
1649 Diet of Bratislava (Posonia) art. 32 — restored Jablanac and Starigrad to Frankapans; lost again to Senjani after death of last Frankopan (doc. 281).
1699 Imperial-Venetian boundary commission referenced Obrovac as “antico feudo dei conti Frangipani” (per Imperial side claim) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Frletic.title: Frletic
surnames/Frletic.content:
Frletić
Vlach kindred whose ancestors appear as “sons of Firultić” in 1528–30 (Tornik, Podgorje) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Settled on Venetian side (Kukalj, Trščani, novigradski distrikt) after 1538 in plaćenička military service; later in Ljubač and Žman (1608). Some moved to Venetian Istra (around Poreč). Late 16th c.: among Senj uskoks (Andrija-Frletic-b????-Dracevac, Vuk); some who returned to Ottoman side converted to Islam (Hasan-aga-Frletic-b????-Dracevac).
Bearers in this wiki

Pavko-Firultic-b????-Tornik, Vojo-Firultic-b????-Tornik, Juraj-Firultic-b????-Tornik, Milovan-Firultic-b????-Tornik — sons of Firultić, Tornik (1528)
Andrija-Frletic-b????-Dracevac — uskok kapetan (“Andre kapetan”)
Vuk-Frletic-b????-Dracevac — uskok, brother of Andrija
Hasan-aga-Frletic-b????-Dracevac — Muslim, Venetian informant (1590)

surnames/Gabrieli.title: Gabrieli
surnames/Gabrieli.content:
Gabrieli
Single attestation: fra Cirilo (Cirillo) Gabrielli — Greek-rite Orthodox monk, parohiski svešenik of Sv. Zulijan Šibenik 1654–1668. Conducts baptisms (Iuan Šarić 1654, Lukas Zubičević 1665, Đurđe Busović 1663). Defended in 1654 by 37 Šibenik Morlach harambaše against Jovan Vuković’s plot to oust him (doc. 84). 1668-10-06 his parish brawls with Mihovil Kapuano spill into provveditor Priuli’s office (doc. 162). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

surnames/Gaeta.title: Gaeta
surnames/Gaeta.content:
Gaeta
Bearers

Gaeta — single-mention surname in chunk-2 documents Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Gagic.title: Gagic
surnames/Gagic.content:
Gagić
Bearers

Ostoja (Osta) Gagić — Lika Morlach resident at Biljane; imprisoned 29 January 1686 by commissario Marin Michiel for an unliquidated debt to Rade Tepšić; bailed out by Stojan Janković with Ivan Bortulačić signing for the illiterate Stojan (doc 124) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Galesic.title: Galesic
surnames/Galesic.content:
Galešić
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

surnames/Galiotovic.title: Galiotovic
surnames/Galiotovic.content:
Galiotović
Bearers

Bose Zuppanovich + Luca Glumaz Giurliich + Zorzi Galossich + Ivan Ivancevich da Poglie — 1647-08-31 enumerated by pop Sorić as the harambaše who failed to march (doc. 16). NB: Galossich may be a variant of Galiotović but uncertain.
dvojica braće Galiotović — 1648-08-01 due fratelli Galliotovich, uno de’ quali pero é fatto priggione at the Battle of Zečevo I (doc. 43, Mihaljević’s deposition).
Grgur (Gregorio) Galiotović da Voinich, alfier del capitano Luca Glumaz — 1653-10-24 “di statura comune, barba rasa, mostacchi pel castagno, d’ anni 30 in circa” — beheaded the kninski aga Asan Cuna under Knin and presented the head to Dolfin; awarded peso di biscotto/month for life of war (doc. 77).

surnames/Gambiroza.title: Gambiroza
surnames/Gambiroza.content:
Gambiroža
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Zuanne (Ivan) Gambirasi (Gambiroža) — fratello of Bortolo; partner with Zaviša Mitrović in Obrovac trading company 1692-08-20; Zaviša contributed 1000 ducats capital, recorded by notary Lomazzi (doc. 254) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Bortolo (Bartol) Gambirasi (Gambiroža) — fratello of Zuanne; co-partner with Zaviša 1692 (doc. 254) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Gargurica.title: Gargurica
surnames/Gargurica.content:
Gargurica (Grgurica)
Bearers

Petar Gargurica (Pietro Gargurizza) — 1661-03-01 named (with Marko Milković) capo de Morlacchi by Andrea Korner, 10 ducati/month; serdar over castel Venier, Ražanac, Posedarje, Novigrad area (doc. 118). 1663-05-08 leads guards at Dramotich pass with men of Krmpote, Čučulovci, Rodaljice, Novigrad (doc. 130). Killed valorously combatting Turks 1663-11-21 (doc. 135).
Jovo (Giuco) Garguricić — 1684-03-01 named capitano of Castel Venier (doc. 381).

surnames/Garkinic.title: Garkinic
surnames/Garkinic.content:
Garkinić
Single attestation: Bože Garkinić of Ražanac, killed 1662-02-13 at Otres (doc. 119).

surnames/Garkovic.title: Garkovic
surnames/Garkovic.content:
Garković

surnames/Hrabren.title: Hrabren
surnames/Hrabren.content:
Hrabren
Notable medieval Hercegovinian vlach lineage. Foremost member: vojvoda Petar-Hrabren-b????-Hercegovina of Donji Vlasi, ktitor of Hercegovinian Orthodox monasteries Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
The Hrabreni 1477 katun aglomeracija in nahija Blagaj (Aličić 1985) is one of the strongest pieces of evidence that the Buna-river area was predominantly Orthodox-Vlach in the late 15th c., contrary to the constructed Bunjevac-from-Buna legend.

surnames/Hrkac.title: Hrkac
surnames/Hrkac.content:
Hrkač / Rkać
Counter-etnonym to Bunjevac in the Tromedja vlach milieu. The two together formed a confessional-onomastic dichotomy (Bunjevac = Catholic vlach :: Hrkač = Orthodox vlach) emerging on the Klis-Lika frontier around 1550 — at the core of Šarić’s argument that the Bunjevac etnik formed in interaction with its Orthodox-vlach neighbor Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Surname attestations
1743 biskupska vizitacija registers Catholic surname-bearers (Pribinovići u Mostarskom blatu, Duvno, Stipanići, Prisoje):

Rkać, Arkać, Arnjkaš.
Near Ljubuški: Catholics with surname Rkač.
Catholic rodovi Džajkići and Draškići near Ljubuški preserve oral tradition that they were once “Hrkač” coming from “od Vrljike” (Čulinović Konstantinović 1989:114).

The pattern matches that of Bunjevac — the surname attaches in the opposite confessional milieu to which it points (Catholic Hrkač = former Orthodox; Orthodox Bunjevac = former Catholic), as a marker of integration through inter-confessional movement.

surnames/Husrev-beg.title: Husrev-beg
surnames/Husrev-beg.content:

surnames/Iljanovic.title: Iljanovic
surnames/Iljanovic.content:
Iljanović
Bearers

The Venetian State Inquisitors flagged this as a Ragusan intrigue (docs 147, 154); treat as low-confidence historical claim Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Notes

Source-page summary: “the Iljanović letter (doc 139, 30 July 1686) purporting to derive Stojan Janković from Hercegovinian dukes was flagged by State Inquisitors as a Ragusan intrigue” Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Jagodic-Kuridza.title: Jagodic-Kuridza
surnames/Jagodic-Kuridza.content:
Jagodić-Kuridža
Bukovica family with a parish-priest line; the surname appears in many spellings across the Italian-script documents.
Bearers in Desnica II

pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža (c. 1666 – 9 April 1749) — Orthodox paroh of Sv. Petar in Bukovica; principal instigator of the 1704 Bukovica revolt; condemned to death in absentia, fled to Lika; later imprisoned ~40 years in the Pozzi (Venetian state prison); released 29 March 1746 at age 80, blind and deaf; died at Zadar (matica umrlih, Sv. Ilija parish, 9 April 1749). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Petar Jagodić (lay brother of pop Petar) — d. ~1733. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
pop Mihailo (Mijat) Jagodić — paroh of Bilišane; cousin (germano) of pop Petar. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Magdalena (Manda) Jagodić — daughter of pop Petar; traveled to Zadar 1737 to claim father’s property (doc 387). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Notes

The compound surname Jagodić-Kuridža combines two designators (kin name + nickname/topographic). Pop Petar’s Italian-script renderings all coalesce on a Jagodić root; Kuridža drops in Italian renderings. Latin-script Giadovich is the most distorted form.

surnames/Krmpotic.title: Krmpotic
surnames/Krmpotic.content:
Krmpotić (Krmpote / Carapotani)
Catholic Vlach (Bunjevac) lineage of western Hercegovinian origin — one of the three core Bunjevac katuns (with Vojnic and Sladovic) named in the 1477 Ottoman defter. The article calls them “izrazito vitalna i oportuna vlaška grupacija” — exceptionally vital and adaptive — and a “sociodemografska paradigma tromeđe” for their reversible cyclical migrations across all three imperial frontiers Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
1477 attestation
Hercegovina defter, nahija Humska zemlja: džemat of Vukic-Krmpotic-b????-Hercegovina, 11 houses (poreznih jedinica). The defter notes they had returned from refuge: “od ranije su to bile njihove baštine pa su ponovo došli pod tim uvjetom.” Winter pastures (zimišta) in Buhovo, Borajna, Ledinac, Veselivstak (W. Hercegovina, 22–35 km from river Buna). Summer pastures (ljetišta) on Cvrsnica, Vran, Ljubusa Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Migration trajectory (Civran 1615 + Šarić reconstruction)

c. 1528 — moved into Lika, settling around Gracac; possibly attested in the stećak of Ivan Balenović in Kijani (knez Mihovil, 1528–30 popis ličko-pounskoga krajišta).
post-1573 — after Cyprus War, settled by Ottomans in zaleđe Karina (nahija Obrovac); their village named Medvidja “Krmpote” (today Staro Selo, with a bunar žive vode called Krmpot). Mletačke izvore: Morlacchi Caranpotani.
1605 — first migration to Habsburg territory: 24+ named families settle Lic on Zrinski estate of Hreljin. Surnames: Balinović (Balen), Barulović, Božić, Budisalić, Butorčić (Butorac), Cvitić, Draganović, Hromić, Kovač, Krivalica, Krmpotić, Krnjac, Malovridnjak, Matijević, Marković, Mihovilović, Mikulić, Miletić, Oproković, Pećanić, Petrović, Skorupović (Skorup), Šimunović, Vukoslavić.
1615 — kapetan gulfa Andrea-Civran-b????-Venice records their oral tradition in negotiations to relocate to Venetian Istria.
1627 — second wave to Lič: Blažević, Deranja, Filipović, Jovanović, Krpan, Pavelić, Pavličević, Peričić, Prpić, Radošević, Starcevic, Šojat, Tomić, Tomičić, Tomljanović, Vukelić (Pavličević 1989 reconstruction; medium confidence).
1636 — Forza vizitacija: župa Bukovica (Krmpote, Popovići, Ervenik, Parčić, Žužule), 1180 souls under fra Ivan Visovački; ~400 in selo Krmpote alone.
1647 (Candian War) — harambaša Harambasa-Njegovan-b????-Medvidja led 40–50 Krmpote families from Medviđa to Vinjerac and Starigrad; some onward to Pag.
1605–1690 — settled also Krmpote-Senj (Sv. Jakov), Krivi-Put, Ledenice, Senjska-Draga, Radovin, Poljica-Zadarska, Vinjerac; some to Mletacka-Istra.
1690+ — major participation in Lika–Krbava recolonization, especially Pazariste, Smiljan, Lovinac.

Confessional note
Mixed-confession at start of 17th c. (some Orthodox families joined the Lič migration); by ~1700 fully Catholic. The article cites Sladović 1856, Roksandić 1982, Pavličević 1989 on this multiconfessional aspect Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

Krmpote disambiguation
The Bukovica Krmpote settlement of Mede Milcović (near Zelengrad) is a third Krmpote distinct from (a) the Senj-area Krmpote-Senj and (b) the older Bukovica Krmpote at Medvidja (Staro Selo) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Šibenik-zaleđe lineage of harambaše. Vuk (Vučen) Mandušić — the Vuk Mandušić of the kotarski epic — was childless; the lineage continues through his sister’s son Tadija Vrančić, after whom the family-name shifts to Mandušić-Vrančić (cf. doc. 60, 1652-04-21).
Bearers

Vuk (Vučen) Mandušić — d. 1648-08-01 at Zečevo; harambaša / kapo de Morlacchi di Šibenik.
Tadija Vrančić (a/k/a Tadija Mandušić-Vrančić) — sister’s son of Vuk; capitan of his uncle’s company from 1648-08-03; later named Mandušić alias Vrančić (doc. 60).
Žorži Mandušić-Vrančić — Tadija’s father; received 4 ducati + peso di biscotto/month 1652 (doc. 60, sharing pay with son Tadija).

surnames/Mihaljevic.title: Mihaljevic
surnames/Mihaljevic.content:
Mihaljević / Miljević / Miličević
Drniški origin family of harambaše. Spelt Mihaglievich in Italian.
Bearers

Matija (Mattio) Mihaljević da Drniš, habitante nel borgo della Marina (Šibenik) — 1648-08-01 deposes about the Battle of Zečevo and Vuk Mandušić’s death (doc. 43 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).

Smoljan Smiglianich (alias Mihalevich) — see Smoljan Smiljanić — 1656 lawsuit names him “Smoglian Smiglianich o Mihalevich” (doc. 103). His paternal patronymic was Mihaljević; the more famous Smiljanić surname comes from his maternal kin.

surnames/Miljanic.content:

Bearers

Žure (Giure) Miljanić — 1647-08-16 led the Grazac raid as guide (doc. 15 — Petar Smiljanić’s deposition). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

Mattio Miglianich da Cuculovaz — 1653-01-16 co-signs the proxy authorising Smiljanić to plead in Venice (doc. 70).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Multiple Miljanić bearers in 1696 Obrovac inhabitant list (doc. 284) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II:

Giadrijem Miljanić (Jadrijem Miglianich) — Obrovac 1696.
Mattio Miljanić (Mate Miljanić) — Obrovac 1696. (Possibly same as 1653 da Cuculovaz.)
Stipan Miljanić — Obrovac 1696.
Bože (Boso) Miljanić — Obrovac 1696.
Nikola Miljanić — Obrovac 1696.
Mattio Miljanić (Mattio Miglianich) — captain of Krušev (Crussevo); 1704 rebel leader in Bukovica revolt (doc. 352) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

The Miljanić Obrovac group is one of those families noted by Desnica’s footnote as still living in Kruševo, the village adjacent to Obrovac (continuity to modern times) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Milkovic.title: Milkovic
surnames/Milkovic.content:
Milković
Bunjevac starešina family from Medviđa Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre (Šarić identifies the Milkovići as a Bunjevac starešina family).
Bearers

Mate Milković of Kruševo near Obrovac — 1554, debtor of a Šibenik butcher (Šarić citation).
harambaša Ilija Milković — second-in-command in Mitrović’s Žegar circle. 1648-07-29 deposes about Sorić’s Udbina raid (doc. 32). 1654-07-01 promoted to cavalleria leggera by Dolfin for blowing up Zvonigrad (doc. 80). 1656-03-04 assigned to guard the Krka passes (doc. 101). 1658-06-28 named alongside Janko in Bernardo’s concerto with Petar Zrinski (doc. 106). 1659-02-11 wounded with Janko at Cetina (doc. 112). 1659-03-01 — died in Zadar; buried Sv. Domenico (docs. 114, 115).
Marco Milković — 1661-03-01 named (with Petar Grgurica) capi de Morlacchi by Andrea Korner (doc. 118). 1663-11-21 — died bravamente combattendo (doc. 135). 1664-05-21 succeeded by Matia Mirković.
Šimun Milković — 1668-09-21 supplica to Doge: of his 12 uskočio family men, 10 perished, he and brother Mihail are slaves; supplicates ransom (doc. 160).
Mihail Milković — Šimun’s brother, slave in Turkey 1668.
harambaša Šimun Milković — 1672-02-05 originally promised Bokanjac as settlement site for 25 families of Ivosevci + 11 of Butoraz (doc. 200). The Parčići dispute the assignment.
kapetan Šimun Milković — 1671-12-17 settles in Dračevac with brother and son (doc. 199; “fratello et nipote — no. 3”).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Bože Milković (Boze Milcovich) — serdar of Lower Kotari by 1691; previously already governor; brother killed by Ilija Janković’s followers 1692; led 2,000 men to Malpaga; reconciled with Zaviša Mitrović 1692 by Dolfin’s mediation; partook in Liga 1696; led mission of Filip Jakić & Stankovic to expose Žegar raid 1693 (docs. 224, 236, 243, 247, 268, 286). 1699 supplied 25 sessane and 8 horses for Grimani; testified in Sfakioto’s protocols (docs. 314, 316, 319). Bedridden ill Dec 1699 (doc. 323); died ~1700, succeeded by Lazar Smiljanić as serdar of Lower Kotari Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Bože Milković’s “barba” (uncle) — anonymous; destroyed Zvonigrad in past war (“fu ravinato nella guerra passata da mio barba”) per Bože’s 1699 testimony (doc. 316) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
harambaša Mede Milcović (Mede Milicovich) — see Krmpotić entry; settled Bukovica Krmpote and Parčić, granted Medvidja fields 1693 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs. 263, 301).

surnames/Milohanic.title: Milohanic
surnames/Milohanic.content:

Nikola-Milokanic-b1521 — Istria-born former Muslim (“Osman”), testified 1591 about ~50-year cycle Istria → Ottoman → Istria with 184 kin. Grgur-Milohanovic-b????-Nova-Vas founded Miljacki (Zemunik Gornji) 1561, retreated 1570 with 40 families to Žbandalj near Poreč.

surnames/Mirkovic.title: Mirkovic
surnames/Mirkovic.content:
Mirković
