Aurelio Mirković (Aurelio Mircovich) — difensor of Pago; signer of Pago salt contract 1694 (doc. 279) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Mistakieli.title: Mistakieli
surnames/Mistakieli.content:
Mistakieli
Single attestation: dottor Nicolò Mistakieli — 1656-06-15 medic in Zadar, sued Smoljan Smiljanić for treatment fees (43 reali) for repeatedly tending the wounds of Smoljan’s uncles Ilija and Filip Smiljanić (doc. 103). Probably Greek-of-Latin-rite Zadar surname.

surnames/Mitrovic.title: Mitrovic
surnames/Mitrovic.content:
Mitrović (later Janković-Mitrović)
The clan that would become the legendary kotarska lineage Janković-Mitrović. Per Stojan Janković’s 1670 supplica (doc. 170, Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I), five brothers — Janko, Giovanni, Stefan, Pavle and Andrija — abandoned their patria of Žegar at the start of the Candian War (~1646–47) and brought ~70 households / ~150 fighting men into Venetian Ravni Kotari, settling at Posedarje.
The change of family-name from Mitrović (the patronymic from grandfather q. Dimitri) to Janković (from Janko, the eldest brother) happens in Venetian usage during Janko’s own lifetime; the official pay-rolls and documents continue to call them Mitrovich into the 1680s.
Bearers attested in this source

Janko Mitrović q. Dimitri — Žegar → Posedarje; harambaša → serdar; d. 1659-02-28 in Zadar.
Vukadin Mitrović (probably brother or cousin of Janko) — Žegar; harambaša; d. 1653 defending Novigrad.
Jakov Mitrović, son of Vukadin — slave at one point; pay assigned to him 1653 (doc. 74) and again 1681-05-08 by ducal of Doge A. Contarini for unpaid biscotto arrears (doc. 274).
Giacomo Mitrović da Islam — captured by Stojan Janković (doc. 187, 1671 plundering of Greek merchants in Posedarje); separately Giacomo Mitrović bandit of Posedarje pardoned 1673 (doc. 204).
Stojan Janković (= Stojan Mitrović) — son of Janko; the famous kavalier.
Sabba Janković — son of Janko; m. Maria Lase 1676-08-17.
Ilija Mitrović (the bandit) — son of Janko; banished 1680; instigator of the Vrana uprising 1683–84.
Konstantin Janković — son of Stojan; capitan of 50 fanti from 1679-02-09.
Zorzi-Alvise Janković b. 1674-04-23, son of Stojan and Vinka.
Anastazija Janković b. 1675-02-26, daughter of Stojan and Vinka.
Josip Janković b. 1677-09-30, son of Stojan and Antonia Reci.
Nikola Janković — son of Stojan, in cavalry from 1675.
Janja Janković (b. ~1655 d. 1680) — daughter of Janko; m. Dimitri Nikolić-Pivljanin.
Mitar/Dimitri Mitrović “da Grazaz” — slave of Stojan in his Zadar house, escaped 1680 (doc. 266, 267).
Alil son of Mitar Mitrović da Grazaz — captured slave (10 May 1680, doc. 266).

Notes

The kin-link Mitrović ↔ Pivljanin (through Janja’s marriage) is essential context for the 1683–84 Vrana uprising: Bajo Nikolić-Pivljanin and his brother Mitar shared this family.
The Sinobad case (April 1684, docs. 391, 396) accuses Ilija Mitrović of murdering Perica Sinobad (Jovan’s father) and burning his houses in Budin.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
The Mitrović/Janković lineage is the central thread of Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II from 1684 through 1731, with extensive documentation of the second and third generations.
Second generation (children of Janko)

Stojan Janković — repeatedly referenced as “quondam kavalier Gianco” by 1689 onwards; the 1689 Cornaro attestation for his brother Zaviša notes Stojan’s earlier service Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 225).
Zaviša/Sabba Janković (Saviša Mitrović detto Janco) — central figure of the chunk; Cornaro’s 1689 attestation documents his deeds at Sinj, Zadar, Vrcerev Vakup (where wounded), and Knin Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 225). 1692-08-20 partnership contract with Bortolo and Zuanne Gambiraži of Obrovac for 1000 ducats trading capital, brokered by Lomazzi (doc. 254). 1692-03-17 surety bond of 2000 ducats with Oratio Lantana for behavior of brother Ilija (doc. 246). Pay raised from 30 to 50 ducats/month by Doge Silvestro Valier dukal of 1697 (docs. 303, 306). 1696-06-27 made cavalier of San Marco by Doge Valier (doc. 288). 1701-06-05 took oath at relics of St. Šimun in Zadar challenged by conte Frane Posedarski (doc. 330). 1701-11-26 bought half of Olib island from conte Giacomo Califfi q. Francesco for 8000 ducats (doc. 336). 1702 led troops to Italy in War of Spanish Succession; died early 1702 leaving widow + 3 creatures including son Ilija. Pay raised to 50 ducats. Could not write Italian — Tomadelli signed for him (doc. 279); signed in Cyrillic (“Ja Zaviša Mitrović potrugjem”, doc. 270). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Ilija Mitrović (the rebellious) — central villain 1690–1693; refused to meet provveditor Molin 1690 (doc. 228); fled Obrovac on Molin’s arrival; killed Bože Milković’s brother and other Morlachs (doc. 243); reconciled with Milković and Sinobad parties by Dolfin’s mediation 1692 (doc. 247); 15 ducats/month restored by terminacija of 1 April 1692 (doc. 248); accused of murdering Andrea Tomišić in Gorica 1692 (doc. 268); died of natural causes (“rilasciata natura”) late 1693 (doc. 269); per docs. 305, 379 he was the third brother of Stojan and Zaviša, lived in Zadar with wife and children. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Third generation (children of Stojan, Zaviša, Ilija)

Konstantin Janković — son of Stojan; capitano of Croat cavalry from 1686 (ducal 7 Nov 1686, no public expense); died 1692-02-27 aged ~12; buried in Greek church of Sant’Elia by curato don Andrea Caldana. Death recorded by Caldana (doc. 244). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Nikola Janković — son of Stojan; raised 500 oltramarini per ducal 7 Nov 1686 (doc. 249).
Mijat (Michiel) Janković — son of Ilija; died 1692-08-23; buried at Sant’Elia (doc. 255).
Nicolò Mitrović — son of Ilija; appointed capitano of Croat cavalry company (formerly Konstantin’s) on 1692-04-01, with tenente training troops until of age (doc. 249); ducal of 21 Sept 1702 confirmed life tenure (doc. 369); died 1709, replaced by brother Stojan (younger).
Stojan Mitrović (younger) — son of Ilija (the rebellious), nephew of original kavalier Stojan; made captain of new 50-man company guarding Keglević fort 1701 (doc. 325); given Šimun Jere’s cavalry company by Carlo Pisani in 1712/13 (doc. 371); 1709 inherited brother Nicolò’s cavalry company.
Marija Mitrović — daughter of Ilija the rebellious; married Vučen Stojisavljević of Vrlika; mother of Petar Mitrović-Stojisavljević raised in the Mitrović household (doc. 379).
Ilija Janković (younger) — son of Zaviša; minor at father’s death 1702; reserved 50 ducats then 20; 1701 captain of Italy-bound company; 1705-08-20 granted hereditary count title with Nicolò and Stojan (doc. 360); 1717 made full serdar of Upper Kotari (40 ducats/month); died ~1731. Possibly party to alleged duel with priest Marko Mesić at Lukovo (doc. 364, footnote). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Fourth generation

Kirijak Dedić-Mitrović (Janković) — sister’s son of deceased serdar Ilija Janković (the younger); alfiere; appointed serdar of Upper Kotari 1731-11-01 by Vendramin (docs. 381–384); minor at appointment, deputy assigned. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Other Mitrović bearers

Filippo Mitrović — capitano of 56-foot company in Obrovac, dismissed by Molin Jan 1690 (doc. 227). Distinct from Filip Smiljanić. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Rade Mitrović — Obrovac inhabitant 1696 (doc. 284). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Petar Mitrović (= Petar Stojisavljević) — assumed Mitrović cognomen having been raised in the Mitrović house; appointed serdar of Knin Krajina 1726-02-23 by Niccolò Erizzo (docs. 376, 379); removed by ducal of 1 Dec 1729 in favor of Giacomo Sinobad (doc. 380). See Stojisavljevic. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

1705 hereditary count title
Doge Alvise Mocenigo dukal of 1705-08-20 granted hereditary conte title to Ilija (younger), Nicolò, and Stojan Janković-Mitrović in recognition of family service Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 360).
Notes

Doc. 288 ducal confounds “carambassà Gianco Mitrouich capo principale de Morlachi di Obrouazzo” with “sardar Stojan Mitrovich detto Gianco” — these are two distinct persons (Janko = founder; Stojan = Janko’s son called Gianco).
The 1670 Janković investitura on the house of Jusuf-aga Tunić at Islam continued to be referenced as a Mitrović holding in 1700 with 400 gognali (docs. 329, 330).

surnames/Mivcanica.title: Mivcanica
surnames/Mivcanica.content:
Mivčanica
Pejan-Mivcanica-b????-Podgorje was a primićur recorded in the 1530 sumarni defter Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Pejan-Mivcanica-b????-Podgorje — primićur (1530)

surnames/Mocenigo.title: Mocenigo
surnames/Mocenigo.content:
Mocenigo
Venetian patrician house. Bearers in this source served as provveditor general and doge.
Bearers

Domenico Mocenigo — Provveditor General estraordinario dell’armi in Dalmazia et Albania, arrived May 1684; main correspondent docs 1–43; eventual scapegoat for Sinj defeat April 1685 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Alvise Mocenigo II — doge from 1700; signs ducali on Dalmatian affairs through volume’s later docs Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

In Desnica II (1684–1749) — extended

Mocenigo (the predecessor provveditor) — 1684-07-15 terminacija granted Ilija Mitrović 15 ducats/month (doc. 248) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Aluise (Alvise) Mocenigo — provveditor generale of Dalmatia late 1696–1702, succeeding Daniel Dolfin; ordered Resep Budisalić’s release Jan 1697 (docs. 300, 301); later Doge; dukal 1705-08-20 granted hereditary count title to Ilija, Nicolò, Stojan Mitrović-Janković (doc. 360); dukal of 22 March 1702 (doc. 342) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Cà Mocenigo — Venetian residence in Venice; 1704 lodging of Franciscan Pavlo Vušković where Mattio Žabetić was seen during the Bukovica revolt aftermath (doc. 357) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Modre.title: Modre
surnames/Modre.content:
Modre
The “Turco Modre” gave his name to Modrino selo village near St. Peter’s church in Bukovica, his casale assigned to Jovan Sinobad 1692 (doc. 259) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Described as congiunto (relative) of Sinobad — implying the family had Christian and Muslim branches separated by religion. The casale dispute with Radoš and Sava Kresović continued into 1697.
Notes

Likely a personal name/byname rather than a heritable surname; preserved in the toponym Modrino selo.

surnames/Molin.title: Molin
surnames/Molin.content:
Molin
Venetian patrician.
Bearers in Desnica II

Alessandro Molin (Aleksandar Molino) — provveditor generale in Dalmatia 1689–1692; established Obrovac salt scale; appointed Casanova governor of Obrovac; divided Kotari into upper/lower; appointed serdars Zaviša Mitrović (Upper) and Bože Milković (Lower); appointed Sinobad governor of Knin; etc. (docs. 226–242, 257) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Succeeded by Daniel Dolfin Feb 1692.

surnames/Morosini.title: Morosini
surnames/Morosini.content:
Morosini
Venetian patrician (Doge).
Bearers in Desnica II

Francesco Morosini — Doge of Venice; ducale of 1690-05-21 awarding 10 ducats/month to capt. Marko Smiljanić (doc. 233); ducale of 1692-10-22 confirming Lomazzi as Illyrian interpreter (doc. 257) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Movicuna.title: Movicuna
surnames/Movicuna.content:
Močivuna
Morlach lineage that uskočio from Ottoman village Jakorševci “molti anni” before 1669 (Priuli’s terminacija doc. 167) and settled in Bokanjac above Zadar (Spianata). Multi-generational pravoslavni line — christened at Sv. Ilija Zadar.
Bearers

Vuk (Vučko) Močivuna — d. 1666-05-01 at Zečevo (doc. 151, glagolska zabeleška from Filipjakov: “poginu dobri junak Vučko Močivuna” — in a battle in which 73 Kotarane were killed). Pay 4 ducati/month assigned 1653-10-22 by Dolfin (doc. 76 — “di statura bassa, giovane sbarbato d’ anni vinti due in circa” → b. ~1631) for beheading a Turk and presenting the head to the provveditore. Earlier 1650-09-20 same pay, transferred 1666-05-21 to brother Vučen (doc. 155).
Vučen Močivuna — brother of Vuk; 4 ducati/month inherited 1666-05-21. Distinct from a Vučin Močivuna who held two Turkish slaves (Vuk Cusat and Vido Pagin) on the Spianata 1665 (doc. 146).
Vučko Močivuna — likely the same as Vuk; harambaša 1662-04-12 (doc. 125) — Korner forbids him assembling raids without written permission.
Milisav (Milissa, Milosav) Močivuna — uskočio “many years before” 1669 from Jakorševci (doc. 167); harambaša; pay 4 ducati + peso di biscotto/month from 1669-10-10 by Priuli. Wife Kata baptised slave-girl Maria 1677-01-07 at Sv. Ilija (doc. 231). Son Matija (Matio) baptised 1663-07-12 stile vecchio (doc. 134); compare Sapissa Giancovichia and comare Anizza Murlaca. With Smoljan Đevrsković and Luka Kožulović 1671-06-21 represented the pravoslavni Morlaci against the Trećoredci re Sv. Ivan church in Spianata (doc. 193). Bokanjac capitan 1684-03-01 (doc. 381).
Todor Močivuna — d. in Cetina (the 1666 conflict); widow Anica relicta (doc. 164, 1668-12-23). Children: son Dragoslav + 3 daughters in pupillar età. Anica granted 1 peso di biscotto/month for support of children (doc. 164).
Anica (Anizza) udovica Toda Močivune — 1668; possibly the same as the comare Anizza Murlaca at the 1663 baptism of Mate (doc. 134).
Dragoslav Močivuna — son of Todor (1668).

surnames/Municasa.title: Municasa
surnames/Municasa.content:
Municasa
Bearers

major Municasa — major of corazze (heavy cuirassier cavalry) Feb 1685 (doc 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Murgic.title: Murgic
surnames/Murgic.content:
Murgić
Lika surname (not necessarily Bunjevac itself). Foremost member: Ivan-Murgic-b????-Perusic († 1881) — career officer in the Vojna krajina, whose posthumous Vienac article (1882) is the last izvorna svjedočanstva of self-identifying Bunjevci in Lika–Primorje Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Erdeljanović 1930 mistakenly assumed Murgić was Bunjevac (Šarić corrects this).

surnames/Muskovic.title: Muskovic
surnames/Muskovic.content:
Mušković
Old Vlach kindred — territorialized katun at Muskovci near Obrovac (catunar Dien Mušković, 1433 Lika kraljevski Vlasi charter) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1544: 25 families fled Lika summer pasture across to Habsburg, settled at Prilisce under Nikola-Zrinski-b???? as hereditary libertini. Catholic, čakavski-ikavski.

surnames/Najcinovic.title: Najcinovic
surnames/Najcinovic.content:
Najčinović (Jančić)
Vlach kindred attested in Benković nahija from 1528. Surname forms appear interchangeably (“Petar Jančić” in 1528–30 register = “Petar Najčinović” in later sources) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. After 1538 defection: kapetan in Podnovje (novigradski distrikt); some moved to Venetian Istria (Dvigrad, Labinština).
Bearers in this wiki

Petar-Najcinovic-b????-Dobruca-Vas — knez, head of Benković dzemat
Pavel-Najcinovic-b???? — brother of Petar
Nenad-Jancic-b????-Dobruca-Vas — relative
Pavel-Jancic-b????-Glucje, Radul-Jancic-b????-Glucje, Juraj-Jancic-b????-Glucje — relatives in Glučje (Karin)
Milic-Jancic-b????-Kucista, Mihovil-Jancic-b????-Kucista, Biljan-Jancic-b????-Kucista, Martin-Jancic-b????-Kucista — Kućišta (Zrmanja)

surnames/Najerlovic.title: Najerlovic
surnames/Najerlovic.content:
Najerlović
Bearers

Radko (Radivoj) Najerlović — conte of Vrana; signatory of the 1684 Vrana petitions to Mocenigo (docs 35, 36) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Nakic.title: Nakic
surnames/Nakic.content:
Nakić
Bearers

harambaša Matija Nakić — 1683-12-09 with the Petropolje conti pleads via fra Petar Tintić for protection (doc. 349). 1684-01-04 with Frane Mirčetić petitions for uskakanje of 1000+ households (doc. 362). 1684-01-05 Donà gives him a panno-suit and 2 cechini (doc. 363). Sent to Venice; awaited at Šibenik with hostages 1684-03-14 (doc. 382).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

karambaša Nakić — leader of 500 Trogir-territory Morlaks; July 1684 mentioned in dispatches (docs 17, 18); at the Sinj defeat April 1685 he gave his own horse to the wounded provveditor Marin Michiel, saving him (doc 61); January 1686 reports the Bosnian Pasha’s march from Banja Luka toward Livno (doc 125); November 1686 sent by Stojan Janković with Vuconie Cvitanović to warn the Zadar contado of the Turkish irruption (doc 155) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Nanic.title: Nanic
surnames/Nanic.content:
Nanić
Bukovica surname attested in Žegar.
Bearers attested

Ilija Nanić of Žegar — co-leader of the 1704 Bukovica revolt alongside pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža and Mattio Žabetić.

Notes

Per Desnica’s 1951 editorial footnote, the Nanić surname is still present in Žegar today (1951). Together with Zelić, Radmilović, and Vukčević, the families “came in 1648 with the Jankovićs to Budim near Posedarje and during the Morean War many returned to Lika; Budim is today (1951) ruins” (footnote to doc 115). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

In Desnica II (1684–1749) — extended

Ilija Nanić “da Xegar/Segar” — captain of Islam and Kašić 1698 (doc. 309); 1702 named arbitrator by Brgud villagers in Lisičić-Brgud dispute (doc. 348); one of three ringleaders of the 1704 Bukovica revolt alongside pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža and Mattio Žabetić (docs. 352, 356, 357); banished, condemned to death in absentia, fled to Lika (Imperial side) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Negri.title: Negri
surnames/Negri.content:
Negri
Bearers in Desnica II

Marin Angelo de Negri (Marin Negri) — segretario of the Doge; signed several dukals 1697–1702 (docs. 306, 345, 347) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Nenadic.title: Nenadic
surnames/Nenadic.content:
Nenadić
Poljica family. 1506: Ivanis-Nenadic-b????-Poljica (brother of the then Mostar voivod) fled to Ottoman territory at Ottoman invitation Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Ivanis-Nenadic-b????-Poljica — defected 1506

surnames/Nizic.title: Nizic
surnames/Nizic.content:
Nižić
Single attestation: don Šimun (Simon) Nižić — 1647-04-01 sent by Foscolo to the Velebit Podgorje to persuade Morlachi to uskočiti (doc. 3). The accompanying note mentions “li 4 moscettoni che gia feci pretar al quondam Nisich” (doc. 7) — a relative previously deceased.

surnames/Nuncovic.title: Nuncovic
surnames/Nuncovic.content:
Nuncović
Bearers

Nuncović — Venetian confidente (informant); July 1685 wrote letters from Ottoman territory to governator Marinović of Forte Opus reporting the Bosnian Pasha’s preparations against Duare (Zadvarje) (doc 82, line 3903) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Obradovic.title: Obradovic
surnames/Obradovic.content:
Obradović
Lika family, attested at Bruvno.
Bearers in Desnica II

Conte Obradović of Bruvno — Bruvno headman; his son was killed alongside the haiduk Vid Petrović in 1707 at Bruvno when the Senjska četa under colonel Canagetti captured/killed Vid. See Vid-Petrovic-Banditry-1702-1707. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

surnames/Oluic.title: Oluic
surnames/Oluic.content:
Oluić
Bearers

Vučić Oluić — Morlach newcomer settled at Bilišane above Obrovac; in late January 1686 reported to Stojan Janković that the Croatian ban had crossed into Bosnia four days earlier with great damage; Oluić’s partita had been at Sinogora (= Siva Gora / Sitna Gora?) between Lika and Krbava and had seen the smoke (doc 123, 28 Jan 1686 deposition of Stojan) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Omeljic.title: Omeljic
surnames/Omeljic.content:
Omeljić
Bearers

Marko Omeljić (Omelich, Homeglich) da Čitluk — 1647-12-17 signed (with X) the Petropolje uskakanje contract (doc. 18). 1648-11-03 listed as one of the harambaše who took pieggiarija for the slave-girl Zahire (doc. 48).

surnames/Osmanovic.title: Osmanovic
surnames/Osmanovic.content:
Osmanović
Bearers in Desnica II

Andrea Osmanović — escaped attackers in 1693-11-04 Gorica raid (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Palese.title: Palese
surnames/Palese.content:
Palese
Bearers

capo Palese — Zadar officer killed at the Sinj defeat April 1685 (doc 60) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Palikuca.title: Palikuca
surnames/Palikuca.content:
Palikuća
Bearers

Palikuća — capo of the Šibenik-Skradin territory Morlachs; with Goreta and Žinović during the November 1686 Bribir defeat (doc 155) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Pancic.title: Pancic
surnames/Pancic.content:
Pančić
Bearers

Mattio Pančić — harambaša of Vrana; signatory of the 1684 Vrana petition (doc 35) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Papafava.title: Papafava
surnames/Papafava.content:
Papafava
Italian noble.
Bearers in Desnica II

Roberto Papafava — capitano di Zara 1689; received Pietro Calčina’s report on the defeat of Popržen Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs. 224, 225).

surnames/Parisic.title: Parisic
surnames/Parisic.content:
Parišić
Bearers

Parišić — harambaša of Vrana; signatory of the 1684 Vrana petition (doc 36) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Pasic.title: Pasic
surnames/Pasic.content:
Pašić
Bihać-area Muslim aga family; possessed a fortified palace and recinto near Boričevac.
Bearers

Ibrahim Pašić — uglednik of Ripač; January 1686 his palace and recinto in the villages around Boričevac were burned by Stojan Janković in a 12-day raid into Lapac; many Turks and Christian Morlachs had taken refuge in the palace and surrendered, the Turks setting fire to it as a sign of withdrawal (doc 118, 14 Jan 1686 deposition of Stojan) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Mehmed-beg Pašić — nephew of Ibrahim; Udbina spahija; April 1687 captured by Zaviša Janković’s četa together with the dizdar of Udbina and Ara Kumalić while supervising the ploughing of his lands (doc 133, 12 April 1687) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Pasini.title: Pasini
surnames/Pasini.content:
Pasini
Bearers

Jerolim (Girolamo) Pasini — 1678-04-15 sopraintendent of the Liga (doc. 242). 1682-11-06 sopraintendent in Vrgada / Nin Liga (doc. 297).

surnames/Pasqualigo.title: Pasqualigo
surnames/Pasqualigo.content:
Pasqualigo
Venetian patrician house.
Bearers

Alvise Pasqualigo — Provveditor General; held interim authority October 1684 (docs 41, 43) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Pastrovic.title: Pastrovic
surnames/Pastrovic.content:
Pastrović
Bearers in Desnica II

Vincenza Pastrović (Pastrouich) — recipient in Marija Smiljanić’s 1693 will, has son Antonio (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Antonio Pastrović — son of Vincenza (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Paukovic.title: Paukovic
surnames/Paukovic.content:
Pauković
Single attestation: Šimun (Simon) Paucovich da Lucar — 1647-12-17 signed (with X) the Petropolje uskakanje contract (doc. 18).

surnames/Paulucci.title: Paulucci
surnames/Paulucci.content:
Paulucci
Italian curial family.
Bearers in Desnica II

Cardinal Paulucci — papal Secretary of State (Cardinale-Segretario di Stato) c. 1717; requested 300 Morlach recruits for papal anti-pirate galleys (galiotte) — see Papal-Anti-Pirate-Recruitment-1717. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

surnames/Pavelic.title: Pavelic
surnames/Pavelic.content:
Pavelić
Bunjevac surname; one of the 16 reconstructed families of the second (1627) Krmpote migration to Lič per Pavličević 1989 Saric-2008-Bunjevci (medium confidence — reconstruction, not register-direct).

surnames/Pavlicevic.title: Pavlicevic
surnames/Pavlicevic.content:
Pavličević
Bunjevac surname; among the 16 reconstructed families of the second (1627) Krmpote migration (Pavličević 1989) Saric-2008-Bunjevci (medium confidence). Notably the historian Dragutin Pavličević (1989 study of Krmpote migrations) shares the surname.

surnames/Peraica.title: Peraica
surnames/Peraica.content:
Peraica
Bearers

Ilija Peraica — famoso harambaša/sardar; in March 1685 led 600 armed men plus families with 30,000 small animals and 10,000 cattle from the Cetina region to Trogir territory; awarded 10 ducats/month and made sardar for c. 1600 souls (docs 59, 60, 61, 66) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
karambassà Peraizza — same person; on 8 September 1685 his partita of c. 175 people (men and women) was attacked and his band defeated by Turkish fuste off the coast (doc 112, undated; date from internal “ottavo giorno del mese sudetto”) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Frane Peraica — see person page; mentioned later in the volume Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Peri.title: Peri
surnames/Peri.content:
Peri
Bearers in Desnica II

Giacinto Peri — captain of Novi Vinodolski (Korčulan, exiled from Venetian state); wrote 1695 detailed report on Lika/Krbava/Turkish Croatia for Imperial Chamber of Graz (doc. 281) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Peric.title: Peric
surnames/Peric.content:
Perić
Bearers in Desnica II

Giacomo Perić (Jakov Perich) — wounded in 1693-11-04 Gorica raid; arquebus ball in right arm + sablada on left index finger (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Perini.title: Perini
surnames/Perini.content:
Perini
Bearers

sopraintendente Perini — sopraintendente aboard Korponež’s galeotta March 1686 beneath the Pastrovići towers (doc 131) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Petkovic.title: Petkovic
surnames/Petkovic.content:
Petković
Single attestation: harambaša Vido Petković — 1663-05-08 jointly with Ilija Glumac leads the guard at Roški Slap with men of Vrana, Tinj, Pakoštane, Zaravecchia, Sv. Filip-Jakov, Torrette (doc. 130).

surnames/Petrovic.title: Petrovic
surnames/Petrovic.content:
Petrović
Common patronymic; the Desnica II attestation is for a single haiduk figure.
Bearers in Desnica II

Vid Petrović — haiduk operating on Mt. Prolog 1702–1707; killed at Bruvno in 1707 by colonel Antonio Canagetti’s men, alongside conte Obradović’s son. See Vid-Petrovic-Banditry-1702-1707. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

surnames/Pierantonii.title: Pierantonii
surnames/Pierantonii.content:
Pierantonii
Zadar patrician family.
Bearers

Antonio Maria Pierantonii — husband of Caterina Grizogono; abandoned his wife (Sept 1686 had left her c. 1.5 years earlier); his property was the subject of doc 143 (14 Sept 1686), in which Caterina Grizogono ceded to Stojan Janković her perpetual right to redeem a house in the parish of San Stefano / San Simeone (Zadar), originally pledged to Michiel Angelo Gioachini (doc 143) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Piric.title: Piric
surnames/Piric.content:
Pirić
Bjelaj-area capi family of the 1692 mass migration.
Bearers in Desnica II

Nicolo Pirić (Nicolo Pirich) — capo of Bjelaj province with Đurić and Zorić; led ~5000 souls to Venetian devotion 1692; settled in Plavno, given the tower of Muhamedbeg Durakbegović in Plavno Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs. 251, 252, 253).

surnames/Pisani.title: Pisani
surnames/Pisani.content:
Pisani
Venetian patrician.
Bearers in Desnica II

Girolamo Pisani — savio/consigliere of Venetian Senate 1697 (doc. 303) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Carlo Pisani — provveditor general 1712/13; appointed Stojan Mitrović (the younger) to Šimun Jere’s cavalry company (doc. 371) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Pivljanin-Nikolic.title: Pivljanin-Nikolic
surnames/Pivljanin-Nikolic.content:
Nikolić-Pivljanin
Hajduk family from Piva (Plav region), resident in Zadar from end of the Candian War to start of the Morean War (Desnica’s footnote on doc. 211). Brothers’ names: Bajo, Mitar/Dmitar, Petar.
The family’s link to the Mitrović-Janković of Žegar is established by Mitar’s marriage to Janja Janković (sister of Stojan), 1675-01-17 at Sv. Ilija Zadar (doc. 210). Their son Nikola Nikolić was baptised 1677-10-01 (doc. 236).
Bearers

Bajo Nikolić-Pivljanin — the celebrated hajduk; in this corpus 1675–1684 lives in Zadar as paid cavalryman of capt. Soliman’s company. 1675-04-26 offers to take in the Turkish slave Omer Mustafa (doc. 138 — wait, that’s a different transaction). 1680-05-03 leasing the prado in Sovare at Suhovare from Turks (doc. 265). 1682-06-02 Korner orders him not to abuse his brother Petar (doc. 284). Joins his nephew/brother-in-law Ilija Mitrović in the Vrana uprising 1683; pardoned by Donà 1683-12-08 (doc. 347). Reassigned to Kotor 1684-04-12 with brother Mitar (doc. 393).
Mitar (Dmitar/Dimitri) Nikolić-Pivljanin — Bajo’s brother. Married Janja Janković 1675-01-17 (doc. 210). Son Nikola Nikolić b. 1677-10-01 at Sv. Ilija (doc. 236). Goes AWOL Jan 1684; pardoned 1684-02-19 (doc. 376). Per Desnica’s footnote on doc. 376: “Mitar Nikolić, brat Baja Pivljanina, boravio je, kao i ovaj, u Zadru, kao plaćeni vojnik mletačke konjice” — and joined Ilija Mitrović’s rebellion (Mitar was married to Ilija’s sister, that is, was Stojan and Ilija’s zet).
Petar Nikolić — 1682-06-02 Korner forbids Bajo to abuse him (doc. 284).
Nikola Nikolić — son of Mitar and Janja, b. 1677-10-01.
Simeon Nikolić-Pivljanin — son of Bajo and his wife Manda, baptismal record (doc. 226 head — birth attestation in the Sv. Ilija registers).

Notes

The 1685 attestation by Bajo “havendo già 7 anni in Zadar” implicit places him in Zadar from c. 1671. (Desnica’s footnote on doc. 211 puts the Pivljanini in Zadar from “od svršetka kandijskog pa do početka morejskog rata” — i.e. 1669–1684.)

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Bajo Pivljanin — receives Venetian cavalry pay alongside Janković Jan 1685 (doc 44); a separate “fatto del harambassa Bajo” mentioned March 1685 (doc 57) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Demetrio (Dmitar) Nikolić-Pivljanin — 1696 granted 12 fields and ruined tower of Mustajbeg Ćerinagić in Padglivie/Trebinje as benemerito brother of late Bajo Pivljanin (doc. 287). The source’s text “figliolo” is corrected by Desnica’s footnote to “fratello” — i.e., he is Bajo’s brother, not son Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Pizzamano.title: Pizzamano
surnames/Pizzamano.content:
Pizzamano
Bearers

tenente colonnello Pizzamano — soggetto d’attitudine e di fede; with two cavalry companies and sopraintendenza at the 1686 Sinj operation (lines 6457, 6469, 6487); later as colonnello Marco Pizzamano with major commands (line 10486, 1688) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Pizzocara.title: Pizzocara
surnames/Pizzocara.content:
Pizzocara
Bearers in Desnica II

Caterina Pizzocara/Pezzocara — pious recipient mentioned twice in Marija Smiljanić’s 1693 will (one residing near terraferma) (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Pletikosic.title: Pletikosic
surnames/Pletikosic.content:
Pletikosić
Bearers

Zorzi (Žorži) Pletikosić da Prkos — 1653-01-16 co-signs proxy (doc. 70).
harambaša Žorži Pletikosić — 1658-07-11 leads partita that captures the spahija Mustafa Torlaković of Rama at Zadar (doc. 110).
Vido Pleticossa — 1684-03-01 capitan of Malpaga (doc. 381).

surnames/Podgorica.title: Podgorica
surnames/Podgorica.content:
Podgorica
Bearers

Podgorica — single-mention surname appearing in the chunk-2 1685–86 documents Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Podjognak.title: Podjognak
surnames/Podjognak.content:
Podjognak
Bearers in Desnica II

Zuio Podjognak (Podiognach) — Morlach who fled from Ostrovica to imperial side with Radoica Bubić 1690 (doc. 229) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Pokupic.title: Pokupic
surnames/Pokupic.content:
Pokupić
Bearers in Desnica II

padron Francesco Pokupić (Pocupich) — captain of tartana from Cherso (Cres); transported cannons from Fiume to Karlobag 1696 (doc. 290) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Pop.title: Pop
surnames/Pop.content:
Pop
Likely an occupational surname from pop (priest). The same name in this period frequently appears as part of double surnames like Pop-X among the Bukovica/Lika Orthodox population.
Bearers

Mattio Pop — Vrana harambaša; signatory of the 1684 Vrana petition (doc 35) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Popovic.title: Popovic
surnames/Popovic.content:
Popović
Surname appearing across the Tromeđa as both clergy and lay knez.
Bearers

pop Petar Popović (paroh of Miranje and surrounding Ottoman villages) — 1646-03-26 with harambaše Petar Grudarović and Milinko Dević offers Foscolo to bring 20 Morlach families across; pay 4 ducati/month (doc. 2). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
knez Radivoj Popović (1683) — capo of village Dejanović (Petropolje, between Skradin and Drniš); listed by pop Lazar Dragović in 1500-family Zagorje uskakanje petition (doc. 358). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Đuro Popović detto Opačić (Jura Popovich Opacich) — harambaša of Mokro Polje; received 15 stara of millet from Dolfin to distribute as seed; obliged to return same amount; signed 1693-02-23 in Zadar (doc. 265) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Poropat.title: Poropat
surnames/Poropat.content:
Poropat (Poropatić)
Old Vlach kindred attested in Zadar sources from late 14th c. as part of Butko Brančić’s katun Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Surname derives from the Vlach anthroponym poropat (“nomad / beskrevetnik”). Returned from Buzetski Kras to Zrmanja c. 1528. Some defected to Venetian territory 1538 (Novigrad distrikt); a long-term concentration remained on the Buzet Venetian side (Trstenik, Dane, Lanišće).
Bearers in this wiki

Jakov-Poropat-b????-Zacadje — primićur, Začađe (1528–1530)
Ivanis-Poropat-b????-Mirko — brother of Jakov, timar in Donje/Gornje Miranje
Alija-sin-Poropata-b????-Karin — Muslim convert, Karin (1528)
Husein-sin-Poropata-b????-Krupa — Muslim convert, Krupa (1528)
Jakov-Poropatic-b????-Rezane — kmet, Režane (1562)
Juraj-Poropatic-b???? — kapetan, brought Morlachs to Istria after Cyprus War
Pavko-Firultic-b????-Tornik, Vojo-Firultic-b????-Tornik, Juraj-Firultic-b????-Tornik, Milovan-Firultic-b????-Tornik — sons of Firultić, Tornik (1528)

surnames/Posedarski.title: Posedarski
surnames/Posedarski.content:
Posedarski (Benja-Posedarski)
Croatian noble kindred holding Posedarje on Novigrad more, on the original Tromeđa frontier. Continuous from the late-medieval period into the Mletačka era, ennobled and integrated into the Venetian colonnellato della nazione. The Posedarski “zlatna knjiga” and family archive are now held by knez Anton Benja-Posedarski in Zadar — extensively cited by Desnica.
Pre-1646 bearers (per Šarić)

Stjepan-Posedarski-b???? — chaplain who spoke before Pope Leo X (1519); possibly the same as the Stjepan converted to Islam.
Frane Posedarski (early 16th c.) — knez, converted to Islam.

1646–1684 bearers (per Desnica)

Frano (Francesco) Posedarski the Elder (d. 1671-01-06 in Zadar, age ~70 — doc. 185): governator → colonnello of cernide. Lost two nepoti at the 1647 Diklo / Bokanjac ambush (doc. 13). Buried Sv. Domenico Zadar.
Žorži (Zorzi) Posedarski — son of Frane the Elder; named capo di tutti li Morlacchi (general superintendent of all Venetian Morlachi) by ducal of 9 Dec 1664 (doc. 143); pay 500 ducati/year. Died 1679-07-21 at Posedarje, taken to Zadar and buried at Sv. Domenico (doc. 259). His widow appears in the 1680s correspondence.
Frano (Francesco) Posedarski the Younger — nipote of the elder Frane (and son of Žorži per doc. 232 — his father is Žorži the colonnello). Governator of Nin from 1672-03-20 (doc. 202); after Žorži’s death named capo de Morlacchi e sopraintendente delle cernide by Valier 1679-08-01 (doc. 260) — but the Senate did not approve, so Stojan Janković got the post 1681 (doc. 275 footnote). One of the four 1684 direttori over the Morlachi (doc. 395).
Pietro Posedarski — capo / capitan of cavalry (compagnia di cavalli) of Zadar; assigned to investigate the Greek-merchant murder 1671-01-14 (docs. 187, 188).
Paolo Posedarski — capitan of a Zadar compagnia paesana de fanti, posted at Ervenik 1670-08-12 (doc. 174).
Antonio Posedarski — capitan of cavalry, posted at Zara Vecchia (doc. 322, 1683).
Juraj/Žorži Posedarski — capitano d’ cavalli on the Knin campaign 1655; banished by ducal of Doge Francesco Molino for cowardice (fled the field with Battista Benzon) — doc. 92, 93.
Anton Benja-Posedarski — Zadar nobleman who in the 1930s held the family archive; not in the historical narrative but the source-fond’s custodian.

Notes

The family-archive, Posedarski Zbornik, is one of Desnica’s principal sources: it preserves Foscolo’s correspondence with Frane the Elder (the governator Possedaria of doc. 5 et seq., 1647 onward) and other otherwise-untranscribed material.
The dispatch in doc. 105 (1656-08-10) shows Žorži Posedarski lobbying to be named colonnello sopra di Morlacchi, a move Janko Mitrović and the Morlach harambaše explicitly resisted on the grounds that they would not accept a non-patrician commander.

Sources

Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre — pre-1646.
Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 5, 7–10, 13, 92, 93, 104, 105, 143, 174, 185, 187, 188, 202, 232, 259, 260, 275, 289, 322, 395.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
The Posedarski continue as the senior Zadar-noble Morlach commanders into the 18th c.
New context for Frane (Francesco) the Younger

1689 (Cornaro Liga reform, doc. 224): family service noted.
1691-02-08 named colonnello sopraintendente of Kotari by Molin (doc. 235); both his father conte Francesco (the elder) and uncle Žorži were predecessor joint colonnelli.
1692 helped Dolfin reconcile the Mitrović and Milković parties (doc. 247).
1696 one of Liga giudici under Dolfin (doc. 286); visited Starigrad, Dračevac, Jasenice, Obrovac for Doge Valier and reported on cannon-deliveries to Karlobag (doc. 290).
1701 leased decima at Kotari (per chunk 4); 1701-06-05 challenged Zaviša Janković to oath at relics of St. Šimun (doc. 330).
1701-09-10 sent on diplomatic mission to Bosnian Pasha with extensive gift list to Halil-pasha (doc. 333).
1702 served Lisičić–Brgud arbitration. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

New bearer

conte Pietro Posedarski — nobile zaratino, age 43 in 1699 (b. ~1656); witness re Morlacca possession in Sfakioto’s Grimani-commission protocols (doc. 315). Probable brother or cousin of Frane the Younger. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Family note

Per Molin’s 1691 doc. 235: the new colonnello Francesco is “figlio e nipote respective de medemi” — son of conte Francesco the Elder and nephew of his fratello conte Žorži. Both elder brothers were joint colonnelli. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

surnames/Pravica.title: Pravica
surnames/Pravica.content:
Pravica
Bearers in Desnica II

Martin Pravica (Perauizza) — Obrovac inhabitant 1696 (doc. 284) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Prejic.title: Prejic
surnames/Prejic.content:
Prejić (Prijić)
Distinguished Vlach lineage — only common surname (versus single-name) recorded in 1528–30 register among Vlasi Istre, sign of high social standing Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Petar-Prejic-b???? held the largest non-Muslim timar in vilajet Hrvati 1530. Some converts to Islam (Ferhad, Hasan, Bogdan); some uskoks in Bela krajina (Stanoje-Prijic-b????-Marindol 1551).
Bearers in this wiki

Petar-Prejic-b???? — knez, largest non-Muslim timar holder (1530)
Bogdan-Prejic-b???? — son of Petar, Muslim convert, returned to Ottoman side, timar 1557
Martin-Prejic-b????-Nunic — Nunić (1528)
Fran-Prejic-b????-Opatija — Opatija/Kula Atlagića (1528)
Ferhad-Prejic-b????-Novosel — possibly read “Pribić”, Novosel (1528)
Hasan-Prejic-b????-Surozani — Surožani (1540), Muslim convert
Ivan-Prejic-b????-Zacadje — Začađe (1540)
Prejic-sin-Matijasa-b????-Brdar — Brdar (1540)
Stanoje-Prijic-b????-Marindol — desetnik in Marindol (1551)

surnames/Presevic.title: Presevic
surnames/Presevic.content:
Prešević
Bearers in Desnica II

monsignor Simon Prešević (Simeon Prenčević / Simon Prancovich) — Orthodox bishop of Belgrade; received vineyard in Vodmac/Valmaz village (Podhumnica, near Hercegnovi) previously owned by Turk Resul Aga Babović, May 1697 (doc. 307). Granted 15 fields in Trebinje + 15 more in 1696 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 295).
Ivan Prešević — brother/relative of bishop Simeon; granted 15 fields in Trebinje + 15 more 1696 (doc. 295) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Avakum Prešević — sugino (cousin) of Ivan; nephew of bishop Simeon (doc. 295) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Vojin Prešević — sugino of Ivan; nephew of bishop Simeon (doc. 295) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Notes

Multiple spellings in source: Presevich, Prancovich, Prenčević. Canonical form here adopted as Prešević.

surnames/Prolosic.title: Prolosic
surnames/Prolosic.content:
Prološić
Bearers in Desnica II

Zorzi Prološić (Đorđe Prološić) — serdar of Goranci; 10 ducats/month (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Nicolo Prološić — harambaša of Brochno (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Prpic.title: Prpic
surnames/Prpic.content:
Prpić
Bunjevac surname; among the 16 reconstructed families of the 1627 Krmpote migration (Pavličević 1989) Saric-2008-Bunjevci (medium confidence). 1712 popis: present in Švica and Kompolje parishes in Otočka regimenta.

surnames/Pugnic.title: Pugnic
surnames/Pugnic.content:
Punjić (Pugnić)
Single-cluster attestation: Piero Pugnich con due fratelli et figlio — 4 souls in the 1671-12-17 Dračevac roster (doc. 199).

surnames/Punos.title: Punos
surnames/Punos.content:
Punoš
Bearers

Pietro Punoš — 1648-05-07 brought Mehmed Jelovac of Babodol to provveditore Foscolo on the galley of Lorenco Donà as ransom for his two children (doc. 27).
Žorži (Zorzi) Punoš — 1652-09-20 master of Turkish slave Tale Burić of Vakup; Foscarini grants Burić 20-day leave to gather his ransom (doc. 63). 1653-01-16 co-signs the Smiljanić proxy (doc. 70).

surnames/Quirini.title: Quirini
surnames/Quirini.content:
Quirini
Venetian patrician house.
Bearers

Benetto Zorzi Quirini — nobil homo sopracomito (galley captain); his galera carried Cornaro’s correspondence in 1686 (line 7081) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Radasinovic.title: Radasinovic
surnames/Radasinovic.content:
Radašinović
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)

conte Ilija Radašinović of Vrana — pre-war Vrana noble; signatory of the 1684 Vrana petitions to Mocenigo together with the Vrana harambaše (docs 34, 35) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Radic.title: Radic
surnames/Radic.content:
Radić
Bearers

Steffano Radich, harambaša — 1653-01-03 captures alaj-beg Filipović with the Šibenik Morlachi (doc. 68).
Luca Radich, harambaša — 1654-07-26 in 1654 Sv. Zulijan list (doc. 84).
alfier Petar Radić — 1683-11-09 with harambaša Vid Bačić (doc. 332) — co-petitioner for the Boraja-area uskakanje.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Zuanne (Ivan) Radić — harambaša of Blato (Hercegovina) 1694; one of 22 harambašas in the 5000-soul Brochno-Blato-Goranci migration (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Radmilovic.title: Radmilovic
surnames/Radmilovic.content:
Radmilović
Bukovica surname attested in Žegar.
Bearers attested

Mihajlo Radmilović — Morlach who escaped from Žegar to Venetian territory; goods stolen in transit by villagers of Razanci (Marko Matak) and Radovin (Ivan Brkljača and Giacomo Bistrić); ordered restored by Mocenigo (doc 31, 1684). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Notes

Per Desnica’s 1951 editorial footnote (to doc 115), the Radmilović surname is still present in Žegar today (1951). Together with Zelić, Vukčević, and Nanić, the families “came in 1648 with the Jankovićs to Budim near Posedarje and during the Morean War many returned to Lika; Budim is today (1951) ruins”. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

surnames/Radnic.title: Radnic
surnames/Radnic.content:
Radnić
Bearers in Desnica II

prete Gian Francesco Radnić (Ivan Franjo Radnić) — Catholic priest accompanying Zuanne Maršić’s group from Bochno 1693; 10 ducats/month confirmed 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Notes

Possibly related to existing Mijo-Radnić in the wiki person index — confirmation pending.

surnames/Radobilic.title: Radobilic
surnames/Radobilic.content:
Radobilić
Single attestation: Ive Radobilić of Ražanac, killed 1662-02-13 at Otres (Ražanačka godovna knjiga, doc. 119).

surnames/Rados.title: Rados
surnames/Rados.content:
Radoš
Trogir/Klis-area officers; a slaveholding consortium owning Mandići of Sinj.
Bearers

Ivan (Zuanne) Radoš — conte cavalier; head of the consortium that owned Hasan-beg Mandić as slave (docs 5, 33, 60, 65, 68) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
collonello Radoš — brother of Ivan; killed at the Sinj defeat April 1685 (doc 60) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
collonello Rados (later) — galeotta-commander operating with Korponež off Pastrovići March 1686 (doc 131) — possibly the same family Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Rasic.title: Rasic
surnames/Rasic.content:
Rašić
See also Rušić — the source spells Ivan Rašić’s name as both Rassich and as derived from village Rusić (near Mostar). The two pages represent the same kinship cluster.
Bearers in Desnica II

Ivan Rašić (Giovanni Rassich) — see Rušić page. Catholic harambaša of 1692 Mostar→Makarska migration Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 258).

surnames/Razzetini.title: Razzetini
surnames/Razzetini.content:
Razzetini
Bearers

Gerolimo Razzetini (collonel Razzetine) — co-signatory with Pietro Tartaglia and Bortolo Geliseo of the dispatch from the Castelli of Traù to Pietro Valier (line 4522); commanded granatieri alongside Geliseo and govvernator Casotti (line 4542) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Relic.title: Relic
surnames/Relic.content:
Relić

harambaša Giuseppe Relić (Josip Relić) — Goranci 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Renessi.title: Renessi
surnames/Renessi.content:
Renessi (Reneši)
Bearers

kapetan Bošičio (Bossichio) Renesi — 1647 commands the company in which Petar Smiljanić was first enrolled (doc. 20).
Žorži (Zorzi) Renessi — 1677-02-17 governator of Zaravecchia and 4 littoral villages (doc. 232).
Ana of alfier Reneši — 1677-10-01 comare at the baptism of Nikola Nikolić, son of Mitar Nikolić-Pivljanin and Janja Janković (doc. 236).
Francesco Renessi — 1682-11-11 testimonio at Stojan Janković’s signing for Marko Pozder’s horse (doc. 298).

surnames/Renier.title: Renier
surnames/Renier.content:
Renier
Bearers in Desnica II

Giovanni Renier (kavalir) — Venetian consigliere 1697 (doc. 303) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Notes
