surnames/Resincic.title: Resincic
surnames/Resincic.content:
Rešinčić
Single attestation: padre guardian fra Andrija Rešinčić — 1683-12-09 with fra Petar Tintić mediates the Zagorje plea to Donà (doc. 349).

surnames/Rizzi.title: Rizzi
surnames/Rizzi.content:
Rizzi
Bearers

Rizzi — single-mention surname appearing in chunk-2 documents Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Rkac.title: Rkac
surnames/Rkac.content:
Rkać
Bearers

Rade Rkać — companion of Jovan Sudarović of Parčići, Lika; in the original Italian text named Rado Grego — Desnica’s footnote (n. 1, doc 114) explains: “U originalu ‘Grego’, prezrivi naziv za pravoslavne, koji odgovara nazivu rkać”; appeared with Sudarović before Valier in Split on 23 November 1685 and proposed Venetian-side settlement in Žegar (doc 114) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

Notes

The “surname” here may be a confessional epithet rather than a true family name; rkać is not a name a person used of themselves, so this entry preserves the archival usage rather than asserting a continuing lineage.

surnames/Roic.title: Roic
surnames/Roic.content:
Roić
Single attestation: Zorzi Roich da Camegnane — 1653-01-16 co-signs the proxy authorising Smiljanić to plead in Venice (doc. 70 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).

surnames/Rojic.title: Rojic
surnames/Rojic.content:
Rojić (Rožić)
Vlach starešina lineage in Podgorje. Mate-Rojic-b????-Podgorje was head of the largest Vlasi Istre dzemat in 1528 (80 houses) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Mate-Rojic-b????-Podgorje — primićur (1528)

surnames/Rojnovic.title: Rojnovic
surnames/Rojnovic.content:
Rojnović
Vlach starešina lineage in Podgorje. Mikula-Rojnovic-b????-Podgorje led a 57-house dzemat in 1528 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Mikula-Rojnovic-b????-Podgorje — primićur (1528)

surnames/Rorcic.title: Rorcic
surnames/Rorcic.content:
Rorčić
Single attestation: Luka Rorčić — 1648-07-17, “Uskoci iz Kistanje naseljeni u Žeravi više Nina, od 132 pješaka izgubili četvoricu” at Ribnik (doc. 39 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).

surnames/Rosic.title: Rosic
surnames/Rosic.content:
Rošić
Bearers

Vukašin Rošić (Rosić) — harambaša from Čitluk Lički; in February 1685 led 20 Morlak families from Čitluk near Novi (Lika) to the Starigrad/Velebit area; petitioned for the Perušić castle (doc 45) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Rudelic.title: Rudelic
surnames/Rudelic.content:
Rudelić (Rudelja)
Pre-Ottoman Vlachs of the wider Zadar hinterland Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Toponyms Rudele (Kistanje) and Rodaljica reflect their old katun. By 1528 a small dzemat under Pavel-Rudelja-b????-Obrovac in nahija Obrovac. Branches migrated to Rovinjsko Selo in Istria (village judges) and Radovin in Zadar district; from Radovin in 1683 to Karlobag and Šugarje, with some to Smiljan in Lika.
Bearers in this wiki

Pavel-Rudelja-b????-Obrovac — knez, primićur Obrovac dzemat (1528)
Pavo-Rudelic-b????-Smiljan — Smiljan, Lika (1686)

surnames/Rukavina.title: Rukavina
surnames/Rukavina.content:
Rukavina
Major Bunjevac lineage of Lika and Podgorje. The family preserves an oral genealogy tracing its origin to the Vladimirovići of Hum — a noble line said to have been driven out of Raška by the Nemanjići. Šarić treats this as a “raška reminiscencija” reflecting how Bunjevac elite memory absorbed early-Hercegovinian “raško razdoblje” rather than a literal medieval pedigree (the legend was nourished by 18th-c. baroque Slavism and Kačić Miošić’s pjesmarica) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Documented presence

Pre-Candian War — Rukavine were starešine of catholic Morlachs in Jasenica in Morlakija (per Forza 1636 supplementary information cited by Šarić) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
1691 — granted estates by Habsburg authorities in Sv-Mihovil, Sv-Rok, Vratnik, Ricice, Kosinj as part of the Bunjevac influx into recovered Lika (Fras 1835).
1712 Lika–Krbava popis — Rukavina present in the parishes of Budak, Ribnik, Udbina (Lika regiment); Perušić, Kompolje (Otočac regiment); Drežnik-grad, Vaganac (Ogulin regiment).

Andrija Kačić Miošić’s 1756 pjesmarica names Rukavine among “vitezovi hrvatski” alongside Starcevic, Balenovic and Dosen — illustrating the surname’s military prominence by mid-18th c. Saric-2008-Bunjevci

surnames/Rusic.title: Rusic
surnames/Rusic.content:
Rušić (Rusić)
Hercegovinian Catholic family from Mostar district.
Bearers in Desnica II

Ivan Rašić/Rušić (Giovanni Rassich) — from Rusić village (near Mostar); Catholic; led 200 souls / 25 families from Mostar district to Makarska area; settled Zavojane, Stigli, Hadži Lukovo on lands of late Salin-aga Đikić; appointed harambaša Oct 1692 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 258).
Šimun Rusić (Simon Rusich) dalla Torretta (Tornik) — named arbitrator by Lisičić/Podgrađe side in 1702 dispute with Brgud (doc. 348) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Ruzic.title: Ruzic
surnames/Ruzic.content:
Ružić
Vlach kindred originating from Šibenik area, members of the medieval “kraljevski Vlasi” (royal Vlachs) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Migrated to Vodice on Kras 1518; returned to nahija Kličevac (Miranje, Jagodnja) under Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik 1528. After 1538/40 returned to Šibenik area; 1540 morlački katun “Ružić”, with katunar Jure-Heracic-b???? in 1553.
Bearers in this wiki

Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik — knez, head of Kličevac dzemat (1528–~1538)
Jure-Heracic-b???? — katunar of Ružić katun (1553)

surnames/Ruzzini.title: Ruzzini
surnames/Ruzzini.content:
Ruzzini
Venetian patrician house.
Bearers

Marco Ruzzini — Venetian senator (line 4508, 1685) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Sabbini.title: Sabbini
surnames/Sabbini.content:
Sabbini
Bearers

conte Sabbini — Venetian conte exchanged for Zelel-aga Babahmetović during the Candian (1645–1669) War; mentioned retrospectively in March 1685 (doc 56) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Salentich.title: Salentich
surnames/Salentich.content:
Salentich
Bearers in Desnica II

Salentich (governor) — son-in-law of Marija Smiljanić; received green velvet jacket bequest in her 1693 testament (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Husband of Margarita Smiljanić (daughter of Smoljan and Marija).

surnames/Salihagic.title: Salihagic
surnames/Salihagic.content:
Salihagić
Bearers (Muslim Lika)

Murat-aga Salihagić — disdar perušićki; killed February 1663 by Ivan Čačić of Vinjerac on the cestmma of Perušić-area; head exhibited at Castel Venier (doc. 127).
njegov otac (anonymous) — 1663 unsuccessfully offered ransom for his son’s head (doc. 127).
Salihagini ćato (1682) — killed on the road from Sukošan to Zadar; the slave Handan was abducted (doc. 281, Mehmed-beg Filipović’s letter).

surnames/Salomonic.title: Salomonic
surnames/Salomonic.content:
Salomonić
Single-mention surname noted in the source-page summary as one of “hundreds of single-mention surnames with place attestation” captured by this volume.
Bearers

Salomonić — see source page Desnica II summary; specific document citation pending fuller transcription.

surnames/Santic.title: Santic
surnames/Santic.content:
Šantić
Bearers

Damjan Šantić — member of the Radoš consortium that owned Hasan-beg Mandić as slave (doc 65) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Sarcevic.title: Sarcevic
surnames/Sarcevic.content:
Šarčević
Bačka variant of Šarić. Foremost member: Boza-Sarcevic-b????-Subotica (Ambrozije Šarčević) — launched the Bunjevački kalendar in Subotica in 1868, foundational publication of the 19th-c. Bunjevac narodni preporod alongside Ivan-Antunovic-b1815-Backa’s 1870 Bunjevačke i šokačke novine in Kaloča Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

surnames/Saric.title: Saric
surnames/Saric.content:
Šarić
Surname documented in vlach/Bunjevac milieu of the Tromeđa from the 17th c. onward. The major kotarski uskočka branch is Šibenik-based pravoslavna, centered on serdar Cvijan/Cvitko Šarić (active 1647–1668+).
Bearers in this wiki

Cvijan-Saric-b????-Sibenik — serdar šibenskih pravoslavnih Morlaka 1647–1668+; recorded 1660 by Evlija Çelebi as “hrvatski razbojnik” Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Wife Dessa. See his page for the multi-generational genealogy.
Iuan/Ivan Šarić — son of Cvijan & Dessa; baptised 1654-07-02 Sv. Zulijan Šibenik (docs. 81, 83 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).
Žorži (Zorzi) Šarić — harambassa in 1654 Sv. Zulijan parish protest list (doc. 84).
Zuanne/Jovan Šarić — son of Cvijan; family pay transferred to him 1662-03-14 by Korner (doc. 123); back-pay arrears settled by ducal of Doge Alvise Contarini 1682-06-03 (doc. 285).
Đeno Sarić (1842) — early recorder of the Buna-river origin legend, who wrote that the “stara postojbina Bunjevaca” was on the Buna Saric-2008-Bunjevci (no separate page).
Marko-Saric-b????-Zagreb — modern historian, author of Saric-2008-Bunjevci and Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

The 1868-launched Subotica Bunjevački kalendar of Boza-Sarcevic-b????-Subotica is the same surname in its Šarčević variant — bačka spelling of Šarić Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Ibrahim Sarić (Ibrahim Sarich) da Cliuno (Livno) — slave; testified about Knin cadi jurisdiction over Strmica, Bošnjake, Komazlić, Golubić, Starčević etc. (doc. 315, 1699) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Sbizza.title: Sbizza
surnames/Sbizza.content:
Sbizza
Bearers in Desnica II

quartier mastro Luca Sbizza — compare of Marija Smiljanić; executor and legatee in her 1693 will; testimon (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Scutari.title: Scutari
surnames/Scutari.content:
Scutari
Bearers in Desnica II

padre Scutari (provinciale) — Dominican father, recipient in Marija Smiljanić’s 1693 will (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Segotic.title: Segotic
surnames/Segotic.content:
Šegotić
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

surnames/Selakovic.title: Selakovic
surnames/Selakovic.content:
Selaković
Bearers

Iviša Selaković da Scardona, habitante a Visovaz — 1647-12-17 in Šibenik signs (with X) the Petropolje uskakanje contract (doc. 18 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).
Petronije Selaković, kaluđer iz Kistanje (“Krčki kaluđer”) — 1647-05-18 already at work for Foscolo on Morlach defection (doc. 11 footnote); 1648-04-15 Foscolo grants him 4 ducati/month, “Calogero Petronia. Barba e mustacchi castagni, occhi uarii, pel oscuro. Segno sopra la tempia sinistra” (doc. 23). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

surnames/Sfakioto.title: Sfakioto
surnames/Sfakioto.content:
Sfakioto
Greek family of Cretan (Sfakià) origin in Venetian service.
Bearers in Desnica II

Sfakioto — lawyer/advocate working under Provveditor Generale Grimani during the 1699–1701 border demarcation commission following the Treaty of Karlowitz; drafted the cinque processi establishing Venetian rights at Knin, Sinj, and Zvonigrad. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

surnames/Sikic.title: Sikic
surnames/Sikic.content:
Šikić
Morlach colonist family in southern Istria. 1586: Sime-Sikic-b???? and Mate-Sikic-b???? founded the Šikići hamlet near Pula — first attested “bunjevačka” stream into southern Istra Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Sime-Sikic-b???? — Šikići founder (1586)
Mate-Sikic-b???? — Šikići founder (1586)

surnames/Sikiric.title: Sikiric
surnames/Sikiric.content:
Sikirić
Single attestation: Mate Sikirić of Ražanac, killed 1662-02-13 at Otres (doc. 119).

surnames/Siljanovic.title: Siljanovic
surnames/Siljanovic.content:
Šiljanović (Siglanović)
Istrian Vlach starešina Rade-Siljanovic-b???? led peasants to former Vrana district as zakup on Venetian land in 1549 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Possible but unconfirmed continuity with the medieval kraljevski Vlach katun Šiglanovići of Knin županija (14th c.).
Bearers in this wiki

Rade-Siljanovic-b???? — Vlach starešina, settler-leader (1549)

surnames/Sincevic.title: Sincevic
surnames/Sincevic.content:
Sinčević
Bearers

Grubiša Sinčević (father) and Žorži Sinčević (son) — 1684-01-24 hold 4 gold rings, 1 silver ring, 9 silver buttons, gold collana with 8 perusini and 250 pearls — Krivelari pawn jewellery later raided (doc. 366).
Gregorio Cusinovich detto Sian (1684-01-24, doc. 366) — susach worth 5 reali — possibly the same family.

surnames/Sinobad.title: Sinobad
surnames/Sinobad.content:
Sinobad
Budin (Ravni Kotari) capitanska family. Per Desnica’s footnote on doc. 181: in 1684-07-01 Mocenigo granted Jovan Sinobad the kula at Karin when he settled the area with Morlaci from Modrino Selo; the kula is still standing and known as “Sinobaduša.”
Bearers

Pera (Periza, Petar) Sinobad — kapetan di Budin (per doc. 279 his son Jovan is called “figlia [sic, figliolo] del capitano di Budin”). Killed by Ilija Mitrović with his band; houses burned in Budin (doc. 396).
Jovan (Zuanne) Sinobadović = “Zuan Sinobad” — son of Pera; alive 1682-02-17 (doc. 279, deposing about Ćosić’s sheep); 1683-12-26 attests in the murder/plunder by Ilija Mitrović and others of his father and brother (doc. 391, 396); subsequently received the Karin kula.
(1684 unnamed brother) — also killed by Ilija Mitrović’s band.
uncle of Jovan — 1684 prevented from cultivating the family lands by Ilija Mitrović (doc. 396).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
The Sinobad family rises across the Morean War period to become the principal Venetian Morlach kapetanska family of the Knin–Zvonigrad region. Major figures span four generations.
Genealogy (per Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II)

Petar (Pietro/Pera) Sinobad of Posedarje — killed at Brgud at start of Morean War by Radan Matić of Brgud (doc. 331); blood vendetta carried by son Jovan into 1701 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Jovan / Zuanne Sinobad (kavalier) — son of Petar; appointed governor of Zvonigrad 1690-05-24 with company of 50 paesani, salary 14 ducats (doc. 234); appointed governor of Knin krajina 1691-06-20 with 60 fields and vineyards near Bulin Most plus houses in Knin from late Turks Hadži-Kurtović, Hadži-Emorić, Acmet-aga Livaković (docs. 239, 241); reconciled with Mitrović family 1692 (doc. 247); house in Modrino selo, Bukovica, near St. Peter’s church 1692 (doc. 259, casale of Turk Modre, his congiunto); appointed sopraintendente of Knin krajina 1696-10-16 (doc. 293); cavalier of San Marco 1696-01-30 by Doge Valier (Sinj, Čitluk, Klivno) (doc. 283). Died 1715 in Glamoč clash (doc. 372). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Filippo Sinobad — alfier then capitano of Zvonigrad; brother of Jovan; appointed June 1691 to replace Jovan; died before Aug 1694 (docs. 240, 277).
Mihail (Michiel) Sinobad — nephew of Jovan and Filippo; previously held tower of Topolje; appointed captain of Zvonigrad 1694-08-21 to succeed late Filippo (doc. 277); died ~1697, replaced by Andrea (doc. 304). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Andrea (Andrija) Sinobad — son of kavalier Jovan; appointed captain of Zvonigrad company 1697 as a child with tutor “governatore” on father’s merit (doc. 304); later serdar of Knin; died 1725 (referenced 1726, doc. 376). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Giacomo (Jakov) Sinobad — cornetta riformato; cousin of deceased Andrea Sinobad; “ultimo superstite della famiglia”; supplicated 1727 to be made serdar of Knin per family tradition; appointed serdar Knin 1729-12-01 by Vendramin replacing Petar Mitrović-Stojisavljević (docs. 378, 380). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Gvozden Sinobad — uncle (“zio”) of kavalier Jovan; ordered 1699 to return cloak with silver to Anđelija Krišanova Kolundžija (doc. 313). Distinct from Gvozden Radasović. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
The unnamed nephew (sister’s son) of Jovan — leader of haiduks on Mt. Prolog with Vid Petrović and 60 men; attacked Ottoman travellers and a village near Atlagić tower 1702 (doc. 346). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Houses, lands, slaves

Modrino selo, Bukovica — village named after Turk Modre, congiunto of Sinobad; casale assigned to Jovan 1692; later disputed 1697 with Radoš and Sava Kresović who refused to return (docs. 259, 302). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Knin Turkish properties — houses of Acmet-aga Livaković, Hadži-Kurtović, Hadži-Emorić; 60 fields near Bulin Most + Aqua Radeglievaz (doc. 241).
Slave Seifulah of Travnik — confessed in 1702 ransom of 200 reali, silver saber, silver horse-tack (doc. 343).

Notes

The old feud between casa Mitrović and casa Sinobad (“engami implacabili”) was reconciled by Dolfin in 1692; Sinobad moved to Knin to physically separate the two houses Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 247).
Family origin: Posedarje. Ancestors had worked under Turks at Modrino selo (doc. 259).

surnames/Sinovcic.title: Sinovcic
surnames/Sinovcic.content:
Sinovčić
Bearers

Tomo Sinovčić — of Novigrad (Dalmatia); rewarded by Mocenigo on 5 September 1684 for killing 5 Turks at Grahovo plus the kjehaja (lieutenant) of Mazut-paša (doc 32 footnote) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Tomaso Sinovčić — from Novigrad; complained-against by Obrovac inhabitants for taking lands across the river 1690 (doc. 230) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Likely the same man as 1684.

surnames/Skulic.title: Skulic
surnames/Skulic.content:
Škulić
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers (Desnica)
Two Ražanac members killed at the Otres battle 1662-02-13 (doc. 119 — Ražanačka godovna knjiga):

Grubiša Škulić
Ivan Škulić

surnames/Sladovic.title: Sladovic
surnames/Sladovic.content:
Sladović
Catholic Vlach (Bunjevac) lineage — third of the three core Bunjevac katuns named in the 1477 defter (with Krmpotic and Vojnic). Least documented of the three.
1477 attestation
Hercegovina defter, nahija Mostar: džemat of Milosav-sin-Sladica-b????-Mostar, 19 houses. Unusually for the 1477 popis, the džemat is organized by villages (Podci = Podaca in Makarsko primorje; Igre = Igrane on Biokovo; Kozica in Vrgoračka krajina) rather than by transhumant pastures. This suggests either “vlahizirano” sedentary peasants given Vlach status, or a fully territorialized Vlach katun Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
17th c. — westward migration
Early 17th c.: present across Bukovica and Podgorje under vojvoda Gvozden-Sladovic-b????-Mostar; group known as “Gvozdenovi ljudi”. 1605: 20 families joined the Krmpote migration to Lic — surnames Balinović, Brošković, Ilnić, Karanović, Lovrić, Martinović, Mihovilović, Mikulić, Sladović, Veljanić, Vilenica.
After 1605 the group’s fate intertwined with the Krmpote branch. Some Sladovići joined the Senjska-Kapetanija garrison; a Senj-line branch later settled in Licko-Lesce (Otočac). The historian Manojlo-Sladovic-b????-Lika (1856 Pověsti biskupijah Senjske i Modruške) probably descends from this branch Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Bearers in this wiki

Milosav-sin-Sladica-b????-Mostar — 1477 katun head
Gvozden-Sladovic-b????-Mostar — vojvoda, early 17th c.
Manojlo-Sladovic-b????-Lika — historian (1856)

surnames/Smiljanic.title: Smiljanic
surnames/Smiljanic.content:
Smiljanić — poreklom iz Udbine
One of the senior kotarski uskočki lineages, with multi-generational prominence. Originally from Udbina, not Smiljan — Desnica’s correction is critical and overrides the legend.
Genealogy

Petar Smiljanić (founder; d. 1648-07-17 at Ribnik): had two armed sons — Ilija and Filip.
Ilija Smiljanić (b. ~1622, d. 1654-09-08 at Vučjak): serdar; childless? — widow Kata remarried Milivoj Zubičević 1655.
Filip Smiljanić (b. ~1633, d. Jan 1656 in a Šibenik brawl): kapetan; killed before producing heirs.
Smoljan Smiljanić (a/k/a Smoglianovich, also Mihalevich): nephew (nipote) of Ilija and Filip; serdar from 1664; heir of the family pay; uterine half-brother of Šimun and Marko Brajinović (their mother Anka had a first marriage to Frane Brajinović of Spianata-behind-Sv. Marko).

Lazaro Smiljanić (in tenera età 1679): son of Smoljan; capitan of a 50-man company.



Bearers attested in this source

Petar Smiljanić — d. Ribnik 1648.
Ilija Smiljanić — d. Vučjak 1654.
Filip Smiljanić — d. Šibenik 1656; alfier Frane Marininić killed with him.
Smoljan Smiljanić (Smoglianovich) — serdar; kavalier; commandant of Nadin.
Lazaro Smiljanić — capitan, 1679 (doc. 255).
Bartulo Banenović da Pavičići — Germano del carambassà Elia Smiglianich (doc. 66, 1652-10-05) — a kinsman of Ilija ransomed by him.
Kata — Turkish-born wife of Ilija, remarried Milivoj Zubičević (Šibenik). Their son Lukas Zubičević was b. 1665-10-15.

Notes

The Smiljanići of Udbina led the Bukovčani uskakanje — Petar (1648), then his sons Ilija and Filip in succession.
The legend of “Smiljanić Ilija” / “Filip Smiljanić” / “Vuk Smiljanić” in epic poetry goes back to this family but is layered over historical fact.

Sources

Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I — docs. 20 (and footnote 1 for the Udbina correction), 36, 38, 41, 42, 53, 66, 71, 72, 75, 86, 87, 88, 89, 97, 98, 99, 103, 139, 144, 163, 165, 166, 184, 190, 255, 395.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Smiljanić family continues prominently through Morean War and into 18th c.; widow Marija (née Bolić) and son Lazaro provide the testamentary archive.
New bearers and contexts

Marko Smiljanić — capitano; brother of Smoljan; awarded 10 ducats/month 1690-05-21 by Doge Morosini for service in the Morean campaigns (Calamata, Navarino, Modon, Napoli di Romania, Negroponte, Malvasia) (doc. 233). Died 1693-02-23 aged ~46 (b. ~1647) in Zadar; given last unction by don Andrea Caldana; buried San Domenico (doc. 264). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Marija Smiljanić (née Bolić) — widow of Smoljan Smiljanić; testament in Zadar 1693-10-05; died between then and 1694-04-13 when will opened; buried San Domenico; mother of Lazaro and Margarita; sister-in-law of Marko (doc. 267). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Lazzaro (Lazaro) Smiljanić — son of Smoljan and Marija; heir per Marija’s will; wrote his own will 1696-07-28 leaving estate to wife Maria (Bolić) and unborn child, alternately to slaves and Dominicans; commended at siege of Ulcinj 1696 (docs. 267, 289, 299). 1700 supplicated to be made serdar — claimed he was last surviving member of Smiljanić family (doc. 320, with footnote noting supplica’s exaggerations: Filip actually killed in Šibenik brawl 1656, not by Turks; Smoljan’s death at Sinj not corroborated). Eventually appointed serdar of Lower Kotari (succeeding Bože Milković after his ~1700 death); led troops to Italy 1702 (replaced provisionally by Antonio Vujanović); died ~early 1709 (docs. 320, 322, 323, 338, 352, 367, 368, 377). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Maria Bolić-Smiljanić — wife of Lazzaro Smiljanić; pregnant when he wrote will 1696 (doc. 289). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Margarita Smiglianich — daughter of Smoljan and Marija; living 1693 (doc. 267); married a “Salentich governor” who received green velvet jacket bequest. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Marko Smiljanić (the younger) — minor son of Lazar Smiljanić; reserved as serdar of Lower Kotari 1709-02-20 by Vendramin; held captaincy of paesana company in terraferma (docs. 367, 368, 377). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Aloisi (nephew of Marija Smiljanić) — bequeathed silver buttons (doc. 267).
Giovanni / Zuanne (other nephew of Marija) — bequeathed silk sash (doc. 267).
Smiljanić (governor) — one of three serdars sent to negotiate with rebellious Bukovica Morlachi 1704 alongside Gvozden Radasović and Spingaroli (doc. 352) — likely Lazar.

Notes

Per supplica footnote in doc. 320: Filip’s death was in a Šibenik brawl with Venetian soldiers (drunk), not killed by Turks as Lazaro claimed. Smoljan’s claimed death at conquest of Sinj is also doubted by editor.
Marija’s testament debtors include don Gregorio Begna (4 zecchini); recipients include Caterina Pizzocara, Vincenza Pastrović, padre Scutari (provinciale Dominican), Ellena daughter of dottor Cassio (diamond ring), her compare quartier mastro Luca Sbizza.
Notary: Andreas de Toris; consigliere/giudice: Biagio Soppe; commissario: Casseretti; conte di Zara: Giovanni Mirelli (doc. 267).

surnames/Smirich.title: Smirich
surnames/Smirich.content:
Smirich
Bearers in Desnica II

Zorzi Smirich — testimon at opening of Marija Smiljanić’s will 1694-04-13 (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Smolic.title: Smolic
surnames/Smolic.content:
Smolić
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

surnames/Sojat.title: Sojat
surnames/Sojat.content:
Šojat
Bunjevac surname; among the 16 reconstructed families of the 1627 Krmpote migration (Pavličević 1989) Saric-2008-Bunjevci (medium confidence). 1712 popis: present in Priboj parish (Otočac regiment).

surnames/Sokolic.title: Sokolic
surnames/Sokolic.content:
Sokolić
Bearers in Desnica II

Toni Francesco Sokolić — still alive at time of Peri’s report 1695; collected dues at Starigrad and Jablanac during last Frankopans’ time (doc. 281) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Sokolovic.title: Sokolovic
surnames/Sokolovic.content:
Sokolović
Bosnian Ottoman beylik family. Ferhat-beg-Sokolovic-b???? served as kliški sandžakbeg, settled ~200 Istrian Vlach families in Knin area 1568, and uvakufio Tinj (1574) for the Zemunik vakuf with Vojnić Bunjevac colonists Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Ferhat-beg-Sokolovic-b???? — kliški sandžakbeg (1568+)

surnames/Solimano.title: Solimano
surnames/Solimano.content:
Solimano
Bearers

captain Solimano — captain of light cavalry Feb 1685 (doc 51); Italian rendering of Sulayman — bearer possibly a convert from Islam in Venetian service Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Soppe.title: Soppe
surnames/Soppe.content:
Šope (Soppe)
Zadar patrician family with multiple branches active over the period.
Bearers

Petar (Pero) Šope (Soppe) — governator, capitano equitum of Zadar; 1655-02-25 banished by ducal of Doge Molino for cowardice at the Knin battle (doc. 92, 93).
knez Julio (Giulio) Soppe — capitano delle ville littorali. Active across 1683–84: 1683-10-23 leads the company that at Bokanjac–Boccagnazzo turned back the looters; burned the houses of 4 ringleaders (doc. 322). 1683-12-09 with col. Posedarski sent to investigate (doc. 348). 1684-03-01 governator of Zaravecchia (doc. 381). One of the four 1684 direttori (doc. 395).
Giovanni Battista Soppe Fortezza, kavalier — 1668-12-09 leads the Bribir ambush as direttore (doc. 163, 165). 1679 (undated) sent by Valier to Žemunik to confer with Hasan-beg Durakbegović and the krčki kadi (doc. 261).
Biagio (Biasio) Sope dottore — 1682-11-06 nominated for the Liga oversight (doc. 296).
Simon Sope — 1682-11-06 same source.

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

conte Giulio (Julio) Soppe — consigliere in Zadar, witness to the 14 September 1686 Stojan-Janković purchase contract (doc 143); also serving as one of the four 1684 direttori (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
kavalier Giovan Battista Soppe Fortezza — appears across the early Morean War correspondence (docs 15, 19, 24, 32) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Biagio Soppe, dottor — consigliere of corte di Zara, executor of Marija Smiljanić’s 1693 testament (doc. 267) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Giovanni Battista Soppe Fortezza, magnifico signor governator — nobile zaratino consigliere 1701; co-owner of half of Olib island (the other half sold by conte Giacomo Califfi to Zaviša Mitrović 1701-11-26, doc. 336) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Soric.title: Soric
surnames/Soric.content:
Sorić
Catholic Vlach surname, Zadar-hinterland origin. Šarić lists it among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. The line straddles the 1636 župnik through to the Vrana uprising 1683.
Bearers

don Stjepan (Stipan) Sorić — 1636 župnik in Gorica/Tinj parish; 1647 governator de Morlacchi; killed at Ribnik 1648-07-17. See Stipan-Soric-b????-Gorica for full bio.
Mate Sorić — brother of don Stjepan; succeeded him 1648-07-31 as Goričanski capo; received the gold chain originally meant for Stjepan.
Gregorio Sorić — 1683 implied as relative pursuing recovery of pop Stjepan’s preserved hand from Margarita Ivančević (doc. 311).
pop Stevan Sorić of Tepšinci — 1684-03-23 with knez of Tepšinci and Parčići (Lika), pleads to provveditore Donà for asylum and bread for the would-be migrant Lika families; wants to be settled at Obrovac (donji + gornji), per his Cyrillic letter (doc. 385). NOT obviously the same family but the pop Stevan / pop Stjepan coincidence in the same diocese is suggestive.

Notes

The same surname appears among the Šibenik pravoslavni Morlaci — Steffano Sare harambašša at Sv. Zulijan (doc. 84, 1654) — but Sare may be distinct from Sorić, hard to pin down.

surnames/Sorini.title: Sorini
surnames/Sorini.content:
Sorini
Bearers

abbate Sorini — abbot, present as witness in the cancelleria civil pretoria of Zadar (doc at line 4134, 1685) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Spachioto.title: Spachioto
surnames/Spachioto.content:
Spachioto
Bearers

Nicolò Spachioto — witness in the Zadar cancelleria civil pretoria alongside abbate Sorini (doc at line 4135, 1685) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Spingaroli.title: Spingaroli
surnames/Spingaroli.content:
Spingaroli
Zadar noble; long-serving Venetian governator.
Bearers in Desnica II

Francesco Spingaroli — appointed governor of pertinenza 9 (Zaravecchia) by Cornaro in 1689 Liga reform (doc. 224); reappointed governor of Biograd, Pakoštane and Vrana by Dolfin March 1694 (doc. 275); helped at sieges of Castelnuovo and Knin (doc. 286). Age 32 in 1699 (b. ~1667), testified in Sfakioto’s protocols (doc. 315); supplied 25 sessane and 8 horses for Grimani 1699 (doc. 314); in 1704 one of three serdars sent to negotiate with rebellious Bukovica Morlacchi (with Gvozden Radasović and Smiljanić, doc. 352); 1726 governor of Zaravecchia for Lower Kotari (doc. 377) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Spiro.title: Spiro
surnames/Spiro.content:
Spiro
Greek family resident in Venice.
Bearers in Desnica II

Petar (Piero) Spiro Greco — Greek who maintained pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža in Venetian custody for ~40 years. On 29 March 1746, after Jagodić’s release by the State Inquisitors, Petar Spiro was entrusted with him: ordered “non lasciarlo sortire dal circondario de Greci” (not to leave the Greek quarter) and to send him home at the first opportunity (doc 390). Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

surnames/Spolverino.title: Spolverino
surnames/Spolverino.content:
Spolverino
Bearers

conte collonello Spolverino — distinguished himself in the early actions at the 1686 Sinj-Salona campaign (lines 6457, 6467) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Stanisic.title: Stanisic
surnames/Stanisic.content:
Stanišić
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Zorzi (Đurađ) Stanković (Stancovich) — Gorica resident; goods stolen in 1693-11-04 raid; recognized Žegar dialect of raiders (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Surname spelled Stanković in the source.
See also separate Stojanović entry.

Note: a Nikanor Stanković of Velika appears at Šaramprov of Kalinika 1698, protected from Bishop Busović’s harassment (doc. 308) — surname Stanković, possibly distinct from Stanišić Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Stankovic.title: Stankovic
surnames/Stankovic.content:
Stanković
Bearers in Desnica II

Zorzi (Đurađ) Stanković (Stancovich) — Gorica resident; goods stolen in 1693-11-04 raid; recognized Žegar dialect of raiders (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Nikanor Stanković (Nichinor Stancouich) — from Velika; location Šaramprov of Kalinika; protected from Bishop Nikodim Busović’s harassment 1698 (doc. 308) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Starcevic.title: Starcevic
surnames/Starcevic.content:
Starčević
Bunjevac lineage that became one of the most consequential families in 19th-c. Croatian political history. The surname appears in the 1627 (second) Krmpote migration to Lic Saric-2008-Bunjevci; settled in Veliki Žitnik / Pazarište after the 1690 colonization of Lika.
Lika progenitor and the Bunjevačka buna
Porkulab Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik (1656–?) settled at Pazariste in 1690. Per the 1712 popis (Kaser 2003), he held 168 štrikova (parcels) in Pazarište, Vaganac, and Žitnik, with one son Jakov (age 20) and five other family members.
His conflict with vojvoda Marko-Butorac-b????-Lika in 1702 sparked the Ribnicka-Buna-1702 (also “Bunjevačka buna”).
Lika regiment officers (mid-18th c.)
Miloš’s sons Jakov-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste and Matija-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste became kapetani in the newly formed Lika regiment in 1746. Andrija Kačić Miošić, in Razgovor ugodni naroda slovinskoga (1756), celebrated Jakov among the “vitezovi hrvatski” — early evidence that Bunjevac kin in Lika were absorbing a Hrvatski (regimental/zemaljski) identity Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
The grammarian and the founder of HSP

Jakov’s grandson Filip-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste — village knez at end of 18th c.
Filip’s son Sime-Starcevic-b1784-Lika (1784–1859) — priest and grammarian, promoter of “zemaljski” / “pučki” hrvatstvo.
Šime’s nephew Ante-Starcevic-b1823-Veliki-Zitnik (1823–1896) — founder of modern Croatian etnonacionalni identity (Hrvatska stranka prava).

The Klan Starčevića continued in the political work of David and Mile Starčević. Šarić uses the lineage as the paradigmatic case of how Lika Bunjevci absorbed a modern Croatian national identity within a single century Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Note on confessional drift
The 1712 popis lists Starčević as a surname shared between Bunjevci (Catholic) and Orthodox Vlasi in Lika–Krbava — one of 37 such overlapping surnames documenting common Dinaric origin Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Bearers in this wiki

Milos-Starcevic-b1656-Veliki-Zitnik — porkulab Pazarišta, 1702 buna
Jakov-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste — Lika regiment kapetan, 1746
Matija-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste — Lika regiment kapetan, 1746
Filip-Starcevic-b????-Pazariste — knez (late 18th c.)
Sime-Starcevic-b1784-Lika — priest, grammarian
Ante-Starcevic-b1823-Veliki-Zitnik — founder of HSP

surnames/Stipcevic.title: Stipcevic
surnames/Stipcevic.content:
Stipčević
Single attestation: Gabriel Stipčević — 1663-04-21 compare (godparent) at the baptism of Đurđe (Zorzi) son of Dragosav Busović and Todora at Sv. Zulijan Šibenik (doc. 129).

surnames/Stojanovic.title: Stojanovic
surnames/Stojanovic.content:
Stojanović
Bearers

Constadin (Kostadin) Stojanović of Oton — 1652-10-05 Turkish-subject slave on the galley of Antonio Barbaro; offered as ransom for Bartul Banenović of Pavičići (Ilija Smiljanić’s germano) (doc. 66).
Mihovil Stojanović — 1684-03-01 named capitano of Pakoštani (doc. 381).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Nikola Stojanović (Nicolo Stoianovich) — courier; named in 1734 as messenger to forward money to imprisoned pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža in Venetian Pozzi/Camerotti prisons (doc. 385) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Stojisavljevic.title: Stojisavljevic
surnames/Stojisavljevic.content:
Stojisavljević
Vrlika-area family connected by marriage to the Mitrović line.
Bearers in Desnica II

Novko Stojisavljević — patriarch of the line. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Vučen Stojisavljević (son of Novko) — married Marija Mitrović (of the Žegar Janković-Mitrović line); adopted compound name Mitrović-Stojisavljević. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II
Petar Mitrović-Stojisavljević — descendant carrying the compound surname. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

Notes

The marriage tied the Vrlika line to the Janković-Mitrović clan; compound surname preserves this kin-link in matica records.

surnames/Stoljic.title: Stoljic
surnames/Stoljic.content:
Stiljić
Single attestation: Jurašin Stiljić, novi habitant Posedarja — 1663-05-08 ordered by Contarini to be brought before him by force if necessary by the kotari sudci Mirko Knežević, Stojan Mitrović, Pavle Vučević, Milinko Barićević (doc. 131).

surnames/Strmic.title: Strmic
surnames/Strmic.content:
Strmić
Bearers

Matija (Mattio) Strmić — member of the Radoš consortium that owned Hasan-beg Mandić as slave (doc 65) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Sudarovic.title: Sudarovic
surnames/Sudarovic.content:
Sudarović
Bearers

Jovan (Zuanne) Sudarović of Parčići — Lika Morlach harambaša with c. 150–300 men under arms, settled in Karlobag and upper Obrovac on the Habsburg side. The Imperial commissar (a Karlović) tried to retain him with the offer of life-tenure as captain of Karlobag plus privileges, but Sudarović preferred Venice; on 23 November 1685 (doc 114) appeared with his companion Rade Rkać before Pietro Valier in Split and proposed to settle in the abandoned Žegar castle with a paid 100-man company plus food provisions until harvest, bringing a small cannon captured from the Udbina Turks. Awarded 4 cecchini for travel and sent back to Janković and the cavalry provveditor Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Sugaric.title: Sugaric
surnames/Sugaric.content:
Šugarić
Surname listed by Šarić among Zadar-hinterland anthroponyms with medieval-modern continuity Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Šugarje in Podgorje is the relocation site for Rudelic families from Radovin in 1683.

surnames/Susic.title: Susic
surnames/Susic.content:
Šušić
Bearers

harambaša Radivoj Šušić — 1648-07-17: “Uskoci iz Ugaraka naseljeni u Žeravi od 60 ljudi izgubili trojicu” at Ribnik (doc. 39 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).
Martin Suskovich da Budin — 1683-12-16 missing after the Pađen-Knin battle, possibly killed (doc. 353); 1684-04-07 in the Sinobad case complainants list (doc. 391).

surnames/Sutic.title: Sutic
surnames/Sutic.content:
Šutić
Single attestation: fra Grga (Gregorio) Šutić — Bosnian Franciscan; 1683-11 reports to Donà his secret meeting with the rebel knez Ilija da Radassinovzi, conte Marko Klarić of Stankovci, harambaša Martin Đagnimić and harambaša Idero (Ždero) at the village Uselize sopra Vrana — pivotal document for the Vrana uprising (doc. 333).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)

fra Grgur Šutić — continues to act as Bosnian Franciscan cappellano / mediator; appears in the 1684 Vrana petitions to Mocenigo and in the post-rising negotiations (docs 34, 36) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Svetacki.title: Svetacki
surnames/Svetacki.content:
Svetački
Slavonian noble lineage, members entered Ottoman service in 1540 — example of frontier elite ambivalent loyalties (Mujadžević 2023, cited by Šarić) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

surnames/Tadic.title: Tadic
surnames/Tadic.content:
Tadić
Bearers

knez Nikola Tadijić — 1648-07-17 uskočki leader: “Uskoci iz Krmpote naseljeni ispod Poljica, od 150 pješaka izgubili 10” at the Battle of Ribnik (doc. 39 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).
Nicolo Tadich da Carpote — 1653-01-16 same individual; co-signs the proxy authorising Ilija Smiljanić to plead the Morlachi case in Venice (doc. 70).
Tadić (capitan) of Starigrad — owner of Mlin del conte Tadijch in the perimeter of the 1679 land allocation to the Sv. Juraj uskoks (doc. 258).

surnames/Tagga.title: Tagga
surnames/Tagga.content:
Tagga
Single attestation: captain of Knin Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc. 224 context). Stub page.

surnames/Tanusi.title: Tanusi
surnames/Tanusi.content:
Tanusi
Likely an Albanian / Oltremarini surname (cf. the medieval Albanian tribe Tanushi).
Bearers

major Tanusi — major in the Oltremarini; killed at the Sinj defeat April 1685 (docs 17, 60) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Tardic.title: Tardic
surnames/Tardic.content:
Tardić (Gajdić)
Croatian-Šibenik lineage of Murat-beg-Gajdic-b????-Sibenik (formerly Tardić), the first sanjakbeg of Sandzak-Klis. Old surname Tardić; the Ottoman variant “Gajdić” appears alongside it in sources. Origin and Šibenik kin documented in Juran 2016 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
Bearers in this wiki

Murat-beg-Gajdic-b????-Sibenik — subaša/voivod of Vilajet Hrvati, first sanjakbeg of Klis

surnames/Tartaglia.title: Tartaglia
surnames/Tartaglia.content:
Tartaglia
Trogir/Kaštela-area officer family.
Bearers

Pietro Tartaglia — officer at Duare (Zadvarje) 1685; co-signatory with Geliseo and Razzetini of dispatches to Valier from the Castelli of Traù (docs 60, and lines 4522, 4586) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Tepsic.title: Tepsic
surnames/Tepsic.content:
Tepšić
Bearers

Rade Tepšić — Lika Morlach resident in Zadar city; January 1686 brought legal action against Ostoja Gagić of Biljane for an unliquidated debt; agreed to release Gagić under bail (doc 124, 29 Jan 1686) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Tiepolo.title: Tiepolo
surnames/Tiepolo.content:
Tiepolo
Bearers in Desnica II

provveditor Tiepolo — earlier provveditor de cavalli who had Gorica burnt because 10 banditi were there; recalled retrospectively in 1693 (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Tintic.title: Tintic
surnames/Tintic.content:
Tintić
Single attestation: fra Petar (Piero) Tintić — capellano da Petropoglie. 1683-12-09 envoy of harambaša Matija Nakić and the conti of Petropolje (1000 households) to provveditore Donà, asking either war declaration or guidance how to be protected from Venetian-side raids (doc. 349).

surnames/Tintor.title: Tintor
surnames/Tintor.content:
Tintor
Bearers

Filippo Tintor — capo of Šibenik-territory horse; arrived at Bribir with ten cavalrymen during the November 1686 Bosnian Pasha incursion; sent by Stojan Janković to alert the Zadar contado capi (doc 155, Stojan’s deposition 16 Nov 1686) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Tomadelli.title: Tomadelli
surnames/Tomadelli.content:
Tomadelli
Bearers in Desnica II

Gerolamo Tomadelli — signed for Zaviša Mitrović because Zaviša couldn’t write Italian (doc. 279) — Zaviša signed in Cyrillic only Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Tomasoni.title: Tomasoni
surnames/Tomasoni.content:
Tomasoni
Bearers in Desnica II

Francesco Tomasoni — owned a botteghetta (small shop) in Obrovac 1696 (doc. 290) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Possibly = the merchant Tomasoni of Zadar referenced in Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I doc. 234.

surnames/Tomicic.title: Tomicic
surnames/Tomicic.content:
Tomičić
Bearers

harambaša Martin Tomičić — 1648-07-17: “Uskoci iz Drvenika naseljeni kod Nina od 100 ljudi izgubili petoricu” at Ribnik (doc. 39 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).

Notes

The same name Tomicich is one of three sub-villages of Rudopolje in Lika that don Sorić burned in 1648-06-18 (with Vodena Glava and Pancino selo — doc. 32). Whether Martin Tomičić’s family stem from this Lika locality is plausible but not directly attested.

surnames/Tomisic.title: Tomisic
surnames/Tomisic.content:
Tomišić
Bearers in Desnica II

Andrea Tomišić (Andrija Tomišić) — killed by Ilija Janković in 1692; from Gorica (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Tomljanovic.title: Tomljanovic
surnames/Tomljanovic.content:
Tomljanović
Bunjevac surname; among the 16 reconstructed families of the second (1627) Krmpote migration to Lič (Pavličević 1989) Saric-2008-Bunjevci (medium confidence). 1712 popis: present in Lika regiment parishes (e.g. Kompolje); also Tomljenović variant in Zavalje (Ogulin regiment).

surnames/Torbic.title: Torbic
surnames/Torbic.content:
Torbić
Bearers in Desnica II

harambaša Michiel Torbić (Mihovil Torbić) — Goranci 1694 (doc. 274) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Tori.title: Tori
surnames/Tori.content:
Tori
Bearers

surnames/Vojnic.title: Vojnic
surnames/Vojnic.content:
Vojnić (Vojihnić)
Catholic Vlach (Bunjevac) lineage from western Hercegovina — one of the three core Bunjevac katuns of the 1477 defter (with Krmpotic and Sladovic).
Medieval and early-Ottoman attestations

1408 — first mention as Vlasi Vojihnići in a charter of Bosnian king Stjepan Ostoja; subjects of the W. Hum noble line Radivojević-Vlatković Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
1477 — Hercegovina defter, nahija Mostar: džemat of Vukasin-sin-Vojihne-b????-Mostar, 10 houses + 3 unmarried. Wintered/summered with vojvoda Vladimir’s katun across W. Hercegovinian planinas and župas.

Klis sandjak phase
Colonized into the conquered Croatian frontier in the early 16th c. The village Vojnić near Trilj likely a transit toponym. By Hrabak’s evidence, also at Dobropoljci in Bukovica. After the Cyprus-War-1570-1573, Ferhat-beg-Sokolovic-b???? resettled them on his new Tinj vakuf (1573–1574); the area thereafter known as Vojnići or Županovići, after starešine Milos-Zupanovic-b????-Tinj and Filip-Zupanovic-b????-Tinj. 1550: dzemat of knez Mihovil-Vojihnic-b????-Sinj in nahija Sinj Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
17th c. — split between three powers

1605 — 15 Vojnić families joined the Krmpote migration to Lic: Božić, Galešić, Jurjević, Matijević, Pavličić, Petković, Stojčević, Vojnić, Vojnović.
1619 — starešine Miloš Županović and Mate-Vuksic-b????-Tinj negotiated with the senjski kapetan to bring ~1500 Vojnići to Habsburg territory; migration did not happen.
1636 — Forza vizitacija reports župa Županovići: 6 villages (Gorica, Raštane, Prkos, Bubnjane, Lišane Tinjske, Brkljačina Polača), 1550 souls; župnik Stipan-Soric-b????-Gorica.
1647 (Candian War) — most Vojnići crossed to Venetian territory. Knez Filip-Zupanovic-b????-Tinj led part of them to Valtura near Pula.

Possible Bačka connection
Per Sekulić 1986, the Vojnić family of Subotica (ennobled 1741, listed among Subotica graničari 1687) traces origin to Dalmatia — Šarić raises but doesn’t resolve whether they descend from the Tinj/Županović Vojnići Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

surnames/Vukcevic.title: Vukcevic
surnames/Vukcevic.content:

Pavle (Paval) Vukčević — 1663-05-08 harambaša guarding the Brusevo pass with men of Žegar, Ervenik and Posedarje (doc. 130). 1666-05-06 elected vice-harambaša of Posedarje by unanimous vote during Stojan Janković’s captivity (doc. 152).
Nikola Vukčević — 1673-05-01 piezzo for Vuko Kovač (doc. 204). 1684-04-07 with Jovan Sinobad and others, victim of Ilija Mitrović’s plundering (doc. 391).
Vuk Vukčević — 1679-05-16 protected by mandate from his son’s kidnappers (doc. 247): “ne per se ne per interposte persone ardiscano offender, molestar, o inquietar…” Vule (a son of Dragosav Capelletto Budin) and Bogoie his nephew are warned off Radojica Garković’s house — Vukčević / Garković feud spillover.
Vukadin Vukčević — 1679 son of Dragosav (doc. 247).
Bogoje Vukčević — 1679 nephew of Dragosav (doc. 247).
Guozden Vuccevich — 1684-04-07 also among the Sinobad case complainants (doc. 391).
Simon Vuccevich — 1684-04-07 ditto (doc. 391).

Notes

The Vukčevići of Budin are documented in 1684 in feud (krvarina) with the Mitrovići; Polo Michiel asked to mediate (doc 15, Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II).
Per Desnica’s 1951 editorial footnote (to doc 115), the Vukčević surname is still present in Žegar today (1951). Together with Zelić, Radmilović, and Nanić, the families “came in 1648 with the Jankovićs to Budim near Posedarje and during the Morean War many returned to Lika; Budim is today (1951) ruins”. Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II

surnames/Zabetic.title: Zabetic
surnames/Zabetic.content:

Bearers in Desnica II

Notes

The two events bracket Žabetić family involvement in faction violence against Venetian-recognised authority over an ~12-year span: brother executed for the Vrana murder of 1692, then Mattio himself ringleader of the 1704 Bukovica revolt.
Connected family: Tubić (Tomaso Tubić, banished and pardoned for the same 1692 cluster).

surnames/Zuljevic.title: Zuljevic
surnames/Zuljevic.content:
Žuljević
Bearers

don Pavao (Pava) Žuljević — redovnik (priest) from the Poljica province; volunteered to enter slavery at Sinj as a hostage substitute for vojvoda Ivan Marušić in the cell of Šain-aga Mandić, while Marušić travelled to discuss his ransom with the generale Valier (doc 110, undated, Marušić’s Bosnian-Cyrillic letter to Stipan Garković) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/Zupanovic.title: Zupanovic
surnames/Zupanovic.content:
Županović (Župan)
Vojnić starešina family — gives name to the “Županovići” subregion around Tinj Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. The Catholic-Vlach population of this župa was pastorally tended by don Stjepan Sorić in 1636 Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Bearers (Desnica)

harambaša Bose (Bože) Županović — 1647-08-31 capitan in Foscolo’s command (doc. 16); 1652-09-24 holds the Turk Rustem-beg as his slave purchased from Janko Mitrović after the Grahovo battle (doc. 64); 1653-01-16 governator Bose Zuppanovich co-signs the proxy authorising Smiljanić to plead in Venice (doc. 70). Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I

In Desnica II (1684–1749)

Jadre Zuppanović (Župan) — from Gorica; killed by Ilija Janković in 1692 (doc. 268) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Tomica Župan (Tomiza Zupan) — Obrovac inhabitant 1696 (doc. 284) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

surnames/del-Borro.title: del-Borro
surnames/del-Borro.content:
del Borro
Tuscan-Italian marchesi in Venetian military service.
Bearers

Nicolò del Borro — marchese, sergente maggior battaglia Dalmatia 1684–85 (docs 33, 60–61); later sargente generale di battaglia (doc 10388) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
